Request for Information (RFI): Enterprise Document Management Platform & CEDMS Modernization

BLUF: The Department of War (DoW) is seeking information on cloud-native, platform-as-a-service (PaaS) capabilities via the Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC) to establish a foundational Enterprise Document Management Platform. The immediate mission is the modernization of the Corporate Electronic Document Management System (CEDMS) and the digitization of 1.5 billion legacy microfiche records. The architecture must be designed from the ground up as a multi-tenant environment capable of transforming unstructured document text into highly reportable data, and eventually subsuming future document management systems across the enterprise.

1.0 Vision, Problem, and Foundational Strategy

For several years, the Department has been challenged by a complex and fragmented landscape of legacy document management systems, creating data silos and complicating enterprise-wide reporting and auditability. The goal is to move away from these siloed, custom-coded applications and toward a standardized, cloud-native data fabric.

The platform must be built to support:

Initial Mission: Rapid ingestion, Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and management of 1.5 billion legacy microfiche records, transforming this unstructured data into a queryable asset.

Mid-Term Mission (CEDMS Modernization): Completing the CEDMS modernization effort by fully subsuming all existing CEDMS functions and serving as the primary enterprise document management system for the organization.

Long-Term Mission: Serving as an extensible, multi-tenant repository capable of onboarding disparate document systems across the Department while providing unprecedented, enterprise-wide business intelligence and data exploitation capabilities.

1.1 Summary of the Modernization Initiative

The Problem: The core issue is the 5.88 million physical microfiche sheets which are degrading, non-compliant with NARA standards, and incur over $1.1 million in annual manual retrieval costs.

The Vision: The project aims to execute a full digital transformation by digitizing approximately 1.5 billion records to the stringent FADGI 3-Star standard, building a new secure IL5 cloud Document Management System (DMS), and eventually decommissioning existing systems like CEDMS to achieve significant ROI.

The Strategy: The project is broken into two parallel efforts:

Digitization: A vendor will be contracted to scan the physical microfiche, creating both preservation-quality TIFFs and searchable PDF access copies.

Platform Modernization: A new, multi-tenant cloud DMS will be built on the Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC) infrastructure to ingest these records and serve as the foundation for future enterprise document management.

1.2 CEDMS System Overview

CEDMS includes two primary sub-systems:

CEDMS-CDA (Corporate Electronic Document Management System - Custom Designed Application)

CEDMS-MSS (Corporate Electronic Document Management System - Monarch SharePoint Solution)

CEDMS-CDA

CEDMS-CDA serves as a centralized, secure archival repository for a wide range of official financial and accounting documents for the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) and other DoD organizations. Its primary purpose is to automate the conversion of hard-copy documents into a searchable electronic format, reducing dependency on paper records.

Core Capabilities:

Document Capture and Ingestion: The system is capable of ingesting documents from multiple sources, including batch scanning of hard copy documents, web-based uploads, and secure file transfers (SFTP). It supports various file formats such as TIF, PDF, Microsoft Office files (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), and text files.

Archival and Storage: CEDMS-CDA provides a secure, web-based repository for the permanent storage of documents. All data at rest is protected through encryption.

Document Processing: It utilizes Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology (Kofax Capture, ERM Perfect) to make the full text of documents searchable. This includes the ability to automatically identify and index document content.

Search and Retrieval: The system provides sophisticated search capabilities, allowing users to find documents based on specific index fields or through full-text keyword searches. It offers both a basic and an advanced search module for precise document retrieval.

Access Control and Security: Access is restricted to authorized users via Common Access Card (CAC) authentication. The system enforces a role-based access control (RBAC) model, ensuring that users can only view documents based on their assigned site, organization, document category, and document type permissions.

Reporting and Auditing: CEDMS-CDA provides a variety of reports, including statistical, productivity, access level, and log event reports. It maintains an audit trail of user and system activities.

CEDMS-MSS

CEDMS-MSS is an electronic replacement for printed financial reports. It provides a secure, web-based application for the storage, retrieval, and management of reports for DFAS and other DoD organizations, significantly improving the timeliness of financial information and generating cost savings by eliminating paper and printing costs.

Core Capabilities:

Report Processing and Publishing: CEDMS-MSS receives report files from various source systems. It uses Altair Monarch to automatically process and model these reports, which are then published to secure SharePoint sites.

Centralized Repository: The system provides a single, secure, and reliable centralized repository for storing and managing a large volume of DFAS and DoD reports.

Web-Based Access and Retrieval: Authorized users can access and retrieve reports through a secure SharePoint web interface. Users can search for specific reports and display them on their local workstations for viewing.

"View-Only" and User-Centric Data Manipulation: Reports stored within CEDMS-MSS are presented as "view-only" to preserve the integrity of the original report. Any data manipulation is performed by the user on their local workstation after the report has been downloaded.

Security and Access Control: Like CEDMS-CDA, access is restricted to authorized CAC holders. The system utilizes SharePoint's robust permission model to enforce access control, ensuring users can only access reports for which they have a "need-to-know."

Report Retention: Reports are retained in accordance with DFAS Retention Policy, allowing for future viewing and auditing as required.

2.0 Information Requested from Industry

Please provide detailed responses to the following areas, focusing on how your approach creates a scalable, highly reportable, long-term foundation without relying on proprietary custom software:

 

3.0 Submission Instructions & Disclaimer

 

Disclaimer: This Request for Information (RFI) is for market research and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Request for Quotation (RFQ). Information received will not be disclosed outside of the U.S. Government. A response to this RFI is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with submitting a response to this RFI.

Area of Inquiry | Specific Questions for Industry

1. Cloud-Native Foundation | Detail how you leverage JWCC-native services for OCR, indexing, search, and user interface. How does this approach reduce sustainment labor and TCO compared to a custom software stack? The platform must possess Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) capabilities capable of retroactively analyzing a massive backlog of ingested, basic-OCR'd PDFs (~1.5 billion records) to autonomously classify document types and extract structured metadata fields without manual human data entry.

2. Massive Ingestion | Provide the technical strategy for the rapid ingestion and indexing of 1.5 billion microfiche records. 
Describe plan for integrating the specific deliverables from the FADGI 3-Star digitization. This includes:
Automated ingestion of dual-file (TIFF/PDF) deliverables.
Processing of the specific metadata manifest format (CSV/JSON) that the digitization vendor will provide.
A workflow for handling the "Batch" delivery and quality control process, including how the system will support the government's QA validation process before records are accepted.
Process for automatically linking the files and indexing the PDF text layer for immediate enterprise search.


3. Data Exploitation & Reporting | How does your solution utilize native cloud analytics (e.g., AI/ML, NLP, and native BI tools) to transform 1.5B OCRed documents into a highly reportable dataset? Detail the platform's ability to support dynamic dashboards and cross-document trend analysis.

4. Multi-Tenant Scalability | Describe how the architecture supports multiple tenant organizations. How is data isolation maintained at scale while utilizing shared cloud-native services?

5. API-First Integration | How does your design utilize standardized APIs to enable future legacy systems to migrate data or "plug in" to the platform without requiring core redesigns?

6. Zero-Trust & Records Mgmt | How does the solution integrate native cloud Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) to enforce Zero-Trust at the document and metadata level?

7. Future Subsumption | Provide a detailed notional roadmap for migrating an application like CEDMS, while maintaining MOSA compliance.
Respondents should describe:
Their proposed methodology for analyzing, mapping, and migrating the two distinct CEDMS sub-systems (CDA and MSS).
How their platform would replicate or replace core CEDMS capabilities (e.g., role-based access based on site/org/category, report processing from Altair Monarch).
How their API-first approach would specifically connect to the source systems that currently feed CEDMS.

8. Cost Estimate (ROM) | Provide a non-binding Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) for planning purposes. Please break this down by: (1) Initial implementation and ingestion of the 1.5B records, and (2) Estimated annual sustainment/cloud consumption costs for the steady state.

9. Corporate Experience | Provide a list of recent and relevant contracts from the last 3-5 years (include contract number, dollar value, period of performance, and scope). Provide CAGE code, UEI/DUNS, and small business status.

Detail | Instruction

Response Format | White paper (PDF or Word format), maximum of 25 pages.

Point of Contact | Gerald Whitsett          Gerald.l.whitsett.civ@mail.mil

Suspense Date | June 15th, 2026   at 1pm EST

Classification | All responses must be UNCLASSIFIED.

Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source – Data Analysis and Harmonization Services for the 
Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP)  
Notice ID:  NIH-NOI-26-PCA-NIA-05203 
Department/Ind. Agency: Department of Health and Human Services  
Sub-tier: National Institutes of Health 
Office: NIA/CARD 
General Information  
• Notice Type:  Special Notice / Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
• Posted Date: June 11, 2026 
• Response Date:  June 23, 2026 
• Response Time:  11:00 AM Eastern Time 
• Classification Code:  B – Special Studies and Analysis – Not R&D 
• NAICS Code:  518210 – Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web 
Hosting, and Related Services  
Description 
This is a Notice of Intent to Sole Source and is not a request for competitive quotations or 
proposals. The National Institute on Aging (NIA), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Department 
of Health and Human Services (HHS), intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed-price purchase 
order on a sole source basis to:  
Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania  
D102 Richards Building  
3700 Hamilton Walk  
Philadelphia, PA 19104  
UEI: GM1XX56LEP58  
for Data Analysis and Harmonization Services  in support of the  Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing 
Project (ADSP).  
The anticipated period of performance is  August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2027 . 
Authority 
This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of  FAR 13.106- 1(b)(1), Soliciting from a 
Single Source, as only one source is reasonably available to satisfy the agency’s requirements.  
Requirement Description  

The Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP) is a large NIH -funded effort to identify the 
genetic architecture of Alzheimer’s disease through sequencing and analysis of DNA from tens of 
thousands of individuals. The Government requires contractor supp ort for the processing, 
harmonization, and storage of  4,799 unaligned raw sequencing datasets  from Vanderbilt 
University Medical Center and the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center.  
Required services include, but are not limited to:  
• Genome analysis and harmonization on Amazon Cloud using the ADSP SNV/INDEL and 
SV calling pipelines  
• Processing raw sequencing data, including CRAM to BAM conversion, read remapping 
using BWA, sorting reads, and marking duplicates  
• Base quality score recalibration using GATK BQSR and realignment around known indels 
using GATK IndelRealigner 
• Calling SNVs and indels using GATK HaplotypeCaller  
• Calling structural variants using tools such as Strelka, Manta, and Smoove  
• Performing quality assurance checks, including sex check, contamination check, and 
relatedness checks  
• Staging sequencing data on Amazon S3 standard storage for two months  
• Providing storage of up to 50 GB per genome, including CRAM and genomic VCF outputs  
• Providing Amazon S3 and Glacier storage for three years 
• Ensuring the Government’s 4,799 samples are directly comparable with the existing 
ADSP combined sequencing datasets to maintain full methodological continuity  
Sole Source Rationale  
The Government has determined that the  Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania, through 
the Genome Center for Alzheimer’s Disease (GCAD)  and the NIA Genetics of Alzheimer’s 
Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS), is the only source capable of meeting the requirement 
without unacceptable risk.  
GCAD has established and maintained the standardized processing and joint -calling pipeline 
used across existing ADSP whole genome sequencing data releases. The required work must be 
performed in a manner fully consistent with the existing ADSP dataset to a void technical 
heterogeneity and batch effects that could compromise downstream analyses. NIAGADS is the 
NIH-designated controlled- access repository for ADSP data and provides the established 
infrastructure, governance, access controls, and dissemination framework necessary to securely 
host, manage, and share these data.  

While other vendors may possess general cloud- based genomic data processing capabilities, the 
Government is not aware of any other source that can provide the required  full methodological 
continuity,  direct comparability with the existing ADSP dataset, and integration with the 
established ADSP repository environment.  
Responses 
This notice is for informational purposes only. Interested organizations may submit a capability 
statement demonstrating their ability to meet the Government’s requirement as stated in this 
notice. Capability statements must clearly address the ability to:  
1. Process 4,799 genomes using the established ADSP SNV/INDEL and SV calling 
pipelines; 
2. Maintain full methodological continuity with the existing ADSP harmonized dataset;  
3. Provide secure cloud -based staging, storage, and dissemination consistent with ADSP 
and NIH controlled- access requirements; and  
4. Deliver the required services within the stated period of performance.  
Responses must be received no later than June 25, 2026, at 11:00 AM Eastern Time. Responses 
received after the closing date and time may not be considered. 
Responses shall be submitted via email to both points of contact below with the subject line:  
Response to NOI Sole Source – ADSP Data Analysis and Harmonization Services  
Primary Point of Contact  
Linda Smith  
Contracting Officer  
linda.smith2@nih.gov  
Secondary Point of Contact 
Danielle Tines 
Procurement Technician 
danielle.tines@nih.gov  
Disclaimer 
This notice does not constitute a solicitation, request for quote, or request for proposal. This

STATEMENT OF WORK 
 
 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
Title of Project: 
Data Analysis and Harmonization Services   
 
Statement of Need and Purpose: 
Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP) is a large, NIH-funded effort to uncover the 
genetic architecture of Alzheimer’s disease by sequencing and analyzing DNA from tens of 
thousands of individuals. Contractor will provide data processing and data storage related to the 
ADSP project.  
 
Background Information and Objective: 
ADSP is a massive multi-cohort genomic dataset built from diverse Alzheimer’s populations 
designed to uncover genetic drivers of disease continuously expanding in scale, diversity, and 
datas types. As more samples are added to the dataset, samples need to be harmonized by 
making data from different studies, cohorts, or platforms consistent, comparable, and usable 
together. Data analysis and harmonization is essential because ADSP data comes from dozens 
of cohorts collected over many years using different methods. 
 
Period of Performance: 
August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2027 
 
SCOPE OF WORK 
General Requirements: 
Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall furnish all the 
necessary services, qualified personnel, material, equipment, and facilities, not otherwise 
provided by the Government as needed to perform the Statement of Work below.  
 
Specific Requirements: 
The Contractor shall perform genome analysis and storage on 4799 unaligned raw sequencing 
data from Vanderbilt University Medical Center and National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center. 
Contractor’s services must include specifications as follows:   
 
• ADSP genome analysis and harmonization shall be carried out on Amazon Cloud 
using the ADSP SNV/INDEL and SV calling pipelines  
• ADSP genome analysis and harmonization shall process raw sequencing data 
(Convert CRAM to BAM format, read remapping using BWA, sorting reads, 
marking duplicates)

Page 2 of 3 
 
• ADSP genome analysis and harmonization shall calibrate base calling quality 
scores using GATK BQSR and realigning reads around known indels using 
GATK IndelRealigner. 
• ADSP genome analysis and harmonization shall call SNVs and Indels using 
GATK HaplotypeCaller 
• ADSP genome analysis and harmonization shall call SVs using programs such 
as Streka, Manta and Smoove 
• ADSP genome analysis and harmonization shall include quality assurance 
checks (sex check, contamination check, relatedness checks) on the processing 
genome 
• ADSP genome analysis and harmonization shall include staging of sequencing 
data on Amazon S3 standard storage for 2 months 
• ADSP storage shall include up to 50GB of storage space per genome. 
• ADSP storage shall include up to 30GB of CRAM sequence read alignment 
• ADSP storage shall include up to 10GB of genomic VCF produced by GATK 
genotype caller 
• ADSP storage shall include up to 10GB of genomic VCF produced by ATLAS 
genotype caller 
• ADSP storage shall include Amazon cloud storage on S3, and Glacier for three 
years. 
• The Government’s 4799 samples shall be directly comparable with all the ADSP 
combined set of sequencing datasets to maintain full methodology continuity with 
the existing ADSP dataset.   
 
 
LEVEL OF EFFORT: 
To accomplish these requirements, the Contractor shall provide dedicated project manager to 
coordinate genome analysis and storage.  
 
GOVERNMENT RESPONSIBILITIES 
The government will provide 4799 FASTQ files of unaligned raw sequence data to the 
Contractor via electronic cloud transfer

The Contractor will meet with NIA in monthly recurring meetings and over email to discuss

The principal place of performance is the vendor’s work site. Travel for contractor employees 
will not be necessary.

The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration, Office of Mental Health and Suicide Prevention (11MHSP) intends to award a Firm Fixed Price contract on a sole source basis to Aurelius Talent Solution, LLC, 8341 Governor Run, Ellicott City, Maryland 21043 (UEI: EH1WWE7KUFT7), for iterative clinical workflow and protocol design, implementation toolkit development, in-clinic piloting, and optimization and augmentation of the SOPHROSYNE prototype substance use disorder-focused chatbot.

SOPHROSYNE is a VA-owned clinical intervention tool designed to support patient education on substance use disorder (SUD) risks and treatment options, motivate treatment engagement, and reduce substance use risk among Veterans through a Motivational Interviewing approach. The contractor will provide support for the following principal activities, as described in the Performance Work Statement:

Iterative design, testing, and revision of clinical workflows and protocols for in-clinic and independent Veteran use of the SOPHROSYNE chatbot;

Optimization and versioning of the SOPHROSYNE chatbot to ensure clinical accuracy, usability, and alignment with Motivational Interviewing principles;

In-clinic piloting at VA pilot sites in coordination with VA Center of Excellence in Substance Addiction Treatment and Education (CESATE) leadership;

Formative evaluation, including structured usability testing, end-user walk-throughs, and collection and analysis of feedback from Veterans, clinic staff, and subject matter experts; and

Development and maintenance of an implementation toolkit, user guides, training materials, and a final maintenance guide enabling VA staff to operate and modify the tool after contract completion.

Option Year 2, if exercised, is limited to sustainment, maintenance, and policy-driven updates only. No new pilot site additions are authorized in Option Year 2 without written approval from the Contracting Officer via contract modification.

All work shall be performed within VA-approved systems and in accordance with VA security, privacy, and information technology requirements, including VA Handbook 6500 and the One-VA Technical Reference Model.

PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

Primary performance at Aurelius Talent Solution, LLC contractor facilities, Ellicott City, Maryland (Howard County). Limited temporary access to VA Philadelphia, VA Puget Sound, and participating pilot sites may be requested by the contractor in support of pilot activities, consistent with PWS Section 3.2.

CONTRACT TYPE

Firm Fixed Price

ESTIMATED VALUE

$1,731,864 (base year); $4,680,640 (base year plus all options)

Note: Option Year 2 estimated value reflects a materially reduced scope limited to sustainment and maintenance only, consistent with PWS Section 3.1.

SET-ASIDE

None — Sole Source. Award is intended for Aurelius Talent Solution, LLC, an SBA-certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), pursuant to the Veterans First Contracting Program.

PROCUREMENT METHOD

FAR Part 12 Simplified Procedures (FAR 12.201-1; 41 U.S.C. 1901). Sole source authority: 38 U.S.C. 8127(c) and VAAR 819.7007 (Veterans First Contracting Program — SDVOSB Sole Source).

BASIS FOR SOLE SOURCE DETERMINATION

The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to make a sole source award to Aurelius Talent Solution, LLC pursuant to 38 U.S.C. 8127(c) and VAAR 819.7007, which authorize VA to award contracts on a sole source basis to SBA-certified SDVOSB concerns under the Veterans First Contracting Program when the award is in the best interest of the Government and the contract value is within the applicable statutory ceiling.

Aurelius Talent Solution, LLC is an SBA-certified SDVOSB (entrance date: April 17, 2023; exit date: October 17, 2027) and holds an active SAM.gov registration. Award to this firm is consistent with the highest priority in VA's Veterans First Contracting hierarchy under VAAR 819.7004.

The Contracting Officer's business decision to award on a sole source basis without seeking competitive SDVOSB offers is further supported by the following: Aurelius Talent Solution, LLC served as the original developer of the SOPHROSYNE chatbot under FY24 and FY25 VA contracts and possesses comprehensive, system-specific knowledge of the chatbot's architecture, coding, logic, and content that no other vendor currently holds. Effective modification and optimization of SOPHROSYNE requires this system-specific technical understanding. VA's Office of Information and Technology (OIT) has confirmed it lacks the capacity and specialized skillset to perform the required work. Any alternative vendor would require several months of onboarding to reach a sufficient level of system familiarity before productive performance could begin. In accordance with VAAR 819.7007(b) and (c), the Contracting Officer is not required to first determine that only one SDVOSB source can meet the requirement; this award reflects the Contracting Officer's business decision that a sole source SDVOSB award is in the best interest of the Government.

A Determination for SDVOSB Sole Source Award has been prepared pursuant to 38 U.S.C. 8127(c) and VAAR 819.7007. The Determination will be made publicly available within 14 calendar days after contract award in accordance with FAR 6.305(a).

SECURITY NOTICE — LIMITED DISCLOSURE

This notice is published in accordance with FAR 5.201. However, pursuant to FAR 5.202(a)(1), certain technical details regarding the SOPHROSYNE system have been withheld from this notice because disclosure of the agency's specific system requirements would compromise the security of VA information systems and Veteran health data protected under VA Handbook 6500 and 38 U.S.C. § 5705. The SOPHROSYNE chatbot resides in a VA-secured cloud environment; detailed technical specifications, system architecture, and codebase information cannot be released publicly without VA credentialing and security review processes that are not practicable in the context of a public synopsis.

Interested parties who believe they can satisfy the requirement are invited to submit a capabilities statement as described below. All capabilities statements will be reviewed by the Contracting Officer. However, given the system-specific nature of the requirement and the VA security environment, access to the technical details necessary to meaningfully evaluate any competing offer cannot be provided through this public notice process.

Consistent with FAR 12.202(b), a combined presolicitation and solicitation notice has not been issued for this action. Because this acquisition is conducted as a sole source under FAR 12.201-1, no competitive solicitation will be issued. This notice satisfies the FAR 5.201 presolicitation requirement to the maximum extent practicable given the security considerations described above and the sole source nature of the award.

RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS

This notice is for informational purposes and to satisfy the FAR 5.201 synopsis requirement for proposed sole source contract actions. The Government is not soliciting competitive offers at this time.

Interested parties who believe they possess the unique technical qualifications necessary to perform this requirement — specifically, detailed system-specific knowledge of the SOPHROSYNE chatbot's architecture, coding, logic, and content — may submit a written capabilities statement to the Contract Specialist no later than June 26, 2026.

Capabilities statements shall be limited to five (5) pages and shall address, at a minimum:

The offeror's specific technical knowledge of and experience with the SOPHROSYNE chatbot system, including the basis for and extent of that knowledge;

The offeror's qualifications in AI/chatbot development, software engineering, and clinical workflow consulting for VA or comparable health-care settings;

The offeror's ability to begin effective performance within 30 days of contract award without an onboarding or familiarization period that would delay clinical piloting; and

The offeror's current SBA SDVOSB or VOSB certification status and SAM.gov registration information (UEI, CAGE code, NAICS 541519 size standard confirmation).

Capabilities statements shall be submitted electronically to the Contract Specialist at derek.devine@va.gov. Telephonic inquiries will not be accepted. The Government will evaluate all timely responses and notify respondents of its determination. Receipt of a capabilities statement does not obligate the Government to conduct a competitive procurement or delay award, but a credible demonstration of system-specific knowledge of SOPHROSYNE would require the Contracting Officer to reassess the sole source determination prior to award.

APPLICABLE WAGE DETERMINATION

This contract is subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards (41 U.S.C. §§ 6701–6707). The applicable wage determination is WD 2015-4265, Revision 33 (May 13, 2026), Howard County, Maryland, available at SAM.gov. The Contracting Officer will confirm the currency of this revision immediately prior to award.

ATTACHMENTS / REFERENCED DOCUMENTS

The following documents are incorporated by reference and will be made available upon award or as required by FAR 6.305:

Performance Work Statement (PWS)

Wage Determination No. 2015-4265, Revision 33

Requests for the PWS or other acquisition documents shall be directed to the Contract Specialist. Release of technical documents is subject to VA security review.

SMALL BUSINESS INFORMATION

This acquisition is classified as suitable for small business. Award is intended for Aurelius Talent Solution, LLC, an SBA-certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), consistent with the highest priority in VA's Veterans First Contracting hierarchy (VAAR 819.7004). Although a competitive set-aside is not practicable for this requirement, the intended awardee holds a current SBA SDVOSB certification (entrance date: April 17, 2023; exit date: October 17, 2027) and an active SAM.gov registration (expiration: October 30, 2026).

POINT OF CONTACT

All questions and capability statements must be directed to the Contract Specialist.

This notice is issued pursuant to FAR 5.201 and FAR 5.207. Publication of this notice does not constitute a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or make an award. The Government reserves the right to cancel this notice at any time.

8. Performance Work Statement (PWS)
              for the Bioinformatics Analysis of Livestock Genomics
1 General
1.1 Introduction 
The mission of the FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine (CVM) is to protect 
human and animal health by ensuring animal drugs are safe and effective and that 
food from treated animals is safe to eat. In support of this mission, the Office of 
Applied Science’s Veterinary Research Branch (VRB) requires specialized 
bioinformatics services. This acquisition is to procure the services needed to 
validate genomic variants in CRISPR/Cas9 gene-edited swine samples and 
generate breed-specific naturally occurring cattle, chicken, and swine variant 
resources to improve the robustness of in silico off-target predictions, both of 
which are critical for evaluating the safety and efficacy of intentional genomic 
alterations in animals.
1.2 Objective
The primary objective of this contract is twofold. First, to perform visual 
validation of genomic variants in whole genome sequencing (WGS) data of 
CRISPR/Cas9 gene-edited swine samples, confirming the presence and 
characteristics of both on-target and off-target variants. Second, to generate 
CRISPRme-ready input files, including breed-specific variant call files 
(hereinafter, “breed-specific VCFs”) for cattle, chicken, and swine, representing 
at least two breeds per species, using known databases of naturally occurring 
variants. A successful outcome will result in the delivery of a comprehensive 
dataset of visually validated variants with supporting evidence, the breed-specific 
VCFs that are directly compatible with CRISPRme software, the scripts and 
workflow to generate the breed-specific VCFs so they can be reused to generate 
comparable files for additional breeds, and a detailed final report that meets the 
quality and accuracy standards defined herein.
1.3 Scope of Work
The scope of this contract is to provide specialized bioinformatics services for (1) 
visual validation of genomic variants identified in CRISPR/Cas9 gene-edited 
swine whole genome sequencing data, and (2) generation of CRISPRme-
compatible breed-specific VCFs and CRISPRme input files for cattle, chicken,

Data Innovations Instrument Manager (IM) Software Standard 
Upgrade 
and IM Core Training
W
estern Oregon Service Unit (WOSU) 
Portland Area Indian Health Service 
April 2026 

Page 2 of 8 
1. Purpose and Objectives 
1.1 Purpose 
The purpose of this requirement is to obtain contractor services to upgrade the existing laboratory 
instrument middleware, Data Innovations Instrument Manager (IM), to a current supported version and 
to ensure continued operability in the Government’s target computing environment, including support 
for transition away from end-of-support Windows 10 host platforms. 
1.2 Objectives 
The contractor shall: 
• Plan and execute a standard upgrade of the Government’s existing Data Innovations Instrument 
Manager (IM) environment (including applicable test/non-production and production instances used 
to support laboratory instrument interfaces). 
• The Government will provide the target hosting environment (VDI and/or server-based) that meets 
vendor minimum requirements. 
• The contractor shall validate compatibility of the target environment with the supported IM version 
and document any platform constraints or risks prior to production upgrade. 
• Provide implementation documentation, cutover/rollback planning, and post-upgrade knowledge 
transfer. 
• Deliver Instrument Manager (IM) Core Training to designated Government staff. 
2. Background 
WOSU uses laboratory instrument interface middleware to support the quality delivery of patient 
laboratory results and to reduce manual result entry errors that may impact patient care outcomes. The 
current Instrument Manager environment requires an upgrade to remain supported and to enable 
modernization of the hosting environment. This requirement supports sustainment and standard 
upgrade of an existing CPIC-governed laboratory middleware system and does not introduce new 
system functionality or expand system scope. 
3. Scope of Work 
The scope of work includes contractor labor and expertise to: 
• Perform a standard upgrade implementation for Data Innovations Instrument Manager (IM), 
inclusive of planning, installation, configuration migration as applicable, testing support, production 
deployment/cutover support, and limited post-deployment support. 
• Provide IM Core Training to Government personnel. 

Page 3 of 8 
4. Period of Performance 
4.1 Period 
The period of performance (PoP) shall be up to 15 months, starting from the date of award. The 
extended period of performance is intended to accommodate Government scheduling, hosting 
readiness, and operational constraints; active upgrade execution is expected to occur within a shorter 
window. 
5. Place of Performance 
Work may be performed remotely and/or on-site as required and approved by the Contracting Officer’s 
Representative (COR). 
Primary Government site: Western Oregon Service Unit, 3750 Chemawa Rd NE, Salem, OR 97305. 
6. General Requirements 
6.1 Non-personal Services 
The contractor shall provide non-personal services. Contractor personnel shall not supervise 
Government personnel and shall not represent themselves as Government employees. 
6.2 Project Management 
The contractor shall provide project management sufficient to plan, execute, and control the upgrade 
effort. At a minimum, the contractor shall: 
• Identify a primary point of contact. 
• Conduct a kickoff meeting within 15 business days of award (or as mutually agreed). 
• Maintain an agreed project schedule, action item log, and risk/issue tracking. 
• Conduct periodic status meetings (e.g., weekly) during active phases. 
6.3 Coordination and Change Control 
The contractor shall: 
• Coordinate with Government IT stakeholders for connectivity, accounts, access approvals, and 
maintenance windows. 
• Document proposed changes that affect scope, schedule, risk, or downtime. Any changes beyond 
scope require COR approval and, if applicable, contract modification. 
• Not implement production changes without documented Government approval of the change and 
approved scheduling. 

Page 4 of 8 
7. Performance Requirements and Tasks 
7.1 Task 1 - Discovery and Current-State Assessment 
The contractor shall: 
• Review the current IM environment, including version/build, licensing status as applicable, 
server/desktop topology, and interface inventory. 
• Identify prerequisites and dependencies for operating IM in the Government’s target environment 
(including virtual desktop/virtual server environments as applicable). 
7.2 Task 2 - Upgrade/Migration Planning (including Cutover and Rollback) 
The contractor shall develop an Upgrade Implementation Plan that includes: 
• Planned upgrade path and version target. 
• Required Government actions (e.g., server/VDI provisioning, firewall rules, accounts, certificates if 
applicable). 
• Testing strategy, success criteria, and go/no-go criteria. 
• Cutover plan including planned downtime window(s). 
• Rollback plan to restore prior operations if go-live criteria are not met. 
Performance standard: Plan is complete, actionable, and minimizes operational risk. 
Acceptance: COR approval of Deliverable D-2 prior to production changes. 
7.3 Task 3 - Test/Non-production Upgrade and Configuration Migration 
The contractor shall: 
• Install and configure the upgraded IM software in a test/non-production environment (if 
available/required by the Government). 
• Migrate or recreate configuration elements necessary to validate functionality consistent with 
current operations (e.g., instrument connections, routing, interface definitions, rules, drivers/config 
sets, as applicable). 
• Support Government staff during test execution and document results. 
Performance standard: Test environment upgraded successfully; test results demonstrate readiness for 
production. 
Acceptance: COR acceptance of Deliverable D-3. 
7.4 Task 4 - Production Upgrade and Go-Live Support 
The contractor shall: 
• Perform the production upgrade during an approved maintenance window. 
• Execute the cutover plan and confirm interface communications are restored/operational. 

Page 5 of 8 
• Validate message flow and routing operate consistent with pre-upgrade baseline (orders/results 
where applicable). 
• Provide go-live support (remote or on-site as agreed) to stabilize the production environment. 
Boundary: Validation shall confirm interface connectivity, message transmission, and routing 
consistency with the pre-upgrade baseline.  
Performance standard: Production system returns to service within the agreed window; critical 
interfaces are operational and stable. 
Acceptance: COR acceptance of Deliverable D-4 and successful stabilization. 
7.5 Task 5 - Post-Deployment Support and Transition 
Following go-live, the contractor shall provide limited post-deployment support to address issues 
related to the upgrade, and transition the system back to Government operational ownership. 
Performance standard: Post-go-live issues are triaged and addressed within agreed response times and 
documented. 
Acceptance: COR acceptance of Deliverables D-5 and D-7. 
7.6 Task 6 - IM Core Training 
IM Core Training shall be provided for up to four (4) Government personnel. Training may be delivered 
remotely unless otherwise agreed. Any additional participants or advanced training are outside scope 
unless modified. Training shall include: 
• Scheduling coordination with the Government. 
• Delivery of training content consistent with the vendor’s standard IM Core Training offering. 
• Provision of training materials and/or access instructions. 
• Proof of completion (roster and completion confirmation/certificates if available). 
Performance standard: Training delivered as scheduled; participants receive access to required 
materials. 
Acceptance: COR acceptance of Deliverable D-6. 
8. Deliverables and Delivery Schedule 
The Government may adjust due dates by mutual agreement in writing (email acceptable) via the COR, 
provided the overall completion date remains within the period of performance (PoP).

9. Government-Furnished Property, Information, and Services 
The Government is responsible for maintaining valid Data Innovations software licensing and support 
agreements. The contractor may coordinate with the vendor as necessary to perform the upgrade but 
shall not procure licenses on behalf of the Government. The Government will provide, as applicable: 
• Access to relevant Government systems and environments (e.g., virtual desktop/virtual server 
resources) needed to perform the upgrade. 
• Network connectivity, firewall approvals, and accounts in accordance with Government security 
processes. 
• Availability of Government SMEs (Laboratory, LIS/RPMS, and IT/Network) for testing and 
acceptance. 
• Maintenance window approvals and coordination with clinical operations. 
10. Contractor-Furnished Items 
The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, and technical expertise necessary to perform the 
upgrade and training. The contractor shall furnish any tools used to perform work, provided such tools 
comply with Government security requirements and are approved for use (as required). 
11. Security, Privacy, and Access Requirements 
11.1 Sensitive Information (PHI/PII) 
Instrument Manager processes laboratory messages that may contain PHI/PII. The contractor will have 
no independent access to PHI/PII. Limited viewing may occur only while viewing a Government-
controlled desktop during guided troubleshooting activities. The contractor shall not intentionally 
access, retain, extract, or remove PHI/PII from Government-controlled environments and shall comply 
with all applicable HHS and IHS privacy and security requirements. The contractor shall: 
• Comply with all applicable Federal, HHS, and IHS security and privacy requirements. 

Page 7 of 8 
• Not remove Government data from Government-controlled environments unless explicitly 
authorized in writing. 
11.2 Remote Access 
If remote access is required, the contractor shall use Government-approved remote access methods and 
comply with Government multi-factor authentication (MFA) and access control requirements. 
11.3 System Changes 
The contractor shall not implement production changes without COR-approved scheduling and a 
documented rollback plan.

STATEMENT OF WORK 
ReadyOp   
 
1. Objective/Requirements 
NASA Office of Protective Services (OPS) requires a comprehensive incident management 
system that can effectively coordinate emergency response activities, improve situational 
awareness, and streamline communication among agency personnel. ReadyOp is commonly 
used by organizations in the public safety sector, including emergency management agencies, 
law enforcement and fire departments. It aims to enhance operational efficiency, situational 
awareness, and collaboration among teams during emergencies or critical incidents.  Cleartronic 
Inc.'s ReadyOp system has been identified as a solution that aligns with OPS’s needs. 
 
2. Characteristics, Scope, and Specs 
 
Key features of ReadyOp include: 
 
Incident Management: ReadyOp allows users to create and manage incidents, track progress, and 
allocate resources effectively.  It provides a comprehensive overview of the incident status, enabling 
coordinated response efforts. 
 
Communication: The system facilitates communication through various channels, including text 
messaging, voice communication, email, and collaboration tools. Users can share information, 
updates, and instructions to ensure effective communication among team members. 
 
Resource Management: ReadyOp enables organizations to track and manage resources such as 
personnel, equipment, and supplies. It helps allocate resources based on priority and availability, 
ensuring efficient utilization during emergency situations. 
 
Task Management: The software allows the creation and assignment of tasks to individuals or teams. 
Users can monitor task progress, set priorities, and receive notifications and reminders, streamlining 
workflow and ensuring accountability. 
 
Documentation and Reporting: ReadyOp offers capabilities to document incidents, capture relevant 
information, and generate reports.  This documentation helps in post-incident analysis, compliance 
reporting, and continuous improvement of emergency response procedures. 
 
Mobile Access: The system often provides mobile access through dedicated mobile apps or web 
interfaces, allowing users to access critical information and communicate while on the move. 
 
ReadyOp is a proven platform for planning, communications, command, control, and many other 
actions, including inter-agency and multi-agency, multi-location coordination.  The web-based 
platform (Software as a Service, SaaS) provides a single, secure location to consolidate plans, rosters, 
tasks, roles, groups and more.  Each NASA Center would have a secure website to plan personnel, 
roles, operational and emergency plans, teams, and groups as needed. 
 

ReadyOp provides protective services, first responders and managers with multiple planning, 
response, and communication capabilities in a single secure web application.  ReadyOp has earned a 
reputation for reliability, power and efficiency while also being very simple to learn and use.  Joint, 
multi-agency plans, and operations can also be built on shared ReadyOp sites for coordinated 
planning, response and command and control.  Assets can then be listed along with their location, 
person to contact and other information.  Diagrams, charts, maps, pictures, videos, report forms, and 
other documentation can be securely stored, yet immediately available for dissemination. 
 
It is noteworthy that ReadyOp also provides efficient planning and response for the Department of 
Homeland Security’s National Incident Management System (NIMS) Incident Command System 
(ICS). ReadyOp provides a single, consolidated site for conducting operations and communication and 
is not dependent on any location, server or group of servers and can therefore be used for Continuity of 
Operations, Continuity of Government, and recovery activities as well as communicating within 
NASA and other external partner organizations. 
 
• Every authorized user securely accesses the same information at the same time, regardless of 
their location. 
• Unlimited radio communication recordings. 
• Enable the ability to capture and consolidate all tasks and directives issued by the Incident 
Command Team or emergency operations center during an activation and to track and 
automatically log completion of the tasks.  
• Allow all information to be automatically logged and available for recall and reporting at any 
time. 
• Display Checklist progress, reporting and completion, including pictures, comments and 
time/date stamps can be accomplished quickly, securely, and efficiently from smartphones 
and laptops from any location with Internet or private network access. 
• Radio interoperability that enables two-way radio conversations securely between radio 
groups and two-way radio communications must be capable to extend securely to the 
smartphone or laptop of credentialed users. 
• Ability for using groups to build and use Forms for checklists, reports, instructions, and other 
information and, Forms must be submitted securely by users from any location from their 
laptop or smartphone.

Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
 
The Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences (USU) is the Nation's federal health 
sciences university and is committed to excellence in military medicine and public health during 
peace and war. We provide the Nation with health professionals dedicated to career service in the 
Department of War and the United States Public Health Service and with scientists who serve the 
common good. We serve the uniformed services and the Nation as an outstanding academic 
health sciences center with a worldwide perspective for education, research, service, and 
consultation; we are unique in relating these activities to military medicine, disaster medicine, 
and military medical readiness. USU is located in Bethesda, MD on the grounds of the Naval 
Support Activity Bethesda.  
 
The mission of the USU is to provide the highest quality education programs in the health 
sciences to those selected individuals who demonstrate dedication to a health profession career in 
the Uniformed Services. 
 
Intended Recipient: One Diversified LLC, 2975 Northwoods PKWY , Norcross, Georgia 
30071-1537 
 
Intent to Sole-Source:  
 
USU intends to award a sole -source, firm-fixed-price contract with a base year and up to four 
option years to One Diversified LLC (Diversified) for remote and onsite support of the 
Anatomical Labs Bays A-F and Offset Operating Room and the  Rear Conference Room 
(G028A/B) audio visual equipment.   
 
Sole Source Justification 
 
Diversified is the sole installer and programmer (which involves writing the code) of the 
equipment. Diversified alone has the experience, special skills, knowledge of the installed 
software/algorithms, and technical expertise required to furnish services to properly install the 
additional equipment so that it is compatible with the existing equipment.  Accordingly, 
Diversified is the only known qualified, responsible source that can furnish the supplies and 
services within the required timeframe. This requirement will be procured in accordance with the 
procedures of FAR Part 13.106-1(b)(1)(i).  
In accordance with 5.207(c)(16)(i), all responsible sources may submit a bid, proposal, or

purposes of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will 
not be responsible for any costs incurred by responding to this notice. 
Responses must be received via email to the contact listed in the notice by the closing date 
of the notice.

Centrak MSA 
Michael E. DeBakey VA Medical Center 
Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
 
I. GENERAL REQUIREMENT 
The Michael E. DeBakey VA Medical Center requires the remediation, optimization, and expansion of its 
existing Centrak Real-Time Location System (RTLS) to support clinical operations, staff workflows, and 
asset visibility across the main hospital. The project shall restore full operational health by addressing 
system deficiencies, ensuring room-level accuracy where required, maintaining system reliability, 
implementing a battery lifecycle program for tags and infrastructure, and aligning with current OEM-
supported hardware, software, and cybersecurity standards. 
 
All work shall be performed in accordance with Centrak’s Managed Services Agreement (MSA) 
operational practices and service expectations, including device availability targets, telemetry monitoring, 
battery health management, OEM-compliant configuration, and change control while remaining a project-
based remediation scope. 
 
II. DESCRIPTION OF WORK 
The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, tools, cabling, calibration, transportation, 
software, professional services, technical support, on-site and remote monitoring, and travel necessary to 
complete the installation, upgrade, optimization, and deployment of Centrak RTLS components. The 
Contractor shall comply with all OEM requirements and maintain authorized access to Centrak software 
and tools. Completion shall be determined when all components are installed, configured, validated, 
documented, and fully operational. 
A. Existing RTLS 
The Michael E. DeBakey VA Medical Center operates Centrak RTLS consisting of: 
• Tags (e.g., staff badges, patient tags, asset tags) 
• Infrastructure devices (e.g., IR/visible light locators, LF chokepoint exciter/portals, BLE beacons, 
gateways/controllers) 
• Servers/virtual appliances and client applications used by clinical and operational staff 
The system supports locating, presence detection, and workflow events. The Contractor shall assess 
performance, accuracy, and coverage; recommend upgrades; and implement the following: 
1. Software and Service Upgrades 
a. Upgrade Centrak RTLS platform and software to current, OEM-supported version. 
b. Upgrade/replace server or virtual appliance hardware and OS to meet current 
specifications. 
c. Upgrade licenses, modules and client software required for operations. 

 
2 
d. Migrate/validate configurations, maps, zones, rules, integrations and user groups. 
2. Infrastructure Optimization 
a. Survey and document existing locators, exciters/portals, BLE beacons, gateways, 
power and cable. 
b. Replace or add infrastructure devices to achieve both required and intended coverage 
and accuracy (unit, room, or checkpoint level as specified) 
c. Ensure device placement, alignment, and calibration follow OEM guidelines 
3. Battery Replacement and Health Program (Required) – The contractor shall replace all tag 
batteries and infrastructure batteries that are depleted, offline, or nearing end of battery life and 
shall establish a sustainable battery health program: 
a. Scope: Applies to all Centrak tags (staff, patient, asset) and all battery-powered 
infrastructure devices  
b. Identification: use OEM dashboards, reports, and device telemetry to identify: 
i. “Low battery: or “battery warning” status 
ii. Offline devices (no heartbeat/telemetry for more than 24 hours) 
iii. Projected end-of-life within the next 90 days (or OEM-recommended threshold) 
c. Replacement standards:  
i. Replace any device immediately that has low battery or is offline due to battery 
condition 
ii. Use OEM-approved batteries; labeled with replacement date and next due date 
d. Documentation: Maintain serial numbers, device type/location, date/time of 
replacement, technician, battery type/lot, and post replacement-verification results.  
e. Disposal: Dispose/recycle batteries per VA environmental and local regulations; 
provide chain-of custody documentation upon request.  
f. Verification: Confirm device heartbeat/telemetry restoration and functional 
participation in location accuracy tests post-replacement. 
4. Testing and Acceptance 
a. Develop a validation Test Plan (VTP) covering coverage maps, location accuracy, 
event triggers, system performance, and battery telemetry 
b. Acceptance metrics (minimums unless otherwise specified by COR) 
i. Room-level accuracy: ≥ 95% correct room detection in validated zones 
ii. Chokepoint detection (LF portals): ≥ 99% correct crossing detection 
iii. Tag availability: ≥ 98% of active tags online and reporting 
iv. Infrastructure uptime: ≥ 99% uptime per device class over a rolling 30-day 
period 
v. Battery replacement completion: 100% of identified low/near-EOL devices 
replaced within 10 business days of identification 
c. Provide final as-built documentation, coverage/accuracy reports, and configuration 
backups. 
A. Areas of Expansion 
The contractor shall expand RTLS coverage and functionality at the main hospital and across selected 
CBOCs if needed. At a minimum: 

 
3 
• Provide adequate room-level or chokepoint-level coverage for nurse stations, reception/waiting 
areas, and additional patient-facing areas as designated by the COR. 
• Equip designated units (e.g., impatient Mental Health - 6th floor, Emergency Department - 1st 
floor) with infrastructure and tags sufficient to meet workflow and location accuracy 
requirements. 
• Perform calibration, mapping, and validation testing at each site; deliver site-specific as-built 
documentation and coverage maps.  
B. Integrations 
Where requested and supported by OEM, the Contractor shall integrate RTLS with existing platforms 
(e.g., nurse call, CMMS, clinical workflow, location dashboards) via Centrak-supported APIs or 
connectors. The contractor shall: 
• Provide an integration plan detailing endpoints, security, use-cases, and data flows. 
• Configure event rules, alerts, and dashboards as specified by the COR. 
• Validate Integration Performance and failover behavior. 
III. DESIGN/LINE ITEMS

Performance Work Statement (PWS)

for the

Data Ray

1.0	General

1.1	Introduction 

The mission of the Belcourt IHS is to raise the physical, mental, social, and spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level. The mission of the Chance Wilkie is to ensure the Data Ray devices are covered under service agreement to avoid delays in service.  

This acquisition will allow the customer to call DataRay during business hours 8am-5pm Central Time, M-F 800-477-5317 for technical and user support on the D3 interface. In order for DataRay to provide support there must be a current active support agreement in place between the customer and DataRay. For questions regarding the thermal printer call the printer manufacturer or DataRay. In order to provide support for DataRay products and services, the customer must provide VPN access to DataRay support staff in order to allow electronic communication with the customer’s installed DataRay devices. The below support guarantee applies during normal business hours, with the assumption that the customer stocks required backup units, has an active service/support agreement, and that DataRay is provided with the required access through VPN. 

1.2	Objective

IHS is mandated to provide bar code administration when serving its customers.  Data Ray is the only vendor who has the capability to work with the RPMS database to reformat the data and print it out in the required format for bar code administration. We have been using Data Ray since 2012.

1.3	Scope of Work

Offsite DataRay Interface Setup and Support: Offsite Support requires that there exist an active DataRay Managed Services Agreement between the customer and DataRay. Offsite Integration includes the fundamental components and custom setup required to get the D3 operational with a particular Hospital System. This includes DataRay installing utilities needed to capture data output from the customer’s system, analyzing the data stream, and developing custom formatting instructions to meet the label formatting needs of that system. 

In order for DataRay to provide support for the product, it is essential that the customer grant DataRay VPN access to the D3 Network Devices. The D3 devices provide DataRay advanced tools and diagnostics to troubleshoot networking problems, system output changes, printer status, and other issues. DataRay needs direct network access to the D3 devices to operate these utilities. DataRay always protects the integrity of the hospital’s network and of Protected Health Information, as is required by the signed HIPAA Business Associates Agreement. 

Onsite DataRay Professional Services Setup and Installation: DataRay personnel will meet with the hospital technical team in a “train the trainers” session, to discuss installation procedures, end user training, and potential problem calls. The installation can then proceed by going to each area receiving a printer, installing the printer, and testing for correct operation, as described in the “Implementation” section below. If DataRay Custom Label Formatting work has been completed prior to the Thermal Healthcare Integration Solution installation, then training, installation, and verification of the DataRay formatting can be included as part of the Onsite DataRay Professional Services. DataRay will assist with installation of a minimum of up to half the purchase units, at which time the hospital technicians will have enough experience to install remaining units, and any future units purchased, and will also be able to train the end users.

1.4	Background

We have been using Data Ray since 2012 where they have met our bar code administration needs.

1.5	Type of Contract Contemplated 

	One year service contract.

1.6	Period of Performance

June 1, 2026 through May 31, 2027.

1.7	Place of Performance

The work will be done remotely via VPN as it has always been done.

Applicable Documents

See the attached SOW from Data Ray

2.3	Task Three (etc.)

 The DataRay Patient Safety Solution Thermal Printer Interfaces provide barcode safety solutions for Quentin Burdick Memorial Hospital, as described below: 

The DataRay D4 hardware includes the DataRay’s MedMap Patient Safety Suite software, and interfaces with Hospital Information Systems to parse and interpret output data streams, to merge parsed data with graphical label templates, to provide department specific patient safety features, and to provide utilities that allow for advanced customer support. 

Description of formatting 

The formats are responsible for defining where on the label to print required data, and for specifying what size fonts to use. The position and size of the data on your label can be altered to enhance the readability of key information: providing enhanced patient safety due to enhanced print legibility. 

Description of parsing 

The parsers are responsible for analyzing the print job and determining the required data to be printed on the label. The parser looks for key text strings to determine what data in the print job is required to be present on the label. 

DataRay D4-MMP Patient Safety Suite products and services provided for Quentin Burdick Memorial Hospital include: 

Hardware: DataRay D4 Advanced Network Interface with parsing filter, formatting, and patient safety software 

Software: DataRay D4 Network Interface with the following software packages: 

SafetyPrint for Inpatient Pharmacy Medications 

ScriptPrint for RPMS eRx package for electronic Prescriptions 

MedBand Barcoded Patient ID System 

Chart Label and On-Demand Document Identification System (ODDISY) 

LAB-Enhance Accession Label System 

EHR-Connect Ward Collect Label System and 

Medical Access Record (MAR) Update Label Solution

Statement of Work 
American Battle Monuments Commission 
Financial IT, ERP, and Business Process Support Services 
74330226R0060 
 
1.0 Introduction 
1.1 Agency mission and structure 
1.1.1 The American Battle Monuments Commission (ABMC)—guardian of 
America’s overseas commemorative cemeteries and memorials—honors the 
service, achievements and sacrifice of United States Armed Forces. Since 1923, 
the Commission has executed this mission by (1) commemorating the 
achievements and sacrifices of United States Armed Forces where they have 
served overseas since April 6, 1917, through the erection and maintenance of 
suitable memorial shrines; (2) designing, constructing, operating and 
maintaining permanent American military burial grounds in foreign countries; 
and (3) controlling the design and construction on foreign soil of U.S. military 
memorials, monuments, and markers by other U.S. citizens and organizations, 
both public and private, and encouraging their maintenance. ABMC’s fiscal 
year 2026 appropriation of $110.0 million supports the continued commitment 
to the worldwide responsibilities that flow from this mission. 
1.1.2 In performance of its mission, ABMC administers, operates and maintains 26 
permanent American military cemeteries; 31 federal memorials, monuments, 
and markers; and eight nonfederal memorials. Three memorials are located in 
the United States; the remaining memorials and all of our cemeteries are located 
in 17 foreign countries, the U.S. Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana 
Islands, the Midway Atoll, and the British dependency of Gibraltar. These 
cemeteries and memorials are among the most beautiful and meticulously 
maintained shrines in the world. 
1.1.3 ABMC also administers trust funds to (1) build memorials authorized by 
Congress but financed primarily from private contributions, commemorative 
coin proceeds, and investment earnings; and (2) maintain and repair nonfederal 
war memorials with private contributions. 
1.1.4 ABMC’s policymaking body consists of a Board of Commissioners of up to 11 
members appointed by the President of the United States for an indefinite term 
and whose members serve without pay. The commissioners establish policy for 
the Commission. ABMC’s daily operations are directed by an Executive Level 
Secretary, who is appointed by the President and assisted by a Deputy Secretary 
who is a member of the Senior Executive Service. 
1.1.5 ABMC is staffed by approximately 400 full-time civilian employees, around 75 
of whom are US citizens. The remaining 325+ civilian employees are foreign 
nationals employed in the 10 countries where ABMC cemeteries are located – 
six in Europe (France, Belgium, Italy, Netherlands, United Kingdom and 
Luxembourg), plus the Philippines, Tunisia, Panama and Mexico. 
1.1.6 The Agency is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, near Washington DC.  The 
headquarters (“HQ”) office houses approximately 30 people, most of whom are 
full-time civil servants, as well as a few consultants.  The focus of the 
headquarters office is interfacing with the federal government entities in 
Washington, and conducting the senior executive, managerial, and policy 

2 
 
development aspects of the Agency.  The Arlington office has a small 
Information Technology staff. 
1.1.7 All but three of the facilities that ABMC manages are located on foreign soil, as 
described in Section 1.1.2.  Because a majority of these locations are in Europe, 
ABMC has centralized an Overseas Operations (“OO”) office in Paris, France.  
This office houses about 40 full-time people, and another half dozen temporary 
employees, who oversee and administer the operations of all overseas 
cemeteries, memorials, and markers.   
1.1.8 ABMC provides data network and information services to 26 cemetery sites 
(“CEM”). 
1.1.9 Given the geographical scope of the Agency as described above, conducting 
business across multiple countries, in various time zones, with several 
languages, and multiple currencies creates challenges in communication, 
collaboration, and configuring system functionality to facilitate a diverse user 
community.

1.2.1 The Agency has 2 offices and 26 cemeteries (sites) to which data network 
services and information services are delivered.  The sites are located in 11 
countries on 4 continents.

Requirement Title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Driven Image Search Tool

Background

Patent Prosecution and Prior Art- “Design, Plant, and Utility patent prosecution” refers to the series of interactions between inventors, practitioners, and United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) Patent Examiners that determine whether a patent is granted. When an applicant submits an ornamental design for an article of manufacture or drawings for a utility invention, a Patent Examiner substantively reviews the application disclosure and compares it to existing references, known as “prior art.” Prior art encompasses all information made available to the public in any form before a given date that might be relevant to an application’s claim of novelty and non-obviousness. Thoroughly searching prior art is one of the most critical statutory tasks performed by Patent Examiners in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 1.104(a).

The Need for AI-Driven Image Search-As the volume of global intellectual property filings grows, relying solely on text-based or traditional classification searches (such as USPC, Locarno, and Cooperative Patent Classification [CPC]) is no longer sufficient, particularly for highly visual design and utility applications. To improve search completeness and examiner efficiency, the USPTO requires a FedRAMP-authorized, Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) AI-driven image search tool. This tool will allow examiners to search global patent databases using uploaded images as direct queries.

System Integration and Customization-This AI-driven tool is intended to augment, rather than replace, existing USPTO enterprise search systems. To ensure seamless adoption, the SaaS solution must be highly configurable. The USPTO requires the ability to customize user interfaces, examiner workflows, and data export reports to align with specific Technology Center (TC) practices. By aggregating global Design and Utility patent collections and pairing them with customizable, AI-powered image recognition, the USPTO aims to significantly enhance the quality and speed of patent examination.

Objective

The objective of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to acquire a FedRAMP-authorized, AI-driven Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) image search platform that enhances the prior art search capabilities of USPTO Patent Examiners.

The Contractor shall provide a highly accurate, scalable, and customizable tool that aggregates global Design and Utility patent collections, enabling examiners to execute complex searches using images as direct queries. A key objective of this acquisition is to configure and customize the SaaS interface, examiner workflows, and reporting outputs to seamlessly align with USPTO examination practices and Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) standards. By augmenting existing USPTO search systems with transparent, AI-powered image recognition and tailored user experiences, this tool aims to significantly improve search completeness, examiner efficiency, and overall patent quality.

Scope

The scope of this PWS encompasses the provisioning, configuration, customization, and ongoing maintenance of a FedRAMP-authorized, enterprise-wide AI-driven Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) image search platform for approximately 12,000 users. The Contractor shall deliver a comprehensive solution that augments the USPTO’s prior art search capabilities without replacing existing enterprise systems.

The Contractor shall be responsible for the following core areas:

Project Management, Support and Transition Operations 

Database Aggregation and Maintenance: All Design United States Patent Classification (USPC) and Utility patents across all Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) symbols (e.g., electrical, chemical, biological, and software arts), including corresponding UI and database updates Ingesting, updating, and maintaining global patent and trademark databases from at least 80 international authorities, specifically on Design, Plant and Utility collections. 

AI-Powered Search Functionality: Providing robust image-to-image search capabilities, including multi-image uploads, image manipulation tools (e.g., auto-lasso, photo-to-line conversion), similarity ranking, and automated classification suggestions (USPC, Locarno, and Utility CPC).

SaaS Customization and Workflow Alignment: Configuring and customizing the user interface (UI), user experience (UX), and examiner workflows to meet USPTO-specific requirements. This includes developing custom project folders, tailored dashboard layouts, and specialized export/reporting templates (e.g., PDF, CSV) that integrate seamlessly into the patent file wrapper.

Security, Privacy, and Compliance: Maintaining FedRAMP authorization, integrating with USPTO Identity, Authentication, and Authorization Management (IAAM) via Okta, ensuring AI transparency (per EO 13960 and 14179), and enforcing strict data handling protocols (e.g., immediate session data deletion and automated export redaction).

Training: The Contractor shall employ a Train-the-Trainer (TtT) methodology to equip a core group of USPTO personnel with the expertise required to independently train the broader Patent Examiner workforce on the SaaS platform.	

Specific Tasks

Task 1: Project Management, Support and Transition Operations - The Contractor shall provide comprehensive project management, ensuring seamless phase-in, execution, and phase-out of the contract.

Transition-In & Kickoff: Conduct a kickoff meeting to finalize the plan, clarify scope, and establish reporting formats.

Contract Management: Designate a primary and backup Point of Contact (POC) within 14 days of award. Conduct regular status meetings with the COR to review schedule, productivity, risks, and quality assurance.

Metrics Reporting: Provide monthly usage metrics detailing unique users, session lengths, queries, exports, image imports, and classification metrics (including Design and Utility CPC usage).

Ad Hoc Reporting: Provide additional custom reports upon request by the COR.

Task 2: Security, Privacy, and AI Compliance -The Contractor shall ensure the SaaS solution adheres to all federal and USPTO security, privacy, and AI governance mandates.

Authorization to Operate (ATO) & FedRAMP: Maintain a FedRAMP-authorized solution and obtain/maintain a full USPTO ATO. The system must comply with FISMA, FIPS, and National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) guidelines, specifically the Risk Management Framework (SP 800-37) and security/privacy controls (SP 800-53). The Contractor shall use an independent third-party assessment organization (3PAO) for initial and annual assessments.

Security Documentation & Incident Response: Maintain an up-to-date System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP) and Contingency Plan. Track and mitigate vulnerabilities via a Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M). Perform Security Impact Analyses (SIA) for any system changes and immediately report suspected security incidents to the USPTO Computer Incident Response Team (CIRT), CISO, and I

REQUIREMENT 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration, National Pathology 
and Laboratory Medicine Program, in coordination with Veterans Integrated Service Network 
(VISN) 1, is conducting market research to identify commercially available off-the-shelf 
Artificial Intelligence (AI) pathology solutions and cloud storage capabilities to support the 
National Digital Telepathology – AI initiative.  
 
VA is seeking information regarding solutions capable of: 
• Providing the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared AI assisted analysis of 
digital pathology images for the detection and characterization of prostate and gastric 
cancer. 
• Integrating with the existing Philips IntelliSite Pathology Solution (PIPS) digital 
pathology platform. 
• Supporting pathologist workflows through image analysis, case triage, diagnostic 
decision support, and standardized reporting. 
• Providing scalable cloud-based storage, archival, and retrieval of Whole Slid Images. 
• Operating within VA Enterprise Cloud environment and meeting applicable VA cyber 
security, Technical Reference Model, network connectivity, and Authority to Operate 
requirements. 
• Providing implementation, configuration, clinical validation support, training, 
maintenance, and ongoing technical support. 
• Supporting future expansion to additional VA facilities and VISNs. 
 
The Government is interested in understanding industry capabilities, interoperability approaches, 
FDA clearance status, cloud architecture, implementation timelines, licensing models, and 
support strategies. Information received will be used to refine the requirements, assess market 
capabilities, determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, and evaluate potential socioeconomic 
set-aside opportunities. 
The Contractor shall provide the specific deliverables listed within the performance period 
specified in Section 5.1 through 5.3.13, as well as 6.1.12 through 6.2.2 of the PWS. VA is 
contemplating a firm-fixed-price contract for 1 12-month base period of the Philips IntelliSite 
Pathology Solution, Image Management System Brand Name or Equal Solution for 12 months 
After Receipt of Order, with 4 12-month option periods under the attached PWS. This contract is 
not expected to exceed five years. 
Interested vendors may submit “Equal” solutions that meet or exceed the Government’s Salient 
Characteristics as defined in PWS Section 3.1.

is reasonably notified of such claims and proceedings.

The Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Newport (NUWCDIVNPT) intends to award a firm fixed price (FFP) 
purchase order for the following ThinkMate items on a Sole Source basis to ThinkMate, a Source Code LLC 
company. 
 
The Government currently uses and has used ThinkMate machines for the past 5 years in its infrastructure to support 
research. Migrating to a new manufacturer would necessitate a comprehensive and time-consuming review and 
potential rewrite of algorithms. Many of these configurations that have been fine-tuned have been automated across 
the system. Making the changes to re-configure the optimization and then create new configurations would have a 
significant impact to cost and schedule. ThinkMate is the direct source for this requirement and does not have an 
authorized distribution channel for the required part.

Small Business Programs. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this acquisition is
