Request for Information (RFI) 
 
1. Title & Reference Information 
Project/Program Name: Marauder  
Reference Number: A063714 
Date: May 20, 2026 
 
Point of Contact 
Name: Kelly Puvogel 
Title: Procurement Contracting Officer/Agreements Officer 
Email:  kelly.puvogel@us.af.mil 
 
Name: Jennifer Cashwell 
Title: Contract Specialist 
Email:  jennifer.cashwell.2@us.af.mil 
 
2. Background 
2.1. The Mission Need 
Unit-Level Intelligence (ULI) personnel initially required tools to support end -to-end 
workflows across the Contingency Intelligence Network (CIN). Historically, ULI analysts 
relied on discrete, disjointed tools with dated technology and manual data transfers, which 
hindered battlespace characterization a nd mission planning. To support a wide range of 
Total Force operations  — including air-to-air, air-to-ground, airlift, and personnel recovery  
— the Department of War required a cohesive, data-driven solution. 
As operational realities evolved, the program's core focus narrowed to optimizing the most 
critical phase of the intelligence cycle:  the post -mission debrief and reporting 
workflow. Following combat or training sorties, returning aircrews must conduct rigo rous 
debriefs with analysts to capture critical mission parameters and threat observations. The 
current mission need centers entirely on accelerating this specific workflow —capturing 
pilot insights, minimizing manual data entry, and rapidly generating accu rate Mission 
Reports (MISREPs) for enterprise-wide consumption. 
Ideally, this solution needs to seamlessly connect analysts to aircraft data sources and 
theater Common Intelligence Pictures (CIP), operating securely in both in-garrison and low-
bandwidth Agile Combat Employment (ACE) environments despite threats of jamm ed or 
degraded communications.  However, seamless operation within these contested, low -
bandwidth ACE environments has not yet been fully achieved, representing a critical area 
for future capability development and vendor innovation. 

 
2.2. The Solution: Marauder 
Marauder was developed to meet this critical capability gap, serving as the official Mission 
Report (MISREP), Agile Combat Employment Report (ACEREP), and Tactical Combat Report 
(TACREP) tool of record. It accelerates the operational intelligence cycle by standardizing 
reporting formats and workflows across unit, wing, and Air Operations Center (AOC) 
echelons, ensuring strict compliance with AOC Intelligence Reporting Directives (IRD). 
Marauder provides DoW commanders, mission planners, the Intelligence Community (IC), 
and over 2,000 active users with authoritative post -mission intelligence within 24 hours of 
engine shutdown. Its automated data structuring can feed targeting processes and combat 
assessments across the enterprise. 
 
2.3. Program History and Team Culture 
Now in its eighth year of development and sixth year of continuous production, Marauder 
utilizes a multi-environment architecture. Development occurs at the Unclassified level to 
facilitate rapid, remote collaboration, while production environments run at the Secret and 
Top Secret levels. 
Developed within  Kessel Run (KR), Marauder is a flagship success for the U.S. Air Force’s 
organic software development initiative. It represents a mature implementation of Agile 
methodologies and DevSecOps within the Department, and currently stands as the  final 
program within KR to transition from government -led organic development to vendor -
executed support. The current team operates as a "Balanced Team" utilizing  Xtreme 
Programming (XP)  practices, integrating Engineers, UX Designers, and Product Managers . 
This User-Centered Design (UCD) approach ensures the product remains aligned with both 
high-level stakeholder objectives and the tactical operational needs of the warfighter. 
 
2.4. Technical Architecture and Security 
The technical architecture is built on a microservices model designed to auto-scale and 
withstand cyber threats within a secure cloud environment. The frontend is a reactive 
interface primarily utilizing JavaScript/TypeScript, while the backend is powered by Node.js 
(Express) and Java (Spring Boot). Marauder maintains independent centralized relational 
databases at both Secret and Top Secret levels, providing modern, read-only API access 
for external systems across the DoW. 
Hosted on a government -owned cloud platform, the program leverages a mature CI/CD 
pipeline for automated testing, security scanning, and deployment, enabling production 
releases in minutes rather than weeks. To maintain high technical velocity, the development 
team actively integrates government -approved AI tools into the software development life 
cycle (SDLC) for maintenance and system optimization. 

 
3. Marauder Problem Statement 
The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to conduct market research to identify 
qualified industry partners capable of assuming the execution, sustainment, and 
modernization of the Marauder capability. The Government seeks a vendor to transition 
Marauder from a government-led organic development effort into a vendor-executed 
model. The successful partner will be required to maintain current operational availability 
across all classification levels while aggressively advancing the platform’s automation 
capabilities, external system integrations, and data interoperability to meet the demands 
of a fluid, dynamic, and contested operational environment. 
 
4. Scope 
The scope of this requirement encompasses the full software development life cycle 
(SDLC) support for the Marauder capability. This includes, but is not limited to: 
 
• Transition & Knowledge Transfer: Successfully assuming technical and operational 
responsibility for the existing codebase and production environments from the 
current Kessel Run Balanced Team. 
• Continuous Operations: Sustaining the current production baselines at the 
Unclassified, Secret, and Top Secret levels, ensuring uninterrupted support for the 
20,000+ active users across the Total Force. 
• Modernization & Continuous Development: Designing, developing, and deploying 
new features focused on accelerating the intelligence cycle through advanced 
automation and data integration, considering both in-garrison and low-bandwidth 
Agile Combat Employment (ACE) environments. 
• User Support & Training: Providing help desk support from account management to 
troubleshooting in addition to a training program should be required by the 
warfighter and stakeholders. 
 
5. Desired Outcomes 
The Government seeks industry approaches that can achieve the following operational 
outcomes: 
• Extreme Automation (Streamlined Workflows): Fundamentally accelerate post-
mission reporting through the automated ingestion, correlation, validation, and 
dissemination of mission data. Leverage automation and AI-enabled capabilities to 
improve mission reporting efficiency, data integration, interoperability, and 
informed decision making. The desired outcome is a drastic reduction in manual 
data entry, administrative burden, and cognitive load for Unit-Level Intelligence 

(ULI) personnel through seamless integration of aircraft system data, ATO/ACO 
feeds, C2 and targeting systems, and other relevant intelligence sources. 
Seamless Enterprise Integration (Interoperability): Transform Marauder into a highly 
integrated node within the intelligence enterprise. The capability must actively push and 
pull data at the speed of operations, utilizing modern API endpoints to share published 
intelligence products instantly with the AOC, targeting, and IC enterprises across SIPR and 
AFSCI. 
• Multi-Level Data Sharing: Provide adaptive means to customize and disseminate 
intelligence, accommodating complex sharing requirements (e.g., FVEY, NOFORN) 
without creating data silos. 
• Maintained Technical Velocity: Preserve the Agile/DevSecOps culture currently in 
place, ensuring rapid, continuous delivery of software updates (within 
minutes/hours) using modern CI/CD pipelines. 
 
6. Constraints & Considerations 
Industry partners must incorporate the following constraints and considerations into their 
proposed approaches and technical strategies: 
 
6.1. Security Classification & Environment: 
• The capability operates across multiple security domains. The vendor must be 
capable of providing cleared personnel (up to Top Secret/SCI) to execute 
development, maintenance, and deployment tasks. 
• Development occurs primarily at the Unclassified level, but the vendor must 
manage and sustain production environments on Secret (SIPR) and Top Secret 
(AFSCI) networks. 
• The system must maintain resilience against anticipated threats in contested 
environments, including denied, degraded, or intermittent communications (DDIL) 
and cyberattacks. 
6.2. Regulatory & Compliance Requirements: 
• All development and deployment must occur within the mandated government-
owned cloud platform and adhere to established DevSecOps and continuous 
authorization-to-operate (cATO) protocols. 
• The capability must comply with all Department of War (DoW) and Air Operations 
Center (AOC) Intelligence Reporting Directives (IRD). 
• Data sharing mechanisms must adhere to strict dissemination controls, including 
classified and unclassified environments; physical and cyber. 
6.3. Schedule Drivers & Milestones: 

• A critical schedule driver is the requirement to conduct a seamless transition and 
knowledge transfer from the current government-led (Kessel Run) team prior to the 
expiration of current support mechanisms (anticipated in late 2027). 
• The vendor must maintain the current CI/CD pipeline velocity, ensuring the ability to 
deploy urgent, mission-critical updates to production within minutes or hours, 
rather than traditional milestone-based release cycles. 
6.4. Budgetary & Resourcing Considerations: 
• Note to Vendor: While specific funding lines are not detailed in this Statement of 
Need (SoN), the Government seeks highly efficient team structures (e.g., Balanced 
Teams utilizing XP/Agile) that maximize automation to keep sustainment costs lean 
while surging resources toward modernization and capability development. The 
proposed scope of work addresses the critical need for modernizing and 
automating the current Marauder operational environment. Additionally, due to 
recent fiscal restructuring we have anticipated budget constraints. 
 
7. Information Requested from Industry 
Interested vendors are requested to submit an RFI response addressing the key areas 
identified in this SON. Responses should be submitted in PDF format. 
 
RFI Response Areas:  
 
Interested vendors are requested to provide a concise RFI response addressing the 
following:  
- Recommended approaches and potential solutions to the problem set described 
herein 
- Key considerations, risks, constraints, or opportunities the Government should 
evaluate 
- Relevant capabilities, experience, technologies, or innovations applicable to this 
effort 
- Recommendations for follow-on engagement, collaboration, or further discussion 
with the Government 
 
RFI Response shall:  
- Address all key areas identified in this request 
- Not exceed two (2) pages in length, excluding the cover page 
- Be concise, clear, and focused on relevant capabilities, innovative solutions, and 
experience 
 
Cover Page: 
 
Additionally, vendors shall include a separate cover page containing standard industry 
information, to include at a minimum:  

- Company name 
- Cage Code and/or Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) 
- Business size/status 
- Primary point of contact 
- Email address and phone number 
- Relevant contract vehicles (if applicable) 
- Company address and website 
 
Note: This Request for Information is issued solely for Market Research purposes. It is not 
a solicitation and does not constitute a request for proposals or quotes. Responses will be 
used for informational and acquisition planning purposes only and will not be evaluated for 
award. Funds are not presently available for this requirement no award will be made until 
appropriated funds are made available from which payment for contract purposes can be 
made. The Government reserves the right to cancel this RFI in the event funding does not 
become available during the offer acceptance period.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection

Office of Information & Technology 

Field Support Directorate

Performance Work Statement

Information Technology Refresh Program (ITRP) Support Services

BACKGROUND: 

The U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Office of Information and Technology (OIT) have a requirement for support services that will contribute to implementation of an Information Technology Refresh Program (ITRP) capability across the CBP Enterprise (see Appendix B).  Field Support Directorate (FSD) is the centralized office for implementing an end-to-end ITRP solution for replacing technology, including desktop, laptop, and non-cellular tablet devices; peripherals; network devices; and mobile devices.  FSD coordinates this capability with CBP’s components and trusted partners to ensure CBP customers have functional, effective, and secure day-to-day technologies needed to accomplish their missions.

The ITRP framework is grounded in a pre-determined refresh cycle that maximizes technology access, capability, and maintenance while minimizing cost, complexity, and cybersecurity risks.  The technology refresh requirement will replace an estimated 90,000 desktop, laptop, non-cellular tablet devices on a variable refresh cycle based on Industry Best Practices, Accelerated for Operational Priorities (IBP-O) (see Appendix C).  If exercised through optional Contracting Line-Item Numbers (CLINs), technology refresh will also replace 66,000 peripherals, 2,700 network devices, and 15,000 mobile devices.  The full technology refresh lifecycle includes procurement, deployment, maintenance, and disposal of each device where CBP operates across 1,800 worldwide locations. 

Dedicated ITRP implementation will enable a recurring and predictable out-year investment and implementation strategy resulting in more stable fiscal execution, economies of scale, and enhanced cybersecurity.  Scheduled deployments will maximize usage and warranties and timely modernization will leverage potential advances in technology (e.g., artificial intelligence (AI), Quantum Computing, Graphics Processing Units (GPUs)).  

SCOPE: 

In support of CBP’s implementation of comprehensive lifecycle management and modernization of Enterprise technology assets, the contractor shall provide Program Management, Storefront Capability, Planning / Lifecycle Management, Hardware Procurement Assistance, Asset Management Assistance, Hardware Preparation for Deployment, Evaluation / Process Improvement, and Infrastructure and Endpoint Management support services.  The contractor shall perform these support services for desktops, laptops, and non-cellular tablet devices with options also for peripherals, network devices, and mobile devices.

The contractor shall provide support services for CBP’s implementation of a comprehensive Information Technology Refresh Program (ITRP) initiative for managing all technology assets from planning to disposal.  The contractor shall perform these support services for desktop, laptop, and tablet devices with options also for peripherals, network devices, and mobile devices.  Mobile devices are smartphone and tablet devices associated with a cellular plan.  

The Contractor shall provide technology refresh implementation support in the following areas:

Program Management: Full range of Program Management support services for effective and reliable technology refresh implementation assistance.

Storefront Capability: Sole internal ordering mechanism for CBP to submit order details which will subsequently inform formal required procurement documentation with system data reporting capability. 

Planning / Lifecycle Management: Select activities to inform tech refresh planning and lifecycle management including identifying aging / at risk technology and improved technology opportunities, moderating required device specifications, maintaining and monitoring procured device data, monitoring and tracking device deployment activity.

Hardware Procurement Assistance: Enable the government to efficiently and effectively place hardware procurements and support post-ordering data collection and consolidation.

Asset Management Assistance: Enable the government to track devices, maintain data records, and optimize utilization of devices throughout the equipment lifecycle.

Hardware Preparation for Deployment: Install required peripherals and software and package devices for shipment in adherence to deployment cycles and overall technology refresh cycle.

Evaluation / Process Improvement: Conduct evaluations to ensure technology refresh implementation is seamless to the end user, does not disrupt operations, runs efficiently and effectively, and presents relevant and current product offerings.

(Optional) Infrastructure and End Point Management: Coordinate management of new device model and software testing and integration, security, and infrastructure management.

ITRP implementation shall also adhere to federal guidelines; industry, DHS, and CBP best practices; and the performance standards outlined below. PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) VA Profile program is tasked to validate Veteran mailing addresses, provide geocoding coordinates for Veteran residences, and share this data with VA applications throughout the enterprise. The VA Profile program has implemented the Precisely Spectrum bundle (fka Pitney Bowes (PB) Spectrum) to provide functionality that enables resolution of address validation failures and perform exception analysis for contact information data.  

The contractor shall provide the Precisely Spectrum software licensing bundle’s enterprise capability to ensure that quality postal address and accurate geolocation coordinates are available for the Veteran and that the address and geolocation coordinates can be provided to Veteran-facing systems and applications that need to consume this data, such as the Enrollment system, Vets.gov, and Loan Guaranty. The contractor shall ensure the software accomplishes this by resolving validation failures and erroneous and/or incorrect contact data across the Enterprise.  The address validation information provided by the Precisely Spectrum software licensing bundle shall support the dual purposes of determining a Veteran’s mailing address and residential location (i.e., geocoding) for sending correspondence to Veterans and determining location coordinates of residences in support of VA benefits such as the VA Loan Guaranty (LGY), VHA Enrollment System, etc.. The contractor shall provide Precisely Spectrum software listed on the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) website as a Code Accuracy Support System (CASS)-certified product, to reduce the volume of non-deliverable mail, unsorted mail, and mail that can only be delivered with significant effort due to incorrect mailing data. The contractor shall ensure the delivered Precisely Spectrum software bundle supports Personal Identity Verification (PIV) authentication through a Single Sign-On Internal (SSOi) implementation which allows access by VA Profile program support personnel.

The contractor shall deliver licenses, data subscriptions, software maintenance and support services, and professional services (technical support) for the Spectrum domestic and international address and geocoding data.  In addition, the contractor shall deliver, if exercised by VA, additional software enterprise licenses, data subscriptions, software maintenance, and professional services (technical support) to enhance VA profile capabilities and data sources which in turn shall improve the accuracy of Veteran address data and geocoding data. 

All software licenses and data subscriptions shall be distributed, delivered, and/or available for download within ten days of award.

This action is for a 12-month base period with two 12-month option periods. The base period of performance shall be from August 3, 2026 through August 2, 2027.

NOTICE OF THE FEDERAL ACCESSIBILITY LAW AFFECTING ALL INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) PROCUREMENTS (SECTION 508)

On January 18, 2017, the Access Board issued a final rule that updated accessibility requirements covered by Section 508 and refreshed guidelines for telecommunications equipment subject to Section 255 of the Communications Act.  The final rule went into effect on January 18, 2018.  The revisions and updates to the Section 508-based standards and Section 255-based guidelines are intended to ensure that information and communication technology (ICT) covered by the respective statutes is accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities.

SECTION 508 – INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) STANDARDS

The Section 508 standards established by the Access Board are incorporated into, and made part of all VA orders, solicitations and purchase orders developed to procure ICT.  These standards are found in their entirety at: Revised 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines (access-board.gov).  A single PDF file version of the Revised Section 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines will be supplied upon request, or can be obtained from the Access Board website.  Federal agencies must comply with the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended. 

The Contractor shall comply with “508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements” for all electronic ICT and content delivered under this contract. Specifically, as appropriate for the technology and its functionality, the Contractor shall comply with the technical standards marked here: 

	E205 Electronic Content – (Accessibility Standard -WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA Guidelines)

	E204 Functional Performance Criteria

	E206 Hardware Requirements

	E207 Software Requirements

	E208 Support Documentation and Services Requirements

COMPATABILITY WITH ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY

The standards do not require installation of specific accessibility-related software or attachment of an assistive technology device. Section 508 requires that ICT be compatible with such software and devices so that ICT can be accessible to and usable by individuals using assistive technology, including but not limited to screen readers, screen magnifiers, and speech recognition software.

ACCEPTANCE AND ACCEPTANCE TESTING

Deliverables resulting from this solicitation will be accepted based in part on satisfaction of the Section 508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements standards identified above.

The Government reserves the right to test for Section 508 Compliance before delivery.  The Contractor shall be able to demonstrate Section 508 Compliance upon delivery.

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY USING SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTS AND SERVICES

The Contractor shall comply with Sections 524 and Sections 525 of the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007; Section 104 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005; Executive Order 13221, “Energy-Efficient Standby Power Devices,” dated August 2, 2001; and the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) to provide ENERGY STAR®, Federal Energy Management Program (FEMP) designated, and products and services that meet EPA Recommendations of Specifications, Standards, and Ecolabels in effect as of October 2023 (e.g. Electronic Product Environmental Assessment Tool (EPEAT) registered products) in providing information technology products and/or services. The Green Procurement Compilation (GPC) website available at Green Procurement Compilation - GSA Sustainable Facilities Tool (sftool.gov) provides a comprehensive list of sustainable products and services and sustainable acquisition guidance. 

The Contractor shall provide products that meet the definition of sustainable products and services if the products are delivered to the Government; furnished by the Contractor for use by the Government, incorporated into the construction of a public building or public work, or acquired by the Contractor for use in performing services under a Government contract where the cost of the products is a direct cost to a Government contract (versus costs which are normally applied to a contractor's general and administrative expenses or indirect costs).

Specifically, the Contractor shall provide sustainable products under this contract in accordance with FAR 52.223-23.  The applicable products with their associated certification, designation, and/or ecolabel (e.g. Energy Star, FEMP, and/or EPEAT) are identified within the product specifications in this PD.  The Contractor shall ensure proposed products meet the certification(s) / designation(s) / ecolabel(s) specified at the time of submission of proposals and at the time of award.

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

VA TECHNICAL REFERENCE MODEL

The Contractor shall comply with the VA OIT Technical Reference Model (VA TRM). Compliance with the VA TRM is achieved by using only technologies and standards that are listed as approved for use in the VA TRM.  The Contractor shall provide all necessary information requested by VA to ensure TRM approval is obtained prior to use on VA’s network.

ZERO TRUST – VA CRITICAL SECURITY CONTROLS

VA has established minimum mandatory security requirements and requires that any network connected software system or service must meet the VA Critical Security Controls as outlined in the VA Memorandum, “VA Security Controls”, https://www.voa.va.gov/DocumentView.aspx?DocumentID=5010.  VA Critical Security Controls identify the minimum mandatory requirements that must be implemented across all VA enterprise infrastructure, cloud computing environments, information systems, networks, and specialized devices (medical devices/systems, special-purpose systems, and research scientific computing devices) that process, store, and/or transmit VA data.  Effective July 1, 2025, the Contractor shall implement these VA Critical Security Controls, within any network connected software system or service prior to being authorized for use in the VA.  This functional requirement is not negotiable, and Plan of Action & Milestones (POAM) will not be accepted in the event these controls cannot be implemented for new systems.  Critical Security Controls are intended to increase VA’s security posture and provide security and privacy risk visibility into the VA network and is not a new requirement.  The Contractor’s failure to maintain these VA Critical Controls after implementation will result in VA discontinuing the use of the system.

SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER (SSN) REDUCTION 

The Contractor solution shall support the Social Security Number (SSN) Fraud Prevention Act (FPA) of 2017 which prohibits the inclusion of SSNs on any document sent by mail.  The Contractor support shall also be performed in accordance with Section 240 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act (CAA) 2018, enacted March 23, 2018, which mandates VA to discontinue using SSNs to identify individuals in all VA information systems as the Primary Identifier.  The Contractor shall ensure that any new IT solution discontinues the use of SSN as the Primary Identifier to replace the SSN with the Integrated Control Number (ICN) in all VA information systems for all individuals.  The Contractor shall ensure that all Contractor delivered applications and systems integrate with the VA Master Person Index (MPI) for identity traits to include the use of the ICN as the Primary Identifier. The Contractor solution may only use a Social Security Number to identify an individual in an information system if and only if the use of such number is required to obtain information VA requires from an information system that is not under the jurisdiction of VA.

INTERNET PROTOCOL VERSION 6 (IPV6)

The Contractor solution shall support IPv6-Only based upon the memo issued by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) on November 19, 2020 (https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/M-21-07.pdf). Which defines IPv6-only as the state of an operational system or service when IPv4 protocol functions (addressing, packet forwarding) are not in use. The NIST USGv6 profile defines technical requirements for a product to be capable of operating in IPv6-Only environments.  IPv6-Only technology, in accordance with the USGv6 Program (https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/usgv6-program/usgv6-revision-1), NIST Special Publication (SP) 500-267B Revision 1 “USGv6 Profile” (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.500-267Br1), and NIST SP 800-119 “Guidelines for the Secure Deployment of IPv6” (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-119), compliance shall be included in all IT infrastructures, application designs, application development, operational systems and sub-systems, and their integration.  In addition to the above requirements, all devices, applications, and systems shall support all applicable functionality on native IPv6-Only as well as dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) connectivity without additional memory or other resources being provided by the Government, so that they can function in a mixed environment.  All public/external facing servers and services (e.g., web, email, DNS, ISP services, etc.) shall support native IPv6-Only and dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) users and all internal infrastructure and applications shall support using native IPv6-Only and dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) for all functionality and operations.

SOFTWARE AND LICENSING REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall be responsible for the provision of all software licenses and any associated licensing maintenance required for any development, delivery, integration, operation, and/or maintenance associated with its proposed application(s), software products, software solution, and/or system including, but not limited to, any and all application(s), software and/or software products that comprise, are a part of, or integrate with the Contractor’s proposed application(s), software products, software solution, and/or system for the life of any resulting contract.

TRUSTED INTERNET CONNECTION (TIC)

The Contractor solution shall meet the requirements outlined in Office of Management and Budget Memorandum M-19-26, “Update to the Trusted Internet Connections (TIC) Initiative“ (https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/M-19-26.pdf), VA Directive 6513 “Secure External Connections”, and shall comply with the TIC 3.0 Core Guidance Documents, including all Volumes and TIC Use Cases, found at the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) (https://www.cisa.gov/publication/tic-30-core-guidance-documents.)

COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION 
 
 
1. Solicitation. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial 
services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only 
solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. 
 
The 30th Contracting Squadron (30 CONS), intends to utilize this Request for Quotation (RFQ), 
under solicitation number FA4610-26-Q-0034, to award a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract. The 
Government intends to award one contract to the responsible Offeror whose quotation represents 
the Best Value to the Government. 
 
This requirement is being solicited as a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. For this acquisition, 
the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541519 – Other Computer 
Related Services and the small business size standard is $34 Million. All prospective Offerors 
must have a Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code and be registered with System 
for Award Management (SAM) at http://www.sam.gov. 
 
2. Description of Requirement. Provide SLD 30 Base Chapel with an experienced Audio/Visual 
(A/V) Technician to manage technical support for Sunday services, ensuring a seamless worship 
experience for both in-person and online congregants.  The technician’s primary responsibilities 
include setting up and testing all A/V equipment, managing the live audio mix using a DL32S 
Mackie Mixer, and operating cameras for the Facebook Live stream.  This role involves 
proactive troubleshooting during services and proper equipment shutdown afterward.  The ideal 
candidate will have at least one year of experience in live audio mixing and video streaming and 
be able to work independently in a dynamic environment. 
 
The objective is to acquire a base year of IT Services with 3 12-month option years. Please see 
the attached Statement of Work for detail. 
 
3. Period of Performance (PoP). The PoP for this base contract will be 12 months from award, 
with 3 12-month option years. 
 
4. Contract Line Items (CLIN) Please see attached pricing sheet for CLIN breakdown. Please 
follow the exact CLIN structure to ensure accuracy. 
 
5. Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS) Rating: Not Applicable 
 
6. Quotation Preparation and Submission: 
 
Offerors shall complete and submit a quotation with the following information: Cover Letter, 
Technical, and Price, as identified in this RFQ. The details for assembly of the quotation are 
identified below.

7. Additional Instructions to Offerors. Offerors shall respond to this RFQ via e-mail by 11 June

christopher.hummel.6@spaceforce.mil before the due date and time specified. 
 
All questions regarding the RFQ package must be submitted to the above e-mail addresses by 4 
June 2026 at 1300 PT. Any questions asked over the telephone will not be answered. 
 
Any questions received after this date and time may not be answered. 
 
Offerors must also be registered in Wide Area Work Flow to receive payment through electronic 
funds transfer. If you are not currently registered, please visit the following website 
https://wawf.eb.mil/ to complete your registration. 
 
8. Basis for Award. 
This announcement is the only solicitation. A separate written solicitation will not be issued. The 
Government intends to award one Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract to the responsible small 
business whose quote is determined to be the best value to the Government based on price and 
other factors 
 
Evaluation Approach 
This acquisition will be evaluated using price and other factors in accordance with FAR RFO 

12.203. 
 
The Government will: 
a.   Evaluate each quote under Factor 1 (Technical Approach) as 
either Acceptable or Unacceptable. 
b. Evaluate the total evaluated price of each technically acceptable quote for fair and 
reasonableness. 
c.   Award to the offeror whose quote represents the best value to the Government, 
where best value is defined as the lowest-priced quote rated Acceptable under Factor 
1 with a fair and reasonable price. 
 
A quote rated Unacceptable under Factor 1 is ineligible for award, regardless of price.

Unacceptable 
The quote fails to show understanding of the SOW, the 
proposed technician does not meet minimum experience, or no

 Factor 2 — Price 
The Total Evaluated Price (TEP) is the sum of the base year plus all three option years. 
Evaluation of option prices does not obligate the Government to exercise the options. Price will 
be evaluated for fair and reasonableness.

MEMORANDUM TO THE FILE 
 
Subj:  DETERMINATION THAT ONLY ONE SOURCE IS REASONABLY 
AVAILABLE FOR A FAR PART 12 ACQUISITION UNDER THE SIMPLIFIED 
ACQUISITION THRESHOLD 
 
I. BACKGROUND: 
  
1. FAR 12.102(a) states for purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, 
Contracting Officers may solicit from one source if the Contracting Officer determines that the

eCRB Filing/Management Hosting and Maintenance Services 
C.1. OVERVIEW / BACKGROUND.  
The Library of Congress (Library) requires contract support to provide operations and maintenance to 
the Copyright Royalty Board (CRB) electronic ﬁling/case management system that was constructed and 
completed in 2016 under LCCOP16C0032. This support will be for the electronic submission, 
dissemination, long-term management, tracking and reporting of motions, briefs, exhibits, comments 
and other user-generated litigation or regulatory documents, and orders, determinations and other 
documents generated by the Copyright Royalty Judges (Judges). 
The CRB is an administrative tribunal, located within the Library that adjudicates disputes concerning 
royalty rates and distributions of royalty fees under several provisions of the Copyright Act. It consists of 
Judges, staff attorneys, and a program assistant. In many respects, the CRB functions like a court of law. 
At any given time, the CRB has multiple active “proceedings,” which are similar to court cases. Each 
proceeding has multiple parties— individuals or entities outside the Library— that are generally (though 
not universally) represented by attorneys. The parties frequently file documents with the CRB that 
require action by the Judges in the form of written Orders. The CRB holds hearings, at which the parties 
offer numerous documents as evidence to supplement oral testimony of witnesses (which is transcribed 
by an outside contractor). At the end of the proceeding, the Judges render a “determination” (the 
equivalent of a court’s decision) that is reviewed by the Register of Copyrights, signed by the Librarian, 
and published in the Federal Register. 
 
C.2. SCOPE 
The contractor shall provide hosting, licensing, operation and maintenance for the electronic filing/case 
management system (eCRB) to handle documents filed with or generated by the CRB. The contractor 
shall train Library personnel in using and administering the system and provide customer support to 
internal and external users. 
 
C.3. REQUIREMENTS 
C.3.1 Hosting and Licensing Services 
The contractor shall provide cloud hosting of the eCRB system with security and all software 
modules. The contractor shall provide all applicable application-based licensing for the eCRB system 
including Accusoft. The contractor shall provide a unique and password protected credential with 
"two factor identification" for the staff login. The contractor shall integrate Login.gov single sign on 
functionality into the eCRB system. The eCRB system shall include NIST controls that are designated 
for systems having the moderate security categorization as well as adhere to all the Library’s 
Information Technology Security Directive 5-410.1: Information Technology Security Policy and any 
other Library IT Security requirements. The system is expected to be classified at the Moderate 
level.  
C.3.2 Operation and Maintenance  
The contractor shall provide on-going Operation and Maintenance Support (O&M) for the eCRB 
filing/management system website. O&M support may consist of an average of four (4) technical 
inquiries requested per month and quarterly content updates to the eCRB system. The contractor 

shall provide minimum service levels for O&M to include routine maintenance, bug fixes, and 
patches to correct programming errors, address security updates, and maintain capability and 
performance levels. The contractor shall provide maintenance via ad hoc telephone and/or email 
support to include any advisory assistance. All application, system errors, issues, and bugs identified 
by users will be reported. The contractor shall provide O&M support for work stoppage and work 
degradation.   
C.3.2.1 External Systems 
The contractor shall install updates from external systems eCRB utilizes, such as Login.gov, 
Adaptive, and Accusoft. The contractor shall provide testing for related security patches and 
vendor updates. If the Library requires configuration updates or migration to replacement 
systems, the contractor shall provide the updates or migration services. 
C.3.3 Customer Support to internal and external users of the eCRB system 
Support shall be provided as ad hoc telephone and/or email communication that address inquiries to 
cover any troubleshooting, web application error resolution, performance issue resolution, security 
issue resolution, disaster recovery items. Problem resolution may coincide with the updates to the 
eCRB content. The customer support may include the following: 
• Service Requests 
• Processes 
• Project Support Tasks 
• Non-Routine Tasks 
C.3.4 Remediate Software Vulnerabilities  
The contractor shall remediate software vulnerabilities in accordance with the minimum response 
and resolution times listed in the Service Request Priority Response matrix below. 
Priority Significance Response Time Resolution Time 
P1 Critical 15 minutes 4 hours 
P2 High 30 minutes 1 day 
P3 Standard 4 hours 5 days 
P4 Low 1day 10 days 
P5 Routine Process 1 day 30 days 
P6 Non-Routine Tasks 1 day 3 months 
C.3.5 Service Level Agreements 
Implementation of the following Service Level Agreements (SLAs) to include monthly 
performance and reliability data consistent with SLA measurement requirements reported to 
the Contracting Officer Representative (COR) no later than seven (7) days from the end of each 
month. The Contractor shall meet the Excellent Quality Level for each SLA. In the event the 
Contractor misses the Excellent Quality Level for a month then they shall provide the COR with a 
corrective action plan to address the issue. In the event the Contractor is rated as unsatisfactory 
for any SLA then the Contractor shall reduce the O&M monthly invoice by the weighting amount 
in the Monitoring Method column below. In the event the Contractor shall be rated as 
unsatisfactory for multiple SLAs within the same month then the weighting percentage shall be 
cumulative (Ex: Having an unsatisfactory rating for two SLAs in the same month would be 4% off 
the monthly invoice).

To minimize any decreases in productivity and to prevent possible negative impacts on additional

RFI # 80TECH26RFI0020  
Request for Information (RFI): Strategic Partnerships for 
NASA Data Center Infrastructure 
Introduction 
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY . This RFI is issued solely for research 
and strategic planning purposes as part of NASA’s strategic IT and infrastructure planning 
to consider potential partnerships and engagements between NASA and Industry; it does 
not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) nor a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This 
RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. 
Further, NASA is not at this time seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited 
proposals for any speciﬁc data management related activities discussed in the following. 
Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or 
administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding 
to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does 
not preclude participation in any future competitive announcement, if any is issued. If 
NASA elects to issue a solicitation, it will be released in accordance with the requirements 
applicable to the authority ultimately used. Depending on that authority, a synopsis may or 
may not be required. All interested parties are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for any 
announcements or solicitation postings. 
Purpose 
This Request for Information (RFI) invites industry, academia, and other potential partners 
to help NASA explore innovative, forward-looking concepts for current, modern, and 
affordable data center infrastructure. For purposes of this RFI, the term “partnership” is 
used generically and does not imply the use of any speciﬁc statutory authority at this time. 
This RFI is for market research purposes only and does not represent speciﬁc 
requirements, evaluation criteria, or selection factors for any future procurement or 
partnership activity. Instead, this RFI is intended to: 
• Surface new ideas, partnership models, and emerging capabilities 
• Understand how industry is thinking about modern on-premise infrastructure, 
hybrid and Cloud, AI-driven operations, and high-density computing 
• Explore mutually beneﬁcial approaches to utilizing federal assets 

  RFI # 80TECH26RFI0020  
Why Partner with NASA 
NASA operates and maintains some of the world’s most mission-critical and technically 
advanced environments. These facilities support human spaceﬂight, lunar exploration, and 
advanced scientiﬁc research and modeling, all in service of national space infrastructure 
and security priorities. 
As mission needs continue to evolve, NASA is exploring concepts to modernize aging data 
center facilities and strengthen the digital infrastructure that underpins these activities. 
Through this RFI, the Agency seeks perspectives from organizations interested in helping 
shape approaches for resilient, efficient, secure, cost effective, and scalable environments 
that can support growing compute demands and hybrid architectures. 
NASA is particularly interested in ideas that highlight mutual value. Respondents have the 
opportunity to share concepts that could improve mission continuity, and advance 
infrastructure sustainability, while also identifying ways that collaboration could inform 
commercial capabilities, support research and development, or demonstrate new models 
and technologies at broader scale. The Agency aims to understand approaches that create 
beneﬁts for both NASA and potential partners as it considers future pathways for 
modernizing data center infrastructure in support of national exploration and research 
objectives. 
NASA has a need to right size and modernize its aging Data Center facilities and IT 
infrastructure footprint to ensure mission execution, data access, connectivity, and 
continuous operations while being ﬁscally responsible.  
Data Center Infrastructure 
NASA’s data center infrastructure is in a steady state of decline due to constrained budgets 
and needs to be modernized to ensure safe, continuous, and efficient mission operations.  
In addition, NASA data centers need to meet critical compute and storage demands and 
transition toward a more hybrid, scalable, and mission-aligned architecture while reducing 
(right-sizing) the footprint and to achieve greater cost-effectiveness and overall efficiency. 
The aging infrastructure includes things such as backup generators, HVAC systems, chilled 
water pumps/piping, Uninterruptable Power Supplies (UPS), and structural (e.g. ﬂoors, 
roofs, etc.) that varies by data center facility. NASA also has construction limitations for 
power and water upgrades. With increasing demand for high-density compute and secure, 
resilient environments NASA must address these current obstacles to ensure continued 
mission support and maintain the capability required for future operational needs. 

  RFI # 80TECH26RFI0020  
Questions and Instructions for Respondents 
NASA is seeking ideas, approaches and perspectives for: 
1. Partnership Models & Value Creation 
• What partnership models could unlock value for both NASA and its partners for data 
center capability? 
• How might risk, investment, and operational responsibility be shared? 
• What would make NASA a uniquely attractive partner—and what would our partners 
and service providers need to succeed? 
2. Future Data Center Concepts 
• What does a next-generation data center look like in a mission-critical, hybrid 
environment (hybrid meaning having the capacity to utilize cloud and on-premise 
computing resources together as a uniﬁed system)? 
• How you are approaching: 
o High-density computing  
o Hybrid cloud + on-prem integration 
o Edge or distributed architectures 
3. Modernization of Legacy Data Center Facilities 
• How would you approach transforming aging infrastructure into modern, scalable 
environments? 
• What innovative approaches (modular, phased, software-deﬁned, etc.) could 
accelerate this? 
4. Reliability, Resilience & Security 
• What emerging practices are improving infrastructure resilience, operational 
reliability, cyber and physical security in shared environments? 
• How do you balance automation (including AI) with human oversight in critical 
systems? 
• How do you typically address Federal Information Security Modernization Act 
(FISMA) aligned controls when applicable, recognizing that applicability may vary 
depending on whether future activity is structured as a procurement or a non-
procurement partnership? 
• How would NASA tenants, data and networks be protected/isolated from 
commercial tenants; assuming different levels of data sensitivity from Controlled 
Unclassiﬁed Information (CUI) up to classiﬁed? 

  RFI # 80TECH26RFI0020  
5. Operational & Service Models 
• What operating models are most effective for Mission-critical environments, mixed-
use (government + commercial) infrastructure? 
• How do you ensure ﬂexibility during high-priority mission periods? 
6. Scalability & Future Demand 
• How should infrastructure evolve to support rapid growth in compute demand, 
increasing rack densities, and emerging technologies not yet fully deﬁned? 
7. Sustainability & Efficiency 
• What innovations are driving meaningful improvements in energy efficiency, water 
usage, and sustainable operations at scale? 
• Please describe your strategies for cost-Efficient Modernization with a focus on 
long-term operational sustainment, balancing energy efficiency with strict cost 
controls to navigate shrinking budgets. 
• Please describe your strategies for designing cloud and hybrid storage architectures 
that minimize the risk of vendor lock-in and prevent cost models from compounding 
exponentially over time. 
You may include concept diagrams, case studies or prior experience, strategic business 
models, and links to additional material (instead of attachments where possible). Detailed 
technical speciﬁcations, pricing, and full engineering designs are not required. 
NASA is considering multiple potential pathways for follow on activity. These may include a 
FAR based procurement or non-procurement partnership instruments (such as Space Act 
Agreements). No determination has been made regarding the appropriate authority. This 
RFI is for market research only 
Notes & Submission Guidance 
• Do not include pricing information. 
• Initial notiﬁcation of interest and questions should be submitted via email to, 
Michelle Downs michelle.m.downs@nasa.gov and Kimberly Sandoz 
Kimberly.r.sandoz@nasa.gov,  within ten (10) business days of RFI release in order to 
permit Government coordination and responses. Requested information includes 
general business name, business division, and preferred point of contact(s) to 
include corporate address, phone number(s), and e- mail address(es)  

  RFI # 80TECH26RFI0020  
• RFI responses are due no later than July 17, 2026.  Responses should use visuals 
where helpful, and focus on key ideas and differentiators, real-world examples or 
analogs, as well as lessons learned and emerging trends.  
• Responses are preferred to be limited to 20 pages in combined length (including 
illustrations, graphs, etc.) and shall be either Portable Document Format (PDF) (with 
copy and paste enabled) or Microsoft Word format. The information provided shall 
be formatted to 8.5" x 11" (letter size) paper with type no smaller than 11-point font. 
The page limit and format is for administrative simplicity and does not reﬂect any 
evaluation criteria or selection process. 
• Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and SHALL BE CLEARLY 
MARKED. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and 
will not be returned. 
• Indicate any deviations or exceptions in your response.  
• Where multiple options are offered (retroﬁt, modular, co-lo/edge), provide 
differentiated responses per option. 
• Respondents are not required to answer every question in this RFI.

Statement of Work  
Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) System (LINK) Phase 3 Deployment 
1. PURPOSE OF THE PROJECT 
 
The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to define the services, deliverables, and responsibilities 
required to execute Phase 3 of the IHS NSSC Supply Chain Modernization initiative. Phase 3 focuses on 
expanding, enhancing, and operationalizing the NSSC Supply Chain Resource Planning (SRP) solution 
across IHS’s warehouse network and supporting business processes. This phase delivers significant 
functional, technical, and operational improvements across supply chain execution, warehouse operations, 
Oracle Cloud applications, analytics, and AI-enabled decision support. 
 
Phase 3 includes comprehensive system enhancements such as advanced reporting, executive dashboards, 
expanded VLM integrations, improved warehouse selection logic, and new user-facing capabilities within 
the Order Capture Portal. It also includes the migration of the existing OKC warehouses into one larger new 
facility, ensuring continuity of operations and alignment with future growth. 
 
In addition, Phase 3 introduces AI-driven enhancements across procurement, supply chain, and reporting 
processes. This includes digital assistant capabilities, automated analytics, predictive insights, and workflow 
automation to improve operational efficiency and decision-making. The project also includes the transition 
to the Oracle Redwood User Interface and structured knowledge transfer to the IHS NSSC IT team to 
support long-term sustainability. 
 
2. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS 
 
The contractor shall provide: 
 
Task 1 – Enhancements to Supply Chain Resource Planning solution (Base Year 09/1/2026 to 
08/31/2027) 
2.1 Reporting & Data Analysis Discovery 
• Conduct structured discovery sessions with designated leadership stakeholders to define requirements 
for dashboards, key performance indicators (KPIs), and reporting needs. 
• Document all reporting requirements and provide a consolidated summary of findings. 
• Develop and recommend a reporting framework aligned with business and operational objectives. 
 
2.2 VLM Integration Across All Warehouse Facilities 
• Extend the existing Vertical Lift Module (VLM) integration from the OKC facility to all designated 
warehouse locations, including Gallup and the new facility. 
• Integrate an additional five (5) to ten (10) material handling units. 
• Enhance the integration to support the following capabilities: 
o Integrate receiving transactions  
o One additional workflow enhancement identified during discovery and approved by the 
Government 
 

 
Page 2 of 7 
 
2.3 Order Picking Logic & Warehouse Selection Enhancements 
• Enhance the Order Capture Portal to enable order entry independent of a predefined supply 
warehouse. 
• Design, configure, and implement logic to: 
o Determine the optimal fulfillment facility based on defined criteria 
o Split orders across multiple warehouses when required 
o Automatically generate multiple orders to support multi-facility fulfillment 
 
2.4 Customer Portal Enhancements 
• Implement functionality enabling users to create and manage item “favorites” lists. 
• Enable users to add items from saved lists directly into orders. 
• Enhance portal communication capabilities, including: 
o Display of banner notifications for outstanding surveys and forms 
o Automated email notifications for outstanding surveys and forms 
o Configuration of surveys/forms as optional or mandatory 
o Generation of a weekly summary report to NSSC Customer Service identifying outstanding 
maintenance requests, including both user- and facility-related items. 
 
2.5 Item Location Standardization & Slotting Optimization 
• Analyze item movement velocity and existing warehouse slotting configurations. 
• Provide recommendations to improve slotting efficiency and alignment with sourcing rules. 
• Implement approved adjustments to improve picking efficiency and operational performance. 
• Develop and deliver reporting to support ongoing slotting optimization and inventory rationalization. 
 
2.6 Oracle Redwood User Interface Migration 
• Support the transition of existing system processes to the Oracle Redwood User Interface. 
• Validate system functionality following migration and update configurations as required. 
• Support user adoption, including issue resolution and usability alignment. 
 
 
 
2.7 Digital Assistant & AI Workflow Enablement 
• Identify and document use cases for AI and digital assistant capabilities across the supply chain, 
procurement, and related business processes. 
• Design and implement approved AI-enabled capabilities, including:  
o Workflow enhancements supporting procure-to-pay (P2P) vendor collaboration.  
o GenAI-based virtual assistants capable of interpreting procurement-related queries and providing 
automated responses.  
o Automated reporting processes to generate analytical outputs, including category insights, 
market analysis, cross-functional summaries, and trend identification. 
 

 
Page 3 of 7 
 
2.8 Executive Dashboards for High-Level Decision Support 
• Design, develop, and implement ten (10) executive dashboards to support strategic and operational 
decision-making. The dashboards shall be configured to present data in a clear, structured, and 
actionable format suitable for leadership use. 
• The dashboards shall include capabilities for advanced analytics and data visualization, including, but 
not limited to, the following functional areas: 
o Budget trend analysis, including multi-year trends, variance analysis, and graphical 
representations 
o  Operational performance monitoring, including modeling of order fulfillment cycle times, 
calculation and visualization of average cycle times, and analysis of performance against 
required ship dates. 
• Ensure that all dashboard outputs are accurate, timely, and aligned with approved business 
requirements. 
• Support validation of dashboard requirements, definitions, and prioritization during the Reporting & 
Data Analysis Discovery phase described in Section 2.1. 
2.9 Knowledge Transfer & IT Team Enablement 
• Provide structured knowledge transfer and hands-on training to designated IHS NSSC IT personnel. 
• Enable the internal team to perform routine system configuration changes and provide ongoing 
operational support. 
 
2.10 OKC Facility Migration to New Warehouse 
• Implement inventory management capabilities within the new warehouse facility. 
• Collaborate with NSSC stakeholders to design the inventory management solution. 
• Migrate all data, configurations, and operational processes from the existing OKC facility to the new 
warehouse environment. 
 
2.11 Financial Optimization 
• Implement automation for invoicing of advance payments and generate required data files for the 
UFMS system. 
• Automate cash receipt processing for bill-for-collection and advance payment transactions. 
• Implement enhancements to support reconciliation processes. 
• Support the processing of third-party invoices. 
• Enable reporting and analysis of budget-to-actual financial performance. 
 
2.12 Inventory Optimization  
• Implement inventory tracking using barcode scanning at the location level, including lot number and 
expiration date tracking. 
• Optimize product distribution based on customer geographic location and historical ordering patterns. 
 
 
 

 
Page 4 of 7 
 
2.13 FedEx and Printer Migration to Cloud and Printer  
• Establish and configure the required connectivity to enable FedEx integration within the cloud 
environment. 
• Collaborate with IHS to design and implement a solution to support printing from Oracle Cloud to 
IHS network printers, utilizing methods including, but not limited to, VPN tunneling or approved 
network port configurations. 
 
Task 2 - Production Operations Support (09/1/2027 to 08/31/2029) 
• Provide incident, change, and release management support, including tracking, prioritization, and 
resolution of service requests in accordance with defined service levels. This shall include 
coordination with Oracle support services for issue escalation, service requests (SRs), and defect 
resolution, as well as support for custom-developed applications, including the Order Capture and 
Customer Portal. 
• Support application monitoring, including Oracle Fusion Cloud and all custom-developed 
components, as well as integration and interface management, to ensure reliable system performance 
and data integrity. 
• Support quarterly Oracle Fusion Cloud update cycles, including impact assessment, testing, and 
validation of business processes across both Oracle Fusion and integrated custom applications, 
including the portal. 
• Maintain system configurations within Oracle Fusion, including business rules, workflows, roles, and 
security settings, and shall support configuration and minor enhancements (less than 40 hours), in 
accordance with approved change management processes. 
• Provide support for the custom portal, including user access management, defect resolution, and 
ensuring continued alignment with business requirements. 
• Maintain and update system documentation, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and knowledge 
artifacts for both Oracle Fusion and custom-developed applications to support ongoing operations and 
continuous improvement. 
• Provide periodic operational reporting and participate in governance reviews, including reporting on 
incidents, service levels, system performance, and enhancement backlog status across Oracle Fusion 
and the portal, to ensure alignment with business and technical objectives. 
• Support monthly operational reviews by providing monthly operational reports, including production 
incident metrics and enhancement backlog status. 
 
Task 3 – Optional Task: Additional Process Improvements and Enhancements (Time and Materials,) 
(09/01/2026 to 08/31/2028) 
• Provide additional process improvements, system enhancements, and technical support services on a 
Time and Materials (T&M) basis, as directed by the Government, with a total level of effort not to 
exceed 1 million dollars. 

 
Page 5 of 7 
 
• The scope of this task is intended to support emerging requirements, continuous improvement 
initiatives, and enhancements identified during the execution of Task 1 or at any time during the 
period of performance. 
• Perform activities under this task only upon written authorization from the Government, including 
approval of scope, level of effort, and prioritization of work. 
• Activities performed under this task may include, but are not limited to: 
o Enhancements to Oracle Fusion Cloud configurations, workflows, and business processes 
o Enhancements to custom-developed applications, including Order Capture and Customer Portal 
o Development of additional reports, dashboards, and analytics capabilities 
Process optimization and automation across supply chain, procurement, and warehouse 
operations 
o Enhancements to system integrations, interfaces, and data flows  
o Deployment of additional AI-enabled capabilities, reporting improvements, or decision-support 
tools 
o Usability improvements, user experience enhancements, and functional refinements 
• Shall provide estimates for each requested effort, including level of effort, schedule, and expected 
outcomes, for Government review and approval before execution. 
• Track and report hours expended under this task and provide periodic status updates, including work 
completed, work in progress, and remaining available hours. 
• All work performed under this task shall align with the overall system architecture, security 
requirements, and operational standards established under Tasks 1 and 2. 
 
3. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
 
• Task 1 – Enhancements to Supply Chain Resource Planning Solution (Base Year): 
September 1, 2026 – August 31, 2027  
• Task 2 – Production Operations Support: 
September 1, 2027 – August 31, 2029  
• Task 3 – Optional Task: Additional Process Improvements and Enhancements: 
September 1, 2026 – August 31, 2028

STATEMENT OF WORK  

GENERAL INFORMATION 

1.  Title of Project:  Montana Veterans Affairs (VA) Health Care Center (VAHCS) Physical Access Control System (PACS) - ACRE/Feenics Gov Cloud Annual Software Fee Renewal

2.  Scope of Work:  ACRE/Feenics Gov Cloud Annual Software Fee Renewal for the following CBOCs:  Billings (Majestic and Spring Creek), Bozeman, Butte, Great Falls, and Hamilton.

This service is critical to the (Gov Cloud) access control software. WITHOUT RENEWAL of this SERVICE, the access control software will NO LONGER communicate with the system.** 

Feenics Physical Access Control System (PACS) products have met the security and functional requirements set by GSA’s FIPS 201 Evaluation Program, and have been approved for use by the Federal Government. 

Special Note:  Feenics products and solutions are distributed and installed exclusively by Feenics Certified Partners. These Authorized Partners are required to be extremely well versed in the installation and support of access control technology.

Feenics certifies FICO as an authorized dealer, and sole source for Montana, of Feenics brands and products to the agencies and political subdivisions of the state, and can sell such products so long as FICO remains an Authorized Distributor in good standing. FICO has been a certified Feenics partner in good standing since July 2016 with approximately (4) certified technicians.

Requirements:

During this time frame the vendor will update the system licenses, provide programming support both on-site and by phone as needed, and replace defective hardware.  Montana VAHCS requires a 2.5 hour onsite service call support.

3.  Background:  Montana VAHCS is requesting Annual Software Fee Renewal for our ACRE/Feenics Gov Cloud control access system. The procurement is for annual hardware and software service maintenance with a 2.5-hour onsite response time. 

4.  Performance Period:  This contract is for full annual preventative service and maintenance plan, and quarterly onsite inspections.  Period of performance is one year from the Notice to Proceed (NTP).

B.  CONTRACT AWARD MEETING

A “kick-off” meeting is required.

C.  GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

See Section D for contract task requirements.

D.  SPECIFIC MANDATORY TASKS AND ASSOCIATED DELIVERABLES

Contractor shall comply with all the following: 

Warranty: Software support and warranty information for all components, including Service Level Agreement details, and duration of agreement from date of system acceptance by owner (Montana VAHCS)

Maintenance and support plan will be implemented within this contract.

 Specified Functionality of hardware and service maintenance plan include:

Programing:  Interconnecting software and hardware to optimize logical access control. 

Training:  On-site and formal online training of full usage of entire package system, troubleshooting, maintenance, and services. 

Testing and Commissioning:  Testing the entire package system quarterly to identify functionality, deficiencies, and/or methodologies.  

Service Maintenance Agreement:  1-year annual maintenance and service plan, and quarterly onsite inspections. 

Annual Preventative Maintenance by Certified Technicians.  As required:

Software and Firmware Updates on all Equipment

Provide Proactive and Preventative System Monitoring Technology

Call-In-Support to Certified Specialists

Add/Delete/Modify Users and Credentials

Add/Delete/Modify Schedules and Access

Quarterly Site Visits

Extended Warranty on all Parts and Labor (Full Replacement)

Monthly Alarm Monitoring Costs     

E.  GOVERNMENT RESPONSIBILITIES

Work closely with the vendor and provide access to areas to complete required installation, testing, and maintenance.

Identify internal Montana VAHCS personnel for training and system administration.

Establish access control for contractor to integrate and/or establish personnel profiles within server system. 

F.  CONTRACTOR EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS  

Contractor Requirements:

Be required to provide verification they are a certified and authorized communication company and can provide services in accordance with manufacturer specifications for radio systems.

Ensure only authorized and certified personnel are performing work associated with this contract. This applies to any work sub-contracted as a result of this award.  Appropriate certifications for all individuals performing duties on this project will be required. 

Ensure live maintenance and service personnel are onsite in Ft Harrison, Montana within 2.5 hours of service call.  

G.  CONFIDENTIALITY AND NONDISCLOSURE

1. SUPPLIES OR SERVICES AND PRICES/COSTS 
 
This is a solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with Federal 
Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being 
requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. 
 
Solicitation number 75F40126Q00171 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for CTP Advertising Data 
Monitoring Subscription and Training . Simplified procedures are being utilized in accordance with FAR 
12.201-1. 
 
This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and 
clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at 
www.acquisition.gov. 
 
The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 
518210 (Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services), with a 
small business size standard of $40 million. The product or service code is DH10 (IT and Telecom - Platform 
As A Service: Database, Mainframe, Middleware ). The Government will award a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) 
Purchase Order (PO) resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer, conforming to 
the solicitation, will be most advantageous to the Government (as determined by the solicitation 
evaluation criteria).

characteristics and level of quality that will satisfy the Government’s needs. The salient physical,

2. DESCRIPTION/SPECIFICATIONS/STATEMENT OF WORK 
 
A description of requirements for the items and/or services to be acquired is provided below. 
 
2.1. Background Information and Purpose of the Project 
 
The Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act grants the U.S. Food and Drug Administration 
(FDA) the authority to regulate tobacco products. The FDA established the Center for Tobacco 
Products (CTP) to regulate the manufacture, marketing, and distr ibution of tobacco products to 
protect public health and to reduce tobacco use by youth. CTP oversees the implementation of the 
Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act. To inform tobacco regulatory activities, CTP’s 
Office of Science implements and supports various internal and external research activities designed 
to provide mission -critical data and information to support tobacco product application review and 
other tobacco regulatory activities.  
 
The purpose of this fixed price contract is to provide CTP with advertising data (including actual ads 
and estimated media spend [i.e., estimated money spent by industry to purchase ad placements]) in 
traditional and non -traditional media channels. Tobacco  advertising data provides information on 
tobacco product attributes (e.g., flavors, flavor descriptors, colors, nicotine content), and product 
claims. Tobacco advertising data can also provide information to help understand which audiences 
(e.g., youth) m ay be exposed to certain tobacco ads. Tobacco advertising data includes 
advertisements in traditional (e.g., TV, radio, and print) and non-traditional media (e.g., social media, 
mobile display) channels.  
 
For purposes of this SOW, tobacco products include cigarettes; cigars; dissolvables; hookah tobacco; 
nicotine gels; pipe tobacco; roll -your-own tobacco; nicotine pouches; heated tobacco products; 
smokeless tobacco products, including dip, snuff, snus, and chewing tobacco; and vapes, e -cigs, 
hookah pens, and other Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems (ENDS). For additional information on 
types of tobacco products, see: https://www.fda.gov/tobacco-products/products-guidance-
regulations. 
 
Specifically, the Contractor shall:  1) provide CTP with ongoing online access to its existing advertising 
data monitoring platform and 2) provide technical assistance in setting up and maintaining the online 
subscription so that it can be used by CTP for tobacco regulatory science purposes. The platform shall 
include tobacco industry advertising creative (i.e., actual ads) as well as estimated media spend (i.e.,

estimated money spent by industry to purchase ad placements) for traditional and non -traditional 
media channels.  
 
CTP may publish results in peer-reviewed journals based on research conducted using the advertising 
data obtained through this data monitoring platform. 
 
2.2. Scope 
 
The Contractor shall provide CTP online access to a nd support for its advertising data monitoring 
platform – MediaRadar Magnifier (or equal product) – which shall include tobacco industry advertising 
creative (i.e., actual ads) as well as estimated media spend  (i.e., estimated money spent by industry 
to purchase ad placements) in the U.S. for specified media channels. The sampling frame shall include 
the most popular outlets within each media channel. The estimated media spend shall be calculated 
based on the c ost to purchase ad placements as well as an aud ience factor (dependent on media 
type). The estimated media spend shall be reported by individual ad occurrence, for all channels 
where this information is available. The platform shall have the ability to track and report on the 
following media channels: TV, radio, print, out-of-home, online display, online video, mobile ads, and 
social media advertisements.  
 
The services for this requirement, listed below, will provide information to the CTP Office of Science 
to monitor tobacco industry advertising of tobacco products and to inform tobacco regulatory 
activities. 
 
2.2.1. SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS 
 
The Contractor shall ensure that the proposed solution meets the following salient characteristics: 
• The Contractor shall provide CTP with a subscription or license where CTP can log on via 
a website to view tobacco advertising data collected by the existing platform.   
• The Contractor shall ensure that a minimum of four users can access the system via user 
name and password authentication. 
• The Contractor shall ensure that the platform allows for tracking tobacco ads. For 
purposes of this SOW, tobacco products include cigarettes; cigars; dissolvables; hookah 
tobacco; nicotine gels; pipe tobacco; roll -your-own tobacco; nicotine pouches; heated  
tobacco products; smokeless tobacco products, including dip, snuff, snus, and chewing 
tobacco; and vapes, e-cigs, hookah pens, and other Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems 
(ENDS). For additional information on types of tobacco products, see: 
https://www.fda.gov/tobacco-products/products-guidance-regulations.  
• The platform shall provide creative data (i.e., actual ads) as well as estimated media spend 
data (i.e., estimated money spent by industry to purchase ad placements). The estimated 
media spend shall be calculated based on the cost to purchase ad placements  as well as 
an audience factor (dependent on media type). The estimated media spend shall be 
reported by individual ad occurrence, including details on brand advertised, date of ad 
occurrence, and outlet in which the ad appeared. The estimated media spend shall be 
reported for all channels where this information is available, e.g., TV, radio, print, online 
display, online video, and mobile ads. 
• The Contractor shall ensure that the platform reports on all advertising elements, 
including image, text, and sound, depending on the type of ads.

• The platform shall have the ability to track and report on the following media channels: 
TV, radio, print, out -of-home, online display, online video, mobile ads, and social media 
advertisements.  
• The platform shall allow for creative data to be downloaded.  
• The Contractor shall ensure that the estimated media spend can be viewed in Microsoft 
Excel using either .xls or .csv file format.  
• The platform shall have the ability to provide access to historical data starting from 2012 
or as soon thereafter as available; and provide access to the most recent data. 
• The Contractor shall provide technical support, and training, as specified in Section 2.2.2,

2.2.2. REQUIREMENTS 
 
2.2.2.1. LICENSE / USER ACCOUNTS 
 
The Contractor shall provide access to MediaRadar Magnifier subscription (or equal) and 
support services for a minimum of four users.  
 
2.2.2.2. PLATFORM 
 
The interface and data shall be web-hosted and shall be accessible 24 hours a day, 7 days a 
week with a user ID/password. 
 
2.2.2.3. TECHNICAL SUPPORT 
 
The Contractor shall assign a Project Manager to answer CTP’s questions and assist with 
system issues. The Project Manager shall answer all methodological questions and provide 
CTP accompanying documentation in the form of written email responses. The Proj ect 
Manager shall notify CTP of any changes to the platform’s sampling frame (i.e., the media 
channels tracked and reported by the platform) via email within five business days of the 
change. The Project Manager (or an alternative staff person with knowledge of CTP’s account) 
shall answer CTP’s email and telephone inquiries within two business days. Administrative 
support shall be available eight hours per day, 40 hours per week. In addition, technical 
customer support or service shall be available from 8:0 0 AM to 5:00 PM Monday through 
Friday, US Eastern Time.
