SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE 

832674267


The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) is seeking sources for the United States Marine Corp (USMC) Electronic Security Systems (ESS)

CONTRACTING OFFICE ADDRESS:  

DISA/Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization (DITCO)/PS8312  

2300 East Drive, Building 3600  

Scott AFB, IL 62225 

INTRODUCTION:

This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of small businesses and large businesses (including the following subsets: Small Disadvantaged Businesses, Certified 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Businesses and Woman-Owned Small Businesses) to provide the required products and/or services. 

The United States Marine Corps (USMC) is seeking information from potential sources to provide streamlined delivery of Marine Corp Electronic Security System (MCESS) solutions to warfighter at various Marine Corp installations worldwide. This requirement focuses on the integration of critical security infrastructure, including Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), Automated Access Control Systems (AACS), Closed Circuit Television (CCTV), and Mass Notification Systems (MNS) for a variety of security classifications and facility types as well as installation in Secure & Sensitive Environments, and Virtual Environment Platforms.  This requirement integrates solutions with the ultimate objective of obtaining services to deliver a turnkey ESS end product solution.  

The proposed acquisition will be structured as a Blanket Purchase Agreement with an estimated total ceiling of $99M.  The anticipated period of performance consists of a one-year base period, with four, one-year option periods, with an estimated start date of April 1, 2027. Work under this vehicle will be executed via Call Orders, which will be issued based on the specific scope and geographic requirements of the mission to ensure flexible and responsive support for Marine Corps installations worldwide.

The anticipated place of performance is USMC Bases Worldwide.

DISCLAIMER: 

 

THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL.  IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT.  RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS NOTICE.  NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE.  ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.

CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND:  Not Applicable; this is a new requirement.

REQUIRED CAPABILITIES:

Personnel Certifications

Please provide evidence of current personnel certifications held for the following. For each certification held, please submit corresponding documentation.

Certifications:

AMAG Symmetry 

Genetec SecurityCenter (Omnicast Technical Certification/Advanced Troubleshooting)

Cisco Certified Network Associate, or CompTIA Security+, or CompTIA Network+ 

SIRCOM Smart Alert System Administrator Certification

SIRCOM Certified Engineer/SME Certification

Technical Capabilities

Provide responses to each of  the following technical areas.

Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS)

1. Describe your corporate experience with both the software configuration/programming and the physical installation of IDS within restricted areas, ICD 705 Sensitive Secure Areas, Armories, and Magazines.

2. Detail your company's experience with the following IDS software and programming methods:

DMP Programming in AMAG Symmetry 

DMP Programming with Remote Link

DMP SCS-1R Programming 

Integrating firewalls with DMP SCS-1R and AMAG systems

3. Describe your experience with the physical installation of IDS devices, sensors, and control equipment such as DMP panels, AMAG panels, and various security switches and detectors.

Automated Access Control Systems (AACS) 

1. Describe your corporate experience with the software configuration and physical installation of AACS.

2. Detail your experience programming AMAG Symmetry v8 or later in a virtual (VMware) and/or cloud environment.

3. Describe your experience installing ACS hardware, including client workstations, servers, AMAG and HID card readers, locking mechanisms, and control panels.

Mass Notification Systems (MNS)

1. Describe your corporate experience with the software configuration, programming, and physical installation of MNS.

2. Detail your experience with the following MNS software and programming tools:

MadahCom/Cooper Notification/Eaton WAVES (NCT 5.6.2 and Software Version 7.4.3)

SiRcom Smart Alert (SiSA) MNS Software Version 3.X.X

SiRcom SI.PROG-012 Firmware Flashing and Diagnostics Tool

3. Describe your experience with the physical design, installation, and programming of MNS equipment from Eaton WAVES and SiRcom brands, as well as ancillary components such as mobile radios, antennas, and power systems.

Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) System 

1. Describe your corporate experience with the software configuration, programming, and physical installation of CCTV.

2. Detail your experience with the configuration and programming of the following.

Axis IP cameras, encoders, and POE devices

Genetec AutoVu (ALPR) and Restricted Security Area (RSA) Surveillance

Genetec network video recorders

FLIR Ranger Radars and AXIS radars

Genetec in a virtual (VMware) and/or cloud environment

3. Describe your experience with the physical installation of Axis CCTV devices and the integration of analog cameras into a Genetec digital video system.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: 

Must have a Secret facility clearance.  Please provide your current Facility Clearance Level.

Please provide evidence of reseller/purchasing agreements with Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEMs) from the list of relevant OEMs below. 

AMAG: Authorized Partner/Dealer/Integrator

DMP: Authorized Partner/Dealer/Integrator

Genetec: Authorized Partner/Dealer/Integrator

CISCO: Authorized Partner/Dealer/Integrator

SIRCOM: Authorized Partner/Dealer/Integrator/Reseller Agreement

SOURCES SOUGHT:  

The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) for this requirement is 541512, with the corresponding size standard of $34M.  

In order to make a determination for a small business set-aside, two or more qualified and capable small businesses must submit responses that demonstrate their qualifications.  Responses must demonstrate the company’s ability to perform in accordance with FAR clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting.  If you are a small business, identify your position to propose as a prime or subcontractor.  If as a prime, describe capabilities to convey ability to comply with the Limitations on Subcontracting clause.

To assist DISA in determining the level of participation by small business in any subsequent procurement that may result from this Sources Sought Notice, provide information regarding any plans to use joint ventures (JVs) or partnering.  Please outline the company's areas of expertise and those of any proposed JV/partner who combined can meet the specific requirements contained in this notice.

SUBMISSION DETAILS:

Responses should include:

Business name and address; 

Name of company representative and their business title; 

Small Business Socio-economic status (if small); 

CAGE Code;

Prime contract vehicles; to include ENCORE III, SETI, NIH CIO-SP4, NASA SEWP V, General Service Administration (GSA): OASIS, ALLIANT II, VETS II, STARS III, MAS (including applicable SIN(s), groups or pools), or any other Government Agency contract vehicle that allows for decentralized ordering.  (This information is for market research only and businesses with a valid cage that lack prime contract vehicles are still encouraged to respond to this notice.) 

Businesses who wish to respond must send a response via email NLT 4:00 PM Central Daylight Time (CDT) on  to Contract Specialist, Kyle Brooks, kyle.a.brooks14.civ@mail.mil, and Contracting Officer, Vanessa Gonzalez, vanessa.m.gonzalez2.civ@mail.mil.  Interested businesses should submit a brief capabilities statement package addressing the specific questions above (no more than five pages) demonstrating the ability to perform the services listed under Required Capabilities, Special Requirements, and Sources Sought.      

Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, must be clearly marked on all materials.  All information received that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly.  All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.  All government and contractor personnel reviewing submitted responses will have signed non-disclosure agreements and understand their responsibility for proper use and protection from unauthorized disclosure of proprietary information as pursuant to 41 USC 423.  The Government shall not be held liable for any damages incurred if proprietary information is not properly identified.

For information on DISA’s requirements, you can find current information on our home page: www.disa.mil – that includes current forecast and the current acquisition strategies. If there is no information regarding the requirement you may be inquiring about, then there is no additional publicly available information. Please continue to review www.disa.mil.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

1.  Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR). 

  

a. Primary COR.  See DITCO Additional Text G1 - Points of Contact

b. Alternate COR.  See DITCO Additional Text G1 - Points of Contact

c. Property Administrator (PA) See DITCO Additional Text G1 - Points of Contact 

2.  Contract Title.  United States Marine Corps (USMC) Electronic Security Systems (ESS)

3.  Background. The USMC and Naval Information Warfare Center (NIWC) Atlantic requires engineering development, design, procurement, fabrication, configuration, integration, installation, logistics, maintenance, and life cycle support solutions for ashore ESS.  These systems will support the operational requirements of USMC facilities where emergency management, public safety, law enforcement, security, and command & control are of high or vital interest.  This PWS provides the general guidelines and specific requirements to develop, deliver, and sustain electronic security and emergency management system solutions that protect our Nation's critical infrastructure, personnel, assets, and resources worldwide.  

4.  Objectives: USMC and NIWC Atlantic must be able to respond quickly and effectively in order to meet the operational requirements of the USMC in the rapidly changing environments.  Cost effective and innovative system solutions are required to respond to routine, emergent, and evolving challenges of the warfighter in these regions.  This contract integrates solutions with the objective of obtaining services to deliver an end product or a turnkey solution.   This BPA will be executed through the issuance of call orders that are determined to be within the scope and location of this BPA.  This BPA encompasses project/program management, engineering, procurement, implementation, and testing requirements associated with the development and delivery of ESS solutions.  

5.  Scope. The purpose of this Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) is to provide streamlined delivery of ESS service solutions to the warfighter at shore installations worldwide in response to time sensitive, emergent mission and special security program requirements.  The scope of this BPA covers the entire spectrum of outcomes associated with the full lifecycle of delivery and support of ESS capabilities to include automated Access Control Systems (ACS), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), Closed Circuit Television (CCTV), and Mass Notification Systems (MNS).

This BPA covers requirements as it relates to ESS experience with specific Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) solutions and variations of project environments that range in risk and complexity based on size and other factors.  Support under this BPA includes supply requirements and encompasses project/program management, engineering, and other technical support requirements associated with the development, delivery, sustainment, and management of ESS solutions.

6.  Performance Requirements.  The following paragraphs list all required non-personal services tasks that will be required throughout the BPA.  The contractor shall provide necessary resources with knowledge and experience as cited in the personal qualification clause to support the listed tasks.  Contractors shall perform requirements in accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and/or Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), which do not include performance of inherently Government functions.  The contractor shall complete all required tasks while controlling and tracking performance and goals in terms of costs, schedules, and resources.

Contractor shall perform all the required processes to manage the programs associated with this BPA contract to include but not limited to:

Management of staffing and resources.

Training and certifications of personnel.

Outside Continental Contiguous United States (OCONUS) hiring, deployments, and travel.

Management of Technical Expert Status Accreditation (TESA) applications and applicants.

Quality Assurance.

Integrated Master Schedule (IMS).

Contracts management.

Budgeting, proposal, and cost control.

Procurements.

Communications management.

Facility Management.

The following tasks may be included and/or specified in a call order:

Task 1: Project Management.

Task 2: System Engineering.

Task 3: Software Engineering.

Task 4: Cybersecurity.

Task 5: Equipment/Material Procurement.

Task 6: Pre-Installation Test And Checkout (PITCO).

Task 7: Cutover And Transition Plan.

Task 8: Installation And Integration.

Task 9: System Operational And Verification Test (SOVT).

Task 10: Training.

Task 11: Logistics Support.

The contractor shall coordinate with the COR to schedule the call order kickoff in person or virtual.

**THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION** 
 
 
Audio Visual (AV) / Video Teleconferencing (VTC) Lifecycle Information 
Technology (IT) Support (AV LIT) 
Hill Air Force Base  
Request for Information (RFI) 
Overview  
The Air Force Nuclear Weapon Center (AFNWC) Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) Systems 
Directorate (SD) team is conducting market research to deﬁne the scope and requirements of the 
Audio Visual (AV)/ Video Teleconferencing (VTC) Lifecycle Information Technology (IT) Support (AV 
LIT). For this RFI, the Government is seeking input from industry on the capability to operate within 
a Special Access Program (SAP) environment, as well as to provide feedback on our current 
requirement documentation (see attached Performance Work Statement (PWS) and Price 
Catalogue). The Government intends to award this effort as a Single-Award Indeﬁnite Delivery 
Indeﬁnite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with ﬁxed pricing elements, primarily at Hill AFB, with other 
geographically separated units (GSUs) within the ICBM Systems Directorate.  
Scope 
The primary objective of this contract is to provide lifecycle sustainment for current and future 
Video Teleconferencing (VTC), Audio Visual (AV), and Information Technology (IT) hardware (HW) 
systems across Intercontinental Ballistic Missiles (ICBM) Directorate Operating Locations in the 
Continental United States (CONUS). 
The Contractor shall provide comprehensive Consulting and Design Services for new and existing 
VTC and AV solutions, as well as for IT HW installation. The Contractor shall also provide end-to-
end Maintenance Services which include, but are not limited to, tier 3 support, decommissioning, 
and lifecycle replacement. 
To facilitate the procurement of necessary equipment and services, the Contractor shall follow the 
established Pricing Catalogue of pre-approved HW, standard conference room HW conﬁgurations, 
and associated services. Services and HW may be requested in addition to the standardized 
conﬁgurations. This catalogue will be used for all purchasing and installation activities performed 
under this contract. Individual Task Orders (TO) may deviate from the Price Catalogue as negotiated 
between the requiring activity and the Contractor. 
This contract requires the Contractor to obtain and maintain necessary security clearances and to 
coordinate with ICBM personnel on all matters involving security impact and cybersecurity 
compliance, including the implementation and management of controls under Risk Management 
Framework (RMF). The Contractor shall provide the organizational resources, both technical and 
functional, required for managing contract performance.  
 

**THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION** 
 
 
Request for Information (RFI) 
Capability 
1. Has/does your company support Video Teleconferencing (VTC)/Audio Visual (AV) Lifecycle 
Information Technology (IT) in a TS SAP space? Please provide most recent. 
2. Does your company currently hold a top-secret facility security clearance (FCL) 
(TS/SCI/SAP)?  
3. Does your company currently have personnel who have top secret clearances 
(TS/SCI/SAP)? 
4. Will your company be able to provide a local presence at Hill AFB (within 50-mile radius)?  
5. Does your company have the capability to support multiple Air Force Nuclear Weapons 
Center operating locations (i.e., Hill AFB, Kirtland AFB, Minot AFB, Malmstrom AFB, FE 
Warren AFB, Vandenberg SFB)? If so, provide information.  
6. Does your company have prior experience as a prime contractor working on projects that 
are similar in scope to this effort? If so, please provide the PWS for that work your company 
has completed (if shareable and Unclassiﬁed) and the contract number. 
7. Has your company worked in a multi-class system? Please indicate which federal agency 
and whether an ATO was granted. 
8. What kind of IT certiﬁcations does your company have? 
9. Is your company an authorized reseller or preferred vendor of IT hardware equipment? If so, 
please provide list of suppliers. 
Demographics/Business Information 
1. Please state your company’s demographics (i.e., Small Business, Large Business, etc.) 
2. Does your company currently have any teaming or partnering arrangements? If so, please 
specify.  
3. Does your company have the ﬁnancial capacity to support a requirement at this magnitude 
(see PWS for scope and requirement speciﬁcs)? 
4. Does your company have any current contracts under a Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) or 
Governmentwide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs)? If so, please specify. 
5. What other contract vehicles do your company currently have that could be a good ﬁt for 
this effort? 
PWS 
1. Please review the attached PWS and provide comments/suggestions to improve this 
requirement. For example, consider the following questions: 
a. Do you have any suggestions on the deﬁned room conﬁgurations? 
b. PWS Section 1.0 (Scope): The PWS mentions "decommissioning and lifecycle 
replacement. " From an industry perspective, what are the best practices for 
structuring and pricing the decommissioning and disposal of old equipment under a 
lifecycle support contract? 

**THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION** 
 
 
c. PWS Section 4.2.4 (Service Calls): This section lists response times (e.g., "4 
Business Hours" for Emergency) and separate resolution times (e.g., "within one (1) 
business day" for Emergency). Is this distinction clear? Do the prescribed resolution 
times for Minor, Major, and Emergency repairs appear reasonable from a 
performance and staffing standpoint? 
d. PWS Section 4.2.4 (Service Calls): For service calls from customers using a 
Government Purchase Card (GPC) without a Task Order, the PWS states that 
response times are not guaranteed. How does this uncertainty impact your ability to 
staff appropriately? Would you recommend a different model for ad-hoc support 
requests? 
e. PWS Section 4.4 (Purchasing and Installation): The PWS requires the use of 
"industry-certiﬁed technicians" with speciﬁc certiﬁcations (AVIXA, Crestron, Extron, 
etc.). Are these certiﬁcations requirements appropriate for the scope of work, or are 
there other certiﬁcations the Government should consider? 
f. PWS Section 5.1 (Staffing Requirements): The PWS requires the contractor to have 
technicians "ready to respond...regardless of the number of reported repair orders 
or locations. " To help industry propose adequate staffing, what historical workload 
data (e.g., number of rooms, average monthly service calls by priority, current GFE 
inventory) would be most critical to provide with a formal solicitation? 
g. PWS Section 5.4 (Travel) & Pricing Catalogue: The Government intends for the 
"location multiplier" to account for the varying costs of labor/living at different 
geographically separated operating locations (e.g., Vandenberg SFB vs. Hill AFB), 
while standard Travel Approval Requests (TARs) will be utilized for temporary duty 
(TDY) travel expenses. Is this distinction clear in the current documentation? What 
is the industry best practice for structuring regional labor rate variances alongside 
ad-hoc TDY travel across a wide geographic enterprise? 
Pricing Catalogue 
1. Please review the attached Pricing Catalogue and provide comments/suggestions on how 
to improve the content, formatting, etc.  
2. Is the PWS clear on how the pricing catalogue works? 
3. Government is interested in hearing industry's suggestions to address discounts related to 
quantity of rooms. Should there be a discount for a multiple room requirement vs a single 
room requirement? 
Contract Admin 
1. The Government is considering a 5-year base ordering period with ﬁve 1-year option 
periods. How feasible would it be to price labor under this contract as a ﬁxed price 
arrangement for a 10-year effort? 
 

**THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION** 
 
 
Responses 
Responses shall be UNCLASSIFIED. 
Response shall be limited to 10 pages total (including any cover pages; attachments not included). 
Please provide a cover sheet with the following company information:  
Company Name:   
Designated Point of Contact:  
Name:   
Title:  
Email:  
Phone:   
Business Type/Size:  
CAGE code:  
UEI number:   
Facility Security Clearance:   
 
Interested parties are required to respond in the following format:  
- Microsoft Word for office 2007 (or newer) compatible 
- 1-inch margins  
- 12-point font  
Additionally, please note that the Government reserves the right to hold industry brieﬁngs 
with any of the respondents to this RFI. 
Please submit the responses no later than 1200 MDT on Tuesday, 02 June 2026 to both Mr. Tanner 
Nielsen, Contracting Officer at tanner.nielsen@us.af.mil and Mr. Quade McGuire, Contracting 
Specialist at quade.mcguire@us.af.mil.   
Disclaimer 
This announcement constitutes an RFI issued pursuant to FAR 52.215-3 – Request for Information 
or Solicitation for Planning Purposes. No solicitation exists; therefore, please do not request a copy

RFQ: FA500426Q0020 
 
 Questions Answers 
1 Can you confirm if the newspapers are in bound 
volumes? 
• Nearly all the newspapers were previously bound in volumes with aluminum 
binding screws. 
 
• Nearly all pages have three (or more) holes where those screws held the volumes 
together. 
 
• The screws have been removed from almost all the volumes except for one screw 
that that has been stripped on the 1970 volume.  
 
• That one rod/screw will need to be clipped off by the vendor. 
 
• Perhaps six volumes were bound by thick binding staples.  
 
• The staples have been removed, but the holes are now mostly small tears from 
when the pages were folded over the staples as a joint.  
2 Can the bindings be manipulated up to and 
including disbanding to ensure the best images 
possible? 
• With the exception of one screw on the 1970 collection, all volumes have been 
disbanded. 
 
3 Could you send a few sample pictures so we can 
see the condition? The best pictures would be of 
the volumes open. 
Attached are a dozen sample page scans from the collection.  
 
• Please note the holes where the aluminum binding screws previously bound the 
volumes.  
 
• Deep creases, tears, and extreme fragility due to age, should also be accounted 
for. 
 
• The small tears from staple holes are not obvious in these scans but are uneven 
tears that can easily catch on equipment and must be accounted for when 
handling.  
 
• Also note the curling and water stains on the newspaper sample from 1958. All of 

 Questions Answers 
the collection from 1958 has similar warping and water damage. Most of that 
year’s collection is in much poorer condition than the sample shown.   
4 A Can an estimated box count. A 29 boxes.  
 
• Boxes are Gaylord Archival Metal-edged board newspaper boxes. 
 
B approximate shipment dimensions. B • Twenty-eight boxes measure 18”x 13” x3” each.  
 
• One box, which houses the 1958 volume, measures 25” x 19” x 2.5”. 
 
• Cumulatively, the collection is 26 height, 28 wide, 38 tall (from floor height).   
 
• They will be consolidated and packaged on a palette for shipment.  
 
• All volumes must remain in Gaylord Archival boxes for shipment and be 
returned in the same boxes they are shipped in. 
 
C and/or total shipment weight of the archival 
newspaper collection being provided to the 
contractor be provided? 
C • The project manager does not have access to a scale and is unable to 
estimate the shipment weight. 
5 By what method is government looking to ship 
these to the awardee please? 
• Either via UPS or Fed Ex.   
 
• Once awarded the project manager will work with our shipping department (354 
LRS) to determine shipping method.  
 
• The entire shipment must be wrapped in water tight protective packaging. 
 
6 Can the awarded contractor use qualified commercial 
scanning/digitization support or internal personnel to 
complete the scanning, OCR/searchable PDF creation, 
quality control, and hard drive deliverables, while the 
prime contractor remains responsible for project 
management, secure handling, reporting, shipment 
tracking, and final delivery. 
NO THIS COLLECTION MAY NOT BE SCANNED WITH COMMERCIAL SCANNING 
EQUIPMENT. PER ESTABLISED BEST-PRACTICE GUIDELINES OF THE AIR FORCE 
HISTORICAL RESEARCH AGENC.  
 
• All scanning must be conducted by trained personnel using overhead, touchless 
scanning equipment, with each item placed on the equipment by hand. The 
papers are too delicate to be commercially scanned. 

 Questions Answers 
 
7 Definition of "surface”:  Does the 9,640 figure 
count page sides (front and back as two), full 
pages (front and back as one), or full broadsheets. 
• Newspapers pages are generally printed on front and back and numbered with 
each side of text representing one page or surface.  
 
• Surfaces are one side of printed pages. Page/surface count corresponds to 
printed pages as it would be in a book.  
 
8 Page formats and dimensions —  what mix of 
broadsheet, tabloid, or other formats does the 
collection contain, and what are the largest and 
smallest page sizes? 
• The format of the newspaper fluxuated over its run.  
 
• It mostly was printed in a tabloid format ranging between 4 to 16 pages.  
 
• Tabloid dimensions were 17” x 12”.  
 
• For part of its run, in 1958, it was a broadsheet. Exact dimensions for the 1958 
volume are difficult to be precise because moisture exposure and poor 
preservation warped much of that volume, but it is approximately 15” x 23.”     
  
9 Image capture —  required minimum resolution 
(dpi), bit depth, color mode, and FADGI star 
rating? 
• The proposal specifies archival scanning with standard image processing and 
quality assurance.  
 
• Deliverable images are full color at 300 dpi for both master TIFF files and access 
JPEG files. 
 
10 Deliverable file formats —  what is required for 
preservation masters (e.g., uncompressed TIFF, 
JP2) and for access derivatives (e.g., PDF/A, 
JPEG)? 
• Preservation master files: full-color 300 dpi TIFF format with LZW lossless 
compression.  
 
• Access derivatives: full-color 300 dpi JPEG format and one multi-page, searchable 
PDF/A file per newspaper issue.  
 
• Proposal also includes a finding aid with imaging notes and hard-drive file 
delivery.  

 Questions Answers 
11 OCR —  is OCR required? If so, what is the 
accuracy threshold, output format (searchable 
PDF, hOCR, ALTO XML), and is article-level zoning 
required? 
• OCR and searchable PDF have been a requirement of the project from the 
beginning. Article-level zoning is not required? 
12 Metadata and file structure —  what metadata 
schema is required (Dublin Core, MODS, METS, 
custom), and what file-naming convention and 
folder structure? How will the Government 
provide issue-level metadata? 
Proposal states that the Award Winner will  
 
• create and send a delivery record;  
 
• generate a spreadsheet describing items;  
 
• document conditions that may hinder scanning; and  
 
• deliver a finding aid with imaging notes. 
 
13 Any carrier, insurance, packaging, or chain-of-
custody requirements for round-trip shipping 
from Eielson AFB? All scanning can be done off 
site and no contractor presence is needed at 
AFB? 
• When in transit, the shipment should be able to be tracked.  
 
• Delivery should require a signature.  
 
• No contractor is expected to be at Eielson. 
 
14 "Equipment delivery from government to the 
contractor shall be government responsibility, 
and from contractor returning to government the 
contractors responsibility. “  - Is this in reference 
to the actual scanning equipment or only the 
9,640 surfaces will be shipped to contractor? 
• Eielson personnel will ship no scanning equipment. 
 
• In addition to the documents themselves, proper archival artifact boxes, suitable 
for holding fragile volumes will be shipped with the documents. 
 
• It is expected that the documents will remain in the archival boxes at all times 
except when volumes are being scanned.  
 
• Volumes will be returned in these same boxes.   
 
15 Timing —  Is there an expected timeline or no 
later than date the government requires from 
awarded contractor? 
• The physical collection should be returned to the Historian’s Office, or a 
representative of the office. 
 
• Expected return per the PoP end date. 

 Questions Answers 
 
• Ideally, this will not be in transit over the winter months.  
 
16 Please provide a complete and legible copy of the 
applicable Wage Determination that includes all 
job classifications and corresponding wage rates? 
 
(Service Contract Act (SCA) Wage Determination 
for the State of Alaska.) 
• A new copy has been provided in case of upload errors to the original solicitation. 
17 Are all the newspapers the same size • No.  
 
• Most of the collection is 17” x 12” one portion is 23” x 15.”      
 
• There is also additional variations due to fraying, torn edges, large sections of 
missing pages, and warping from moisture exposure. 
 
18 Can tape be used if needed to prevent additional 
tearing when scanning? 
• Touchless archival scanning, as required by this office, will not result in additional 
tearing in the scanning process.  
 
• Some extremely poor volumes are at risk of breaking just from handling or are 
already torn badly in their current state.  
 
• For pages such as these, acid-free archival translucent repair tape may be used 
sparingly.  
 
• ANY REPAIRS CAN ONLY BE DONE BY TRANINED ARCHIVAL STAFF  
 
• Lineco Archival Document Repair Tape has been used for portions of this 
collection in past by the Historian and is the preferred method of this repair, if 
necessary.  
 
• All repairs must be documented. 
 

 Questions Answers 
19 Please provide any document naming 
requirements; do you have an example of how 
these should be named? 
• Date of issues in civilian format 
 
• Matching the style of the newspapers themselves would be sufficient.  
20 Can you please confirm the # of pages in one 
newspaper? 
• The newspaper fluxuated dramatically over its run between 4 and 16 pages.  
 
• Additionally, there are some volumes that are missing entirely. 
21 Are we expected to name / index per each 
newspaper? If so can you please confirm the 
fields that we need to type in for the indexing I.e. 
date, name etc. 
• Yes.  
 
• The year and date of the issues is sufficient.  
22 Will you ship the boxes through FEDEX or should 
we send the Paid FEDEX label for the shipment? 
• Initial shipping will be Government responsibility. 
23 Can we request to extend the due date for two or 
three days? 
Due date has been extended to June 05 2026 
24 A Could you please confirm the physical 
condition and format of the newspapers 
(e.g., bound volumes, loose sheets, fragile 
condition, etc.)? 
A • The volumes were previously bound.  
 
• They have mostly been removed from their binding but the crude method 
they were held together has resulted in holes and tears in every page of this 
collection.  
 
• Creasing along the binding has weakened or frayed the edges further.  
 
• This is acidic newsprint that is between 50 and 70 years old.  
 
• The inks is faded throughout. It was poorly stored for nearly its entire life.  
 
• It is fragile and can only be handled by trained archival staff with extensive 

 Questions Answers 
experience with such records.     
 
B Does the collection include photographs, 
color pages, microfilm, or any other special 
media formats? 
B • There were a few select issues, usually around the Christmas and New Years 
Holidays, when the paper was published in alternative colors of green, red, 
and sometimes with white.  
 
• A few sample pages have been attached.  
 
• There were no true color issues, just novelty issues that has splashes of 
alternative colors.  
 
• All photos are monochrome.  
 
C The RFQ mentions 9,640 surfaces, could you 
please confirm whether this represents a 
final count or an estimate? 
C • This is an estimate.  
 
• The collection is incomplete.  
 
• Certain issues have already been lost or destroyed.  
 
• Some individual pages are missing or been ripped out.  
 
• This number is the best estimate based on the known or suspected 
deficiencies in the collection.    
 
D Additionally, how will any overages beyond 
this quantity be handled? 
D • The number of 9640 is on optimistic estimate.  
 
• It would be difficult seeing this collection being greater than 10000 pages, but 
overages should account for perhaps 500 additional pages. 
E For clarification, does the term “surface” 
refer to one side of a page (i.e., a single 
image)? 
E • One side of page. 
F Are the materials primarily double-sided, or 
is there a mix of single-sided and double-
sided pages? 
F • Newsprint is two-sided. 

 Questions Answers 
G Will the materials be delivered to our 
facility, or required pickup? Kindly confirm 
the logistics. 
G • Project Manager working with 354 LRS will carefully package the Collection 
and any supporting documentation and ship, deliver the Collection to the 
Award Winner. 
 
• At wrap-up, the Award Winner will package and ship the project deliverables 
back to the Historian’s Office and coordinate return of materials with the 
Project Manager. 
 
H Are there any specific metadata 
requirements, file naming conventions, or 
quality control (QC) standards that we 
should follow? 
H • Each issue should be uniquely named.  
 
• Example: April 2, 1952.  
 
• Since the publication did not use military style dating (day/month/year), it is 
not required to use that format.    
 
I Could you please provide the expected 
project timeline and turnaround 
requirements? 
I • No later than the Pop end date.  
 
• Five external hard drives with the collection and the physical collection should 
be returned to the historian’s office within four months. 
 
25 Is it the Government’s intent that the reference 
to “fragile paper format” requires all imaging to 
be performed using flatbed (glass platen) 
scanning methods? 
NO - NONE OF THIS COLLETION SHOULD BE SCANNED WITH A FLATBED GLASS 
PLATEN SCANNER.  
 
• The entire collation was published on cheap and acidic newsprint from fifty to 
seventy years ago and was often subjected to extreme temperatures upon its 
publication.  
 
• Exposure to the bright light of a flatbed scanner will further degrade the paper 
and bleach out delicate ink that is already faded throughout much the collection.  
 
• Any vendor suggesting flatbed scanning for a project such as this cannot be 
trusted with the collection.  
 
• THIS ENTIRE COLLETION MUST BE SCANNED WITH TOUCHLESS OVERHEAD 
SCANNNING EQUIPMENT BY TRAINED ARCHIVAL STAFF.  

 Questions Answers 
 
• These are standard best practice guidelines for such a delicate historical 
collection.  
 
• This should have been plainly laid out to any vendor as it was part of the original 
proposal put forward by the historian’s office.  
 
26 Are any of the newspaper materials known to 
require repair, stabilization, or conservation 
treatment prior to imaging? 
• Every page in this collection has been damaged by holes and age.  
 
• Much of it has significantly more damage.  
 
• Most of them do not require repair, per se, but it does require careful handling 
from professionally trained and experienced archival staff, using specialized 
equipment made to specifically for such fragile documents.     
 
27 Is there any incumbent/recompete or this is a 
brand-new project? If yes, could you please 
provide us with their award number or even if the 
customer bought similar services in the past. 
• This is a one-time service not the result of a re-compete or prior award.

1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is conducting market 
research to identify qualified vendors and gather input on potential solutions to support the 
upcoming acquisition for Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) processing capabilities. We 
hereby issue the attached Request for Information (RFI)  RFI-CO-42616067 to solicit 
feedback from capable and interested industry partners  of commercial Order of Battle

A. Introduction 
 
1. Further to NCIA/ACQ/2026/06643, t he NATO Communications and Information 
Agency (NCIA) is conducting further market research to identify potential sources  for 
Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) data - outlined at Annex B - to inform the project 
requirements. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for informational 
purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for 
Quotation (RFQ), or invitation for bid.  
 
B. Purpose 
 
1. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain input from industry to help inform the NCIA’s 
acquisition planning. Responses to this RFI will assist in refining requirements, 
identifying capabilities, and shaping the strategy for any future solicitation. 
 
C. Background 
 
1. NCIA seeks to provide analysts within its Open -Source Intelligence (OSINT) 
community with a scalable capability to collect, process, and exploit Open -Source 
Information (OSINF).  
2. This capability will enable OSINT analysts to access and analyse information required 
to satisfy the Commander’s critical intelligence requirements at the speed of relevance, 
whilst maintaining a stringent focus on security aspects.  
3. Whilst the service is envisaged to contain several key capabilities, the purpose of this 
RFI is to focus on  access to OSINT data to provide a n unclassified, assured and 
continually updated Order Of Battle (ORBAT) of adversary military equipment, 
infrastructure and capabilities within NATO areas of interest. 
4. A High-Level Summary of the Open -Source Data requirements are contained within 
Annex B. 
5. The RFI seeks to elicit the view of industry partners on the availability of the envisioned 
data service and facilitate the Agency’s insight into best -in-class industry solutions , 
including current market capabilities, and pricing models of Services offered. 
6. A full list of questions that the Agency would like to canvass industry views on are 
contained within Annex C 
 
D. Submission Instructions

a. Submit responses via the email address in section H no later than 17:00 hours 
Central European Time (CET) on 12 June 2026. 
 
b. Responses should be submitted in PDF or Word format and must not exceed 10 
pages, including:

ii. Responses to the questions in Annex C

1. Background 
 
The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) aims to support the Open-Source 
Intelligence (OSINT) community by providing a scalable capability to collect, process, and 
exploit Open-Source Information ( OSINF). This capability will enable OSINT analysts to 
access and analyse the information required to satisfy the Commander’s critical intelligence 
requirements at the speed of relevance.  
 
Part of this wider solution is to provide analysts access to an unclassified, assured and 
continually updated database of structured adversary military equipment  specifications, 
infrastructure and capabilities , as well as  country-level assessments. This database  will be 
used on both unclassified and classified networks as a baseline dataset for multiple functional 
areas within NATO, providing a persistent, searchable data layer. This data must be available 
through an API and interlinked to enable analysts to search correlated datasets of all known 
military vehicles, vessels, aircraft and their associated capabilities, weapons, locations, etc, 
whilst understanding t he broader associated military and country capabilities.  
 
NCIA is specifically seeking information on commercially available, operationally mature data 
products and services that already exist within the market and are subject to continual 
maintenance and update cycles. Responses focused solely on bespoke consultancy , ad-hoc 
research tasks, or one -off capability assessments are out of scope for this market 
engagement. The intent of this RFI is to understand currently available market offerings that 
provide persistent access to structured defence and military capability data that is accessible 
through an API. 
 
2. Scope 
 
a. Functional Requirements . The Contractor shall deliver a fully integrated API 
capability that functions as a data layer within multiple NATO Functional Area Services 
(FAS). This data layer shall provide structured, interconnected, and continuously 
updated defence intelligence across the following datasets: 
 
i. Equipment & Platforms: Technical specifications, capabilities, imagery, and 
operational status for systems including land, sea, air, and space platforms, 
weapons, sensors, and subsystems. 
ii. Orders of Battle (ORBAT): Global military force structures, unit compositions, 
command relationships, and base locations for all state armed forces. 
iii. Military Installations: Geolocated data on worldwide military facilities, from 
airfields and naval bases to early-warning sites and nuclear infrastructure. 
iv. Country Reporting: Political, Military, Economic, Social, Infrastructure,  
Information, Physical Environment and Time (PMESII-PT) assessments on key 
countries of interest, structured for rapid threat and stability analysis. 
 
b. Non-Functional Requirements 
 
i. Continual update of the above data sets to ensure timeliness of this baseline 
data.

The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Indian Health Service (IHS),  
 Woodrow Wilson Keeble Memorial Health Care Center at Sisseton, South Dakota plans to 
procure, on a sole source basis, licensing and support for Morris-Systems Inventory 
Management Software from: 
 
Morris Systems Incorporated 
3900 S. Stonebridge Dr. #903 
McKinney, TX 75070 
 
The response close date of the notice for this requirement is in accordance with FAR 5.203(b). 
This acquisition will be processed under FAR Part 12 – Acquisition for Commercial Items and will 
be made pursuant to the authority in FAR Part 13.106-1 (b)(1) and is exempt from the 
requirements of FAR Part 6. The North American Industry Classiﬁcation System code (NAICS) is 
541519 - Other Computer Related Services, and the small business size standard is $34M.  
 
The mission of the Sisseton Indian Health Service is to provide the best possible healthcare 
services to the Native American population on the Sisseton Wahpeton Sioux Tribe Reservation. 
To achieve this mission the Service Unit has identiﬁed the need for a Non-Personal Service 
Contract for supply inventory system for the Property & Supply Department. 
 
The Property & Supply Department is responsible for keeping inventory on hand to meet the 
needs of medical staﬀ along with administrative oﬃces. The purpose of using the M-Systems 
software is to maintain a solid awareness of the facility’s needs. The software is especially useful 
in tracking supply usage and preventing waste due to ordering surplus items and having to 
dispose of them when they expire. M-System software is not only essential for Inventory 
Management but is instrumental in providing accurate information when reporting to 
Headquarters. 
 
Morris System is mandated by IHS as the only vendor for this inventory management service.  
HHS has determined that Morris Systems is the only known source for this requirement. 
 
This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, if any interested party, 
especially an Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE). and Indian Small Business Economic (ISBEE), or 
small business, believes it can meet the Government’s needs, it may submit a capability 
statement, proposal, or quote for the Government to consider. The response and any other 
information furnished must be in writing and must contain suﬃcient details to allow NCI to 
determine if the party can perform the requirement.

no later than 12:00 P .M. EST on Friday, June 06, 2026 (06/05/26).

BRAND NAME JUSTIFICATION 
FOR SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITIONS 
From: 104 
To: Simplified Acquisition Section 
Subject: Brand name Justification for IBM Rational DOORS software 
 
 
1. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIRED SUPPLIES/SERVICES, ESTIMATED 
VALUE, AND DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS 
 
IBM Rational Dynamic Object-Oriented Requirements System (DOORS) is a 
software application that provides capabilities to define and manage 
requirements in systems and software engineering projects for manufactured 
products and systems-oriented industries 
 
The software is used within NSWC Philadelphia’s Modeling & Simulation (M&S) 
Labs by various research, development, testing & evaluation (RDT&E) 
engineering groups as a requirements management tool for project testing & 
production; it provides traceability throughout the engineering lifecycle and 
allows users to manage their project’s system requirements. 
 
The subject purchase request provides for the purchase of IBM Rational DOORS 
software maintenance renewal licenses and related technical documentation at 
an estimated dollar value of           . 
 
2. SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION FOR BRAND NAME BASED ON 
CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR NATURE OF THE 
ACQUISITION 
 
This specific brand name renewal request is for a software application that 
currently supports an active NSWC Philadelphia operational activity. The 
application continues to meet all of the government’s current firm, salient 
technical requirements while performing at industry accepted baselines and 
expectations; renewal-in-place guarantees an uninterrupted workflow and 
continuity of fleet operations that no alternative solution can provide 
Additionally, the Navy’s Continuity of Operations Policy (COOP) requires the 
integration of continuity-related functions and activities into operations and 
exercises to ensure that all mission essential functions (MEFs) and activities are 
supported in real-time by assets and resources necessary for the development 
and maintenance of fleet operational readiness. Renewal in-place of the software 
application represents the only continuity-related function in the acquisition 
pathway that guarantees no interruption to ongoing MEFs and naval engineering 
activities. 

Alternatively, any new solicitation/comparable market solution would introduce 
a break in operational service necessary to identify, evaluate, test, configure and 
integrate the new software into existing projects and programs. A learning 
initiative would also have to be undertaken to train the application users and any 
collaborating integrated product team (IPT) members in the use and proficiency 
of the newly adopted software, further introducing latency and delays to all 
current programs and projects the application supports. 
 
Consequently, to maintain this uninterrupted operational support to ongoing 
MEFs, fleet collaborations and naval RDT&E activities, it is requested that the 
license and service support for the current brand application be renewed in-place 
for a 12-month period. 
3. MARKET SURVEY 
 
Results of market research undertaken to identify similar or identical 
requirements through source lists of like items obtained through online 
resources, peer review and research has failed to identify any comparable 
alternative that matches or exceeds the government’s firm, salient requirements 
and at better cost without substantial duplication at cost and technical effort to 
the government that is not expected to be recovered through competition 
4. ADDITIONAL FACTS 
 
 
5. APPROVALS: 
 
I certify that the statements and information provided above, are complete and

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 
 
1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs 
Office of Procurement, Acquisition, and Logistics 
       Technology Acquisition Center 
       23 Christopher Way 
       Eatontown, NJ 07724 
       
2. Description of Action: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Marion, Illinois 
Medical Center has a requirement for a sole source action for a base year and four 
option periods, firm-fixed price (FFP) effort for the complete on-site full service planned 
maintenance and corrective maintenance (repair) of the Pyxis Medication and Supply 
System currently installed within the Marion, Illinois Medical Center and associated 
healthcare facilities with CareFusion, LLC., 3750 Torrey View Court, San Diego, CA 
92130. 
 
3. Description of Supplies or Services: The proposed action is for maintenance, repair, 
and software licenses associated with the existing Pyxis Medication and Supply Units 
which will ensure continuous reliability of the Becton Dickinson Company (BD) 
CareFusion Pyxis systems and ancillary equipment. The Contractor shall supply all 
labor, materials, equipment, tools, supervision, and all incidentals required to complete 
on-site full service planned maintenance and corrective maintenance (repair) of the 
Pyxis Medication and Supply System being utilized within the VA facilities listed in this 
PWS, in accordance with Manufacturer’s recommendations, Joint Commission 
standards, design specifications, and the specifications, terms, and conditions of this 
contract. The currently installed BD CareFusion Pyxis dispensing system provides 
comprehensive medication and supply management. These systems help clinicians 
safely and efficiently access and dispense medications and medical supplies from 
secure cabinets located near the point of care. The Pyxis dispensing system 
streamlines pharmacy workflow, improves financial performance, facilitates regulatory 
compliance, and enhances medication, safety, and patient care. It also allows hospital 
pharmacies to safely and efficiently compound medications for infusion. The expected  
useful life of the equipment/hardware and associated maintenance is estimated to be 5 
years.The period of performance shall include a Base Period of 12 months and four 12-
month option periods. The total estimated price of the proposed action is . 
                         
4. Statutory Authority: The statutory authority permitting an exception to fair opportunity 
is 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition 
Regulation (FAR) Overhaul in 6.103-1b, entitled “One Responsible Source” as Agencies 
may contract without providing for full and open competition when the supplies or 
services required by the agency are available from only one responsible source and no 
other type of supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. 
 
5. Rationale Supporting Use of Authority Cited Above: Based on Market Research 
which is described in Section 8, CareFusion Solutions, LLC is the exclusive 
manufacturer and provider of Pyxis products and services and the sole company 
capable of performing installation and maintenance. Only CareFusion and thier Field 


PYXIS Maintenance Support Services                                      VA-26-00029250 
Page 2 of 5 
Service Technician Affiliates have the capabilities and authorization necessary to 
perform installation and maintenance services for Pyxis products. Performance of 
those services by any other party voids our warranty for the serviced products. Due 
to proprietary constraints, only BD CareFusion and its Field Service Technician 
Affiliates have the capabilities and authorization necessary to perform installation 
and maintenance services for the VA owned Pyxis products. Additionally, Carefusion 
also maintains an active Business Associates Agreement to further enhance their 
capability of providing remote support. Additionally, no other system will work in 
uniting all devices associated with this system. Removing or pausing services 
provided by the BD CareFusion Pyxis dispensing systems would disrupt pharmacy 
workflow, diminish financial performance, jeopardize the VA’s regulatory compliance, 
and present immediate harm to the delivery of medication, safety, and critical patient 
care. 
 
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition: Market research was conducted, details of which 
are in the market research section of this document. This effort did not yield any 
additional sources which can meet the Government’s requirements. Additionally, the 
proposed action will be synopsized on the Contracting Opportunities Page in 
accordance with FAR 5.201. Any proposals that are received shall be evaluated. 
 
7. Actions to Increase Competition: The Government will continue to conduct market 
research to ascertain if there are changes in the market place that would enable future 
actions to be competed. 
 
8. Market Research: In November/December 2025 Government technical experts 
conducted market research in support of this effort. Techniques used to conduct market 
research included acquisition history, verbal communications with subject matter 
experts such as technicians and personnel actively using the services and products 
required for this effort. Additionally, the Government technical experts searched 
SAM.gov. Lastly, market research was conducted to ascertain if any other vendor could 
provide the support required for this effort. Specifically, the Government’s technical 
experts conducted research to evaluate other automated dispensing cabinet systems, 
which included Omnicell XT Series, Capsa Healthcare (NexsysADC), and Touchpoint 
Medical (medDispense); however, these systems are not compatible with VA-owned 
Pyxis systems currently installed and cannot support or service Pyxis equipment.  
 
The Contract Specialist (CS) conducted market research on January 06, 2026, by using 
the National Aeronautics and Space Administration Solutions for Enterprise-Wide 
Procurement V Governmentwide Acquisition Contract Market Research tool by 
searching “Pyxis”, “CareFusion”, and “BD”. This resulted in one provider, CareFusion 
Solutions LLC, with 27 Contract Holder Relationships. Of the 27 Contract Holder 
Relationships, 8 were listed as approved resellers. On January 9, 2026 the CS reached 
out to CareFusion Solutions LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of BD and requested if BD 
or any BD-authorized resellers currently hold Government contracts suitable for this 
requirement. On January 12, 2026, CareFusion Solutions LLC responded that BD has 
two SDVOSB partners who are authorized distributors of Pyxis capital equipment and 
hold SEWP contracts. It was noted that these two SDVOSB’s were approved resellers 
of hardware and do not provide the required services.  

PYXIS Maintenance Support Services                                      VA-26-00029250 
Page 3 of 5 
 
 
On January 13, 2026 BD followed-up and stated the company is the exclusive 
manufacturer and provider of Pyxis products and services and the sole company 
capable of performing installation and maintenance services. Additionally, CareFusion 
Solutions LLC does not currently have any authorization or certification process in place 
for companies performing service or maintenance on Pyxis equipment. Any service or 
maintenance performed by a third-party vendor, other than CareFusion Field Service 
Technician Affiliates, would render null and void any existing warranty and be 
unsupported by CareFusion Solutions, LLC. Therefore, the vendors listed within the 
SEWP Market Research Tool do not possess the capabilities to meet the requirements 
of this effort.  
 
9. Other Facts: N/A

I hereby determine that the anticipated price to the Government for this contract action 
will be fair and reasonable based on comparison to the Independent Government Cost 
Estimate and Market Research provided by the customer. Further price analysis, to 
include an analysis of proposed level of effort and mix of labor and labor prices, will be 
conducted and subsequent negotiations held as necessary. Additionally, price discounts 
will be sought. 
Contracting Officer Certification/Approval 
I certify that this justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and 
belief.

Advocate for Competition Approval 
In my role as the procuring activity Advocate for Competition, based on the foregoing 
justification, I hereby approve the acquisition of for maintenance support services and  
repair associated with the existing Pyxis Medication and Supply Units on an other than 
full and open competition basis pursuant to the authority cited in Section 4 above, 
subject to availability of funds, and provided that the property and services herein 
described have otherwise been authorized for acquisition.

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

The Network Contracting Office (NCO-10) is seeking to identify vendors for performing the following services, replacement of Rauland Responder IV Nurse Call System with the Rauland Responder V Nurse Call System and provide software to integrate the upgraded Nurse Call System into the facilities current Vocera System at the Dayton VA Medical Center (DVAMC).

This is a Request for Information (RFI) to seek capable sources and request industry feedback ONLY. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Interested parties are asked to submit a capability statement that clearly and convincingly identifies their ability to fulfill the requirements. 

Scope:

The contractor shall provide all resources necessary to accomplish the deliverables described in this PWS except as may otherwise be specified.  All parts, labor, material, tools, and supervision required to provide service and support of the installation of the Rauland Responder V Nurse Call System in multiple areas of the Dayton VA Medical Center. During installation of new equipment, the contractor shall be responsible for the removal and proper disposal of all old Rauland Responder Nurse Call IV equipment.

Pertinent Information:

The contractor must use the Rauland Responder V Nurse Call System and provide software to integrate it into the facilities current Vocera System since that system is currently being used in other areas of the DVAMC Campus. Must be able to respond to emergency issues with nurse call system in 1 hour or less. The patient stations need to have proper pin connections for Hill-Rom beds. All trash must be properly disposed of at the end of each workday. Must work with COR on scheduling. Provide weekly updates via email to COR on progression of the project, or any foreseeable delays.   

Specific Tasks include:

Provide all required devices and hardware.

Provide annual licensing and support for equipment and for 1yr following the commission of the Nurse Call System.

Provide maintenance and support during installation and for 1yr following the commission of the Nurse Call System.

Provide programming and testing during installation and for 1yr following the commission of the Nurse Call System.

Provide connection and any software and licenses needed to connect to existing Nurse Call Responder V servers.

Provide software and licensing to add a Reports Server to existing Responder V servers. (VA will provide virtual machine)

Provide software, any licensing and professional services needed to integrate with the facilities Vocera System. 

Provide technical support training to minimum of 10 DVAMC staff members on new Rauland Responder V system and provide end-user training to clinical staff.

Provide all professional services needed to accomplish the above.

Real-Time Location System (RTLS) Remediation at 
Michael E. DeBakey VA Medical Center 
Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
I. GENERAL REQUIREMENT 
The Michael E. DeBakey VA Medical Center requires full restoration, installation, and configuration of 
all missing or damaged information technology infrastructure devices necessary to support clinical 
operations, administrative functions, security systems, and enterprise network services across the main 
hospital campus. This project shall ensure that all infrastructure components including network switches, 
wireless access points, routers, firewalls, structured cabling, optics, rack equipment, and power protection 
systems are replaced, installed, configured, and validated in accordance with OEM specifications and VA 
technical standards. The work shall deliver fully operational, standards-compliant infrastructure capable 
of supporting required availability, performance, security, and interoperability across all dependent 
hospital systems. 
II. DESCRIPTION OF WORK 
 
The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, tools, cabling, transportation, software, 
professional services, technical support, testing instruments, on-site and remote support, and travel 
necessary to install, configure, validate, and place into operation all infrastructure devices required to 
restore full functionality. The Contractor shall comply with all OEM hardware/software requirements and 
maintain authorized access to OEM tools, documentation, and configuration utilities. Completion shall be 
defined as full replacement, configuration, validation, documentation, and acceptance of all restored 
infrastructure systems. 
A. Existing Infrastructure 
The Michael E. DeBakey VA Medical Center operates an enterprise-class IT environment consisting of: 
• Network switches (core, distribution, and access) 
• Wireless access points and controllers 
• Firewalls and security appliances 
• Routers, gateways, and uplink equipment 
• Copper and fiber cabling infrastructure 
• Patch panels, jacks, termination blocks, and structured cabling pathways 
• SFP/SFP+/QSFP optical modules 
• Racks, rack components, UPS units, and PDUs 
• Server appliances supporting management, telemetry, and syslog 
The Contractor shall evaluate the current infrastructure condition; identify all missing, damaged, 
nonfunctional, or technically noncompliant devices; and implement the following actions: 
1. Hardware Replacement and Restoration 

 
2 
a. Replace missing or damaged switches, access points, routers, firewalls, UPS devices, 
patch panels, and cabling components. 
b. Install replacement devices following OEM spacing, airflow, grounding, and mounting 
requirements. 
c. Verify compatibility with existing topology, addressing, VLANs, routes, security 
policies, wireless architecture, and VA enterprise standards. 
d. Install optics, patch cords, and cabling necessary for full restoration of network paths. 
e. Restore all network closets (IDFs/MDFs) to operational conditions, including cable 
management and labeling. 
2. Configuration and Software Alignment: 
a. Load OEM-supported operating systems and firmware. 
b. Apply VA-provided configurations or templates, including VLANs, routing, wireless 
profiles, and security baselines. 
c. Integrate devices into monitoring tools (NMS, syslog, SIEM). 
d. Confirm successful authentication via RADIUS, Active Directory, or certificate-based 
access where applicable. 
e. Validate wireless provisioning, including SSID broadcast, PoE allocation, and signal 
performance. 
3. Structured Cabling Restoration 
a. Identify damaged cables, improperly terminated connections, and mislabeled ports. 
b. Replace damaged copper or fiber cabling with new Cat6 or OM4 cabling meeting TIA 
standards. 
c. Re-terminate, test, and label cable connections to TIA-568 and TIA-606-B standards. 
d. Produce cable certification reports for all replaced cable runs. 
 
4. Testing and Acceptance 
 
The Contractor shall develop a Validation Test Plan (VTP) covering connectivity, throughput, 
wireless coverage, security policy application, redundancy paths, and device telemetry. The 
following minimum acceptance criteria apply: 
 
a. Network device operational status: 100% of replaced hardware fully online and 
reachable 
b. Port-level functionality: ≥ 98% pass rate for data, PoE, and negotiated link speeds 
c. Wireless testing: ≥ 95% coverage success in validated areas 
d. Cable compliance: 100% pass rate on certification tests for replaced cable 
e. Device uptime baseline: ≥ 99% infrastructure availability after 30-day stabilization 
f. Documentation accuracy: 100% of devices labeled, mapped, and included in as-built 
package 
 
The contractor shall submit full-as-built documentation, port maps, test results, rack elevations, 
network diagrams, and configuration backups. 
 

 
3 
B. Areas of Expansion 
The Contractor shall expand infrastructure capacity where required to ensure operational reliability. 
At minimum: 
• Improve coverage and device availability at nurse stations, reception/waiting rooms, inpatient 
units, and additional patient-facing areas identified by the COR. 
• Restore and reinforce infrastructure serving high-dependency departments, including the Inpatient 
Mental Health (6th floor) and Emergency Department (1st floor). 
• Confirm power redundancy, PoE capacity, and wireless saturation in all restored areas. 
• Perform site-specific validation and provide location-specific as-builts for each closet and 
department. 
C. Integrations 
Where required, the Contractor shall integrate all restored infrastructure with supported VA systems 
including: 
• Active Directory 
• Network Access Control (NAC) 
• Wireless controllers 
• Firewall rule sets and logging systems 
• SIEM/SOC monitoring platforms 
• DHCP, DNS, NTP, and certificate services 
The Contractor shall: 
• Provide an integration plan detailing technical steps and dependencies 
• Validate policy enforcement, authentication, and event logging 
• Confirm failover behavior and redundancy 
III. DESIGN/LINE ITEMS 
As a Performance Work Statement, the Contractor is responsible for producing final engineered designs 
ensuring fully functional infrastructure at all designated locations. 
The following line items are required to execute this scope: 
Preliminary line items expected to complete this scope (final quantities to be confirmed via the 
Contractor’s detailed design and site surveys). Any changes post-award require coordination among the 
Contractor, Contracting Officer (CO), and the contractor Officer’s Representative (COR).

IV. CONFORMANCE STANDARDS: 
A. The contractor shall ensure equipment and software operate in full compliance with OEM 
specifications, including all updates/patches. 
B. Work shall conform to applicable Federal, State, and Local requirements, including but not 
limited to: AAMI, The Joint Commission (JCAHO), NFPA-99, CDRH, AHA, IEEE, UL, OSHA, 
CAP, and VAMC SOPs.  
C. System performance shall comply with the latest editions of NFPA-99, UL, OSHA, VA, and 
CDRH requirements. 
V. HOURS OF COVERAGE 
A. Standards hours of performance are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM CST, excluding federal 
holidays. 
B. The Government observes Federal holidays: New Year’s Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, 
Presidents Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, 
Veterans Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day, and any other day designated by Federal 
statute, Executive Order, or Presidential proclamation. 
 
VI. CONTRACT DISCREPANCY REPORT (CDR) AND DAMAGES 
A. The Contractor shall be liable for losses in operational capability resulting from significant system 
downtime caused by Contractor performance issues. 

 
5 
B. A CDR shall be issued for performance below Acceptable Quality Levels (AQL). The Contractor 
shall provide a corrective action plan within five (5) business days. Continued deficiencies will be 
reported to the CO. 
C. The Contractor shall be liable for any damage to Government property caused by its personnel. 
 
VII. PAYMENT 
 
Invoices shall be submitted in arrears on a monthly or quarterly basis and shall include, at minimum: 
Contract Number, Purchase Order Number, item(s) covered (including serial numbers where applicable), 
and service period. Each invoice shall be provided in triplicate. 
 
VIII. COMPETENCY OF PERSONNEL SERVICE EQUIPMENT: 
 
A. The Contractor shall maintain an established business with a staffed office and full-time personnel, 
including a primary and backup Field Service Engineer (FSE). 
B. “Fully Qualified” personnel shall be OEM-certified by Centrak and possess ≥ 2 years of RTLS 
experience (installation, calibration, preventive and corrective maintenance). 
C. All work shall be performed by OEM-authorized, fully qualified personnel. The Contractor shall 
provide credentials and proof of certification upon request. The Government reserves the right to 
reject personnel lacking proper certification or qualifications. 
D. Any subcontractor(s) must be preapproved by the COR and submitted to the CO for approval prior 
to use. 
 
IX. PRIVACY/SECURITY 
The Contractor will require access to VA systems for software upgrades and maintenance, which may 
involve exposure to PHI (e.g., screenshots, databases). All electronic storage devices (e.g., hard 
drives) shall be turned into the Information System Security Officer (ISSO) upon replacement or 
repair and shall not be removed from VA property. 
The following standard items relate to records generated in executing the contract and should be included 
in a typical Electronic Information Systems (EIS) procurement contract: 
1. Citations to pertinent laws, codes and regulations such as 44 U.S.C chapters 21, 29, 31 and 33; 
Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552); Privacy Act (5 U.S.C. 552a); 36 CFR Part 1222 and 
Part 1228. 
2. Contractor shall treat all deliverables under the contract as the property of the U.S. Government 
for which the Government Agency shall have unlimited rights to use, dispose of, or disclose such 
data contained therein as it determines to be in the public interest.  

 
6 
3. Contractor shall not create or maintain any records that are not specifically tied to or authorized by 
the contract using Government IT equipment and/or Government records.  
4. Contractor shall not retain, use, sell, or disseminate copies of any deliverable that contains 
information covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 or that which is generally protected by the 
Freedom of Information Act.  
5. Contractor shall not create or maintain any records containing any Government Agency records 
that are not specifically tied to or authorized by the contract.  
6. The Government Agency owns the rights to all data/records produced as part of this contract.  
7. The Government Agency owns the rights to all electronic information (electronic data, electronic 
information systems, electronic databases, etc.) and all supporting documentation created as part 
of this contract. Contractor must deliver sufficient technical documentation with all data 
deliverables to permit the agency to use the data.  
8. Contractor agrees to comply with Federal and Agency records management policies, including 
those policies associated with the safeguarding of records covered by the Privacy Act of 1974. 
These policies include the preservation of all records created or received regardless of format 
[paper, electronic, etc.] or mode of transmission [e-mail, fax, etc.] or state of completion [draft, 
final, etc.].  
9. No disposition of documents will be allowed without the prior written consent of the Contracting 
Officer. The Agency and its contractors are responsible for preventing the alienation or 
unauthorized destruction of records, including all forms of mutilation. Willful and unlawful 
destruction, damage or alienation of Federal records is subject to the fines and penalties imposed 
by 18 U.S.C. 2701. Records may not be removed from the legal custody of the Agency or 
destroyed without regard to the provisions of the agency records schedules.  
10. Contractor is required to obtain the Contracting Officer's approval prior to engaging in any 
contractual relationship (sub-contractor) in support of this contract requiring the disclosure of 
information, documentary material and/or records generated under, or relating to, this contract. 
The Contractor (and any sub-contractor) is required to abide by Government and Agency guidance 
for protecting sensitive and proprietary information.  
 
Source: The National Archives Records Administration (NARA). http://www.archives.gov/records-
mgmt/handbook/records-mgmt-language.html 
(End of PWS)
