Table of Contents

Enterprise Microfiche Digitization & Modernization Project

1.0 PROJECT OVERVIEW & OBJECTIVE

The Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) requires comprehensive, enterprise-scale digitization services to convert approximately 5.88 million physical microfiche sheets and films into a dual-format, legally admissible digital records repository.

To satisfy the stringent evidentiary requirements of the DoD Financial Management Regulation (FMR), support FIAR audit readiness, and ensure the digital records meet the legal threshold for source record destruction under NARA 36 CFR § 1236.32 and GRS 4.5, DFAS mandates the FADGI 3-Star standard for the preservation master images.

By meeting these standards, this effort will enable DFAS to achieve two primary objectives:

NARA-Authorized Destruction: Secure the legal authority to permanently destroy the physical source media, eliminating associated facility and maintenance costs.

Operational Modernization: Dramatically improve mission efficiency by generating fully text-searchable PDF Access Copies, providing the DFAS workforce with instantaneous, universal retrieval capabilities.

2.0 General Requirements

2.1 Personnel

The Contractor shall ensure all personnel performing work on this effort are U.S. citizens and that all services are sourced from within the United States. See Specific Requirements in Section 3.0 Security Requirements.

2.2 Recognized Holidays

With the exception of customer support calls, contractors are not expected to perform on any federally recognized holidays, to include but not limited to: 

New Year’s Day Labor Day 

Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday Columbus Day 

President’s Day Veteran’s Day 

Memorial Day Thanksgiving Day 

Juneteenth Christmas Day 

Independence Day 

If the holiday occurs on a Saturday the holiday will be observed on Friday. If the holiday occurs on Sunday the holiday will be observed on Monday. 

2.3 Hours of Operation

The contractor shall conduct business between the hours of 0600 - 1800 hours Monday through Friday Eastern Time except federal holidays. Any labor to be performed outside of normal business hours or during federal holidays must be approved in advance by the DFAS System Manager (SM). Overtime rates are not authorized. When hiring personnel, the Contractor shall keep in mind that the stability and continuity of the workforce are essential. The contractor shall, at all times, maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this PWS. 

2.4 Place of Performance

The primary place of performance will be by remote working or teleworking at the Contractor’s location. 

2.5 Type of Contract

The contract will be a Firm, Fixed Price contract.

2.6 Travel 

The Government does not anticipate any travel. 

2.7 Relocation

Relocation costs and travel costs incident to relocation are not allowable and will not be reimbursed hereunder. 

2.8 Shared Data

The DFAS SM will determine what CUI contractor personnel are given access to. CUI may not be disclosed to contractor personnel unless required for contract performance. Contractor personnel shall safeguard CUI in accordance with DoDI 5200.48 and DFAS 5200.1-I. The sponsoring DFAS activity will provide storage capability for all CUI required for contract performance. 

2.9 Identification of Contractor Employees

All contractor personnel attending meetings, answering Government telephones, and working in other situations where their contractor status is not obvious to third parties shall identify themselves as contractors to avoid creating an impression, they are Government officials. Contractor personnel shall ensure that all documents or reports produced by contractors are suitably marked as contractor products or that contractor participation is appropriately disclosed. The Common Access Card (CAC) used for building entrance, computer access, and other situations will identify the individual as a contractor.

3.0 Security Requirements.

3.1 General Requirements.  

Contractor personnel must meet the following conditions of employment.

Must be a U.S Citizen or National.

Registered for Selective Service (males born after 12-31-1959).  A Status Information Letter is required for any male born after 12-31-1959 that is not registered with Selective Service.

This is a national security position which requires a favorable fitness review and background investigation as a condition of employment.  Failure to maintain security eligibility may result in termination.

3.2 Personnel Security Investigation (PSI) Requirements.  

Contractor personnel working on this contract will require a favorably adjudicated Tier 3, or equivalent Noncritical-Sensitive (formerly IT-II) or higher-level Investigation granting National Security eligibility.  Contractor personnel must also have current enrollment (within 5 years) in the Continuous Vetting program, in accordance with Trusted Workforce 2.0 standards.  No access to classified information is required.  In accordance with standard DFAS Personnel Security policy, ALL incoming contractors must submit a new set of fingerprints (taken within the last 30 days) *.  

Contractor personnel must apply for a fingerprint appointment immediately (the next business day) upon award date.  

Contractor personnel shall submit the Contractor Request for Investigation (CRI) (DFAS Form 9035) immediately (the next business day after providing fingerprints) to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR).  The information needed in the Declaration for Federal Employment (OF-306) shall also be submitted to the COR by contractor personnel.  

The COR will submit the OF-306, DFAS Form 9035, and proof of fingerprints to DFAS Personnel Security all at once.  Under no circumstances should this documentation be submitted less than fifteen (15) calendar days prior to the intended performance start date.  DFAS Personnel Security will review all submitted documentation to validate whether contractor personnel meet personnel security requirements to perform work on the contract or if a new background investigation is required.

Contractors obtaining favorable security evaluations and DoD CACs for required contractor employees performing on this contract are a prerequisite for contractor performance and invoicing.  Also, the failure of a contractor to provide employees who can obtain a favorable security adjudication and a DoD CAC in a timely manner may be considered negatively when assessing contractor performance, termination, or other.

*New fingerprints are not required if any of the following apply:

The person has been fingerprinted for the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) within the past 30 days.

The person is currently undergoing a background investigation, or reinvestigation, by DCSA or any other Federal agency.

The person has a background investigation currently being adjudicated by the DCSA Adjudication and Vetting Services (DCSA AVS) or another AVS.

The person has been favorably adjudicated within the past 30 days by the DCSA AVS or a AVS from any other Federal agency: or

The person comes directly from another DoD agency, with no break in service.  This includes any of the military branches as well as the U.S. Coast Guard; however, service members in an inactive reserve status are not included.

The DFAS Personnel Security Office otherwise determines that no new fingerprints are required.

3.3 Regulatory Requirements.  

Contractor personnel shall follow the security and training requirements in DoDM 5220.23, “Industrial Security Procedures For Government Activities,” DoDM 5200.01, Volumes 1-3, “DoD Information Security Program,” DoDI, 5200.48, “Controlled Unclassified Information,” DFAS 2000.1-I, “Force Protection Mission,” DFAS 5200.1-I, “Information Security Program,” DFAS 5200.8-I, “Physical Security Program,” and DFAS 5200.10-I, “Counter Insider Threat Program.”  Contractor personnel shall follow all host security requirements in accordance with Part 117 of Title 32, Code of Federal Regulations; paragraph 117.16.  Ensure that all contracting officers include applicable clauses in all contracts that require work to be performed for a DFAS location.  The contractor shall immediately report any occurrences of violation of stated regulations to the DFAS Manager of the area to which they are assigned, Contracting Officer (CO), COR, Director, Force Protection, and the DFAS Personnel Security Office.

DoD Issuances can be located at the following web link:

https://www.esd.whs.mil/dd/dod-issuances/

DFAS Instructions can be located at the following agency portal web link:

Official Forms and Pubs - All Documents

3.4 DFAS Personnel Security Incident Reporting Requirements, the National Industrial Security Program and Due Process as it Relates to DFAS Contractor Personnel.  

The National Industrial Security Program (NISP) is a partnership between the federal government and private industry to safeguard classified information and CUI.

Executive Order 12829, as amended, "National Industrial Security Program," further amended by Section 6 of E.O. 13691, was established to achieve cost savings and to ensure that industry safeguards the classified information with which it is entrusted while performing work on contracts, programs, bids, or research and development efforts while working for the United States Government.

It is important to note that personnel employed as contractors for DFAS are not covered under the National Industrial Security Program (NISP) and are exempt from the provisions of 5 C.F.R. 731.  This means that DFAS contractor personnel involved in an incident that potentially violates one or more of the National Security Adjudicative Guidelines found at https://www.dni.gov/files/NCSC/documents/Regulations/SEAD-4-Adjudicative-Guidelines-U.pdf , are not entitled to Due Process rights normally afforded to federal civilian employees and those personnel covered under NISP; more specifically, DFAS Personnel Security may suspend or revoke contractor personnel access to DFAS IT systems, sensitive information and/or DFAS facilities.  

3.5 Incident Reporting Requirements.

In all cases, whenever a DFAS contractor displays conduct, or is involved in any incident, which is in violation of any of the thirteen National Security Adjudicative Guidelines*, the contractor must immediately report the incident to the contractor company Security Office/Facility Security Officer, the DFAS Manager of the area to which they are assigned, the CO, the COR, the Director, Force Protection, and the DFAS Personnel Security Office.  Reporting to DFAS Personnel Security may be made by phone to (317) 212-7888, by email to dfas.indianapolis-in.zh.mbx.dfas-inhrsecurity@mail.mil, or, in the case of personnel physically located at DFAS Indianapolis Center, in person to the DFAS Personnel Security Office located on the third floor center hallway at Column 320T.

All incidents will be investigated by DFAS Personnel Security and, depending on the date of the subject’s most recent investigation, may need to have an updated background investigation initiated.  Those that do not require a new investigation will have all relevant information regarding the incident forwarded to the DCSA AVS for review and re-adjudication.  

*The thirteen National Security Adjudicative Guidelines are:

1.	GUIDELINE A: Allegiance to the United States

2.	GUIDELINE B: Foreign Influence

3.	GUIDELINE C: Foreign Preference

4.	GUIDELINE D: Sexual Behavior

5.	GUIDELINE E: Personal Conduct

6.	GUIDELINE F: Financial Considerations

7.	GUIDELINE G: Alcohol Consumption

8.	GUIDELINE H: Drug Involvement and Substance Misuse

9.	GUIDELINE I:  Psychological Conditions

10.	GUIDELINE J:  Criminal Conduct

11.	GUIDELINE K: Handling Protected Information

12.	GUIDELINE L: Outside Activities

13.	GUIDELINE M: Use of Information Technology

Some Examples of Incidents That Require Reporting to DFAS Personnel Security:

An arrest for any criminal offense, not including minor traffic violations, by any law enforcement agency.  This DOES include the traffic offenses of Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol or Drugs, and Reckless Driving.

Violation of any court order.

Civil judgements.

Delinquencies on any debt for 180 days or longer.

Federal, State or Local tax issues or delinquencies.

Delinquencies on any Federal debt (including Federal Student Loans and Federally backed home mortgage loans).

Child Support delinquencies.

Filing for Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 bankruptcy in any Federal Bankruptcy Court.

Foreign Travel.

Marriage or Cohabitation with a Foreign National (person from a foreign country). 

Having a close personal friendship with a Foreign National with regularly occurring contact.

Ownership of property or financial accounts in a foreign country; and

Being approached by a person know to be, or suspected to be, working as an agent of a foreign government or terrorist organization, or any other person, who seeks any information about DFAS, the Department of Defense, or the U.S. Government, especially if the person offers money or something of value to the contractor employee.

It should be noted that a person’s delinquency on Federal debt of any kind may not obtain or maintain favorable personnel security adjudication or be considered for a contractor position with DFAS unless they can provide documentary proof that a payment plan has been established with the Government agency to whom the debt is owed, and that regularly recurring payments are being made.  Contractor personnel who cannot obtain and maintain a favorable personnel security adjudication may not have access to government data, facilities, and/or equipment required under the contract.

NOTE: This list does not cover every potential incident or offense; any incident in which a contractor is involved, and a question exists as to whether it should be reported, should report the incident to DFAS Personnel Security, who will then determine if further action is warranted. Failure to report an incident is, in and of itself, an incident involving personal conduct, and may, in some cases, be more serious than the original incident.

3.6 Foreign Travel by DFAS Contractor Personnel 

Official and Unofficial (Personal) Travel: Official U.S. Government Business: persons employed as contractor employees with DFAS,  to include those with Noncritical Sensitive (formerly IT-II) access, Critical Sensitive (formerly IT-I) access, access to critical program information (related to Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation), sensitive compartmented information, and/or special access program information, in accordance with DoD Directive 5240.06, are required to complete a DFAS Form 9133, Notification of Foreign Travel, not less than 30 calendar days prior to the scheduled travel.

Background:    The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Institute for Learning, Education, and Development (ILEAD) maintains a broadcast facility in St. Louis Missouri, to include live satellite video delivery. ILEAD uses EEG closed caption encoders and the EEG iCAP caption delivery service to provide real-time closed captioning for live satellite video delivery.

ILEAD previously replaced their EEG HD490 caption encoders with a total of (5) EEG HD492-O-O1G Closed Caption Pro Encoders that requires annual support.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is currently undergoing a reorganization that may result in future changes to its organizational structure, processes, responsibilities, and priorities. Such changes could affect the customers, services, or support described in this Product Description (PD). Accordingly, the Contractor shall remain adaptable and responsive to evolving VA requirements and work in close coordination with the Government to assess and implement necessary adjustments, as needed. Any resulting changes will be completed by bilateral contract modification.

The Contractor shall provide annual Encoder Pro HD492 and Encoder Pro Card OpenGear Annual Support and firmware updates on (5) EEG HD492-O-O1G See .  The EEG HD492-O-O1G Closed Caption Pro Encoders salient characteristics:

Records Management Language for Contracts

When Federal agencies acquire goods or services, they need to determine what Federal records management requirements should be included in the contract. Federal contractors often create, send, or receive Federal records. Federal contracts should provide clear legal obligations describing how the contract employees must handle Federal records. 

Agency records officers, procurement counsel, and acquisitions officers must discuss how to integrate records management obligations into their existing procurement processes. NARA has developed the following language to be included as an agency-specific term and condition in Federal contracts for a variety of services and products. The majority of contracts should include language on records management obligations, but each contract should be evaluated individually. For example, the data-rights paragraph (Paragraph 10 below) may not be appropriate for all contracts. Instead, agencies may be better served by one of the established data-rights clauses in the Federal Acquisition Regulations. 

This language should not replace specific records management requirements included within Federal information system contracts. 

RECORDS MANAGEMENT OBLIGATIONS

A.  Applicability

This clause applies to all Contractors whose employees create, work with, or otherwise handle Federal records, as defined in Section B, regardless of the medium in which the record exists.  

B.  Definitions

“Federal record” as defined in 44 U.S.C. § 3301, includes all recorded information, regardless of form or characteristics, made or received by a Federal agency under Federal law or in connection with the transaction of public business and preserved or appropriate for preservation by that agency or its legitimate successor as evidence of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations, or other activities of the United States Government or because of the informational value of data in them.  

The term Federal record:

includes Institute for Learning, Education and Development (ILEAD) records. 

does not include personal materials.

applies to records created, received, or maintained by Contractors pursuant to their ILEAD contract.

may include deliverables and documentation associated with deliverables.

C.  Requirements

Contractor shall comply with all applicable records management laws and regulations, as well as National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) records policies, including but not limited to the Federal Records Act (44 U.S.C. chs. 21, 29, 31, 33), NARA regulations at 36 CFR Chapter XII Subchapter B, and those policies associated with the safeguarding of records covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a). These policies include the preservation of all records, regardless of form or characteristics, mode of transmission, or state of completion. 

In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, all data created for Government use and delivered to, or falling under the legal control of, the Government are Federal records subject to the provisions of 44 U.S.C. chapters 21, 29, 31, and 33, the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552), as amended, and the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a), as amended and must be managed and scheduled for disposition only as permitted by statute or regulation. 

In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, Contractor shall maintain all records created for Government use or created in the course of performing the contract and/or delivered to, or under the legal control of the Government and must be managed in accordance with Federal law. Electronic records and associated metadata must be accompanied by sufficient technical documentation to permit understanding and use of the records and data. 

ILEAD and its contractors are responsible for preventing the alienation or unauthorized destruction of records, including all forms of mutilation. Records may not be removed from the legal custody of ILEAD or destroyed except for in accordance with the provisions of the agency records schedules and with the written concurrence of the Head of the Contracting Activity. Willful and unlawful destruction, damage or alienation of Federal records is subject to the fines and penalties imposed by 18 U.S.C. 2701. In the event of  any unlawful or accidental removal, defacing, alteration, or destruction of records, Contractor must report to ILEAD. The agency must report promptly to NARA in accordance with 36 CFR 1230.

The Contractor shall immediately notify the appropriate Contracting Officer upon discovery of any inadvertent or unauthorized disclosures of information, data, documentary materials, records or equipment. Disclosure of non-public information is limited to authorized personnel with a need-to-know as described in the [contract vehicle]. The Contractor shall ensure that the appropriate personnel, administrative, technical, and physical safeguards are established to ensure the security and confidentiality of this information, data, documentary material, records and/or equipment is properly protected. The Contractor shall not remove material from Government facilities or systems, or facilities or systems operated or maintained on the Government’s behalf, without the express written permission of the Head of the Contracting Activity. When information, data, documentary material, records and/or equipment is no longer required, it shall be returned to ILEAD control or the Contractor must hold it until otherwise directed. Items returned to the Government shall be hand carried, mailed, emailed, or securely electronically transmitted to the Contracting Officer or address prescribed in the [contract vehicle]. Destruction of records is EXPRESSLY PROHIBITED unless in accordance with Paragraph (4).

The Contractor is required to obtain the Contracting Officer's approval prior to engaging in any contractual relationship (sub-contractor) in support of this contract requiring the disclosure of information, documentary material and/or records generated under, or relating to, contracts. The Contractor (and any sub-contractor) is required to abide by Government and ILEAD guidance for protecting sensitive, proprietary information, classified, and controlled unclassified information.

The Contractor shall only use Government IT equipment for purposes specifically tied to or authorized by the contract and in accordance with ILEAD policy. 

The Contractor shall not create or maintain any records containing any non-public ILEAD information that are not specifically tied to or authorized by the contract. 

The Contractor shall not retain, use, sell, or disseminate copies of any deliverable that contains information covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 or that which is generally protected from public disclosure by an exemption to the Freedom of Information Act. 

The ILEAD owns the rights to all data and records produced as part of this contract. All deliverables under the contract are the property of the U.S. Government for which ILEAD shall have unlimited rights to use, dispose of, or disclose such data contained therein as it determines to be in the public interest. Any Contractor rights in the data or deliverables must be identified as required by FAR 52.227-11 through FAR 52.227-20.

Training.  All Contractor employees assigned to this contract who create, work with, or otherwise handle records are required to take ILEAD-provided records management training. The Contractor is responsible for confirming training has been completed according to agency policies, including initial training and any annual or refresher training. 

[Note: To the extent an agency requires contractors to complete records management training, the agency must provide the training to the contractor.] 

D.  Flowdown of requirements to subcontractors

The Contractor shall incorporate the substance of this clause, its terms and requirements including this paragraph, in all subcontracts under this [contract vehicle], and require written subcontractor acknowledgment of same. 

Violation by a subcontractor of any provision set forth in this clause will be attributed to the Contractor.

Statement of Work 
Introduction 
Understanding the eƯects of land use and land cover (LULC) change and ecosystem 
disturbances on wildﬁre vulnerability and fuel loading is a critical requirement for national 
safety and resource management. Modeling how changes in vegetation and land 
management inﬂuence ﬁre behavior is a priority goal identiﬁed for the USGS Ecosystems 
Mission Area. The USGS has previously developed methodologies to quantify past and 
current LULC change and project future scenarios, linking these data with ecological 
models to estimate how "fuels"—represented by biomass and carbon stocks—accumulate 
and interact with natural disturbances over space and time. 
While initial assessments provided a foundation for understanding landscape change, 
signiﬁcant technical gaps remain regarding the integrated linkage between LULC dynamics 
and wildﬁre risk. Speciﬁcally, there is a need for an integrated, easy-to-use, open-source 
model that emphasizes the spatial and temporal variability of fuel loads and the resulting 
ﬁre consequences. Through a collaboration between a contractor and USGS, a proof-of-
concept model was developed: the Land Use and Carbon Scenario Simulator (LUCAS). 
Built upon the SyncroSim/ST-Sim state-and-transition simulation modeling framework, 
this tool was designed to produce reliable estimates of changes in LULC and the 
associated biomass (carbon) stocks that serve as primary ﬁre fuels. 
The next phase of this eƯort involves reﬁning the model to better simulate ﬁre regimes, fuel 
transitions, and the impact of various land-management strategies on ﬁre risk. This 
includes structural improvements to how the model treats biomass accumulation and 
decay, enhancements to ﬁre-spread visualization, and the ability to run high-resolution 
simulations in high-performance computing environments. 
The USGS seeks to continue the development of this model to track land-based fuels and 
ﬁre risk across the conterminous U.S. This contract supports the development of 
operational and scientiﬁc improvements to the model, focusing on its ability to project how 
natural and anthropogenic processes—including climate change, urbanization, and land 
management—alter the wildﬁre landscape. 
As speciﬁed in this contract, the Contractor will design and complete enhancements to the 
ST-Sim software as requested and approved by the USGS Point-of-Contact to support 
these wildﬁre and land-use objectives. 
Deliverables 

Page 2 of 4 
 
Anticipated deliverables are divided into two categories and will be speciﬁcally deﬁned as 
individual tasks: 
A. General Technical Support Provide technical support to the USGS in the use, 
application, and customization of the SyncroSim/ST-Sim software module. This includes: 
• Assisting in the conﬁguration and parameterization of fuel load variables and ﬁre 
transition probabilities. 
• Calculating and processing external data (e.g., remote sensing vegetation data) to 
provide input model parameters. 
• Developing post-processing analytical tools to translate model outputs into ﬁre-risk 
maps and hazard assessments. 
• Collaborating on scientiﬁc meetings, publications, and reports regarding LULC-
driven ﬁre dynamics. 
B. Software Enhancements Provide software enhancements to the SyncroSim/ST-Sim 
application to support ongoing program requirements. This includes: 
• Adding new features to simulate complex ﬁre-regime interactions and fuel 
treatment eƯectiveness. 
• Modifying underlying code to improve the scaling of large-area wildﬁre simulations. 
• Updating documentation and training materials to reﬂect new wildﬁre-centric 
modeling capabilities. 
• Ensuring ongoing compatibility of the software with current USGS data standards 
and high-performance computing requirements.

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE  
842674705   
 
The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) End-to-End Engineering and Analysis 
Division (OE2) is seeking sources to procure cloud computing credits from authorized resellers 
for various Cloud Service Providers (CSPs). 
 
CONTRACTING OFFICE ADDRESS:  
Defense Information Systems Agency 
DITCO-Scott PS8413 
2300 East Drive, Building 3600 
Scott Air Force Base, IL 62225  
 
1. INTRODUCTION: 
 
This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of 
small businesses and large businesses (including the following subsets: Small Disadvantaged 
Businesses, Certified 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses, HUBZone Small 
Businesses and Woman-Owned Small Businesses) to provide the required products and/or 
services.  
 
DISA OE2 requires procurement of cloud computing credits from CSPs: Amazon Web Services 
(AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI).   
The usage of cloud credits by the organization is highly variable and unpredictable.  
 
The anticipated Period of Performance is one year from the date of the award, along with 4 
twelve-month Option Years.   
 
The anticipated Place of Performance is at the contractor’s location. 
 
2. DISCLAIMER:  
  
THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS 
IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL.  IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION 
AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT.  
RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER 
NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS NOTICE.  NO 
FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS 
NOTICE.  ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS IS STRICTLY 
VOLUNTARY. 
 
3. CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND: This requirement is a new 
requirement.  However, portions of this requirement are currently being executed under the 
following and the remainder of the requirement is new and not previously supported. 
 
Contract Number: NNG15SD74B/HC108421F0232 

 
Page 2 of 3 Pages 
Contract Vehicle: NASA SEWP  
Incumbent and their size: Software Information and Resource Corp.  
Small Business Method of previous acquisition: Small Business Set Aside 
Period of performance: 14 SEP 2021 – 13 SEP 2026 
 
4. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES:  
 
1. Describe your company’s experience  providing cloud credits from AWS and Microsoft 
Azure and ideally from  GCP, and OCI.   
2. Describe your company’s ability to monitor CSP cloud credits and provide detailed 
oversight into their usage. 
3. Describe your company’s ability to provide a Service Level Agreement (SLA) that 
includes the following minimums: 
• 4 hour response time for support requests during business hours 
• 99.9% uptime for provisioning and management services 
• Escalation process for unresolved issues 
 
5. SOURCES SOUGHT:   
The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) for this requirement is 
541519 (https://www.census.gov/naics/), with the corresponding size standard of 150 employees.  
(https://www.sba.gov/document/support--table-size-standards).   
In order to make a determination for a small business set-aside, two or more qualified and 
capable small businesses must submit responses that demonstrate their qualifications.  
Responses must demonstrate the company’s ability to perform in accordance with FAR 
clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting. 
To assist DISA in determining the level of participation by small business in any subsequent 
procurement that may result from this Sources Sought Notice, provide information regarding any 
plans to use joint ventures (JVs) or partnering.  Please outline the company's areas of expertise 
and those of any proposed JV/partner who combined can meet the specific requirements 
contained in this notice. 
 
6. SUBMISSION DETAILS: 
 
Responses should include: 
 
1) Business name and address;  
2) Name of company representative and their business title;  
3) Small Business Socio-economic status (if small);  
4) UEI and CAGE Code; 
5) Prime contract vehicles; to include ENCORE III, SETI, NIH CIO-SP4, NASA SEWP V, 
General Service Administration (GSA): OASIS, ALLIANT II, VETS II, STARS III, 
MAS (including applicable SIN(s), groups or pools), or any other Government Wide 
Agency Contract vehicles that allows for decentralized ordering.  (This information is for 

 
Page 3 of 3 Pages 
market research only and businesses with a valid cage that lack prime contract vehicles 
are still encouraged to respond to this notice.)  
 
Businesses who wish to respond must send a response via email NLT 4:00 PM Eastern Daylight 
Time (EDT) on June 15, 2026 to nathan.l.sterling3.civ@mail.mil and 
adam.m.venhaus.civ@mail.mil.  Interested businesses should submit a brief capabilities 
statement package addressing the specific questions above (no more than five pages) 
demonstrating the ability to perform the services listed under Required Capabilities.       
 
Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, must be clearly marked on all materials.  All 
information received that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly.  All submissions 
become Government property and will not be returned.  All government and contractor personnel 
reviewing submitted responses will have signed non-disclosure agreements and understand their 
responsibility for proper use and protection from unauthorized disclosure of proprietary 
information as pursuant to 41 USC 423.  The Government shall not be held liable for any 
damages incurred if proprietary information is not properly identified. 
 
For information on DISA’s requirements, you can find current information on our home page: 
www.disa.mil – that includes current forecast and the current acquisition strategies. If there is 
no information regarding the requirement you may be inquiring about, then there is no 
additional publicly available information. Please continue to review www.disa.mil.

address: shannon.e.price3.civ@us.navy.mil. A determination by the Government not to open the 
requirement to competition is solely within the discretion of the Government. The anticipated 
award date is 12 June 2026.

Amendment 0001 of this solicitation is to 
provide responses to questions received by the 
inquiry deadline, and to extend the submission 
deadline to 6/8/2026 at 11am EST. Vendors must

Q&A
1305M226Q0125
1. What is the Esri end user customer or account number?
a. There is no mention of ESRI in the PWS. 
2. The PWS identifies an "Option Task - Updating the LASER engine to the latest Eigen libraries." 
Should offerors price this option task separately from CLIN 0001, or should it be included in the 
single firm-fixed-price quote for CLIN 0001?
a. Pricing should be within the format provided. Thus, it should be included in the 1 FFP 
CLIN.
3. The PWS includes Task 1, Task 2, Task 3, and the option task. Does NOAA intend to award all 
listed tasks under this RFQ within the one-year period of performance, or may NOAA 
award/exercise tasks in phases based on available funding and priority?
a.This is a FFP order with 1 CLIN. The full requirement should be captured in the 1 CLIN for 
the POP stated.
4. For Task 3, the PWS notes that contractor testing of the antenna calibration data collection 
system will be limited without access to NGS equipment. What level of contractor-side testing is 
expected before NGS conducts in-environment validation?
a.There is no expectation from NGS to be able to test the “Automated data collection” 
(deliverable 3.4, page 17) because NGS cannot provide access to its hardware. 
NGS does expect the ability to test the “Pre-process data”, where NGS will provide 
example input and output for deliverable 3.5 (Page 17)
The expectation is developing a Graphical User Interface (GUI) calling a code that runs 
the GNSS antenna calibration testing. 
5.For technical acceptability, is prior geodetic/GNSS software past performance required, or may 
an offeror demonstrate technical acceptability through relevant numerical/scientific software 
capability, C++/Python experience, and a detailed domain onboarding and validation plan?
a. Yes, it is important to have a basic understanding of geodetic/GNSS software. There is a 
learning curve under the geodetic algorithms and the way they are computed. 
Based on past experience with companies, NGS cannot support contractors that have a 
gap in knowledge about basic geodetic processes. Any company applying to this contract 
needs to understand the tasks.
6. Is subcontracting or teaming with a geodesy/GNSS/numerical-methods specialist acceptable for 
portions of the requirement, provided the prime manages delivery and performs the required 
prime share of work?
a. Yes, it is acceptable to subcontract or team up with a geodesy/GNSS/numerical-methods 
specialist

7. Given that the new program must parse GDX and STARNET data files, which, if any, of the nine 
files listed in section 4.3.1 need to be supported in the new program? This question pertains 
specifically to file types HDS, DES, INST.PAR, TRA, DAT, LVL, HGZ, Inst.dat, Rods.dat.
a. None of the formats outlined in section 4.3.1 needs to be supported in the new program. 
When validating results, NGS will be using their code formats 
8. Does NGS want the C++ GDX and STARNET parsing routines already developed as part of the 
previous LASER work to be rewritten in Python, or would it be sufficient for the new Python 
code to simply call those C++ routines (we acknowledge that the C++ STARNET parser will need 
to be extended somewhat, depending on answers to questions 4-6 below)?
a. Yes, it is acceptable to use Python code to call C++ routines that already exist in LASER.
9.Will the GDX format be finalized by NGS before the start of this contract? If not, when will it be 
finalized?
a. A final draft of GDX is expected in September, 2026.
10. As NGS is aware, LASER already includes programs for baseline calibration adjustments and 
leveling network adjustments. Neither of these programs use any of the following observation 
types: GNSS vectors, horizontal angles, horizontal directions, slant distances, zenith angles, 
elevation angles, "traverse observations." Can NGS specify which of these observation types 
must be included in each of the two respective programs?
a. None of these observation types are required for baseline calibration adjustments. 
Instead, these observation types are needed to be read from an input file for reduction, 
correction, and preparation for a 3-D geometric adjustment that exists in the LASER 
engine. See response to question 12 for how to add vertical angles and slant distances to 
leveling adjustments.
In Task 2, the observations mentioned above shall be ingested using the GDX file format 
into the software. 
11. As a follow up to the previous question, if anything other than slant distances and vertical angles 
reduced to the horizontal plane using equations from plane surveying need to be added to the 
calibration baseline adjustment, can NGS explain how they would be used in that adjustment?
a. See response to the previous question. No additional observation types are needed to be 
added to the calibration baseline adjustment.
12. As a follow up to question 4, if anything other than vertical angles and slant distances (e.g., as 
trigonometric leveling observations) need to be added to the leveling network adjustment can 
NGS explain how they would be used in that adjustment? If zenith angles and slant distances 
must be added, should they be transformed to orthometric height differences using rigorous 
geodetic computations (which would require knowledge of latitude, longitude, and geoid 
undulation for the points involved)?

a. Only vertical angles and slant distances are needed. 
Task 2 is focused on using CBL and differential leveling observations. The task shall be 
able to handle River Crossing situations that incorporate trigonometric leveling, which 
requires transformation to orthometric height differences using geodetic computations 
NGS will provide these computations
With that said, there is an expectation that the code will include the calibration base line 
(in CALIBRATE) to estimate unknown systematic errors between an EDM instrument and 
a specific type of reflector. The systematic errors are of two types: an offset (or bias) and 
a distance-dependent scale factor. These terms are estimated from distance 
measurements made between a number of points arrayed along a line at known 
distances. This is mentioned in the PWS under Task 2 (Section 4.1).
13. Regarding task 3: "Updating Antcal source codes absolute and relative source codes to Python":
The example interface program in Appendix B shows GPS, Galileo, and GLONASS 
constellations. Is BeiDou also supported?
a. The contractor is not expected to include BeiDou support.
Does new Python code need to be written that communicates directly with GNSS 
receivers from various manufacturers? If so, does it need to issue commands to the 
receivers that set items such as their tracking loops, types of observations to log, 
constellations to track, logging rates, mask angle, etc.?
a. The code shall communicate only with Septentrio receivers using Septentrio 
Receiver Command Language (Section 5.2.1). NGS will provide SBF language 
documentation in addition to the simple commands already used in the Perl 
software.

Statement of Work (SOW) for the Air University (AU) Student Information System (SIS) Modernization and Sustainment

Background 

The Student Information System (SIS) is an enterprise solution that consolidated education information technology (IT) services within the United States Air Force (USAF) and United States Space Force (USSF). As AU transitioned from legacy (IT) systems to an enterprise solution, the government is unable to implement a comprehensive model to support and configure the SAP Student Lifecycle Management System (SLcM) to fully meet user interface demands, address existing technical debt, keep pace with growing backlog capability gaps, provide necessary training to enable users to leverage system capabilities, and establish a predictable cycle of continuous capability development and integration. 

Objective 

The core objectives are to establish a mature and stable application and database infrastructure, repeatable and value-added user processes through a modern user interface, tier II and III support services, and initial user training followed by targeted training as new capability enters the operational pipeline. All activities shall be managed under a formal ITIL-based governance framework. The end state shall deliver the SLcM into a capability support phase and enable SLcM to maintain a cycle of continuous development and integration of required upgrades, patches and system owner approved and funded system features and/or new capabilities. 

 

Scope of Work 

The contractor shall perform the tasks necessary to modernize, sustain, and support the AU Student Information System. The scope includes establishing a robust governance framework, providing transformation and operational support, delivering technical maintenance, developing and executing a training plan, and furnishing detailed reporting.

Specific Tasks

Governance and IT Service Management (ITSM) Framework 

The contractor shall establish, operate, and maintain a comprehensive governance framework based on Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) best practices to ensure a structured, predictable, and controlled approach to all service management activities. 

Change Management: The contractor shall implement a formal Change Management process to standardize methods and procedures for the efficient and prompt handling of all changes to the production environment (including infrastructure, applications, and documentation). 

This process must include the facilitation of a Change Advisory Board (CAB) in coordination with government stakeholders. 

All changes must be documented via formal change requests (CRs), undergo impact and risk analysis, receive explicit government approval, and include detailed back-out plans. The entire process must be tracked and auditable. 

Configuration Management: The contractor shall implement a formal Configuration Management process to identify, document, and maintain the configuration of all system components—known as Configuration Items (CIs)—throughout their lifecycle. 

The contractor shall establish and maintain a Configuration Management Database (CMDB) or a logically equivalent system of record that serves as the single source of truth for all CIs, their attributes, and their relationships. 

This system shall provide authoritative system baselines and support the impact analysis required for the Change Management process. 

ITIL Best Practices for ITSM: To ensure services are aligned with the mission needs of Air University, the contractor shall implement and adhere to core ITIL processes, including: 

Incident Management: To restore normal service operation as quickly as possible and minimize adverse impact. 

Problem Management: To identify and resolve the root cause of incidents to prevent recurrence. 

Service Level Management: To define, document, monitor, and report on the agreed-upon levels of service. 

Knowledge Management: To gather, analyze, store, and share information, including the creation of a robust knowledge base to support user training and help desk efficiency. 

Transformation Support 

The contractor shall provide transformation planning and execution from a proof-of-concept activity to a development, modernization, and integration activity. 

Deliverable: The contractor shall create and provide the Government with a Modernization Roadmap for contractor and government actions to remedy technical debt and deliver a modernized user interface as an Initial Operational Capability (IOC). This will be based on an assessment in the first 90 days and delivered 90 days after task award. 

The roadmap must include a schedule for initial and new capability training sessions. 

The contractor shall support a process for including development, configuration, and/or infrastructure changes outside the scope of the approved roadmap as unpriced CLINS through contract modification. 

Operational Support 

The contractor shall provide expert-level Student Information System (SIS) capability support, guidance, and troubleshooting for users and key stakeholders with a focus on incident resolution. This shall include: 

Providing comprehensive project management. 

Providing Tier III support on SIS service tickets, including troubleshooting, documenting solutions, and adding items to the backlog for prioritization. 

Providing experienced, certified, and trained personnel meeting all cybersecurity requirements. 

Managing and providing support for SAP SIS solution enhancements, expansions, and updates. 

Managing and providing support for the SAP Security module, including user access and roles. 

Managing and providing support for the SAP-HCM module. 

Managing and providing support for the SAP S/4HANA Database. 

Maintaining the security posture of all SAP SIS systems and sub-systems. 

Executing the design and development of all government-approved changes. 

Conducting testing for all major change requests and providing resolutions for upgrades and/or patches. 

Application Management via NetWeaver/Basis, including upgrades, patches, and migration to Cloud One environments. 

Supporting SAP PI/PO (Process Integration / Process Orchestration) for internal and external integration. 

Providing support for SIS Solution Out-of-the-Box (OOB) Report Delivery. 

Technical Support 


The contractor shall provide system-related technical support including the maintenance of the solution, the environment it resides in, and connections to other systems. 

SAP Solution Support: Manage and provide technical support including, but not limited to: OSS Notes, Kernel Patches, Support Packages, Enhancement Packages, Release Upgrades, Data Backup, Data Recovery, and maintenance of user interfaces. 

Cloud 1 Hosting AWS Platform Support: Manage and provide technical support including, but not limited to: secure configuration sustainment, component validation, interface maintenance, enclave monitoring, and providing Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) tools. 

Training 


Deliverable: The contractor shall develop a Training Plan that meets AU Academic business needs, including learning objectives, schedule, delivery method, and testing criteria for initial and refresher skills training. 

The contractor shall offer initial and refresher training classes no less than once a quarter for up to 20 students. 

The Training Manager shall coordinate with the Registrar Office monthly to codify requirements. 

The Training Plan shall be updated as new capabilities are delivered. Training for new capabilities will be conducted as “just in time” training, completed no later than 30 days prior to the new release. 

The contractor shall provide individuals experienced with SAP SLcM, Business Objects, Canvas LMS, and instructional design. 

Reporting 


Performance Reporting: The contractor shall use the government-provided ticket platform to generate and deliver service performance reports, including but not limited to: Average Speed to Answer (ASA), First-Call Resolution (FCR), Mean Time to Recover (MTTR), and Backlog Growth. 

System Reporting: The contractor shall generate and deliver system-related technical reports, including but not limited to: Response Time, System Uptime, Hardware Utilization, and Scheduled/Unscheduled Downtime. 

 

System Requirements (Technical Specifications) 

This section defines the mandatory technical specifications the modernized EEMS platform must meet. The tasks outlined shall result in a system that complies with these requirements. 

 General Terms and Conditions 

PERIOD AND PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: The Period of Performance (PoP) shall be a 12-month base period, with four 12-month option period. The Contractor may choose the location(s) from which to perform the required services. 

CYBER SECURITY REQUIREMENTS: The Contractor shall identify qualified cybersecurity personnel and comply with all requirements in DoDI 8500.01 and DoDI 8410.02. All personnel with privileged user access must satisfy all responsibilities for their role and obtain any required certifications. All positions are considered AIS-III – Non-sensitive, and a Tier 1 background investigation is required for computer access. 

HOURS OF OPERATION: Work shall generally be performed between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM CST, Monday through Friday (except Federal holidays), with flexibility as needed to fulfill requirements. 

NON-PERSONAL SERVICES: The Government will neither supervise Contractor employees nor control the method by which the Contractor performs tasks. The relationship shall not give the perception of personal services. 

CONTRACTOR IDENTIFICATION: Contractor personnel shall identify themselves as contractors in all communications and meetings and shall wear appropriate identification badges when on-site. 

QUALITY ASSURANCE: The Government will provide a Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) at contract initiation and will evaluate performance accordingly. The Contractor shall respond to written concerns within five (5) workdays. 

PASS AND IDENTIFICATION ITEMS: The contractor shall ensure all employees obtain required identification, including DoD Common Access Cards (CAC), by following the government-provided TASS application process. 

SERVICE DELIVERABLE SUMMARY (SDS): Key deliverables, performance standards, and thresholds will be formally defined in the SDS provided by the Government at the time of contract initiation. 

Requirement ID  | Category  | Requirement Description 

REQ-GEN-001  | Governance  | The solution shall be maintained in compliance with all applicable DoD, US Air Force, and Cloud One (C1) standards to ensure a continuous Authority to Operate (ATO). 

REQ-ARC-002  | High Availability  | The production and QAS environments must be architected for High Availability (HA) across multiple Availability Zones (AZs) with automated failover. 

REQ-ARC-003  | Disaster Recovery  | A Disaster Recovery (DR) plan must be implemented and tested to meet a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of 12 hours and a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 24 hours. 

REQ-ARC-004  | SAP: S/4HANA  | The core solution shall be deployed on SAP S/4HANA version 2023 or newer, adhering to "Clean Core" principles to minimize customization. 

REQ-ARC-005  | SAP: Fiori  | The S/4HANA deployment shall utilize the embedded Fiori Launchpad architecture, retiring any standalone front-end servers. 

REQ-MSP-001  | Automation (IaC)  | All infrastructure must be managed as code (IaC) using tools like Terraform and Ansible, ensuring the environment is automated, repeatable, and version-controlled. 

REQ-MSP-002  | Automation (CI/CD)  | The system must be sustained via a full DevSecOps CI/CD pipeline for automated builds, security scanning, testing, and deployments. 

REQ-SEC-001  | Access Control  | A least-privilege security model shall be implemented using granular, role-based Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies. 

REQ-SEC-002  | Encryption  | All data must be encrypted at rest (e.g., using AWS KMS) and in transit (using TLS 1.2 or higher). 

REQ-SEC-004  | Continuous Monitoring  | The system shall enable continuous security posture monitoring, threat detection, and automated compliance validation against DISA STIGs and other baselines.

Office of the Secretary of War-Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation (OSW-CAPE) 
Resource Enterprise Services (RES) for Program Review and Enterprise Services Division 
(PRESD)

General Information

Title: Resource Enterprise Services (RES) for Program Review and Enterprise Services Division 
(PRESD)

Sources Sought Response Date: June 9, 2026 at 10:00 AM (Eastern Standard Time) 
NAICS Code: 541511 Custom Computer Programming Services 
 
Sources Sought Notice 
 
This Notice is for informational purposes only. It is not to be construed as an obligation on the 
part of the Washington Headquarters Services /Acquisition Directorate (WHS/AD). 
 
In order to proactively plan for future requirements, WHS/AD is conducting market research to 
locate qualified, experienced, and interested parties who have the capability to provide RES for 
PRESD Support under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 
assigned to this procurement 541511 Custom Computer Programming Services. Small Business 
size standard of $34 million.  
 
This Sources Sought Notice is not a Request for Quotation (RFQ), nor does it restrict the 
Government as to the final acquisition strategy. No contract will be awarded from this 
announcement. At this time, no solicitation exists. Therefore, please do not request a copy of the 
solicitation. Responses in any form are not offers. 
 
The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in the preparation of a 
response to this Notice. 
 
Important Notice to Small Business Concerns: While not responding to this Sources Sought 
Announcement does not preclude participation in any future RFQ if one is issued, it is highly 
recommended that all interested and capable firms respond in order to be considered during this 
market research and acquisition planning phase. 
 

The Government encourages responses from “all” interested, capable sources including 
small business concerns (8(a) Certified concerns, Historically Underutilized Business Zone 
(HUBZone) concerns, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs), Women-
Owned Small Businesses (WOSBs) and Economically Disadvantaged Women-owned Small 
Businesses (EDWOSBs)) are encouraged to respond to this notice. Small businesses are defined 
based on the size standard associated with the NAICS code. For more information, visit: 
https://www.sba.gov/document/support-table-size-standards, and check your size using the SBA 
Size Standards Tool: https://www.sba.gov/size-standards/index.html. 
 
The Contracting Officer will use the responses received from this notice to determine the 
appropriate acquisition strategy such as, if it is appropriate to either solicit as a small business 
set-aside or an unrestricted competition through SAM.gov or an indefinite-delivery/indefinite-
quantity (IDIQ) government wide contract vehicle 
 
1.  Background 
 
The PRESD division of OSW, CAPE is responsible for maintaining of business applications to 
support matters relating to the planning and programming phases of the Planning, Programming, 
Budgeting, and Execution (PBBE) and the preparation of material and guidance for such systems 
PBBE is the Department of War (DOW) process for allocating resources. The annual process 
serves as the framework for DOW civilian and military leaders to decide which programs and 
force structure requirements to fund based on strategic objectives. Products produced include the 
Program Decision Memorandum and the Department of War Future Years Defense Program 
(FYDP) and supplementary data including the data structure. Applications have their authority to 
operate under the DOW Risk Management Framework under the system named Resource 
Enterprise Services (RES). See APPENDIX A for list of applications. 
 
2.  Procurement History for Similar Services 
 
This requirement has previously been procured via the General Services Administration (GSA) 
Multiple Award Schedule (MAS), 54151S, Information Technology Professional Services under 
FAR Part 8 procedures, which was competed in September 2021. Science Applications 
International Corporation (SAIC) is the incumbent on this requirement under Task Order 
HQ0034-21-F-0556.

The Office of the Secretary of War (OSW), Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation (CAPE) is 
seeking sources to provide comprehensive Resource Enterprise Services (RES). The Contractor

implementing analytic solutions to support budgetary systems associated with the PBBE 
specifically the Program Review process. Analytical knowledge and experience of the Program 
Review process is necessary. Knowledge of FYDP data and structures and how to validate data 
between DOW Comptroller Next Generation Resource Management System (NGRMS) is 
required. The ability to create and maintain complex Oracle triggers, procedures, functions and 
ability to adapt to newer technologies is necessary.   Integration with DOW enterprise Identity 
Credential and Access Management (ICAM) for applications is required. 
 
To ensure vendors provide personnel with the required technical expertise to support PBBE 
applications, the following specific skills are listed in Appendix A (including Optional) are listed 
in Appendix A.  Applications are listed under Appendix B. 
 

The contractor shall work with the government to standardize the technology to enable 
developers to be matrixed and able to support multiple applications during the span of this 
contract. 
 
12.  Critical Task Elements 
 
Interested parties submitting a response to this Notice should address the performance of the 
following Service Requirement Critical Tasks Elements in their capabilities statement. Interested 
parties are requested NOT to submit marketing materials; but rather, speak directly and 
specifically to the required capabilities and service requirements critical/tasks elements outlined 
below: 
 
Task Element 1 
 
Application Development, Sustainment, and Modernization: The Contractor shall provide 
comprehensive lifecycle support for applications and databases, ensuring high availability with 
minimal downtime (not to exceed 5% unless pre-arranged). This includes the sustainment and 
configuration of existing applications on both Windows and LINUX operating systems, and 
application testing and performance tuning. 
 
The Contractor must manage the full Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), utilizing test 
and staging environments for load testing and security scanning to maintain the Authority to 
Operate (ATO). All security vulnerabilities must be addressed with a remediation plan within two 
weeks of discovery. 
 
Key modernization efforts include proposing and implementing a standard technology 
framework that incorporates Zero Trust pillars, as mandated by Executive Order 14028. The 
contractor shall also develop and maintain standard, ensure auditability, secure data exchange 
methods (e.g., RESTful APIs) for business-to-business (B2B) interactions and establish common 
business rules and data elements across applications to ensure data quality and reporting 
efficiency. The contractor must be adaptable to new technologies as cloud capabilities evolve, 
and AI capabilities become available. The contractor shall conduct periodic reviews of 
technology solutions and data exchange methods. 
 
(See PWS Section 5.2) 
 
Task Element 2 
 
Maintain Specific Applications: The Contractor shall provide comprehensive operations, 
maintenance, and enhancement support for the portfolio of government-furnished applications 
referenced under Appendix B, which are critical to the Department of War's Program Review, 
Future Years Defense Program, and resource management processes. This support includes 
ensuring the applications for collecting, tracking, and analyzing program issues and alternatives 
remain agile to support senior leadership decisions, integrating AI/ML technologies where 
applicable. The contractor must demonstrate expert knowledge of departmental manpower, 
costing, forces, and Comptroller Information System (CIS) data structures while also 

maintaining the various supporting applications for scheduling, team formulation, and enhanced 
application support related to the Program Review cycle. 
Furthermore, the contractor is responsible for the applications supporting the Future Years 
Defense Program (FYDP), specialized data collections, data warehouse, and other data-driven 
analytical functions. The scope of this work includes the production of official DOW program 
products, management of resource and data structure systems, and operation of numerous 
specialized data collection tools for IT, program budget, and other reporting requirements. Across 
all applications, the contractor must provide general support services, including Business 
Intelligence and Data Visualization (BI/DV), user training, and robust security administration, 
ensuring compliance with the Risk Management Framework (RMF) and Zero Trust architecture. 
This includes working with the ISSO and ISSM reviewing security scans, updating necessary 
documentation and managing remediation plans. 
(See PWS Section 5.3) 
13. Submission Requirements
Interested firms should submit their response to include a capabilities statement covering 
experience, staffing and technical capabilities. The capabilities statement should address the 
Critical Task Elements identified above and for each Task Element demonstrate how the firm’s 
recent contract experience (last 3 years) is relevant to the Critical Task Elements listed including 
the dollar value, period of performance, size and scope of the firm’s prior contracts. Firms need 
to include their business address, point of contact, CAGE code, UEI number, and business size

Do not include proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information in your response to

U.S. Department of Homeland Security     
500 C Street SW, Washington, DC 20472 
Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
for 
 Individual Assistance Housing Cost Data  
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), 
intends to award a Firm Fixed Price sole source contract pursuant to authority of 41 U.S.C 1901, utilizing 
the procedures of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 12.102(a) and FAR Class Deviation 25-21 Rev. 
1 for FAR Part 12. 
NAICS Code: 518210 Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related 
Services 
PSC Code: DA01: IT and Telecom – Business Application/Application Development Support Services 
Intended Contractor: 
THE GORDIAN GROUP, INC. 
30 Patewood Drive, Suite 350 
Greenville, SC 29615 
Requirement Overview: 
FEMA requires a comprehensive, nationwide, line-item residential construction cost database, delivered 
via Microsoft Access and natively structured to match RS Means data for seamless integration with 
FEMA’s National Emergency Management Information System (NEMIS). The requirement includes: 
• Ongoing software licensing
• Real-time cost index updates
• Technical support
• Automated damage repair calculations
• Survivor assistance determinations
T
he anticipated contract will feature a one (1) year base period and four (4) one-year option periods. 
J
ustification for Sole Source: 
Gordian provides a comprehensive, nationwide, line-item residential construction cost database delivered 
via Microsoft Access, natively structured to match RS Means data for seamless integration with FEMA’s 
National Emergency Management Information System (NEMIS) . The requirement includes ongoing 
software licensing, real -time cost index updates, and technical support to automate damage repair 
calculations and survivor assistance determinations. As the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and 
exclusive provider of RS Means- branded construction cost data, Gordian is the only contractor with the 
intellectual property rights and technical capability to supply this specific data framework and its matching 
APIs.  


 
 
U.S. Department of Homeland Security                           
500 C Street SW, Washington, DC 20472 
 
 
Market research, including RFIs on SAM.gov and NASA SEWP, confirmed that no alternative vendor 
can provide a functionally equivalent nationwide, line -item cost database. Third-party integrators do not 
own, generate, or license independent construction cost  data, and any alternate solution would require a 
complete reengineering of FEMA’s core systems. Without Gordian, FEMA would face immediate 
disruption to automated financial assistance determinations, resulting in catastrophic operational 
vulnerabilities, unrecoverable system redesign costs, and multi-year delays.  
 
This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals or quotations.  
 
Instructions for Interested Parties: 
Any party who believes they can fulfill this requirement should submit a capability statement for 
consideration by the government. The government will determine whether to conduct a competitive 
procurement based solely on responses to this notice. The government will not be responsible for any 
costs incurred in responding. 
 
Deadline for Responses: 
Capability statements must be submitted by 02:00pm Eastern Time on June 15, 2026. 
 
Contact Information: 
Submit responses and questions via email to: 
Lassey Wilson-Bahun at  Lassey.wilsonbahun@fema.dhs.gov

DHS-FEMA IA Housing Cost Data SOW  1  
 
Federal Emergency Management Agency 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) FOR: 
Individual Assistance Housing Cost Data 
 
 
 
 
 
 
DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) 
 
 


DHS-FEMA IA Housing Cost Data SOW  2  
Statement of Work (SOW) for  
FEMA IA Housing Cost Data 
1.0 GENERAL 
1.1  BACKGROUND   
The Federal Emergency Management Agency is a Federal agency authorized under 44CFR (Code of Federal 
Regulations) and PL (Public Law) 93-288 as amended by PL 100-707 to provide assistance to disaster victims in 
Presidential declared disasters and emergencies. As a part of these disaster relief efforts, FEMA conducts 
preliminary damage assessments for States/Territories and residential housing inspections for disaster survivors. 
The assessments confirm damage to real (structural components) and personal property utilizing line item costs 
components.  
1.2  SCOPE   
FEMA requires a contractor to develop and maintain a comprehensive database that provides unit costs for home 
repair components across all phases of residential construction. The contractor will also deliver this data through a 
Microsoft Access database. The database will support FEMA in establishing accurate repair costs for use in future 
Presidential Declarations and in providing financial assistance to disaster survivors. 
1.3  OBJECTIVE  
The contractor shall develop and maintain unit costs for home repair components for all phases of residential 
construction per Attachment A using R.S. Means data. The contractor shall deliver the R.S. Means branded data 
through a Microsoft Access database. 
FEMA’s Individuals and Households Program (IHP) and disaster relief partners will use the data in determining a 
survivor’s financial assistance to rebuild or replace lost property. Access to the data will be utilized by FEMA and 
associated partners performing operations in response to or in preparation for Presidential Declarations.  
1.4  APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 
1.4.1  REFERENCE DOCUMENTS 
The following document provides the list of eligible real and personal property line item usage descriptions the 
Contractor shall use to develop a cost methodology to establish the Line Item Mapping Master and provide the 
dataset: 
 Attachment A 

DHS-FEMA IA Housing Cost Data SOW  3  
2.0 SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS/TASKS 
2.1  TASK ONE:  Line-Item Mapping Master 
The Contractor shall disclose the components to establish each line item cost identified in Attachment A using 
Construction Specifications Institutes (CSI) standards generating a National average cost for each line item and 
display the results through a Microsoft (MS) Excel file.    
2.1.1  Each line item cost shall include the following:  
• The materials to meet construction / code requirements for the associated Federal Information Processing 
Standard (FIPS) location, 
• The transportation of materials to the FIPS location,  
• The overhead and profit for the firm providing the services,  
• The labor to remove and install the components, 
• The disposal of debris. 
2.1.2  Each Personal Property line item cost shall represent the average cost of the line item for the specific State 
/ Territory.   
2.1.3  FEMA will provide the following fields within Attachment A to discern output for the Line Item Mapping 
Master :  
• Item ID – A FEMA provided numerical identifier for software integration 
• Category – A FEMA component for software integration 
• Assistance Code – A FEMA component for software integration 
• Description – A short description of the line item provided by FEMA 
• Help Text – A component definition to aid the Contractor to establish costs 
• Unit of Measure – Used to identify the measurable component 
• FEMA Supplied Cost – If listed, this is the cost for the line item across all FIPS locations provided by FEMA.  
2.1.4  The Contractor shall provide two costs;  
• One for moderate construction specifications as the base cost for each line item displayed as a Medium 
Cost,  
• A second for catastrophic cost increasing the base 25 percent when displayed as High Cost.  
2.1.5  The Contractor shall provide the Line Item Mapper Master in a Microsoft Excel format displaying the 
following fields:  
• Item ID – A FEMA provided numerical identifier for software integration 
• Category – A FEMA component for software integration 
• Assistance Code – A FEMA component for software integration 
• Description – A short description of the line item provided by FEMA 

DHS-FEMA IA Housing Cost Data SOW  4  
• Help Text – A component definition to aid the Contractor to establish costs provided by FEMA 
• Unit of Measure – Used to identify the measurable component 
• Medium Cost – Line Item baseline Cost 
• High Cost – Line Item baseline cost plus 25 percent.  
• CSI codes and formulas used to establish the line item cost.  
 
2.1.6 The Contractor shall provide the CORs and designated representatives a Line Item Mapping Master within 30 
days of contract award, then annually on a date established by the COR. With the COR or its designated 
representatives’ approval, the Contractor shall then proceed to provide the Line Item Data Bases for that year.    
2.2  TASK TWO:  Line Item Database 
The Contractor shall create and maintain Line Item costs detailed in Task One for each FIPS CONUS and OCONUS 
locations to include Tribal Nations and Alaska Regional Areas.  
2.2.1 The Contractor shall provide this data electronically, MS Access database to a FEMA secure portal and 
update quarterly.    
2.2.1  FEMA may require the Contractor to revise existing line items, research and provide new line items or 
revise the data delivery where the time to conduct an honest effort will not exceed 80 personnel hours per year.      
3.0 CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL   
3.1  Qualified Personnel   
The Contractor shall provide the personnel and their qualifications to perform all requirements specified in this SOW.   
3.2  Continuity of Support  
The Contractor shall ensure that the contractually required level of support for this requirement is maintained at all 
times.   
3.3  Single Point of Contact (SPOC)   
The Contractor shall provide a Single Point of Contact (SPOC) responsible for all Contractor work performed under 
this SOW. The SPOC will convey contractual concerns with the Government’s Contracting Officer and the COR.  The 
name of the SPOC, and any alternate(s) who shall act for the Contractor in the absence of the SPOC, shall be 
provided to the Government as part of the Contractor's proposal. The SPOC is further designated as Key by the 
Government. During any absence of the SPOC, only one alternate shall have full authority to act for the Contractor 
on all matters relating to work performed under this contract. The SPOC and all designated alternates shall be able 
to read, write, speak and understand English. The SPOC should have advanced education in the field of engineering, 
marketing, program management, or construction to include active listening and interpersonal skills  to establish 
rapport and trust with the Government in the execution of the requirements of this contract. Additionally, the 
Contractor shall not replace the SPOC without prior approval from the Contracting Officer. 

DHS-FEMA IA Housing Cost Data SOW  5  
3.3.1  There may be occasions when the Contractor employee(s) shall be required to work other than normal 
business hours, including weekends and holidays, to fulfill the requirements under this SOW.   
4.0  Other Applicable Conditions 
4.1  Security  
The Contractor has no need to access classified and sensitive information under this SOW.   
4.2  Period of Performance   
The period of performance for this contract is a one-year base period with four one-year option periods as follows: 
Base Period   08/01/2026 – 07/31/2027  
Option Period One  08/01/2027 – 07/31/2028 
Option Period Two  08/01/2028 – 07/31/2029 
Option Period Three  08/01/2029 – 07/31/2030 
Option Period Four      08/01/2030 – 07/31/2031 
4.3  Place of Performance   
The primary place of performance will be the Contractor’s facilities. No regular onsite Government presence is 
required.      
4.4  Post Award Conference   
The Contractor shall attend a Post Award Conference with the Contracting Officer, COR and FEMA representatives no 
later than 15 calendar days after the date of award.  The purpose of the Post Award Conference, which will be 
chaired by the Contracting Officer, is to discuss technical and contracting objectives of this contract and review the 
Contractor's draft project plan.  The Post Award Conference will be conducted via teleconference – MS Teams. 
4.5  Quality Management Plan 
The Contractor shall establish, document, implement and maintain a quality control system throughout the life of the 
contract in accordance with the requirements of a quality management system chosen by the Contractor. A draft 
Quality Management Plan (QMP) shall be provided to the COR within 15 calendar days of receiving the award notice. 
The CORs will review and if acceptable, approve within 10 calendar days of receipt. The QMP, at a minimum, shall 
include the following: 
 Describe the quality monitoring plan providing evidence that a continual quality verification program is in place.   
 The criteria and methods needed to ensure that both the operation and control of the verification process is 
effective.  
 A description of how the Contractor will disclose non-conformities to FEMA to include an annual audit / review of 
its systems.  

DHS-FEMA IA Housing Cost Data SOW  6  
4.5.1  Periodically, FEMA will research certain line items to verify the proposed cost provided by the Contractor to 
be consistent with the intended purpose of the Individual and Households Program. When identified, any 
inconsistencies shall be remedied by the Contractor within 72 hours of notice at no additional cost to the 
Government.  
4.6  Progress Meetings   
The Single Point of Contact (SPOC) shall be available to meet with the COR upon request to present deliverables, 
discuss progress, exchange information and resolve emergent technical problems and issues.  These meetings shall 
take place via MS Teams.   
4.7  Intellectual Property  
This scope of work requires the Contractor to provide line item costs in which repairs are recorded as a 
construction component indicating the quantity and associated unit cost. FEMA’s Individuals and Households 
Program (IHP) and affiliated governmental entities responsible in disaster relief use the data in determining a 
survivor’s eligibility. Access to the data will be utilized by FEMA and affiliated government entities in response to or 
preparation for a Presidential Declaration and shall not be incumbered by licenses restricting the number of users to 
the data.  
4.9  Section 508 Compliance  
Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, as amended by the Workforce Investment Act of 1998 (P.L. 105-220) 
(codified at 29 U.S.C. § 794d) requires that when Federal agencies develop, procure, maintain, or use information 
and communications technology (ICT), it shall be accessible to people with disabilities. Federal employees and 
members of the public with disabilities must be afforded access to and use of information and data comparable to 
that of Federal employees and members of the public without disabilities.

The United States (US) Food and Drug Administration (FDA) intends to award a sole source , Firm Fixed 
Price Purchase Order to The Gordian Group, Inc, 30 Patewood Drive, Suite 350, Greenville, South Carolina 
29615-6810, on a sole source base, under the authority of FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and 
No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.  
 
The FDA / Office of the Commissioner  (OC) / Engineering Management Branch  (EMB) requires a 
comprehensive facility condition and capital project planning solution to support effective management of 
its owned -facility portfolio. This requirement encompasses both software licensing and professional  
support services to ensure optimal utilization of the VFA database platform . This will be a one-year Base
