Mechanistic Chromatography Modeling Software 
Software License Support and Maintenance Services (BRAND NAME OR EQUAL GOSILICO) 
1. Background 
Mechanistic chromatography modeling is a sophisticated approach to understanding and 
predicting the behavior of chromatographic systems. This type of modeling is grounded in the 
fundamental principles of mass transfer and thermodynamics, and consider factors like 
molecular diffusion, adsorption isotherms, convection, and pore diffusion. Digital 
transformation and incorporating mechanistic chromatography models into downstream 
process development and manufacturing processes of biologics has become an increasingly 
important topic for the biopharmaceutical industry as it excels in predicting chromatographic 
behavior, allowing researchers to forecast how changes in operating conditions (like flow rate, 
temperature, or mobile phase composition) will affect the separation process. This predictive 
capability is invaluable for method development and optimization without extensive trial-and-
error experimentation. In addition, the model can help in complying with regulatory standards, 
which demand strict control over manufacturing processes, ensuring consistent batch quality 
and performance. Mechanistic modeling offering insights into process variability, identifying 
critical quality attributes (CQAs), and critical process parameters (CPPs), and ensuring that 
processes consistently meet their predefined criteria. Especially when integrated with 
appropriate software tools, the model can help maintain comprehensive records of how each 
result was obtained, the parameters used, and the assumptions made, thereby ensuring 
traceability and reproducibility. For continuous manufacturing, which is an emerging 
technology, the ability to make real-time adjustments during the process is crucial to ensure 
product quality. Mechanistic models can predict the impact of changes in process conditions, 
allowing for immediate optimization, control, and ensuring consistent product quality. 
Therefore, specific modeling and simulation tools are needed at FDA to investigate the impact 
of process parameters on product quality during process development, process 
characterization, and manufacturing processes.  
2. Objective 
The objective is to purchase a new license for mechanistic chromatography modeling and 
simulation platform including adsorption isotherms model for different mode of 
chromatography, and fluid flow effects in a chromatography column. 
3. Requirements 
The Office of Pharmaceutical Quality Research (OPQR) has a requirement to obtain a 
mechanistic chromatography modeling and simulation software to study emerging 
pharmaceutical manufacturing technologies or equal to software license.  In order for a 
Vendor’s software to be deemed acceptable, the following salient characteristics shall be met: 

3.1 Mechanistic chromatography modeling software 
• Mechanistic modeling environment for conventional pharmaceutical processes 
including a graphical interface with drag and drop functionality. 
• Streamlined modeling workflow from calibration experiments to simulation. 
• Seamless lab integration through optimal linking to AKTA system and UNICORN 
software. 
• Visual tools for easy interpretation of simulation outputs to support the fulfilment of 
quality by design obligation.  
• Component-centric data structure enables plug and play with different methods, 
system parts, and columns.  
• Collaboration and knowledge management shared databased within and between 
projects. 
• Tamper-proof and back-traceable data and user management  
• Simulates preparative liquid chromatography processes with a computer. 
• Creates digital twins of downstream processes using mechanistic models. 
• Enables increased process understanding for smarter and faster process 
development. 
• Applies to a wide range of molecules and applications from early process 
development to late stage, scale-up, troubleshooting; and chemistry, manufacturing, 
and controls (CMC) 
• Custom modeling capabilities to create user defined models. 
• Parameter estimation from experimental data to support model validation. 
• Global sensitivity analysis to analyze the impact of inputs, and model parameters on 
process outputs. 
• Ability to estimate physical properties of components using only a few experiments.  
• Ability to run optimization and characterization.  
• Mechanistic model libraries including different adsorption isotherms that can be 
applied to different mode of chromatography. 
• Mechanistic model libraries for membrane separation 
3.2 Maintenance and Technical Support:  
At minimum the contractor must: 
• Delivery of software updates 
• One business-day response to all software defect inquiries 
• Availability of feature (level) upgrades 

3.3 Training:  
• Standardized 3-day training by the vendor. 
• A standard license package includes the installation on one computer and one user 
account, but you can add more computer licenses and user accounts as you need them. 
• During your chosen license period, updates and technical support are free. 
 
4. Deliverables 
Software and licensing key, Software and User Manuals or equal to in a digital copy provided on 
a CD, DVD or digital download. CD, DVD and hard copies of deliverables shall not be required to 
be returned to the Contractor. 
Deliverables are delivered to the following address:

5901 Ammendale Rd, Ste G, Beltsville, MD 20705

Vendor is not responsible for installation of the software. FDA staff will install the software. 
5. Inspection and Acceptance Criteria

The Government shall have 30 working days to inspect and verify that the

Next-Generation Air Operations Center (AOC) Weapon System 
Questions and Answers, 5 May 2026 
 
Question Response 
Will AFLCMC provide a follow-on opportunity 
for one-on-one industry discussions or a 
technical interchange meeting (TIM) prior to 
RFP release? 
 
Will the Government schedule in person 1-on-1 
engagements with prospective offerors to 
discuss program needs before solicitation 
release? 
Vendor engagement will be ongoing throughout 
the pre-solicitation phase. 
 
The Government will continue to be responsive 
to questions and feedback from industry. 
Has the Government considered a CSO 
approach to the acquisition strategy? 
The Government is considering all acquisition 
strategies. A Commercial Solutions Opening is 
not anticipated as the solicitation vehicle for 
non-commercial systems integration 
requirements. 
What is the Government’s appetite for an OTA 
pathway for the AI component, given that the 
broader sustainment effort may follow a 
traditional FAR-based approach? An OTA for 
the AI prototype with a production OT follow-on 
would maximize speed and innovation while 
the prime contract handles sustainment under 
traditional vehicles. 
The Government is considering all acquisition 
strategies. OTA prototype(s) with follow-on 
production is one approach to achieve more 
rapid and agile inﬂux of innovative capabilities. 
Could the Government clarify whether it will 
establish and maintain a comprehensive 
Technical Bidders Library (TBL) to support this 
acquisition, and if so, what speciﬁc materials 
will be included and when they will be made 
available? 
 
Will the Government provide a comprehensive 
bidders’ library including all weapon system 
components, cloud-hosted applications, and 
all relevant interfaces? 
Yes, the Government will supply a bidder's 
library as part of the draft and ﬁnal solicitation 
to cleared, prospective offerors. 
Can the Government provide draft evaluation 
criteria earlier in the acquisition strategy 
development timeline, so industry has more 
time to build the right team to deliver the best 
capabilities for the Government? 
The draft solicitation will include draft 
evaluation criteria with an opportunity for 
prospective offerors to provide feedback. 
How do you ensure a level playing ﬁeld with all 
offerors and avoid carve outs and  
pay-to-play relationships with a small group of 
vendors? 
The Government is engaging with industry as 
part of market research and seeks to maximize 
competition for this requirement. 

2 
 
What is the anticipated contract classiﬁcation 
level? Will performance require access to 
Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) 
beyond Top Secret? 
Facility clearance level required is Top Secret. 
A draft DD Form 254 will be provided with the 
solicitation. 
Will development be performed primarily at 
government facilities, contractor facilities, or a 
hybrid model? Are any of the AOC locations 
designated as primary places of performance? 
It is anticipated that development will require 
both classiﬁed and unclassiﬁed workspace, 
which may be in government or contractor 
facilities. Performance locations in government 
facilities will be speciﬁed in the draft 
Performance Work Statement (PWS) and draft 
DD Form 254. On-site contractor support is a 
requirement for select CONUS and OCONUS 
AOC locations. 
What cloud environments, security levels, and 
deployment constraints are anticipated for 
operational capabilities? 
All cloud and edge operational, production-
level capabilities will exist in IL6 or higher and 
Secret or higher, respectively. 
Will the Government prioritize cloud-native 
architectures or hybrid tactical-edge 
computing models? 
While cloud-native architectures are very 
favorable in commercial situations, the AOC 
WS requires the ability to operate in a 
disconnected state. Both cloud and edge 
solutions that enable Continuity of Operations 
(COOP) will be prioritized. 
Who controls interface deﬁnitions, data 
standards, API governance, cybersecurity 
boundary approvals, and release 
synchronization? 
The AOC WS is a system of systems, largely 
comprised of 3rd party applications, 
infrastructure, and other related systems. The 
control of interface deﬁnitions, data standards, 
API governance, cybersecurity boundary 
approvals, and release synchronization varies 
greatly by system. 
To enable integration of best-of-breed 
solutions and ensure Government ownership 
of data, models, and interfaces, including the 
ability to transition or replace components over 
time with reduced rework and barriers to entry, 
How does the program office intend to 
maintain open architecture standards and 
interoperability, data portability, and modular 
integration with more closed systems as 
mission needs and AI/ML capabilities evolve? 
The program office will align with PAE C3BM 
architectural decisions. The AOC WS is a 
system of systems, largely comprised of 3
rd 
party applications, infrastructure, and other 
related systems. The contractor will be 
expected to integrate modernized capabilities 
and systems as governed by an engineering 
change management process. 
Does the government have a preference for 
commercial vs developed software? 
The AOC WS includes both commercial and 
noncommercial systems and components. The 
Government prefers commercial software 
when it can meet agencies’ needs.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT

Intelligent Shift Scheduler Tool for 24/7 Continuous Operations

RFI Number: AF-A1-RFI-SKED-APP-2026

Agency: Department of the Air Force, HAF/A1Z

NAICS (anticipated): 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services) Notice Type: RFI/Sources Sought (Market Research) – Not a Solicitation Response Due: 1700EST, 19 June 2026

Points of Contact: Derrick Manning - derrick.manning@us.af.mil, Corey Collins - corey.collins.12@us.af.mil

INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE

This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market research purposes only. It does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), or a commitment by the Government.

HAF/A1Z is seeking information from industry regarding the rapid prototyping and deployment of an automated, intelligent shift scheduling tool. This initiative aims to improve the mental well-being and readiness of 24/7 continuous operations personnel, starting with a Phase 1 pilot for Security Forces (SF). 

The Government seeks to understand the "realm of the possible" regarding: (a) configuring an existing Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) tool, or (b) executing a platform-native custom-coded development effort. If a custom-coded solution is proposed, it must align with established Department of the Air Force (DAF) enterprise software frameworks (e.g., Salesforce PSS, ServiceNow, OutSystems low-code, or Cloud-Native Angular) to ensure long-term sustainment viability and seamless integration within a secure, rule-based scheduling engine operating inside strict Department of Defense (DoD) cyber environments.

BACKGROUND

Current scheduling for 24/7 continuous operations is largely managed via manual Excel spreadsheets, leading to sub-optimal schedule management, increased fatigue, and heavy administrative burdens on Non-Commissioned Officers (NCOs). The objective is to deploy a solution that ensures compliance with rest mandates, incorporates evidence-based principles for shift scheduling, optimizes manning based on qualifications, and handles dynamic roster changes.

ANTICIPATED SCOPE & FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS

The Government anticipates a phased approach: Phase 1 (Pilot at a single installation, <12 months), Phase 2 (Enterprise Scale for all DAF Security Forces), and Phase 3 (Cross-Functional Expansion). Core functional "must-haves" include:

Intelligent Automation & Fair Scheduling Engine: The solution must automatically generate schedules using rule-based logic. It must utilize algorithmic distribution of shifts to prevent favoritism, ensure fairness/equity, and balance workload.

Automated Rotation Policies: The system must automatically rotate personnel through different shifts (e.g., days, swings, mids) based on predefined unit rules to balance workload and ensure equitable exposure to leadership.

Minimum Manning & Qualification Tracking: The system must ensure mission readiness by satisfying specific minimum manning requirements per shift (e.g., mandating a minimum number of NCOs and specific requisite qualifications). It must strictly link personnel skills, weapons certifications, and training statuses to shift assignments.

Fatigue Management & Alerts: The platform must enforce mandated rest periods. It must integrate automated fatigue alerts to warn schedulers and leadership if personnel are at risk of being overworked or violating rest policies.

Duty Limiting Conditions (DLCs): The system must incorporate operational restrictions (DLCs) directly into the scheduling logic, preventing the scheduling of personnel whose DLCs restrict them from certain duties or hours.

Dynamic Leave, Comp Time, & Issue Resolution: The system must include procedures to handle automated leave requests, last-minute absences, and comp time allocation. It must proactively adjust schedules and recommend qualified replacements to maintain operational readiness while ensuring fairness.

Flexibility & Manual Overrides: While highly automated, the system must provide unit leadership and schedulers with easy modification and manual override capabilities to handle unplanned operational changes.

Notifications and Alerts: The system must automatically generate and send notifications (e.g., via AFNet email or internal system dashboards) to personnel regarding upcoming shifts, schedule changes, or expiring qualifications.

TECHNICAL, CYBER & SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

The Government emphasizes that any proposed solution must be capable of operating within strict Air Force networking and security boundaries.

Network Access: The platform MUST be accessible exclusively via AFNet (NIPRNet) connected workstations.

Authentication: The system MUST utilize standard military CAC/PKI authentication for all users.

Data Security & Handling: The system will process Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) related to schedules, duty availability, and operational restrictions (DLCs). It must be cleared to handle CUI but will not store Protected Health Information (PHI).

System Integration: The system must be capable of ingesting basic demographic data (Name, Rank, Unit) from MilPDS and eventually the A1 Data Landing Zone.

Architectural Alignment (COTS vs. Custom): Standalone custom-coded applications that require unique server/database sustainment are highly discouraged. Any custom software components must utilize standard, modern languages and frameworks compatible with the A1 Multi-Cloud Ecosystem target environment, prioritizing:

Salesforce Public Sector Solutions (Apex / Lightning Web Components/PSS)

ServiceNow Platform Configuration (JavaScript / Flow Designer)

OutSystems (Low-Code Platform)

Amazon Web Services (AWS) GovCloud (Angular frontend, node.js, or Java/Python microservices)

SUSTAINMENT & SUPPORT

Maintenance Cost: The vendor must provide the annual cost (in any) to sustain the system for each phase.  

Help Desk & User Support: The vendor must provide a robust sustainment model, including a dedicated help desk or ticketing system for unit schedulers (NCOs) to receive timely technical support, troubleshoot tool errors, and resolve configuration issues.

OBJECTIVE REQUIREMENTS (Desired / "Nice-to-Haves")

Predictive Analytics & Machine Learning: The ability to analyze historical scheduling, leave, and incident data using machine learning to predict future scheduling needs, identify long-term fatigue trends, and forecast manning shortfalls.

Mobile Accessibility: Secure access to the platform via personal mobile devices for schedule viewing and alerts.

Self-Service Portal: A user-facing portal allowing individuals to input their availability, request time off, and propose shift swaps directly for leadership approval.

AI-driven support: A user-facing closed-domain AI assistant that utilizes evidence-based sources to provide brief education to schedulers, leaders, and workers about optimizing shift schedules, rest periods, and individual behaviors for fatigue management and sleep health.

QUESTIONS FOR INDUSTRY

Product Delivery Model (COTS vs. Custom):

Is your proposed solution a commercially available, off-the-shelf (COTS) SaaS/software product, or does it require a custom-coded development effort?

If proposing a COTS product, what percentage of the "must-have" functional requirements in Section 3.0 can be met through standard, out-of-the-box configuration (point-and-click/built-in rules) versus custom code modification?

Tech Stack & Language Specifications (If Custom-Coded):

If your solution is custom-coded or built on an enterprise platform, what specific programming languages, frameworks, and database architectures does it utilize (e.g., Java, C#/.NET, Python, Angular, Salesforce LWC, ServiceNow Javascript)?

How does your development approach minimize technical debt and ensure ease of sustainment for government personnel?

Technical & Cyber Feasibility: Describe your approach to deploying a commercial or newly developed scheduling solution exclusively on AFNet (NIPRNet) utilizing CAC/PKI authentication.

Logic & Rules Engine: How does your software handle complex, intersecting rulesets (e.g., matching weapons qualifications + fatigue limits + NCO minimums per shift)?

Data Integration: Describe your experience ingesting demographic or HR data from authoritative DoD/Federal systems while maintaining CUI compliance.

Acquisition & ROM: Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) and your recommended pricing structure for Phase 1 (Single installation pilot) vs. Phase 2 (Enterprise scaling).

RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS

Interested parties are requested to submit a response of no more than 15 pages, addressing the questions outlined in Sections 3.0, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0, and 7.0. Responses should be submitted electronically in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format to derrick.manning@us.af.mil and corey.collins.12@us.af.mil no later than 17:00 EST on 2026-06-19. The subject line of the email should read: Response to AF-A1-RFI-SKED-APP-2026 - [Your Company Name].

Please include the following in your response:

Company Name, Address, and Point of Contact

CAGE Code and DUNS Number

Business Size and any applicable socio-economic classifications.

Recommended NAICS and PSC

DISCLAIMERS

This RFI is for market research purposes only and does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise, that the Department of the Air Force will take procurement action in this matter.

The HAF/A1 will not be responsible for any costs incurred by any entity in furnishing this information.

Responses to this RFI are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.

All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary; the HAF/A1 will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information for this RFI.

ADAP TEMPLATE 211-002 PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) JUL 2025

Defense Case Activity Tracking System, Enterprise (D-CATSe) Support Services

for the Department of War Office of Inspector General

PART 1

GENERAL INFORMATION

1. INTRODUCTION: This is a non-personal services contract to provide IT operational support. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn, is responsible to the Government.

2. BACKGROUND: The DoW OIG identifies, deters, and investigates fraud, waste, and abuse in the DoW. The DoW OIG keeps the Secretary of Defense and Congress fully and currently informed of fraud, waste, abuse, and deficiencies. The DoW OIG reports to the Secretary of War, the Congress, and recommends corrective actions in cases of fraud, waste, abuse, and deficiency; and on the progress made in implementation of corrective actions. The DoW OIG serves as the primary proponent for the Defense Inspector General (IG) system, for all Military Service, Component, and other IGs assigned to DoW. The DoW OIG has Special Agents, Investigative Personnel, Auditors, and Evaluators who must operate globally, conducting criminal and administrative investigations, audits, and evaluations to support the mission of the DoW OIG - ultimately supporting the DoW and the Warfighter.

DoW OIG organizational interfaces include Mission Support Team (MST) and Defense Criminal Investigative Service (DCIS) Senior Staff, the Defense Business System (DBS) Program Management Offices (PMO), the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), the MST Acquisition Directorate (AQD), and other front-end DoW OIG business Components.

MST Senior Staff

To be apprised of ongoing contractual activities, as well as engaged on strategic and collaborative organizational initiatives.

DBS PMOs

Manage cost, schedule, performance, and risk of their respective systems.

Lead the management, oversight, and implementation of application development and operational support.

Include project and technical management integration points, intent on collaborating with Contractor personnel to maintain the highest level of quality and productivity for operational systems.

OCIO

Include project and technical management integration points, accountable for the following.

Funding, sustainment, and performance of the DoW OIG DECC infrastructure and platform support, remediation of any associated application availability impediments, and vendor access requests for maintaining DoW OIG applications.

Funding, sustainment, and performance of all cybersecurity and information assurance functions, maintaining oversight and authority to formally accept risk on behalf of the DoW OIG.

Sustainment and performance of a central IT license repository, managing and procuring all licensing, reporting regular status updates and notifications of their successful renewals.

Disaster Recovery, Continuity of Operations (COOP), and back up and restoration of DoW OIG applications and services in accordance with the COOP Manager.

AQD

Contractual conduit positioned between the PMOs and Washington Headquarters Services/Acquisition Directorate, designating a Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR); assisting with contract consultation, review, and modifications.

DoW OIG front-end business Components

Leaders of DoW OIG business operation, customers of each PMO, operating as independent Functional Sponsors, providing Subject Matter Expertise (SME) resources regarding their business processes, developmental requirements, and operational needs.

End state, they are the reason for the support required – executing the DoW OIG’s mission on a daily basis.

3. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES: The Contractor shall provide IT operational support across a portfolio of like-systems and technologies as defined in this PWS except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract.

4. OBJECTIVES:

To acquire IT operational support across a portfolio of like systems and technologies, intent on realizing improved quality and performance for our customers, as well as gaining cost efficiencies across the task areas specified in Part 5, specific tasks

5. SCOPE: The DoW OIG is seeking support services, to supply holistic IT support. This partner will collaborate with DoW OIG personnel to oversee our portfolio of systems – ensuring quality, performance, and efficiencies are realized. They will provide strategic and tactical support, integrating with all DoW OIG echelons and external entities.  The DoW OIG requires DoW-approved industry standards and best practices to implement and sustain mature capabilities. These requirements are necessary to support various Functional Sponsors and customer bases, to include internal and external Federal organizations. Internal to DoW OIG, these entities include Administrative Investigations, the Defense Criminal Investigative Service, and other DoW OIG organic personnel. The designated  service provider will be our primary IT operational support integrator for the systems listed, collaborating with DoW OIG and existing Contractor personnel.

The Government may require surge support during the base or any option period, and surge modifications will be within the scope of the contract and provide increased support for the defined task areas of this PWS. Surge support over the life of the contract will not exceed 25% of the contractor’s total proposed cost/price for the base and all option periods, excluding any six-month extension of services pursuant to FAR 52.217-8.

6. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The Period of Performance (PoP) will consist of a base period of 1-year with four 1-year option periods starting as specified in the contract/task order award. 

7. CONTRACT TYPE: The Government will award a Firm-Fixed-Price Level-of-Effort (FFP-LOE) contract.

8. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: The primary place of performance will be at the Mark Center, 4800 Mark Center Drive, Alexandria, VA 22350 and the contractor’s site. The labor categories will be divided as necessary between the Mark Center and the contractor’s site. 

9. TELEWORK: As determined by the COR, contractor employees may work at an alternate place of performance (e.g., home, the contractor's facility, or another approved activity within the local travel area) on a regular, reoccurring basis or in cases of unforeseen conditions or contingencies (e.g., pandemic conditions, exercises, government closure due to inclement weather, etc.). Additionally, the contractor shall account for the whereabouts of their personnel should this information be requested by the COR. Non-emergency/non-essential contractors should not report to a closed government facility. Contractor shall prepare all deliverables and other contract documentation utilizing contractor resources. The contractor shall use best efforts to provide the same level of support as stated in the PWS. In the event the services are impacted, reduced, compromised, etc., the Contracting Officer (KO) or the contractor may request an equitable adjustment pursuant to the Changes clause of the contract.

10. HOURS OF OPERATION: The Contractor is responsible for providing services, between the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., Monday thru Friday except Federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility closings.  The Contractor must maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this PWS when the Government facility is not closed for the above reasons.  When hiring personnel, the Contractor shall keep in mind that the stability and continuity of the workforce are essential.  

11. RECOGNIZED HOLIDAYS: Government personnel observe the following holidays as governed by 5 U.S.C. § 6103. Government facilities will be closed and unavailable to Contractor personnel:

*If the date falls on a Saturday, the Government holiday is the preceding Friday. If the date falls on a Sunday, the Government holiday is the following Monday.

In addition to the days designated as holidays, the Government observes the following days:

Any other day designated by Federal Statute

Any other day designated by Executive Order

Any other day designated by the President’s Proclamation

12. QUALITY CONTROL/ASSURANCE:

12.1. Quality Control: The Contractor shall develop and maintain an effective quality control program to ensure services are performed in accordance with this PWS. The Contractor shall develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-recurrence of defective services. For both positive and negative performances, ratings shall be recorded in the Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS).

12.2. Quality Assurance: The Government shall evaluate the Contractor’s performance under this contract in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP). This plan is primarily focused on what the Government must do to ensure that the Contractor has performed in accordance with the performance standards. It defines how the performance standards will be applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum acceptable defect rate(s). Performance standards are detailed in Part 5 and summarized in Technical Exhibit 1.

13.1. Key Personnel: The personnel listed below are considered essential to the work being performed hereunder. Prior to substituting, removing, replacing, or diverting any of the specified individuals, the Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer 15 working days in advance and shall submit a written request and justification (including proposed substitutions) in sufficient detail to permit evaluation of the impact on this Contract. 23 March 2026 
1. Objective 
The U.S. Army U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) has a requirement to procure Genesis 
64 software application and its associated SupportWorx software support plan from Mitsubishi 
Electric Iconics Digital Solutions (MEIDS).  MEIDS software application is required by the 
Washington Headquarters Service (WHS) Facilities Operations Service Directorate (FOSD).   
 
2. Background 
FOSD has standardized Genesis 64 software application and its associated SupportWorx 
software support plan from MEIDS.  MEIDS software is the primary front-end application for the 
Facilities Related Control System (FRCS) and Building Automation System.  This software 
requires annual Enterprise Software License Agreement (ESLA) for the duration of the FRCS 
M&S Contract. 
   
3. Description 
Iconics Genesis 64 is a Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) software used by Facility engineers 
in control systems for monitoring, controlling, trending, and graphical representation of the 
heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems and equipment. It is a key component 
for maintaining and improving the efficiency of the HVAC systems. 
 
3.1. Iconics Genesis 64 Functions: 
 
• Provide 3D graphical renderings of HVAC equipment, fans, pumps, sensors, and dampers with 
animation of air and water flow. 
• Allow changes to the programs, user defined data point manipulation, and addition of new 
components. 
• Plot trends, status, and data points from all systems integrated. 
 
3.2. Technical Considerations 
 
• Iconics Genesis 64 software application is preapproved to be used on WHS FOSD computers. 
• Must be capable of obtaining software and activate licenses directly through the Iconics Web 
Licensing Utility portal or by direct request to Iconics. 
 
 
4. Requirement 
 
 
4.1.1. Software Delivery 
 
• Must be capable of obtaining software and activate licenses directly through the 
Iconics Web Licensing Utility portal or by direct request to Iconics. Provide FOSD 
access to a self-service portal to allow FOSD representatives to directly access 
ICONICS Web Licensing Utility portal to manage covered licenses without the need for 
any additional approvals   

 
• Licenses are registered to specific computer servers as specified by Licensee. License 
activation occurs when a license key is generated for the software. Upon the 
conclusion of the ELSA Period, any software for which licensee key has not been 
generated will no longer be accessible for activation and will be removed. FOSD shall 
have the right at its sole discretion to deactivate and return license removing it from 
coverage of the Enterprise Level SupportWorX plan.  
• Software License: For avoidance of doubt, the software installed, and the licenses 
granted under the ESLA, shall be perpetual licenses. The License Grant shall be per 
Iconics standard license agreement. 
• The licenses provided under this ESLA shall be limited to software installed, licensed and 
operating within the WHS location.

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Information and Technology (OIT), 
through its Infrastructure Operations (IO) organization, is responsible for delivering 
secure, reliable, and modern IT services that enable VA to fulfill its mission of providing 
healthcare and benefits to Veterans. IO supports a vast and complex enterprise 
environment spanning on-premises data centers, hybrid cloud platforms, and distributed 
systems serving millions of users including Veterans, employees, and partners. These 
services underpin mission-critical systems such as electronic health records, claims 
processing, benefits administration, cybersecurity, and enterprise-wide communications. 
 
Infrastructure Operations and Engineering (IO&E) is a domain within IO, focused on 
delivering comprehensive engineering and optimization support to operational 
environments. These services underpin mission-critical systems such as electronic 
health records, claims processing, benefits administration, cybersecurity, and 
enterprise-wide communications. IO&E domain seeks to unify and strengthen the 
foundational capabilities that support infrastructure operations across the enterprise. 
This functionality plays a critical role in enhancing the performance, efficiency, and 
reliability of infrastructure services by identifying and eliminating inefficiencies, 
streamlining processes, and implementing data-driven improvements. The desired 
outcome is a resilient, cost-effective, and scalable infrastructure that improves system 
availability, reduces operational costs, and enhances end-user satisfaction, ultimately 
supporting the delivery of high-quality services to Veterans. 
 
Within the IO&E domain, VA requires contractor support in three primary areas of focus: 
Infrastructure Enhancements, Data Center Operations, and Business Office Integration. 
 
Infrastructure Enhancements tasks require advanced analytics, automation, and 
architectural best practices to continuously refine infrastructure capabilities—ensuring 
systems are not only resilient and scalable, but also cost-effective and aligned with 
evolving mission needs. By embedding optimization into every layer of infrastructure 
support, VA’s operations aim to achieve greater agility, performance, and value.  
 
Data Center Operations tasks shall ensure the design, deployment, and maintenance of 
existing and future hybrid infrastructure environments that are secure, scalable, and 
aligned with evolving mission demands.  
 
Business Office Integration tasks play a strategic role in aligning infrastructure initiatives 
with enterprise priorities, managing resources, and tracking performance outcomes. 
Business Office Integration outcomes serve as the central coordination point for day-to-
day operational needs, service intake, and stakeholder engagement. 
 
Together, these functional areas form a cohesive, mission-driven domain that 
empowers OIT and IO to deliver optimized, reliable, and future-ready services.

maintaining high availability and reliability. This project will also encompass the 
development and maintenance of a strategic infrastructure plan that monitors 
performance and ensures alignment with VA’s broader objectives. Key components

strategic planning and development of data center and cloud assets, as well as 
monitoring performance to ensure alignment with VA's objectives. The scope also

leveraging best practices in portfolio management, the project aims to enhance 
decision-making processes, prioritize investments, and ensure efficient allocation of 
resources. This will involve the integration of advanced tools and methodologies for 
tracking and reporting on the status and performance of the infrastructure portfolio.

Special Notice of Intent to Sole Source 140M0126Q0029

Synopsis:

This Notice is issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Deviation Parts FAR 12.201-1(c)(2)(i), Simplified Solicitation Procedures, and FAR 12.102(a), Restricting Competition, and FAR 5.101(a), Presolicitation Notice.

The U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI), Office of Acquisition and Property Management, on behalf of the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM), is the contracting office for this procurement. The purpose of this notice is to announce the Government’s intent to award a sole source Purchase Order to KAPPA North America, Inc., 1500 Citywest BlVD STE 741, Houston, TX 77042-2553, for PTA Software.

BOEM requires software capable of performing pressure transient analysis (PTA). The software must have the following technical criteria. Data Input and Processing: ability to load standard Excel and ASCII file formats, accept PVT datasets, run QAQC on pressure gauge data, run shut-in extrapolations and deconvolution. Diagnostic analysis through plotting methods: log analysis, semi-log and other plotting such as Horner, square root, and tandem. Analytical modeling: scaled to various boundaries, including wellbore, well, and reservoir and able to change and accept different fault boundaries. Numerical Models: 2D and 3D capabilities. Post Model manipulation: change parameters to improve fits and run the same model with multiple parameters. Run multiple types of pressure tests: standard pressure transient tests, downhole tests, multi-rate gas tests, multi-layer tests.

In addition to the above requirements, the PTA software must provide results and interoperability with other applications that will be purchased in the future. These additional applications must perform rate transient analysis, formation tests, fluid modeling, and results that may be run through numerical modeling software.

Kappa Engineering is the only source capable of providing the PTA technical criteria required along with interoperability with other applications. The purchase order award will have a period of performance 12 months from award. The anticipated award will be a twelve (12) months base period of performance and four (4) twelve (12) months option years for a total of sixty (60) months. The applicable NAICS Code is 541519 (Other Computer Related Services).

This is NOT a request for competitive quotes. The intent of the Special Notice is for “informational purposes” only. However, any and all information received by the point of contact (POC) listed below, by 9:00 a.m., ET, Monday, June 15, 2026 will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this action based on this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. POC: Ms. Michelle Potter, DOI, Office of Acquisition and Property Management, 45600 Woodland 1Road, Mail Stop VAE-AMD, Sterling, VA 20166. Information can be emailed to Ms. Michelle Potter at michelle_potter@ios.doi.gov.

Statement of Work for Audio Visual Contract in Building 9004 
 
 
1. SCOPE OF WORK 
The scope of this project includes the design, installation, and integration of an audio-visual system 
in Building 9004. The system shall include audio and video conferencing capabilities, digital 
signage, and a control system for easy operation. The project shall also include training for 
designated staff members on the use and maintenance of the system. 
2. SITE SURVEY 
 
Due to the complexity of the existing system and the requirement to integrate new equipment, it is 
highly recommended that the contractor perform a site survey prior to submitting a bid proposal. 
 
3. DESIGN 
The audio-visual system will be engineered to meet the unique requirements of Building 9004. Its 
design will account for the dimensions and layout of the designated rooms, the system's intended 
applications, and a comprehensive plan for all equipment placement and cable routing. All 
programming involving the AV  control system must be coordinated with the Government Project 
Manager during the design phase, and approved by the Government Project Manager prior to ﬁnal 
programming. These requirements must provide a minimum of two weeks prior to the 
commencement of any on premise work. 
4. EQUIPMENT 
The audio-visual system shall include the following equipment: 
Audio and video conferencing equipment 
- Display monitors 
- Projectors 
- Speakers 
- Camera(s) 
- Control system 
- Digital signage player and screens 
- Cables and connectors 
- Mounting hardware 
- Switch, Keyboard, Video, Mouse (KVM) 
- Signal Converts  
- Audio ampliﬁer  
- (1) Elmo/MX-P2 
 
 
 

5. EQUIPMENT REQUIREMTNS 
 
a. Country of Origin: All supplied equipment must be compliant with the Trade 
Agreements Act (TAA). The contractor shall certify that no products are manufactured in 
prohibited countries, including China. 
b. Prohibited Wireless Capabilities inside secure area and mass brief rooms: All Display 
monitors, Projectors, and Speakers are strictly forbidden from having any integrated 
Wireless (Wi-Fi), Bluetooth, or Near Field Communication (NFC) capabilities. 
c. Government Approval for Displays inside secure area: The contractor must submit the 
proposed Make and Model of all TVs/Monitors to the government technical lead for 
written approval prior to procurement. 
d. Camera Connection Standards: All video camera signals that cross the facility control 
line (FCL) must be transported via ﬁber-optic cable. The ﬁber signal must be converted 
to DisplayPort at the destination endpoint. 
e. Audio Ampliﬁer: An appropriately rated commercial-grade audio ampliﬁer must be 
supplied to power all installed speakers. 
f.  All KVM switches provided under this SOW must be NIAP-Approved. To be considered 
compliant, the selected Make and Model must be listed on the NIAP Product Compliant 
List (PCL) at the time of procurement.  
i. Each brieﬁng room inside the secure area, and mission planning area shall be 
equipped with one (1) 8-port, NIAP-approved KVM switch. 
1. To facilitate future maintenance and the addition of new connections, 
the KVM switch must be installed on a professional grade sliding rack 
shelf or hinged service panel. This installation must allow the KVM to be 
pulled forward or swung open, providing clear and unobstructed access 
to all rear ports and connections without requiring the disassembly of 
the podium/credenza itself. 
ii. The contractor shall provide and install a single, integrated video distribution 
system for the secure mass brieﬁng room. This system must be a NIAP-
Approved, 8-input by 6-output Secure KVM Multiview Matrix and Video Selector. 
 
This system must deliver the following integrated capabilities: 
  
• Multiview Function: The system must be capable of simultaneously displaying 
multiple sources (e.g., four of the eight inputs) in various layouts across the 
designated operator monitors. 
• Video Wall Function: The system shall be able to process a single source input 
and display it as one uniﬁed image seamlessly across a multi-monitor array 
(e.g., a 2x2 video wall). 
• Matrix Switching Function: The system must allow for the ﬂexible routing of any 
input source to any of the six display outputs independently. 
• Document Camera: The contractor shall also provide one (1) Elmo MX-P2 
document camera or a similar government-approved equivalent, fully integrated 
into the system. 

iii. The contractor shall provide an 8 input x 4 display output NIAP-Approved Secure 
KVM Multiview Video Wall Controller for the non-secure area brief room. This 
single, integrated system must provide the following three core functions: 
1. A Video Wall function to display any single source system seamlessly 
across all four monitors as one uniﬁed image. 
g. The Security Office inside the secure area shall be equipped with four (4) 4-port, NIAP-
approved KVM switch 
h. Secure Area Mass Brieﬁng Room Podium Conﬁguration: Provide a 24” monitor to be 
mounted with a monitor arm install surface-mounted connection plate featuring, at a 
minimum of one DisplayPort output from the KVM to attach a monitor as well as.  
i. Unsecure Mass Brieﬁng Room Podium Conﬁguration: install surface-mounted 
connection plate featuring, at a minimum of 2 DisplayPort output from the KVM to 
attach a monitor as well as.  
j. All equipment furnished must not require additional licenses for use  
Upon project completion, the contractor is required to furnish the customer with speciﬁc drawings 
and diagrams. These deliverables will include industry-standard functional line drawings for the 
Video Teleconferencing Systems, Program Video/Audio, Control Systems, and Dial Isolation. 
 
6. INSTALLATION 
The contractor shall install all equipment listed in Section 3.0 in a professional manner, adhering to 
all relevant industry standards and the speciﬁc requirements below: 
- Mounting of displays, speakers, and cameras 
- Connection of all equipment and cabling 
- Conﬁguration of the control system 
- Calibration of audio and video equipment 
- Testing and veriﬁcation of the system 
- Cable Management 
 
7. Programing Control Panel 
 
The touch screen control shall be programmed with functionality and ease of use as a priority. The 
system will be utilized by a variety of users requiring the programming interface to be easy to use, 
requiring minimal training, if any. The control system shall, at a minimum, control the following 
functions: 
• Display Monitors On/Off 
• Source Select and Destination Control 
• Video Source select and Destination Control 
• Camera Controls 
• VTC Codecs Control 
• Audio Conferencing Dial Up, Connect, Disconnect, Mute, and 

• Volume Control 
• Program Audio Level Control 
• Multi Classiﬁcation Control features 
• System Wakeup / Shutdown Master Control 
 
8. INTEGRATION 
System integration is a critical component of this SOW. The contractor is solely responsible for 
ensuring end-to-end compatibility. 
- Connection to the network  
- Conﬁguration of the control system to work with existing systems 
- Testing and veriﬁcation of the integrated system 
9. TRAINING 
The contractor shall provide systems training for up to ﬁve (5) individuals after the testing phase of 
the installation. Training shall include system startup and shut down, basic and advanced 
operation of all related systems and basic troubleshooting including trouble reporting procedures. 
 
10.  WORK REQUIREMENTS: 
Work for this project shall be executed in the best and most workmanlike manner by qualiﬁed and 
efficient installers skilled in their trade. The contractor shall perform all operations in a manner that 
will result in a professional and expeditiously completed project. The work shall be in strict 
accordance with the prevailing industry standards and to manufacturers written speciﬁcations. 
Installations which do not meet manufacturer’s speciﬁcations whenever found shall be the 
responsibility of the contractor to rectify at the contractor’s expense. Contractor shall provide all 
incidentals necessary to accomplish a complete and thorough installation. Contractor shall ensure 
all such incidentals do not visually or aesthetically detract from the ﬁnished pieces. All incidental 
hardware shall be installed in accordance with manufacturers’ recommendations. Work areas shall 
be maintained in a neat, clean, safe condition and shall, at a minimum, be cleaned with all waste 
and packing materials removed at the end of each shift. The Contractor shall collect all trash, 
debris, refuse, garbage, etc. generated and remove it from site at the end of each shift. Disposal of 
discarded materials is the Contractor’s responsibility and shall be by sanitary landﬁll or other 
approved methods, and shall conform to all local, state, and federal guidelines, criteria, and 
regulations. The contractor shall take precautions to prevent damage to government property. The 
contractor shall repair or replace damaged items at no additional cost to the government. 
Contractor shall provide all protective materials necessary i.e. carts, moving blankets, taping, etc. 
to ensure all items to be moved and building ﬁnished surfaces are well protected throughout the 
entire process. 
 
 
 

11. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 
The Luke AFB Squad Ops 6 project must begin no later than 01 April 2026 such as the design 
process. Installation dates will be agreed upon at least 4 weeks in advance and ﬁnal installation 
should occur NLT 30 May 2026 unless the government POC agrees upon a later date. 
 
12. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: 
Installation of all furniture/materials will occur inside building 9004, Luke AFB, AZ. Building 9004 is 
a single-story building. Entrance will be coordinated with the Government Representatives at 
B9004. All work shall be completed with minimal disruption and within standard business hours 
outlined in item #9 of this Statement of Work. 
 
13. SCHEDULE/MILESTONES: 
Installation will be completed by adequate number of personnel to expediently ﬁnish the project 
and reduce amount of time impacting is closed to the population. The desired 
installation duration will not exceed 30 business days. All delays must be communicated with the 
government representative if expected. Installation will occur during the hours of 8AM to 5PM 
Monday through Friday, excluding Federal Holidays. 
The following phasing plan will be used to ensure a smooth installation process while installation is 
happening concurrently with the Audio-Visual installers. 
 
- Week 1: Secure Area 
- Week 2: Common Area / Offices outside of Vault / Aircrew Flight Equipment, student rooms, 
and conference room. 
- Week 3: Maintenance Offices, common areas, and maintenance conference room. 
 
The above is not an all-inclusive phasing plan, but a starting point to ensure installers are not 
conﬂicted with additional furniture vendors in the building. Real-time deconﬂiction and 
coordination will prevail.  
 
14.  ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: 
The government shall inspect all work performed by the Contractor. Work performance shall be 
deemed satisfactory and acceptable to the government when the Government representative 
declares the project satisfactory. Contractor representatives are not authorized to leave the job site 
and consider the installation complete until a government representative has reviewed the 
installation for accuracy and signed the installation paperwork. 

All signal converters must be explicitly tested and guaranteed by the contractor to be compatible 
with the entire KVM system. 
The contractor must deliver a complete and accurate Final Equipment Inventory List. This list must 
be a digital spreadsheet detailing the Make, Model, and Serial Number for every piece of 
equipment, broken down by individual room placement 
 
 
15. WARRANTY REPAIR RESPONSE TIME 
 
Contractor shall respond by telephone to receive calls from the Government Project Manager 
for repair service within 4 hours of receipt of telephonic notiﬁcation. Response time shall not 
include holidays or weekends unless prior approval is obtained from the CO. After responding 
to a service call for repair, if the contractor determines the repair is a major repair, then the 
Contractor shall submit a cost breakdown and estimated time frame for repair to the 
Government Project Manager for determination of feasibility of repair on that particular piece of 
equipment. All labor performed by the contractor shall be warrantied for a period of at least one 
(1) year 
 
16. OTHER REQUIREMENTS 
Contractor shall provide the full names, birthdates, and driver’s license numbers of each installer 
associated with this installation as required for sponsorship onto Luke Air Force Base. Quantities 
and work time schedules of installation crews must be provided prior to the start of any work. Such 
information shall be submitted to the government representative two weeks prior to the start of 
work. Base access will be granted to those listed on the above-mentioned document on a daily 
basis.

Annual Maintenance and Support for Thermo Fisher Watson Laboratory Information 
Management System (LIMS)  
 
FDA-75F40126Q00183

SECTION 1 – PRODUCT LIST AND DELIVERY INFORMATION 
This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the Federal 
Acquisition Regulation (FAR) format, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. 
This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; Offers are being requested and a separate written 
solicitation will not be issued.  It is the Government's intent to issue a Firm Fixed Priced Purchase Order in 
accordance with FAR Part 12.  
The solicitation number is FDA- 75F40126Q00183. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Quote 
(RFQ).  This is a  Full and Open Competition requirement.  
The Government is in no way obligated to make an award, nor to pay any costs incurred by the Contractor 
in preparing and submitting its quote.  
1.1 Background 
The Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) perform an essential public health task by making 
sure that safe and effective drugs are available to improve the health of people in the United States. As part 
of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), CDER regulates over the counter and prescription drugs, 
including biological therapeutics and generic drugs. This work covers more than just medicines. For 
example, fluoride toothpaste, antiperspirants, dandruff shampoos and sunscreens are all consider ed 
"drugs.".  
The Division of Applied Regulatory Science (DARS) with CDER’s Office Translational Science/ Office 
of Clinical Pharmacology also does internal research requiring best in class data and sample management 
capabilities. The need to track materials and informa tion both internally and with many external 
collaborators and contractors is driving the necessity for a robust Laboratory Information Management 
System (LIMS). The chosen system will reduce manual and flat file manipulations, increase efficiency, and 
adhere to Federal regulation and compliance standards. 


1.2 Objective 
The Division of Applied Regulatory Science (DARS) currently operates 9 licenses of Watson LIMS for use 
by bioanalytical scientists and management. The DARS bioanalytical lab executes a variety of internal and 
external studies including clinical and non- clinical pharmacokinetic- pharmacodynamic modeling, 
bioequivalence, drug metabolism and transport, in-vivo/in- vitro correlations, and drug- drug interaction 
studies bioanalytical analyses at both the clinical and pre- clinical levels. Often these projects are of high -
visibility, and mission critical (Opioids drug interaction, In- vivo conversion of ranitidine to carcinogen, 
sunscreens dermal absorption, cannabinoids, etc.) for the FDA leading to stringent deadlines and necessity 
for high quality data. The objective is to extend maintenance and support for Watson LIMS for the Division 
of Applied Regulatory Science (DARS).

SECTION 2 – CONTRACT ADMINISTRATION 
2.1 Contract Management

2.2 Contracting Officer’s Authority 
 
The Contracting Officer (CO) is the only person with authority to act as agent of the Government under 
this contract. Only the Contracting Officer has authority to: (1) direct or negotiate any changes in the RFQ; 
(2) modify or extend the period of performance; (3) change the delivery schedule; (4) authorize 
reimbursement to the Contractor any costs incurred during the performance of this contract; or (5) otherwise 
change any terms and conditions of this contract. No statement, whether oral or written, by anyone other 
than the Contracting Officer, shall be interpreted as modifying the terms and conditions of this award. It is 
the Contractor’s responsibility to contact the CO immediately if there is even the appearance of any 
technical direction that is or may be outside the scope of the  award. The Government will not reimburse 
the Contractor for any work not authorized by the Contracting Officer, including work outside the scope of 
the award.  
The Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) is responsible for: (1) monitoring the Contractor's 
technical progress, including the surveillance and assessment of performance and recommending to the 
Contracting Officer changes in requirements; (2) interpreting the contract and any other technical 
performance requirements; (3) performing technical evaluation as required; (4) performing technical 
inspections and acceptances required by this contract; and (5) assisting in the resolution of technical 
problems encountered during performance.  
2.3 Security and Privacy 
A. Baseline Security Requirements 
1) Applicability. The requirements herein apply whether the entire contract or order (hereafter 
“contract”), or portion thereof, includes either or both of the following: 
a. Access (Physical or Logical) to Government Information:  A Contractor (and/or any 
subcontractor) employee will have or will be given the ability to have, routine physical (entry) 
or logical (electronic) access to government information. 
b. Operate a Federal System Containing Information:  A Contractor (and/or any subcontractor) 
will operate a federal system and information technology containing data that supports the 
HHS mission. In addition to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 2.1 definition 
of “information technology” (IT), the term as used in this section includes computers, ancillary 
equipment (including imaging peripherals, input, output, and storage devices necessary for 
security and surveillance), peripheral equipment designed to be controlled by the central 
processing unit of a computer, software, firmware and similar procedures, services (including 
support services), and related resources. 
2) Safeguarding Information and Information Systems.  In accordance with the Federal 
Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS)199, Standards for Security Categorization 
of Federal Information and Information Systems, the Contractor (and/or any subcontractor) shall: 
a. Protect government information and information systems in order to ensure: 
• Confidentiality, which means preserving authorized restrictions on access and disclosure, 
based on the security terms found in this contract, including means for protecting personal 
privacy and proprietary information; 
• Integrity, which means guarding against improper information modification or destruction, 
and ensuring information non-repudiation and authenticity; and 

• Availability, which means ensuring timely and reliable access to and use of information. 
b. Provide security for any Contractor systems, and information contained therein, connected to an 
FDA network or operated by the Contractor on behalf of FDA regardless of location.  In 
addition, if new or unanticipated threats or hazards are discovered by ei ther the agency or 
contractor, or if existing safeguards have ceased to function, the discoverer shall immediately, 
within one (1) hour or less, bring the situation to the attention of the other party.  This includes 
notifying the FDA Systems Management  Center (SMC) within one (1) hour of 
discovery/detection in the event of an information security incident. 
c. Adopt and implement the policies, procedures, controls, and standards required by the 
HHS/FDA Information Security Program to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability 
of government information and government information systems for which the Contractor is 
responsible under this contract or to which the Contractor may otherwise have access under this 
contract. Obtain the FDA Information Security Program security requirements, outlined in the 
FDA Information Security and Privacy Policy (IS2P ), by contacting the CO/COR or emailing 
your ISSO.   
d.  Comply with the Privacy Act requirements and tailor FAR clauses as needed.   
3) Information Security Categorization. In accordance with FIPS 199 and National Institute of 
Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-60, Volume II: Appendices to 
Guide for Mapping Types of Information and Information Systems to Security Categories, 
Appendix C, and based on information provided by the ISSO or other security representative, 
the risk level for each Security Objective and the Overall Risk Level, which is the highest 
watermark of the three factors (Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability) of the information 
or information system are the following: 
Confidentiality:   [  ] Low [X] Moderate [  ] High 
Integrity:   [  ] Low [X] Moderate [  ] High 
Availability:   [X] Low [  ] Moderate [  ] High 
Overall Risk Level:  [  ] Low [X ] Moderate [  ] High 
Based on information provided by the Privacy Office, system/data owner, or other privacy 
representative, it has been determined that this solicitation/contract involves: 
[  ] No PII [ X] Yes PII 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII). Per the OMB Circular A-130, “PII is information that 
can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, either alone or when combined with 
other information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual.” Examples of PII include, but 
are not limited to the following: Social Security number, date and place of birth, mother’s maiden 
name, biometric records, etc. 
PII Confidentiality Impact Level has been determined to be:  
[ ] Low [X] Moderate [  ] High 
The Privacy Act does not apply. 

4) Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI).  CUI is defined as “information that laws, 
regulations, or Government-wide policies require to have safeguarding or dissemination controls, 
excluding classified information.” The Contractor (and/or any subcontractor) must comply with 
Executive Order 13556, Controlled Unclassified Information, (implemented at 3 CFR, part 2002) 
when handling CUI. 32 C.F.R. 2002.4(aa). As implemented the term “handling” refers to “…any 
use of CUI, including but not limited to marking, safeguarding, transporting, disseminating, re- 
using, and disposing of the information.” 81 Fed. Reg. 63323.   All sensitive information that has 
been identified as CUI by a regulation or statute, handled by this solicitation/contract, shall be: 
a. marked appropriately; 
b. disclosed to authorized personnel on a Need-To-Know basis; 
c. protected in accordance with NIST SP 800- 53, Security and Privacy Controls for 
Federal Information Systems and Organizations  applicable baseline if handled by a 
Contractor system operated on behalf of the agency, or NIST SP 800- 171, Protecting 
Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Information Systems and 
Organizations if handled by internal Contractor system; and 
d. returned to FDA control, destroyed when no longer needed, or held until otherwise 
directed. 
Destruction of information and/or data shall be accomplished in accordance with NIST SP 800-88, 
Guidelines for Media Sanitization and the FDA IS2P Appendix T: Sanitization of Computer -
Related Storage Media. 
5) Protection of Sensitive Information. For security purposes, information is or may be sensitive 
because it requires security to protect its confidentiality, integrity, and/or availability. The 
Contractor (and/or any subcontractor) shall protect all government information that is or may be 
sensitive in accordance with OMB Memorandum M -06-16, Protection of Sensitive Agency 
Information by securing it with a FIPS 140-2 validated solution.

Questions and Answers – FA487726QA136 – 355 Wing VTC Upgrade 
Questions in black, USAF responses in red. 
1. Would the government consider an extension to provide a response within 14 days 
vs the current 5 days to allow for Q&A and mitigate risks?

are due 26 May 2026. 
 
2. The PWS does not provide sufficient information to provide a quote and timeline, as 
is. Was a site visit conducted to gather this information, or can additional 
information be provided?

and USAF stakeholders. What additional information are you requesting? 
 
3. Or is the intent to a provide a quote for a PM and Lead Engineer? Post-award, they

␟Questions+and+Answers-+Wing+VTC.pdf␞

1. Secure VTC Codec Platform: 
For the secure VTC capability, the codec platform traditionally utilized in many 
government deployments has been the Cisco Codec Pro; however, that platform 
has recently reached End-of-Life status. Its replacement, the Cisco Codec Pro G2, 
is currently showing an estimated manufacturer lead time of approximately 140 
days. Does your organization have any existing standards, operational preferences, 
or prior approvals regarding Cisco versus Poly codec platforms that would assist 
offerors in determining the preferred approach for this requirement? 
A: Because we are working to build a homogenous Cisco environment whenever 
possible, our preference tends to be Cisco.   
2. DPAS Rating: 
Due to current manufacturer lead times affecting certain AV and collaboration 
hardware, will this requirement be issued with a DPAS rating to assist with 
procurement prioritization and schedule compliance? 
A: No. 
3. Lectern / Podium Quantity: 
The RFQ appears to indicate a quantity of one (1) lectern/podium. During the site 
visit,  two existing lecterns were observed within the conference room. Can the 
Government please conﬁrm whether the requirement is for replacement of one 
lectern only, or whether both lecterns should be replaced to maintain a matching 
appearance within the room? 
A: The requirement should be for two matching podiums.  One will have the setup with 
2 monitors, docking stations, and KVM to switch between NIPRnet and SIPRnet 
smoothly. 
4. Cisco GEMSS: 
If the proposed solution utilizes Cisco collaboration components, does your 
organization have an active DoD Cisco GEMSS agreement/contract available for use 
on this project? If so, providing the applicable GEMSS contract information 
(Available from you A6 / CIO), may allow offerors to leverage existing DoD enterprise 
licensing and support entitlements, potentially reducing duplicated software and 
maintenance costs within the proposal. 

A: Our guidance for GEMSS use is solely for network equipment and licenses, such as 
routers, switches, and Catalyst Center.  It is not meant to be leveraged for VTC 
procurement and maintenance. 
 
 
5. How many rooms will be involved in this quote? 
A: 2 rooms (conference room and communication room) 
 
6. Are there any dimensions / drawings / photos available for the rooms? Seating 
capacity per space? Is the ceiling accessible in each space? 
**The equipment selection and quote relies heavily on the dimensions of the 
spaces and intended usage. ** 
A: Please see the attached diagram and additional 3 pictures.  
 
7. Are there any specs as far as number of inputs / outputs and displays for each 
space? 
A:  At least 5 spaces at the conference table (head seat, plus 4 side seats) should have 
NIPR ethernet drops and the ability to push their display if desired.  The majority 
of the time, the display will be pushed from the podium or the head seat at the 
table.  But if the other 4 spaces with drops can push their display, that would 
lend itself to a collaborative environment. 
 
 
8. Are there any special concerns about any of the spaces that you would like 
addressed? 
A: The 5 ethernet drops and display ports at the conference table should be easily hidden 
for increased aesthetic appeal.   
9. Are there existing cable paths? 

A: There must be, due to what equipment has existed there in the past, but we can only 
speculate where they are.  Be prepared to create a new path if the old one can’t 
be determined. 
 
10. Will equipment be housed in the spaces or in adjoining closets? 
A: Equipment will be housed in the 2 rooms. 
 
11. Will there be any clearance requirements for personnel performing the installation? 
A: Secret clearance will be needed as we are asking for both NIPRnet & SIPRnet systems. 
 
 
12. Most AF locations are moving away from codecs and adopting MS Teams for NIPR 
and SIPR. Do you still require the NIPR and SIPR codecs? I believe GVS ended 
support for NIPR Codecs a while back. 
A: I don’t believe a CODEC was ever speciﬁcally requested by the govt in this tech 
solution.  We want the ability to host NIPR and SIPR teams meetings, as well as 
GVS.  Whether that’s through a CODEC or something else is not a sticking point.  
A simple UI with a good audio/vis set-up is the goal.   
 
13. Is there any ﬂexibility on the 8-hour on-site response time? We estimate a 24-hour 
on-site response time for your location given current resources. 
A: Yes, there’s ﬂexibility.

Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
For NIPR/SIPR Audio/Visual VTC Suite Integration & Support 
1.0 Introduction & Background 
This Performance Work Statement (PWS) outlines the requirements for a non-personnel services 
contract to provide all necessary management, personnel, equipment, and services for the turn-
key design, integration, installation, and maintenance of NIPRNET and SIPRNET Audio/Visual (A/V) 
and Video Teleconferencing (VTC) suites. The contractor shall ensure the ﬁnal solution is fully 
compliant with all applicable Department of War (DoW), Air Force, and local directives and 
standards. 
• 1.1 Scope: The contractor shall perform the design, engineering, procurement, installation, 
testing, training, and ongoing maintenance of complete VTC suites. The solution must 
support both unclassiﬁed (NIPR) and classiﬁed (SIPR) operations and be fully interoperable 
with the Microsoft Teams application and the Global Video Services (GVS) application. 
• 1.2 Period of Performance: The period of performance shall be for one (1) twelve-month 
base year, with four (4) twelve-month optional ordering periods for subsequent extension of 
services. 
• 1.3 Place of Performance: The work shall be performed at the 355th Wing, Davis-Monthan 
AFB, AZ. 
• 1.4 Applicable Documents: The contractor shall comply with the latest versions of the 
following: 
• DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) relevant to VTCs, networked 
equipment, and related software. 
• DoDIN Approved Products List (APL). 
• Trade Agreement Act (TAA) Compliance regulations. 
 
2.0 Speciﬁc Tasks 
The contractor shall perform the following tasks to deliver a complete and operational VTC solution. 
• 2.1 Task 1: Program Management 
• 2.1.1 Project Management: The contractor shall manage all aspects of project 
execution, including planning, scheduling, and implementation to ensure timely 
delivery and installation with minimal disruption to government operations. 
• 2.1.2 Project Plan: The contractor shall develop and deliver a detailed Project 
Management Plan (PMP) within 10 business days of contract award. The PMP shall 

include, at a minimum, a project schedule (Gantt chart), risk management plan, and 
key personnel list. 
• 2.1.3 Quality Control: The contractor shall develop and maintain a Quality Control 
Plan (QCP) to ensure all services are performed in accordance with this PWS and 
industry best practices. 
• 2.1.4 Key Personnel: The contractor shall provide qualiﬁed key personnel, including 
a Project Manager, Lead Engineer, and certiﬁed technicians to oversee and execute 
all contract requirements. 
• 2.2 Task 2: System Design, Engineering, and Installation 
• 2.2.1 System Design: The contractor shall provide a comprehensive technical 
design package for government approval prior to ordering equipment. The design 
package shall include detailed engineering plans, equipment placement drawings, 
wiring diagrams, and a complete network diagram.  
• Using the system should not require any advanced understanding of 
network architecture or hardware/software troubleshooting.  
• A streamlined user guide should be furnished to allow users to power on/off 
the system and include troubleshooting steps for common issues.  The 
guide should be tailored to the speciﬁc system install. 
• 2.2.2 Equipment Procurement and Installation: The contractor shall provide and 
install all necessary A/V and VTC equipment, including, but not limited to: 
• TAA-compliant, DoDIN APL-listed VTC codecs, displays, cameras, 
microphones, and control systems. 
• A podium that has separate laptop docking capability for NIPRNET and 
SIPRnet computers.. 
• VTC codecs that are current models, sustainable for a minimum of ﬁve 
years, and interoperable with Cisco bridge/expressway technology and 
laptop devices from multiple manufacturers. 
• 2.2.3 Cabling and Cleanup: The contractor shall perform a complete installation, 
including all necessary cabling. All cabling shall be consolidated, organized, and 
hidden from view when possible. Upon completion, the contractor shall be 
responsible for the removal and disposal of all legacy wiring and equipment being 
replaced. 
• 2.3 Task 3: System Functionality and Performance 

• 2.3.1 Video Performance: The system shall support a video matrix with multiple 
inputs/outputs at 1080p resolution or better. High-deﬁnition PTZ (Pan-Tilt-Zoom) 
cameras shall be installed to provide high-quality video. 
• 2.3.2 Audio Performance: The system shall include a digital sound processor with 
acoustic echo cancellation. The contractor shall install a combination of ceiling-
mounted and tabletop microphones as required to achieve the best audio feedback 
on the distant end. All tabletop microphones must feature individual physical 
mute/unmute controls. 
• 2.3.3 Control System: The contractor shall provide and program a user-friendly 
touch-panel control system (e.g., Crestron or equivalent). The system shall include: 
• A ﬁxed primary touch-panel and a portable touch-panel for the head of the 
conference room table. 
• A "one-touch" function to seamlessly switch all room systems (displays, 
audio, VTC classiﬁcation) between NIPRNET and SIPRNET sessions without 
requiring manual re-cabling by the user. 
• 2.4 Task 4: Security 
• 2.4.1 STIG Compliance: The contractor shall ensure all installed equipment and 
system conﬁgurations are compliant with all applicable DISA STIGs. The contractor 
shall provide a completed STIG checklist as a deliverable. 
• 2.4.2 Network Separation: For the SIPR suite, the system must be designed and 
installed to enforce strict physical and logical separation between classiﬁed and 
unclassiﬁed networks, preventing any data crossover. Physical separation of 
hardware and cabling should meet the National Security Agency’s TEMPEST 
requirements for separation of unclassiﬁed and classiﬁed equipment. 
• 2.4.3 Personnel Security: All contractor personnel performing work on-site shall 
possess the appropriate security clearances required for the work location and data 
being handled. 
• 2.5 Task 5: Support and Maintenance 
• 2.5.1 Preventative Maintenance: The contractor shall perform and document 
regularly scheduled preventative maintenance inspections (PMI) on a quarterly 
basis to inspect, clean, and test all installed equipment. 
• 2.5.2 Technical Support: The contractor shall provide technical support during 
normal business hours (0730-1630, M-F), with an option for emergency after-hours 
support. This shall include remote troubleshooting and on-site repairs as needed. 
Contact information should be posted clearly on or near the system. 

• 2.5.3 Training: The contractor shall provide comprehensive on-site training to 
designated government personnel on the operation and basic user maintenance of 
the VTC suites. The training shall include a laminated user guide for each room. 
Training from the contractor can be given as required when new government 
personnel are onboarded throughout the duration of the contract. 
• 2.5.4 Warranty: The contractor shall provide a comprehensive warranty covering all 
equipment and workmanship for a period of one year from the date of ﬁnal system 
acceptance by the government.
