PURCHASE DESCRIPTION
SALES TAX EXEMPTION
The contractor is hereby advised that the United States Government and Agencies thereof are exempt from State and Local Government tax by virtue 
of Article 6 of the United States Constitution. No exemption certificate is required. 
1. INTRODUCTION
The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Corona Division, requires software licenses.
2. BACKGROUND
Corona Division requires procurement of software license renewal.
3. REQUIREMENTS
3.1 The contractor shall provide the required brand name equipment listed in Section B - Supplies.
3.2 Offerors shall be an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), authorized dealer, authorized distributor or authorized reseller for the proposed 
supplies, equipment and/or services. Offerors shall provide proof of authorization verified by an authorization letter or other documents from the 
OEM at the time of offer submission and prior to closure of solicitation.
3.3 The contractor shall provide preventative maintenance and system/equipment coverage on the stand-alone unclassified T1V collaboration system 
in the PEO IWS War Room system to ensure no malfunctions and underlying errors/issues.
3.4 The contractor shall conduct one on-site preventative maintenance inspection per option year to ensure the stand alone classified system is fully 
functional. The contractor shall repair malfunctions and errors as required from these preventative maintenance site visits.
3.5 The contractor shall provide, within two days of request, helpdesk and remote support for requested issues and malfunctions of the stand-alone 
classified system from PEO IWS Staff. 
3.6 The contractor shall provide, within two days of service call, on-site system support to troubleshoot and repair errors and malfunctions of the 
stand-alone classified system. 
3.7 The contractor shall provide repair and replacement of classified system products through warranty and return manufacturer authorization support. 
3.8 The contractor shall provide Plus Maintenance for repair War Room functionality as required and shall enable full functionality of War Room 
systems and requirements.
3.9 The contractor shall provide a 3-year, 365 day per year Support Agreement for the existing products and services to maintain the existing 
unclassified War Room system/equipment requirement and functionality.
3.10 The Contractor shall provide three (3) T1V ThinkHub licenses to enable continued use of the existing classified system. The system consists of a 
primary video wall and two separate video panel displays. Software licenses will cover the system for three (3) total years. The contractor shall 
perform the software license updates on-site as the system is a stand-alone system.
 
USE OF NAVY SUPPORT CONTRACTORS FOR OFFICIAL CONTRACT FILES 
(a) NAVSEA may use a file room management support contractor, hereinafter referred to as "the support contractor", to manage its file room, in 
which all official contract files, including the official file supporting this procurement, are retained. These official files may contain information that 
is considered a trade secret, proprietary, business sensitive or otherwise protected pursuant to law or regulation, hereinafter referred to as 
"protected  information". File room management services consist of any of the following: secretarial or clerical support; data entry; document 
reproduction, scanning, imaging, or destruction; operation, management, or maintenance of  paper based or electronic mail rooms, file rooms, or 
libraries; and supervision in connection with functions listed herein. 
(b) The cognizant Contracting Officer will ensure that any NAVSEA contract under which these file room management services are acquired will 
contain a requirement that:  
(1) The support contractor not disclose any information;  
(2) Individual employees are to be instructed by the support contractor regarding the sensitivity of the official contract files;

(3) The support contractor performing these services be barred from providing any other supplies and/or services, or competing to do so, to NAVSEA 
for the period of performance of its contract and for an additional three years thereafter unless otherwise provided by law or regulation; and,  
(4) In addition to any other rights the contractor may have, it is a third party beneficiary who has the right of direct action against the support 
contractor, or any person to whom the support contractor has released or disclosed protected information, for the unauthorized duplication, release, or 
disclosure of such protected information. 
(c) Execution of this contract by the contractor is considered consent to NAVSEA's permitting access to any information, irrespective of restrictive 
markings or the nature of the information submitted, by its file room management support contractor for the limited purpose of executing its file room 
support contract responsibilities.
(d) NAVSEA may, without further notice, enter into contracts with other contractors for these services. Contractors should enter into separate non-
disclosure agreements with the file room contractor. Contact the Procuring Contracting Officer for contractor specifics. However, any such agreement

(c) The contract/order Schedule and Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions--Commercial Items, shall take 
precedence over any conflicting provisions in a Commercial Supplier Agreement.
(d) If any requirement in the Commercial Supplier Agreement conflicts with Federal law or regulations (see FAR 12.212(a)), the following shall 
apply:
(i) Any such requirement is unenforceable against the Government.
(ii) Neither the Government nor any Government authorized end user shall be deemed to have agreed to such requirement by virtue of it appearing in 
the Commercial Supplier Agreement. If the Commercial Supplier Agreement is invoked through an "I agree" click box or other comparable 
mechanism (e.g., "click-wrap" or "browse-wrap" agreements), execution does not bind the Government or any Government authorized end user to 
such requirement.
(iii) Any such requirement is deemed to be stricken from the Commercial Supplier Agreement.
(e) Automatic renewals. License Agreements will expire at end of the term identified in the Purchase  order/Contract. Automatic renewals are not 
permitted and any such provision is void.
(f) Changes to the Commercial Supplier Agreement. Unilateral changes of the Commercial Supplier Agreement are impermissible and any 
requirement authorizing such changes is unenforceable. Changes must be in writing and executed by both parties to be effective.
(g) Third Part License (Embedded Software).
(i) The Contractor agrees that it has obtained all necessary licenses for the Government for any third party materials (including without limitation all 
Open Source licenses) provided within the product.
(ii) Contractor agrees that it complies with and shall continue to comply with all of its obligations under Third Party Licenses (including without 
limitation all Open Source licenses) associated with any third party materials provided within each product.
(iii) To the extent that the Government's use of the software products licensed herein is in compliance with the Contractor's Commercial Supplier 
Agreement, the Government's use will also be in compliance with any Third Party Licenses.

(h) Audits. In lieu of any audit provisions in the Commercial Supplier Agreement, the Government agrees that, no more than once every twelve (12) 
months or within a reasonable time after a transfer, the Contractor shall, upon reasonable notice, have the right to require that the Government conduct 
an internal audit to ascertain and verify the number of licenses in use and to verify that the Government's use of the product is in conformity with this 
Agreement. The Government is not required to use any tools provided by the Contractor to conduct the audit and shall not be required to pay for any 
tools provided by the Contractor to conduct the audit. The results of any such audit shall be kept confidential. If verification discloses that the 
Government's use is not in conformity with this Agreement, the Government agrees to resolve any noncompliance by either removing or correcting 
the unlicensed installation and use of the software identified by the audit as not in conformity with this Agreement.
(i) Confidentiality. Commercial Supplier Agreements' terms and the final contract pricing may not be deemed confidential. Other marked confidential 
information will be appropriately guarded.
(j) Assignment. The Government shall have the right, without the prior written consent of the Contractor or its authorized resellers, to assign, reassign, 
or transfer software licenses among Government employees or the  government's rights in the Contractor's product to any governmental organization 
that is managed, operated, or controlled by the Government.
Such authorization includes sublicensing, and assignment or transfer among or between authorized users. In the event authorized users are 
reorganized or restructured such that their responsibilities and operations are transferred to another government agency, the agency shall have the 
right to assign the affected program licenses to a successor agency. The licensed agency and the successor agency agree to be bound to the 
Commercial Supplier Agreement as modified. The transferee shall be bound by the license metrics and limitations in this license. Government shall 
complete any documentation required by the Contractor to facilitate the transfer of this license, and continuation of support shall be the responsibility 
of the transferee.
For the avoidance of doubt, any assignment or transfer of licenses of the Contractor's products is also subject to all other terms of the Commercial 
Supplier Agreement, as well as the Contractor's policies governing product dependencies and version compatibility. Reassignment does not require 
that the license be under maintenance or support in order to execute a transfer.
(k) Litigation. Any requirement insisting that the commercial supplier or licensor control any litigation arising from the government's use of the 
contractor's supplies or services is deleted and unenforceable.
(l) Equitable Remedies. Equitable remedies, injunctive relief, and binding arbitration requirements shall not be enforced unless explicitly authorized 
by agency guidance or statute.
(m) Venue. Any claim or dispute shall be resolved under the Contract Disputes Act and FAR 52.233-1. The forum for resolution of disputes and 
applicable statutes of limitation shall be governed by federal law.
(n) Applicable law. In accordance with FAR 52.233-4, United States law shall apply to resolve any claim of breach of this contract and such actions

Description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Patuxent River, MD intends to 
negotiate and award a sole source Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to DCS 
Corporation (DCS) for the procurement of continued development, delivery, and sustainment of 
the Weapons and Store Loading (WASP) Foreign Military Sales (FMS) software application. The 
WASP software application provides automated weapons and store loading, and delivery planning, 
and is certified as a permanent flight clearance application for the F/A-18A-F and EA-18G. 
 
DCS Corporation possesses the highly specialized domain knowledge and technical expertise 
required to support the concurrent development and testing of WASP for both U.S. Navy and 
FMS customers. DCS Corporation has been the sole developer of WASP for almost twenty 
years. DCS Corporation has been responsible for the design and execution of all updates to the 
WASP application architecture, logic and code as well as data updates for F/A-18 and EA-18G 
aircraft and association weapon systems making them uniquely qualified to meet the 
Government’s need for WASP Legacy development and delivery. 
 
This contract is being pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 
3204(a)(1), as only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency 
requirements. Award of this follow-on requirement to any source other than DCS Corporation 
would result in unacceptable delays. DCS Corporation is the only source with the requisite in-
depth knowledge and specialized expertise required to perform this effort without unacceptable 
delays. Updates of WASP software versions developed under the WASP Legacy BOA will run 
concurrently with the WASP FMS IDIQ. Data and code from the previous WASP series must be 
merged into the next version of WASP during its development. Accordingly, only the incumbent, 
DCS, can manage the merge of the data without unacceptable delays or impact to the fleet.

Background:  DLA operates a variety of radio communication systems and equipment at several 
DLA locations throughout the world, such as ASTRO25 Trunked Systems. Given the criticality 
of these communications systems to daily operational functions, DLA must ensure that all 
trunked radio equipment is functioning at all times. The primary means of communications for 
DLA Emergency Services is the Trunked Radio System. This Statement of Work identifies the 
Government’s requirements to ensure continuous operational efficiency related to the DLA 
Enterprise Radio communications infrastructure.

for DLA radio infrastructure, services, and subscriber units. There will be 
Infrastructure Repair with Life Cycle Support Services to include Technical Support

etwork Preventative Maintenance Services

he Contractor shall provide an operational test and alignment of infrastructure or fixed network 
equipment to ensure that it meets original manufacturer’s specifications. 
O
nce a year, trained Motorola technicians will: 
• Physically inspect equipment.
• Remove dust and foreign substances.
• Clean filters.
• Measure, record, align, and adjust the equipment to meet the original manufacturer’s
specifications.
T
his service will be performed based on a schedule agreed upon between the Government and 
Motorola. 
L
ocal Radio Support for Consolettes and Mobile Radios 
C
ontractor shall provide an operational check of any defective consolette radio and any mobile 
radio to identify external or internal defects.  If the equipment has an external defect or can be 
restored without opening the radio case, the equipment will be restored and returned to DLA.  
All cabling and antennas associated with the consolettes, and mobile radios are to be checked for 
problems and repaired if installed or provided by a Motorola Service Provider. 
P
ortable Radio Repairs 
• C
ontractor shall provide service to keep subscriber radios at 100% operating condition.
• When a repair is required, DLA will ship the radio to the Motorola Depot which shall test,
repair, and return the radio to its original factory specifications and return ship to the
proper DLA location.
• Radio Firmware shall be upgraded to the latest version.
• The Contractor shall provide a 90-day repair warranty, as well as expedited turnaround
repair times.
• Radios damaged from normal wear and tear will be restored to Factory Specifications and
if applicable, FM-Approved standards and operationally tested.
• The Contractor shall clean external housings of the radios.
• The Contractor shall upgrade DLA’s LMR’s (Land Mobile Radios) to the latest firmware
version and returned within five (5) workdays from date received.
• The Contractor shall, upon request, provide the government with packing/shipping
material to minimize risk of damage to the radios during shipment. This includes special
custom-made Consolette base station shipping containers.

• The Contractor shall provide the government with a Motorola Federal Express ‘next-day’
account number for the outbound shipment of radios.
• The Contractor shall install subscriber updates (operating software/firmware
enhancements) currently published by Motorola under its Field Service Bulletin (FSB)
program.
• The Contractor shall reprogram radios to the original operating parameters based on
DLA’s template. If DLA’s template or code plug is not usable, a generic template or
code plug will be used requiring additional programming by DLA to restore the original
template.
S
ystem Security Updates 
• The Contractor shall test the latest commercial security software updates as they are
released by the software vendors and validate them for safe deployment to the DLA
ELMR radio network.
• The Contractor shall provide Security Updates ensuring that antivirus definitions for both
Microsoft and UNIX platforms, operating system software patches, and Intrusion
Detection System (IDS) signature files for Motorola- provided IDS are compatible and
will not interfere with ASTRO 25 network functionality.
• The Contractor shall release the Security Updates (i.e. patches) to a web link, from which
the Government can download and manually apply tested and compatible patches to the
system.
• The Contractor shall perform quarterly vulnerability scans of Motorola’s test systems
using third-party scanning tools to identify and address new vulnerabilities and
compliance issues.
• The Contractor shall obtain Information Assurance Vulnerability Management (IAVM)
alerts issued by the Department of Defense Computer Emergency Response Center
(DoD-CERT) and Original Equipment Manufacturer bulletins and technical tips for
vendors such as Microsoft, Oracle, Solaris, RedHat, Adobe, etc. to address identified
vulnerabilities.
ST
IG Backporting

he Contractor shall provide STIG Backporting that will address Security Technical 
Implementation Guidelines (STIGs).

his service will enable DLA to bring the security of certified Microsoft Windows operating 
systems and Internet Explorer (for supported releases) on ASTRO system infrastructure up to

his service shall consist of a Motorola trained and security certified technician

• The technician shall validate the updates and apply proper integrity controls to make sure

Performance Work Statement  
 
Michigan Fingerprint Channeling 
Data Collection & Analysis – Outreach 
June 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
Version October 2023  Page 2 of 20 
 
Performance Work Statement 
Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency 
Data Collection & Analysis – Outreach 
Michigan Fingerprint Channeling 
 
Part 1 
General Information 
 
1. General: This is a non-personal services contract to provide for digitizing fingerprints and transmitting 
to the State of Michigan to provide criminal history record information (CHRI). The Government shall not 
exercise direct supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. 
Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn is responsible 
to the Government.  
 
1.1. Description of Services/Introduction: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, 
supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and services necessary 
to perform fingerprint channeling for the purpose of obtaining CHRI from the State of Michigan as 
defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as Government 
furnished property and services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract. 
 
1.2. Background: The mission of the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) is 
continuously ensuring a trusted federal, industrial, and affiliated workforce, and enabling industry’s 
delivery of uncompromised capabilities by leveraging advanced technologies and innovation. The 
mission of the DCSA Data Collection & Analysis (DC&A) is to obtain data source records for inclusion in 
the Federal Personnel Vetting program, including: background investigations, continuous vetting, and 
adjudications programs. This acquisition will allow DCSA to complete its mission by obtaining CHRI 
throughout the DCSA personnel vetting mission. 
 
DCSA has a recurring requirement for a simplified method of filling the repetitive needs for fingerprint 
channeling for the purpose of obtaining CHRI from the State of Michigan. DCSA is committed to 
conducting background investigations on individuals (employees or applicants) for federal employment, 
members of the military, consultants, volunteers, and/or vendor personnel for national security 
purposes. This requirement is for CHRI in support of background investigations as DCSA obtains criminal 
history records in order to meet the requirements of the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention 
Act of 2004. 
 
The following authorities provide DCSA and its Agents the authorization to request and maintain 
information, depending on the purpose of the investigation: Executive Orders (E.O.s) 9397, 10450, 
10577, 10865, 12333, and 12968, as amended; E.O.s 13467, 13488, and 13549; 5 U.S.C. sections 1103, 
1302, 1303, 1304, 3301, 7301, 9101, and 11001; 22 U.S.C. sections 272b, 290a, and 2519; 31 U.S.C. 
section 1537; 42 U.S.C. sections 1874(b)(3), 2165, 2201, and 20132; 50 U.S.C. section 3341; Public Law 
108-136; 5 C.F.R. parts 2, 5, 731, 732, 736, and 1400; and Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 
(HSPD 12). Public Law 101-647, Crime Control Act of 1990.   
 
1.3. Objectives: Digitizing fingerprints and transmitting to the State of Michigan in order to collect CHRI 
as a routine part of conducting background investigations on individuals (employees or applicants) for 
federal employment, members of the military, consultants, volunteers, and/or vendor personnel for 
national security purposes.   

 
 
Version October 2023  Page 3 of 20 
 
 
1.4. Scope: These are commercial, non-personal services which include digitizing and transmitting 
fingerprints to the State of Michigan to CHRI. The Contractor shall accomplish digitizing fingerprints and 
transmitting to the State of Michigan to provide CHRI in accordance with (IAW) the PWS. 
 
1.5. Period of Performance: The period of performance (PoP) shall be for one (1) 12-month base period 
plus four (4) 12-month option periods as follows: 
 
Base Period:         17 June 2026 through 16 June 2027 
Option Period I:   17 June 2027 through 16 June 2028 
Option Period II:  17 June 2028 through 16 June 2029 
Option Period III: 17 June 2029 through 16 June 2030 
Option Period IV: 17 June 2030 through 16 June 2031 
   
1.6. General Information: 
 
1.6.1. Quality Control: The Contractor shall develop and maintain an effective quality control program, 
including a Quality Control Plan (QCP), to ensure services are performed IAW this PWS. The Contractor 
shall develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-recurrence of defective 
services. The Contractor’s quality control program is the means by which they assure themselves that 
their work complies with the requirement(s) of the contract. The QCP shall be delivered within 30 
Calendar days of contract award via email to both the Contracting Officer (KO) and Contracting Officer’s 
Representative (COR) and within five (5) Business days when changes are made thereafter. After 
acceptance of the initial QCP the Contractor shall be required to solicit and receive the KO’s acceptance 
in writing of any proposed change to their quality control system and/or QCP.  
 
1.6.2. Quality Assurance: The Government shall evaluate the Contractor’s performance under this

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

The Minneapolis VA Health Care System is conducting market research in accordance with FAR 17.207 Exercise of Options for Nurse Management Software and Support Services as described in the Statement of Work below.

This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE only looking for businesses to provide the services listed in the Statement of Work below for market research purposes.  No proposals are being requested or accepted with this notice.  THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS OR PRICING AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS NOTICE.  This notice shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs.

Responses to this notice will be treated only as information for the Government to consider as part of their market research efforts.  The information provided will be used by the Government in developing its acquisition strategy regarding possible set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Veteran-Owned, and other socio-economic categories of small business.  Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response.  The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this notice and parties responding will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs incurred in responding to this notice.  

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541519, Other Computer Related Services, with an SBA Small Business Size Standard of $34.0 Million.

If you are a vendor capable of providing the requested information and required services described below with competitive pricing, send your information with a description of proof of capability and answers to all questions to:  Alisha.Milander@va.gov on or before Tuesday, June 2, 2026 at 12:00 PM Central Time. 

Please provide answers as appropriate to the following questions in the table below with your response to this Sources Sought.  Failure to respond accurately to the following questions may affect the acquisition strategy.  Failure to respond to the questions at all will result in your response being determined as non-responsive.

PLEASE PROVIDE ESTIMATED PRICING/QUOTES BELOW FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES WITH YOUR RESPONSE TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT.

ITEM INFORMATION

*If applicable, FAR Provision 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting, will apply to the potential solicitation if set-aside for Small-Businesses.*

*If applicable, 852.219-75  VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting—Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction, will apply to the potential solicitation if set-aside for SDVOSBs/VOSBs.*

DISCLAIMER 

This Sources Sought is issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation.  All information received in response to this Sources Sought that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly.  In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.  Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Sources Sought. 

The deadline for this information is 12:00 PM Central Time on, Tuesday, June 2, 2026.

PRELIMINARY STATEMENT OF WORK

 Description

The Minneapolis VA Health Care System requires a services solution to automate nursing resource management processes, to include: Staff scheduling and staffing activities; real-time decision support for staffing management, enhance the availability of data and information relevant to patient care and deployment of nursing assets, provides self-scheduling options to nursing staff at multiple levels. This system will be cloud ready.

Objectives

Implement an automated, cloud-based, product and software management service tailored for managing nurse staffing and nursing assets throughout the facility.

Match staff in numbers, skill and competency to support the acuity and needs of patients.

Reduce the time and costs associated with scheduling and staffing activities.

Manage budgets and costs.

Accurately track staff movement.

Use real-time data to support nurse staffing and nurse staff management decisions.

Retrieve and organize data through a robust reports mechanism.

Eliminate redundant work and improve data reliability through product interfaces with VHA data systems.

Meet requirements as outlined by statute, VHA regulations and directives and local policies.

Scope

An integrated system and automated data extraction tool to effectively assign staffing resources and monitor resource management and utilization of nursing assets. This system will have proven ability to interface with a variety of VHA data management systems and provide minimally for unilateral data exchange. Capability for bilateral data exchange is preferred. The intent is to purchase products/services and not individual or facility software licenses. The primary users of the system will be nursing executives, nursing management, program assistants and front-line nursing staff.

Tasks or Requirements

Support appropriate responses to the fluctuations in patient census and acuities by using embedded decision support tools.

Ensure adequate staffing numbers and skills mix based on patient acuity and other care related variables.

Demonstrated ability to interface with VHA data systems for the collection, retrieval and organization of period-defined (hourly, shift, daily, monthly, annually, etc.) including, but not limited to :

management of nursing resources and associated costs

nursing hours (HPPD) data

patient admission, discharge, and transfer activity

clinically relevant reports 

Demonstrated ability to support compliance with public law and other regulatory and agency mandates for staffing regulations and monitors. 

Demonstrated ability to consolidate data from multiple sources to support multiple administrative decision functions into a single system (licensure, certifications, emergency notifications, etc.) 

Possess robust reporting capability including both parameters defined standardized and ad hoc reports. 

Demonstrated ability to accommodate staff self-scheduling based on sets of predetermined parameters. 

Deliverables or Deliver Schedule (Salient Characteristics) 

Specifications 

Utilizes an HL7 interface with Vista to transfer ,(unidirectional and bidirectional) real-time data including, but not limited to:

Patient admission, discharge and transfer information 

Snapshots of inpatient census at pre-determined intervals 

Select staff data and information from human resource and payroll automated systems 

Capable of cloud computing with VHA approved entities. 

Vendor offers product as a service with no requirement to purchase actual software licenses. 

Vendor is responsible for support, general maintenance, fixes-patches, interface and updates installations which are included in the service cost. 

Vendor supplied 24/7 support. 

Required functional capabilities:

Staff Scheduling Tools:

demographic, skills and competency tracking tools 

create and maintain prospective schedules 

create schedules in increments of 6 weeks with flexibility for fewer or more weeks. 

create prospective schedules for, at a minimum 12 months. 

provide real-time staffing

provide for auditing of changes made in the product by users including date/time and name of individual making changes 

provide archival functions 

allow staff to sign up for open and overtime shifts with notifications via email, text or users preferred method of communication. 

allow shift swapping among peers 

provides a module or function that specifically allows supervisors to view , interact and monitor shift schedules from a central or “birds-eye” vantage point. 

accommodate multi-level permissions-based access 

manage position control 

Staff Evaluation/Performance Monitoring Syst 

ability to maintain repositories of anecdotal notes for individual staffs’ performance evaluations 

ability to track: licensure currency, specialty certifications, skills-based competencies and education 

Tools for staff to self- report information into a professional portfolio. 

Rule engines to facilitate scheduling:

apply regulations — hour limits, time off, requirements, staffing ratios, etc) as they apply to individuals being scheduled to work: 

apply union requirements stored in the system to create staffing schedules 

use staff preferences to create staffing schedules. 

match competencies to staffing needs. 

match nursing staff with patient needs. 

apply unit preference to competencies, e.g., ICU nurses are ACLS certified. 

apply permanent schedules requests to when generating schedules. 

apply rotating shifts rules when generating schedules. 

accommodate scheduling changes based on patient census 

apply patient acuities to staffing needs 

track hours per patient day 

generate alternate work schedules 

allow or restrict swapping unit assignments based on competencies. 

restrict overtime assignment based on defined rules/regulations 

predict staffing needs based on previous trends (eg. high surgery days) 

provide functionality to maintain disaster preparedness (notifications and callbacks). 

Communication Tools: 

creates a personalized web-based dashboard for all stakeholders 

web-Based for employee access 

web-based for manager access 

provide options for staff bidding on open positions (Staff to staff communications (e.g. to swap shifts) 

produce reports for budge, operations and strategic planning. 

Training/Implementation

Vendor to provide on-site training at facility targeting specific user groups:

first line staff users 

managers 

schedulers and program assistants 

supervisors 

On-site implementation of the system is required as follows: 

Project Definition

establishing project goals

assigning project roles & workgroups

define interfaces 

workload 

define and document existing workflow processes 

configuration of job codes and units and leave schedules 

present projections for workflow process 

System Configuration

system Administrator Training

security Configuration 

workload and Unit Budget 

validate Interface Data 

User Training

pilot unit training

user training 

system-wide project roll-out 

employee access 

position tracking 

Courses and Consultation

staffing methodology class 

executive analytics class 

reports workshop 

data mining & scorecards 

set up alerts 

Security Considerations: 

In accordance with VA Handbook 6500.6 Appendix B, contractor, their personnel, and their subcontractors shall be subject to the Federal laws, regulations, standards, and VA Directives and Handbooks regarding information and information system security 

An interconnection between contractor and MVAHCS will exist with interfaces to VistA: Human Resources information, Census data, and Health Level 7 information. All interfaces will feed contractors system to eliminate points of double data entry and improve efficiencies. All data from these feeds will be compliant with protections for PHI 

The vendor must have an established Information Security Officer, who can provide oversight through the duration of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) phases (development, deployment, operations, and disposal) of the interconnection. 

All contractor employees who require access to the Department of Veterans Affairs' computer systems shall be the subject of a background investigation and must receive a favorable adjudication from the VA Security and Investigations Center and must complete TMS Training VA 10203 to meet privacy training require

4800 MARK CENTER DRIVE 
ALEXANDRIA, VA  22350-1400 
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION - HE12542051426 
Freedom of Information Act  
(FOIA) Management Software 
1.0 Description 
1.1 Th e Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) s eeks information on how an interested contractor 
could provide cloud-based FOIA management software that complies with all Federal laws/regulations.   
1.2 D oWEA anticipates making a single award. The anticipated period of performance is August 7, 2026 – 
August 6, 2031.  
1.3 This request  for information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning and does not constitute 
a request for quote (RFQ) or a promise to issue an RFQ in the future.  
 The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI,
i.e., all costs associated with responding to this RFI are solely the responder’s responsibility.
 Not 
responding to the RFI does not preclude a contract or from responding to a future RFQ/RFP.  If  a
solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the SAM.gov website.  Potential responders are responsible
to monitor the relevant site for additional informatio n pertaining to this requirement. Do not submit
proposals or quotes. The Government will not evaluate, nor entertain, any unsolicited proposals or offers
received in response to this RFI. Any such submissions will be discarded.
2.0 Overview 
2.1 Ag ency : For school year 2025-26, the Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) will provide PK-12 
instruction in 161 schools to approximately 66,000 dependents of active-duty military and civilian employees. In 
the Americas, DoWEA operates 50 schools located in seven states, Puerto Rico, and Cuba. In Europe and the 
Middle East, DoWEA operates 64 schools located in Germany, England, Netherlands, Belgium, Spain, Italy, 
Turkey, and Bahrain. In the Pacific, DoWEA operates  46 schools located in Korea, Japan (mainland and 
Okinawa), and Guam. DoWEA also operates a fully accredited virtual high school with teaching hubs in each 
region.  Our curriculum, resources and student achievement scores on standardized assessments compare favorably 
to those of high-performing US public school systems.   
2.2 Ba ckground : The DoWEA Freedom of Information Act (FOI A) Office currently us es the FOIAXpress 
application to process FOIA requests made to the Ag ency. In accordance with the FOIA Improvement Act 
of 2016, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) created a national FOIA request portal. It mandated 
federal agencies to connect to the portal by the end of the fiscal year 2021. The current contract includes the 
FOIAXpress Public Access Link (PAL) setup and subscription to connect to the national FOIA portal which 
has brought DoWEA into compliance.    
2.3 Requ
irements : DoWEA requires a commercially available, off-the-shelf (COTS), enterprise license for FOIA 
management software.  The proposed solution shall include related data migration and technical support. 
Supporting Tasks: The tasks below are to help the Contr actor gain a better understanding of the requirements. 
They are not all inclusive, so the Contractor shall develop the total solution to meet all the requirements 
in accordance with a performance-based approach.   
2.4 Draft Summary 
Subscription Licenses: The Contractor shall provide one enterprise FOIA management software subscription. 
It shall include upgrades and customizations and address any concerns about the system after upgrade deployment 
and any concerns about the frequency of upgrades.  The Contractor shall: 
2.4.1 The proposed Case Management System shall possess the following capabilities: 
1)
Distinguish between privileged accesses.
2
) Assign a tracking number to a request automatically .
3)
Include email templates or other information out using DoWEA’s SMTP server.

2 
4) Ensure fields in the correspondence template are auto populated with the required information.
5)
Maintain documents and notes associated with a case.
6) Retain all outgoing correspondence such  as emails, as part of the case file.
7)
Track fees generated during the FOIA process.
8
) Compile statistics on requests and requ esters.
9)
Support Federal retention policies for records management for case files.
2.4.2 The proposed case management system shall allow users to perform the following: 
1) Enter a FOIA request into the system manually .
2)
Use an automated workflow system from the beginning of the process to final disposition.
3) Print 
correspondence and documents.
4
) Upload file formats such as PDF/Word/Exc el/PPT.
5) St
ore and manage electronic records.
6) R
edact documents within the system.
7)
Generate reports on the number, types, and nature of FOIA requests processed.
8) Pull custom reports, save, download, print, and email reports.
9) View the dashboard with statistics and metrics in the sy stem.
2
.4.3  The proposed Electronic Data Review (EDR) shall possess the following capabilities: 
1) Email deduplication to consolid ate email threads and attachments.
2)
Rank, categorize and identify relevant content by concept automatically.
3) Provide role-based permissions to assign cases to select users and give or limit access to features 
or secure content by role.
4)
Include advanced keyword search to uncover responsive terms in large document sets.
5) Create audit logs automatically to ensure compliance and support legal actions .
6)
Perform side-by-side document review to certify accuracy.
2.4.4  The proposed artificial intelligence (AI) redaction shall leverage machine learning to find and redact 
sensitive information on requested documents automatically. 
2.4.5 The proposed public access link (PAL) shall possess the following features: 
1) Connection to the National FOIA Portal (NFP).
2
) Public websites configured to sup port DoWEA.
3
) Secure requestor portal with unique logins to  submit requests/appeals, track status, communicate
and receive records for download.
4)
Automatic case tracking.
Dat
a Migration: The objective is to migrate the FOIAXpress data into the proposed FOIA management 
software solution at the beginning of the contract period and to assist, if necessary, a new Contractor in 
migrating data to a new solution at the end of the contract period.  The Contractor shall:

solution without losing interoperability with DOJ’s FOIA website/portal. Ensure the connection with 
DoJ remains seamless throughout the process.  Note: This clause is only applicable if the incumbent 
is not awarded a new contract. 
2.4.7 Close Out (if required): Assist the new Contractor’s migration of data to the new FOIA management 
software solution.  Ensure the connection with DoJ remains seamless throughout the process.  Note: 
This clause is only applicable if the incumbent is not awarded a new contract. 
Cloud Service and Support: The objective is to (1) ensure rapid deployment, installation, and configuration 
of the SaaS solution, and (2) provide project management services, technical architecture review/design, 
system setup, system engineering, and security.  The Contractor shall: 
2.4.8 Provide application and environment documentation needed for DoWEA to complete security reviews 
such as a privacy impact assessment and cloud questionnaires. 
2.4.9 Be responsible, as a SaaS provider, for server and application maintenance, upgrades, patching, and 
hosting services for 24/7/365 availability. Note: The Contractor shall no tify DoWEA a minimum of 
one business day prior to upgrades and downtime. 

3 
2.4.10 Provide a document containing their customer support center standard operating procedures (SOP) for 
support call handling within 24 hours of the contract award date. The SOP shall include, at a minimum: 
1) Contact information for the Contractor’s helpdesk.
2) Initial information required to open a ticket (e.g ., name, agency, phone number, product, etc.).
3
) Steps the Contractor will take to process and complete the incident request.
2.4.11 Provide weekly or bi-weekly updates to the C ontracting Officer’s Representative (COR), who will be 
identified at the post-award conference.  
User Acceptance Testing: The objective is to succes sfully complete User Acceptance Testing (UAT). The 
Contractor shall: 
2.4.12 UAT Test Plan and Checklist Submission : Deliver a comprehensive UAT test plan and associated 
checklist to the Contracting Officer's Representativ e (COR). This deliverable shall be submitted no 
later than five business days prior to the scheduled UAT walk-through. 
2.4.13 Checklist Revisions: Incorporate all DoWEA-provided feedback and requested changes into a final 
UAT checklist. The revised checklist shall be used for the official UAT event. 
2.4.14 Pre-UAT System Walkthrough: Conduct a virtual walkthrough of the complete DoWEA instance of 
the application. This event, serv ing as a preparatory demonstration, shall be completed at least two 
business days prior to the scheduled UAT. 
2.4.15 UAT Execution : Conduct the formal UAT, which shall be completed 20 business days after the award. 
2.4.16 Discrepancy Resolution: Document all discrepancies, errors, or defects identified during the UAT and 
provide them to the COR. 
Final Acceptance Testing: The objective of Final Acceptance Testing (FAT) is to confirm that the software is 
ready for its intended uses and the production environment.  This task includes verifying that the system meets 
all the agreed-upon business requirements and functions correctly in real-world scenarios. The Contractor shall: 
2.4.17  Correct all documented UAT findings prior to FAT. 
2.4.18 Complete the FAT in a timely manner. 
General Requirements—The Contractor shall: 
2.4.19  Technical Support: provide industry-standard technical support for its digital resources for the life of 
the contract via telephone or email within one business day from the initial contact to include but not 
limited to assisting with service problems, product setup, upgrades, and troubleshooting, 
2.4.20 Third-Party Programs, Software, and Applications: Ensure its own and its subcontractors’ (third-party) 
programs, software, and applications meet—at a mi nimum—the same technical requirements as the 
Contractor must meet, such as single sign on (SSO) and Federal Risk and Authorization Management 
Program (FedRAMP) Level 2, etc.  On a case-by- case basis, DoWEA may honor requests to waive 
the FedRAMP Level 2 requirement.

ful
ly realize that you will be able to give a much more refined answer once the solicitation is released, but we 
hope you can provide some general information in this regard based on your experience. In that regard, please 
include the following information: 
3.1.1 Administration & Subcontracting 
1) Company name, DBA name (if applicable), mailing address, CAGE code, unique entity identifier
(UE
I), and North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) codes.
2) Design
ated point of contact’s name, title, phone number, and email address.
3) Descri
be, if applicable, any subcontracting possibilities.  Note: The prime must perform at least 51
pe
rcent of the work.
3.1.2 Capability: Describe your proposed enterprise solution for handling FOIA requests to include your 
experience handling them for Federal agencies. 

4 
3.1.3 Data Migration: Briefly describe the plan and estimated timeline to migrate DoWEA’s FOIAXpress data, 
including what support will be required from the current contractor and from DoWEA. 
3.1.4 Pricing: Provide a non-binding  price estimate or estimated range—th at will be kept confidential. 
Please use the attached Excel spreadsheet.  If the breakdown that is provided does not fit your 
solution, please revise the spreadsheet as needed. 
3.1.5 Recommendations: Please provide any recommendations you believe might improve the Government’s 
performance work statement. 
3.2 Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and be  clearly marked.  Please segregate the proprietary 
information.  Note: All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 
4.0 Industry Discussions 
DoWEA representatives may or may not choose to speak with potential offerors.  Such discussions would only 
be intended to get greater clarification on such things as capability and pricing. 
5.0  Questions 
Qu
estions regarding this announcement shall be submitted by email to Contract Specialist, Mr. Wardell Gordon. 
at wardell.gordon@dodea.edu and Contracting Officer, Ms. ShaHannah Brown, at shahannah.brown@dodea.edu. 
Verbal questions will not be accepted.  Questions will be answered via email and will not contain proprietary or 
classified information.  The Government does not guarantee that questions received after May 19 will be answered. 
6.0  Summary 
This RFI is issued solely for information and planning and does not constitute an RFQ/RFP. The information 
herein is subject to change and not binding on the Government.  Release of this RFI is not a commitment that 
DoWEA will issue an RFQ/RFP in the future or that it au thorizes costs to be incurred for which reimbursement 
would be required or sought.  All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 
SUSPENSE 
Submit your RFI resp onse no later than 1PM EST on Tuesday, May 26, 2026.  Please email your responses 
to Contract Specialist, Mr. Wardell Gordon at wardell.gordon @dodea.edu and Contractin g Officer, Ms. 
ShaHannah Brown at shahannah.brown@dodea.edu.

The 42nd Contracting Squadron at Maxwell AFB, AL hereby gives NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE to Instructure, Inc. to provide subscriptions for user-access subscription for commercial digital badging and micro-credentialing solution to support enterprise-wide faculty and student development in accordance with (IAW) the attached Statement of Requirement (SOR).

Brief Description of Requirement: The system will provide a scalable automated capability to issue, manage, and verify digital credentials aligned with modernizing learning, incentivizing faculty development and enhancing recognition of competency-based achievement.

Period of Performance: POP: 15 June 2026 to 14 June 2029. Base plus two (2) option years.

Place of Performance: Maxwell AFB, AL.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 518210 - Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services.

There will be no written solicitation issued. This is an intent to purchase a sole source procurement under the authority of RFO 6.103-1. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract utilizing Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, Commercial Products and Services.

The contractor needs to be registered in the DoD System for Award Management (SAM).  Register via the SAM website https://www.sam.gov, and also be eligible to process invoices through Wide Area Workflow (WAWF).  Register via the WAWF website https://wawf.eb.mil.

Those capable of meeting the requirement IAW the SOR are requested to provide the following information in their response:  1) Current capability that demonstrates your company's ability to meet the above requirement, 2) Company name, point of contact, e-mail address, telephone and fax numbers, type of business and size, Cage Code and Unique ID Number.  IMPORTANT NOTES: 1) Information submitted will not be returned to the respective respondents. Oral submissions of information are not acceptable and will not be accepted in response to this notice. 2) Respondents may respond via e-mail no later than 2 June 2026 1:00 pm. Central Standard Time (CST) to SSgt Bryant Nguyen, bryant.nguyen@us.af.mil (334) 953-5755 and LaChandra Thompson as lachandra.thomspn@us.af.mil. (334)-953-6569.

If no responsible, responsive offers are received by the above date, a sole source contract will be issued to Instructure, INC. under the authority of RFO 6.103-1.

NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT 
Department of the Interior 
National Park Service 
Great Smoky Mountains National Park & Blue Ridge Parkway 
Project Title: CAD System – Maintenance & Support 
NAICS: 541519 – Other Computer Related Services 
PSC: DA10 – IT and Telecom – Application Development/Support Services 
 
1. Purpose 
The National Park Service (NPS), Great Smoky Mountains National Park (GRSM) and Blue 
Ridge Parkway (BLRI), intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract for Computer 
Aided Dispatch (CAD) System Maintenance & Support. This acquisition is conducted under 
the authority of FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source. 
 
2. Description of Requirement 
The NPS requires comprehensive maintenance and technical support for its proprietary CAD 
system, which is used to process and track emergency calls, coordinate responders, and support 
mission-critical law enforcement and public safety operations. Due to the life-safety nature of 
dispatch operations, the CAD system must maintain continuous availability. 
Required support services include: 
• 24/7/365 remote diagnostics and help desk support 
• 4-hour telephonic response-time service level agreement 
• SQL database maintenance and support 
• System and interface support, including IMARS and TN/NC integrations 
• Installation of software updates, cybersecurity patches, and version releases in 
accordance with NPS security guidance 
• Quality assurance testing prior to deployment 
• Technicians meeting NPS background check, confidentiality, and IT security training 
requirements 
 
3. Basis for Sole Source 

The CAD system in use by GRSM and BLRI is proprietary, and the original equipment 
manufacturer (OEM) retains exclusive control and rights to: 
• Source code 
• System architecture 
• Interface modules 
• Software update utilities 
• Cybersecurity patch mechanisms 
Only the OEM is authorized to provide software maintenance, updates, troubleshooting, and 
database-level support essential to system functionality. 
Third-party resellers: 
• Are not technically capable of performing required maintenance 
• Cannot meet NPS security, interface, or integration requirements 
• Are no longer small businesses and do not contribute toward small-business credit 
The OEM remains a small business, and similar CAD support requirements at other NPS units 
have historically been met exclusively through direct sole-source awards to this vendor. 
Given these technical, proprietary, and security constraints, no other source is capable of 
meeting the Government’s minimum needs. 
 
4. Period of Performance 
The anticipated period of performance is one (1) base year from the date of award, with the 
option for annual renewal. 
 
5. Intent to Sole Source 
The Government intends to award a sole-source contract to: 
Computer Information Systems INC (CIS) 
 
6. Response Instructions 

Vendors who believe they possess the capability and OEM authorization necessary to meet all 
technical, proprietary, and security requirements may submit a detailed capability statement 
addressing: 
• Demonstrated authorization from the OEM 
• Technical ability to meet all requirements in the SOW 
• Evidence of certified access to proprietary CAD system components 
Responses must be submitted no later than 06/05/2026, 15:00 ES to: 
Arcoiris Cuetara-Higa 
Contract Specialist 
Email: arcoiris_cuetara-higa@ios.doi.gov 
Late or incomplete submissions will not be considered. 
 
7. Disclaimer 
This Notice of Intent is not a solicitation. No competitive solicitation will be issued. The 
Government will not reimburse any costs incurred in response to this notice.

INVOICING: Use of the invoicing procedures set forth in this Contract is mandatory and supersede any other invoicing procedures otherwise used by the Contractor. Invoice payment, including the calculation of late fees when applicable, shall be conducted in accordance with current Department of Veterans Affairs policies and procedures at the time an invoice is submitted. Under no circumstances shall a late payment be grounds for termination of this Contract.

Invoices Submitted in Arrears: Invoices shall be submitted electronically, monthly, in arrears in accordance with: VAAR 852.232-72 ELECTRONIC SUBMISSION OF PAYMENT REQUESTS (NOV 2018). Invoices shall not be submitted for work not yet performed.

Invoice Payment: Payments will be made in arrears upon receipt of a properly prepared invoice. Advance payments for work not yet performed is not authorized under this Contract. All payments by the Government to the contractor will be made in accordance with FAR 52.232-33 PAYMENT BY ELECTRONIC FUNDS TRANSFER – SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (OCT 2018).

Invoice Processes and Procedures:

Electronic Invoicing Required: Facsimile, e-mail, posted mail, and scanned documents are not acceptable forms of submission for payment requests.

FMS Registration: Contractors new to the Department of Veterans Affairs must first register with the VA’s Financial Management System (FMS). In order to register a company with FMS, the contractor must first register with https://www.id.me/, which is a simple and secure identity verification system. Once a contractor has registered with https://www.id.me/, the contractor can then access the digital registration form through the VA's Customer Engagement Portal at http://www.cep.fsc.va.gov/. For assistance, contractors may call 1-877-353-9791 or e-mail vafsccshd@va.gov.

Tungsten Network: Once registered in FMS, a contractor may now electronically submit invoices. The VA has mandated electronic invoice submission to the Veterans Affairs Financial Services Center (VAFSC). VAFSC has partnered with Tungsten Network e-Invoicing network, for submissions of all electronic invoices to the VA. Tungsten Network electronic invoicing is free to all VA vendors. In order to submit electronic invoices, all VA vendors must register with Tungsten Network by submitting an email to VA.Registration@Tungsten-Network.com or calling 1-877-489-6135 for enrollment. Once successfully enrolled, please go to Tungsten Network (tungsten-network.com) to begin submitting electronic invoices. 

Invoice Information: All invoices shall reference the vendor’s name and address, customer name, contract number, appropriate obligation/funding order number, description of services provided, quantity, unit price, and total invoice amount (any additional info). Invoices shall also include any payment discount terms, if applicable. 

Electronic Invoice Submission: Contractors shall submit an electronic invoice by the tenth (10th) of the following month services were performed to the Veterans Affairs Financial Services Center (VAFSC) e-Invoice through the website at https://portal.Tungsten-Network.com/Login.aspx. For questions regarding the submission of VA electronic invoices, Tungsten Network customer service may be contacted at 1-877-489-6135.

CONTRACTING OFFICER AUTHORITY: If the contractor receives a request from VA personnel directing or requesting work that the Contractor believes is not within the scope of the Contract, the Contractor must notify the COR and the Contracting Officer of the request. Only the Contracting Officer is authorized to issue changes or modifications that will affect price, quantity, or quality of performance of this contract. Additional tasking required by changes in mission assignments must be documented by a bilateral contract modification, in accordance with FAR 52.212-4(c). In the event the Contractor effects any such change at the direction of any person other than the Contracting Officer, the change shall be considered to have been made without authority and no adjustment will be made in the contract price to cover any increase in cost incurred thereof.

Firm-Fixed-Price Contract: This Contract is a firm-fixed-price contract, as defined in FAR 16.202-1. As such, the prices set forth in Section B.2 Price Schedule are, “not subject to any adjustment on the basis of the contractor’s cost experience in performing the contract.” The Contractor shall not perform any services outside the scope of this Contract without a properly awarded bilateral modification, in accordance with FAR 52.212-4(c).

NONPERSONAL SERVICES CONTRACT: This Contract is a nonpersonal services contract, as defined in FAR 37.101. VA personnel will not exercise any supervision or control over Contractor personnel performing work under this Contract. Such personnel shall be accountable solely to the Contractor, which in turn is responsible to the Government for execution of the services under this Contract.

GOVERNMENT LIABILITY: The Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA), 28 U.S.C. §§ 2671-2680, prescribes a uniform procedure for handling of claims against the United States, for money damages only, on account of damage to or loss of property, or personal injury or death, caused by the negligent or wrongful act or omission of a Government employee while acting within the scope of his or her office or employment, under circumstances where the United States, if a private person, would be liable in accordance with the law of the place where the act or omission occurred. Under the FTCA, the federal government acts as a self-insurer. See Claims Under the Federal Tort Claims Act - Office of General Counsel (va.gov) for additional information.

FACILITY REQUIREMENTS: In addition to any other requirements set forth in this Contract, the Contractor, including its employees, agents, and subcontractors (collectively “the Contractor”), shall comply with the following facility requirements. Failure to comply with these requirements shall be considered a material breach of this Contract and may be a violation of Federal law resulting in charges answerable in the United States District Court.

Parking: It is the responsibility of the Contractor to park in the appropriate designated parking areas. Information on parking is available from the VA Police Section. The VA will not invalidate or make reimbursement for parking violations of the Contractor under any conditions.

Drug-free Policy: All VA facilities are drug-free. Possession of non-prescribed drugs, including alcohol, marijuana, and CBD products, is prohibited.

Non-smoking Policy: Smoking—including all tobacco products, e-cigarettes, and vaping products—is prohibited on the entire campus, both inside and outside the VA Facility.

Weapons Prohibited: Possession of any type of weapon on VA property is prohibited. Enclosed containers, including tool kits, are subject to search without consent while on VA property.

Facility Directives: All persons shall comply with all facility directives while on-campus, including the wearing of masks as required.

VHA DIRECTIVE 1192.01 (Seasonal Influenza Policy): This Veterans Health Administration (VHA) directive establishes policy and provides guidance for the prevention of seasonal influenza in VHA facilities through the vaccination or masking of health care personnel (HCP). AUTHORITY: Title 38 United States Code (U.S.C.) 7301(b), 7318(b). Contractor is responsible for providing face masks and influenza vaccines for all employees working at a VA facility. If Directive 1192.01 is applicable the Contractor, in conjunction with the COR, is responsible for ensuring that all aspects of this directive are implemented.

Statement of Work

Contract Title: 

Upgrade of the BD Pyxis Server

Background:

The Pyxis server upgrade will support the BD Pyxis technology currently deployed. The Edward Hines Jr. VA Hospital currently uses automated dispensing cabinets (ADC) throughout the facility provided by BD Pyxis. The Central Inpatient Pharmacy currently utilizes the inventory management system (BD Logistics) and carousel to store manage medication inventory. The 9th floor Chemotherapy pharmacy lacks an IV prep workflow compounding system which has been deployed to the Central Pharmacy. The IV Prep system is needed to ensure products are prepared accurately with system safety checks. Central Inpatient Pharmacy utilizes the Controlled Substance manager which is integrated with the other ADC to help with both storage and inventory control. The Anesthesia carts are deployed in the OR rooms to help facilitate workflow. Software is needed to support nursing’s ability to dispense and waste drugs remotely, analytics to review dispensing trends and program to prevent drug diversion. Service to the Pyxis system is provided by Four Points who has a Current National BAA on file. 

The purpose of this procurement is to the server upgraded to support the functionality of all currently owned BD Pyxis equipment for the Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 12 facilitity, Edward Hines Jr. 

Scope of Work:

Services to be provided by the Contractor: 

Customer Support includes (but not limited to):

Software updates

Hardware updates that fix a defined functionality problem

Routine inspections and annual maintenance scheduled 3 days in advance during normal business hours (see below for business hours).

24 hours, 7 days per week, 800# Helpline for software, hardware, and user questions.

On-site service technician

Guaranteed 8-hour response time

Hours of Operation: Normal hours of operation are Monday through Friday from 7:30 am to 4:00 pm Central Standard Time, excluding national holidays.  All planned onsite service and repairs will be performed during normal hours unless otherwise agreed.    

The contractor shall not be expected to perform service on the following Federal Holidays:

When one of the above designated Federal Holidays falls on a Sunday, the following Monday shall be observed as a Federal Holiday. When a Federal Holiday falls on a Saturday, the preceding Friday is observed as a Federal Holiday by United States Government agencies.

The Contractor shall have his/her own service manuals, specifications, schematic diagrams, and parts list to assist in the evaluation/repair of all equipment included in this contract.

 

3. SYSTEM ACCESS. In accordance with the Conformance Standards, the Contractor shall be granted reasonable access to the system to fulfill the obligations set forth in this agreement.

4. CONFORMANCE STANDARDS. All work shall be performed, and equipment shall function in conformance with all VA safety standards, manufacturer's/industry standards, and other applicable state, local, national and industry standards.

5. MAINTENANCE SERVICES.  

Technical Support: The Contractor shall provide a 24-hour toll-free Technical Support number for contact by Pharmacy and/or IT employees for maintenance service, repair, or other assistance that is required. Systems and processes shall be in place for thorough documentation of issues reported by Edward Hines Jr with having the ability to request these reports when needed. The Contractor shall have the ability to remotely access the Pyxis system to diagnose and solve problems as well as provide user training.

Diagnostic and Repair: If the Pyxis system needs repairs that cannot be performed remotely, the contractor shall dispatch a Field Service Engineer (FSE) next business day to troubleshoot, service and repair the issues. The FSE assigned by the Contractor shall arrive on-site during, normal VA business hours, as stated above. Work performed outside of the normal hours of operation at the request of the FSE shall be considered service during normal hours of coverage.

Preventive Maintenance:

Preventive Maintenance shall be performed by the contractor at intervals that are in accordance with the manufacturer’s recommendations, but no less than annually. All exceptions to the Preventive Maintenance (PM) schedule shall be arranged and approved in advance with the pharmacy designee.

Contractor shall furnish any required “PM kits” needed to perform Preventive Maintenance. 

The Contractor shall provide written description of Preventive Maintenance Inspections (PMI). This description shall include an itemized list of the procedures performed, including electrical safety.

Service reports shall be provided for all service activities including preventive maintenance, emergency repair, and safety inspections, and shall contain the following information:

Serial Number Serviced or Replaced

Signature of Pharmacy Staff member who witnessed service event (available upon request within 90 days of service date)

Service Reports shall be e-mailed at the completion of work or when the problem resolution is set to be completed. The email shall be sent to the COR or any other designee with a valid e-mail address located within Pyxis’s Email Communication list. 

All required parts, services, manuals, tools or software needed to successfully perform Preventive Maintenance shall be provided by the Contractor at no additional cost to the VA, unless otherwise, specifically stated in writing.

Corrective (Emergency) Maintenance:

Corrective Maintenance (CM) shall be performed onsite or remotely by the Contractor and shall be performed by the next business day. Corrective Maintenance shall not be an additional cost.

If new equipment or components are obtained, either through new purchase, upgrade or replacement of existing equipment, that equipment may be added (and the replaced equipment deleted) from the contract as needed upon notification of the Contracting Officer (to be documented in writing via contract modification). Deleted equipment shall be credited in the full amount if deleted before any maintenance or repair has been performed on it.

Sole Source Special Notice / Pre-Solicitation Notice for a project involving contractor-work to be performed on a Tellabs-Based Passive Optical Local Area Network (LAN) Upgrade for the U. S. Department of Transportation (DOT)

This document is not a Solicitation.  

This document is instead a SOLE SOURCE SPECIAL NOTICE / PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE in support of the U. S. Department of Transportation’s (DOT’s) contemplated awarding-----to VTG, LLC-----of a Purchase Order under which VTG, LLC will perform work on a Tellabs-based Passive Optical Local Area Network (LAN) Upgrade for the U. S. Department of Transportation  (DOT).  ACCORDINGLY,  DOT DOES NOT EXPECT TO HAVE ANY NEED TO PUBLISH ANY SOLICITATION FOR THAT PROJECT.  Further details are given below.

IDENTIFICATION OF THE REQUIRING ACTIVITY AND CONTRACTING ACTIVITY AGENCY (REQUIRING ACTIVITY)

Department of Transportation (DOT) Office of the Secretary (OST) 

Departmental Office of Intelligence, Security and Emergency Response (S-60)

CONTRACTING ACTIVITY

U.S. Department of Transportation/OST Acquisition Services Division, M-63 1200 New Jersey Avenue, SE Washington, DC 20590

NATURE/DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING APPROVED

The Department of Transportation’s (DOT), Office of the Secretary (OST), Departmental Office of Intelligence, Security and Emergency Response (S-60) has an existing Tellabs-based Passive Optical Local Area Network (LAN), on which upgrade-work needs to be performed by a contractor.  Further details are given in the following paragraph numbered 3.

DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY’S NEED

DOT requires a critical system upgrade of its current Tellabs-based Passive Optical Local Area Network (POL). That needed contractor-work is specifically a lifecycle modernization of an active system, not a new installation. The project involves replacing 12-year-old, end-of-life (EOL) hardware while maintaining the existing fiber-optic backbone. Based on technical necessity, historical performance, and the unique constraints of the existing architecture, VTG is believed, by DOT, to be the only firm capable of performing that needed upgrade-work at the high level of quality and dependability and “know-how” indispensable to DOT, and at the low level of risk indispensable to DOT.  VTG’s unique qualifications are specified below in this document’s section numbered 5.

STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION

In accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul’s (RFO’s) Part 6 (section 6.103-1), I hereby determine that the subject procurement’s contemplated Tellabs-upgrade-project is available from only one source, VTG, LLC, and that competition is precluded for the reasons indicated below. There are no substitutes available.

STATEMENT DEMONSTRATING THE UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OF THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR OR THE NATURE OF THE ACTION REQUIRING THE USE OF THE AUTHORITY

DOT requires a critical system upgrade of its current Tellabs-based Passive Optical Local Area Network (POL). This procurement action is specifically a lifecycle modernization of an active system, not a new installation. DOT’s needed upgrade-project involves replacing 12-year-old, end-of-life (EOL) hardware while maintaining the existing fiber-optic backbone. Based on technical necessity, historical performance, and the unique constraints of the existing architecture, VTG, LLC is the only firm, known to DOT, which is capable of performing this needed upgrade-project at the high level of quality and dependability and “know-how” indispensable to DOT, and at the low level of risk indispensable to the Department.  VTG’s unique qualifications are as follows:

Twelve Years of Continuous Institutional Knowledge: VTG, LLC is the original equipment integrator that designed and installed the current system in 2014. VTG, LLC has maintained the system continuously for the last 12 years. This decade-plus of uninterrupted service has provided VTG, LLC with an exclusive understanding of the site-specific fiber pathways, signal degradations, and software configurations that no other firm can replicate without risking major faults in DOT’s existing system due, in part, to significantly elongating the procurement process.

Unique Expertise in Legacy-to-Modern Migration: Because VTG, LLC has managed the system’s maintenance and performance since its inception, VTG, LLC is the only firm with the knowledge required to migrate legacy data structures to new hardware without data loss. A new contractor would have to reverse-engineer the 12 years of maintenance context necessary to troubleshoot the inevitable complexities of upgrading a decade-old network-----in a cost-risk that would be unacceptable to DOT.

Infrastructure Preservation and Risk Mitigation: The existing Tellabs-specific fiber plant must remain in place to avoid the costs of a total replacement, which would likely measure in the hundreds-of-thousands of dollars. VTG, LLC’s 12-year history with this specific hardware allows VTG, LLC to guarantee a seamless, no-downtime upgrade. Any other firm attempting to interface with this infrastructure would pose an unacceptable risk of system failure.

Exclusive Single-Source Warranty: Because VTG, LLC has maintained the equipment for its entire lifespan, VTG, LLC is the only vendor able to provide a continued warranty that bridges the gap between the existing infrastructure and the new upgrades. This continuity of care is indispensable to DOT, as it prevents the "warranty gaps" that occur when a new firm attempts to service or upgrade a system previously maintained by another entity.

Local Proximity and Mission Readiness: VTG, LLC’s local office in St. Mary’s County, Maryland, coupled with that firm’s 12 years of cleared access and familiarity with DOT’s Piney Point facility, ensures VTG, LLC can execute this needed upgrade in a timely manner. VTG ,LLC’s proximity allows for a less-than-30-minute emergency-response-time—a level of service which VTG, LLC has consistently proven and attained over the last 12 years.

Authorized Vendor and Proprietary Integration: The current network's logic is built on Tellabs proprietary protocols. Only Tellabs-authorized hardware can integrate with the existing software suite. VTG holds specialized, high-level authorized integrator rights with Tellabs. These rights grant VTG, LLC exclusive access to proprietary firmware and engineering support required to bridge 12-year-old legacy hardware with modern components. 

The 12-year-old existing hardware is probably not far-distant from the end of its engineering life.  Failure to award this upgrade-project to VTG, LLC—the firm that has successfully designed, installed, and maintained the system since 2014—would introduce unacceptable risk to DOT.  The loss of VTG LLC’s 12 years of institutional knowledge during a critical upgrade would likely lead to system-wide failure, compromising DOT’s  ability to execute essential functions during a national crisis.

A DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS MADE TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS ARE SOLICITED FROM AS MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS IS PRACTICABLE, INCLUDING WHETHER A NOTICE WAS OR WILL BE PUBLICIZED AS REQUIRED BY SUBPART 5.2 AND, IF NOT, WHICH EXCEPTION UNDER 5.202 APPLIES

This Sole Source Special Notice / Pre-Solicitation Notice, as published in SAM.gov, constitutes DOT’s primary effort to identify as many fully-QUALIFIED-sources as possible.

THE ANTICIPATED DOLLAR VALUE OF THE PROPOSED ACQUISITION, INCLUDING OPTIONS IF APPLICABLE, AND A DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED COST TO THE GOVERNMENT WILL BE FAIR AND REASONABLE. 

The estimated total price of the subject contemplated Tellabs=upgrade project is $239,027.23.  Before the subject procurement’s contemplated Tellabs-upgrade-Purchase Order is awarded, DOT’s cognizant Contracting Officer and cognizant Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) will jointly make a determination regarding the fairness and reasonableness of the project’s price.           . 

DESCRIPTION OF MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED AND THE RESULTS OR A STATEMENT OF REASON MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED

Although S-60 and the cognizant Contracting Officer did search the Internet, this Sole Source Special Notice / Pre-Solicitation Notice, as published in SAM.gov, constitutes DOT’s primary effort to identify as many fully-QUALIFIED-sources as possible.

ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION

All indications so far are pointing to VTG, LLC as the only company capable of providing DOT’s needed Tellabs-upgrade-project at the high level of quality and dependability and “know-how” indispensable to the Department, and at the low level of risk indispensable to DOT.

A LISTING OF ANY SOURCES THAT EXPRESSED A WRITTEN INTEREST IN THE ACQUISITION

None so far—except for VTG, LLC.

A STATEMENT OF ANY ACTIONS THE AGENCY MAY TAKE TO REMOVE OR OVERCOME ANY BARRIERS TO COMPETITION, IF SUBSEQUENT ACQUISITIONS ARE ANTICIPATED

In support of any future procurement seeking services similar to those envisioned in the instant acquisition, it is likely that DOT would hereafter publish a Sole Source Special Notice / Pre-Solicitation Notice similar to this one.

Any entity interested in this procurement—OTHER THAN VTG, LLC—which believes that it could perform DOT’s needed Tellabs-upgrade-project, as described herein, at the high level of quality and dependability and “know-how” indispensable to DOT, and at the low level of risk indispensable to DOT, may attempt to prove those points by e-mailing a Statement of Qualifications for receipt by james.mowery@dot.gov and Carlos.Marrero@dot.gov and Leonel.Raba@dot.gov not later than 11:30 PM Eastern Daylight Time June 11th, 2025.
