5. Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS):
Effective 14 August 2017, NCACS credentials will no longer be accepted for base access. Any new contractor, vendor or supplier requesting base 
access will be required to obtain a Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) credential. NCACS credentials will no longer be issued. Only 
DBIDS credentials will be issued to ALL contractors, vendors and suppliers seeking base access AFTER 30 June 2017. Defense Biometric 
Identification System (DBIDS) increases installation security and communications by receiving frequent database updates on changes to personnel
/credential status, law enforcement warrants, lost/stolen cards, and force protection conditions. The system provides continuous vetting anytime the 
DBIDS card is scanned at an installation entry point. 
If you currently have a Navy Commercial Access Control System (NCACS) card, the following is required to get a DBIDS credential:
Present your NCACS Card and a completed copy of the SECNAV FORM 5512/1 to the base Visitor Control Center (VCC) representative.
The VCC will pull up your information in the computer, ensuring all information is current and correct.
Once your information is validated, a temporary DBIDS credential is provided.
Your temporary credential will have an expiration date, prior to which you will need to obtain your permanent DBIDS credential (~ 180 days).
For each additional U.S. Navy installation to which you need access, the first time you visit you only need to bring your DBIDS credential and 
statement of purpose for base access when arriving at the Visitor Control Center.
The representative will enter base access authorization and then you may proceed to work.
If you do NOT have an NCACS Card, the following is required to obtain a DBIDS credential:
Present a letter or official document from any government sponsoring organization that provides the purpose for your access.
Present valid identification, such as a passport or Real ID Act-compliant state driver's license.
Present a completed copy of the SECNAV 5512/1 form to obtain your background check.
Upon completion of the background check, the Visitor Control Center representative will complete the DBIDS enrollment process, which includes 
your photo, finger prints, base restrictions, and several other assessments; after all this is done, you will be provided with your new DBIDS credential.
All deliveries must pass through the base Truck Inspection Station. All delivery vehicles are subject to inspection. Drivers should expect delays due to

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
FOR 
DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY  
CYBERSECURITY & INFRASTRUCTURE SECURITY AGENCY  
CYBER TECHNOLOGY SERVICES 
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION NUMBER: 70RCSJ26RFI000001 
 
INTRODUCTION 
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency 
(CISA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as a means of conducting market research 
to identify potential qualified companies having an interest in, and the resources to support the 
Cyber Technology Services (CTS) requirement. This RFI is for planning purposes only and shall 
not constitute an obligation on the part of the Government. This is NOT a Request for Quotations 
or Proposals. No solicitation document exists, and the Government may or may not issue a 
formal solicitation resulting from the responses received to this RFI. 
 
The Government will not pay for any response expenses. All costs incurred responding to this 
RFI will be solely at the interested party's expense. Failure to respond to this RFI will not 
preclude participation in any future solicitation. Any information received will become the 
property of the Government and will not be returned to the respondent. Interested parties are 
responsible for adequately marking proprietary or sensitive information. Government technical 
experts drawn from staff within CISA, and other federal agencies may review responses. The 
Government may use selected support contractor personnel to assist in the review of the RFI 
responses. These support contractors will be bound by appropriate non-disclosure agreements to 
protect proprietary information. 
 
The purpose of this RFI is to provide interested companies with the opportunity to submit 
information regarding their capabilities to meet the Government’s requirements. Responses to 
this RFI will assist the Government in refining the scope, technical approach, contract type, 
potential contract vehicles, and the method of acquisition.   
 
PROGRAM BACKGROUND 
The CTS requirement will provide support services in carrying out the day-to-day operations 
through the sustainment of Government networks and related services utilizing cybersecurity 
activities and computer network defense initiatives for the Cybersecurity Division (CSD), Threat 
Hunting (TH) Sub-division which entails Information Technology (IT) Development Operations, 
IT Security Operations, Operation and Maintenance (O&M) activities, and Technology and 
Innovation services.  
 
Additionally, the requirement will provide services designed to improve operations, to include 
cybersecurity activities and computer network defense initiatives to satisfy the task areas listed 

2 
below and described in the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) for a proposed single task 
order.  
Task Area 1 – Program Management 
Task Area 2 – IT Architecture, Technology, and Innovation Services 
Task Area 3 – IT Engineering, Development Operations and Services 
Task Area 4 – Data Management & Analytics 
Task Area 5 – IT Sustainment, Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Services 
Task Area 6 – IT Security Operations and Services 
Task Area 7 – Laboratory Support Services 
Task Area 8 – IT Service Desk, Asset Management & Logistical Support

Respondents that believe they possess the capabilities to provide all the task areas should submit 
documentation of their ability to meet each of the task areas. 
Respondents that believe they possess the capabilities to provide four or more of the task areas 
should submit documentation of their ability to meet those task areas. 
It is imperative that responses be brief and concise, yet articulately and clearly demonstrate the 
ability to perform each task area listed with appropriate documentation supporting claims of 
organizational and staff ability. 
Include the type of work your company performed within the last three years in support of the 
same or similar requirements, size, and complexity, indicating the customer, contract type and 
approximate value, and scope and major functional areas delivered. 
Descr
ibe your organization’s core capabilities and provide one example that reflects your 
company’s experience in each task area outlined in the draft PWS, particularly: 
• L
arge‑scale cybersecurity engineering and operations in Federal environments;
• Development, Security, and Operations (DevSecOps) for mission‑critical systems
(classified and unclassified);
• 24x7x365 SOC operations and incident response;
• Threat‑hunting tools, platforms, and services;

ndicate your organization’s size and socio-economic status (e.g., large business, small business,

Federal Civilian Executive Branch) and as a result implemented new tools and/or data
sources.

scribe how your Company leveraged roles such as Project Managers, Tech Writers,

escribe your Company’s experience successfully delivering full-lifecycle architecture,

s your Company currently performing or have in the past performed same or similar

ased on the scope and risk described in the draft requirements document, what contract

dentify any sections or task areas of the draft requirements document that you believe

dentify any innovative practices, technologies, or approaches (technical, operational, or

rovide feedback on the realism and feasibility of the described key roles (e.g., Senior

ELIGIBILITY 
The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 541519 – Other Computer Related Services

Note: In accordance with DHS Directive 060-01, Development and Use of Strategic

SUBMISSION DETAILS

THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)

Procurement Type: Request for Information (RFI) Sources Sought 

Title:  	 Commercial Off-the-Shelf Computer Aided Dispatch System

NAICS Codes:           541512 Computer Systems Design Services

Primary POC: 	Brad Clark, Office of Shore Forces – Bradford.D.Clark@uscg.mil 

A. Background 

The USCG uses its 45 Command Centers (CCs) as the 24/7 Command & Control (C2) and Information Management (IM) hub for Operational Commanders to execute the service's eleven statutory missions. The USCG's historic investment in new sensor and AI-driven analysis capabilities is creating a new demand signal for process improvement supported by greater integration, automation and efficiency in the CC operational workflow.

The current operational environment requires watchstanders to pivot between numerous disparate systems, paper-based checklists, and manual data entry to manage a single incident. This fractured workflow degrades all CC functions and slows the speed of operational decision making. 

B. Scope

The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is seeking information from potential offerors who are interested in, and are able to, provide a modernized, cloud-based/cloud capable, Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) system to serve as the foundational workflow engine for the CC(s). Selected offerors will be expected to provide a demonstration of advertised capability to representatives of the Coast Guard. The Coast Guard is seeking a CAD system to provide the following specific operational functions to support the operational workflow:

Provide the capability to plan missions and assign resources in advance of a defined operational period;

Provide the information and visualization necessary to manage an incident from the time the initial time an incident is reported to the conclusion of the incident; 

Provide transparency regarding the status of all current and planned missions;

Integrate all tactical communications capabilities and provide voice to text transcription;

Provide capability to enable CC to send and receive tasking data and updates to/from deployed teams, cutters, boats, or aircraft via machine-to-machine communications (e.g. Tactical Awareness Kits (TAK);

Provide capability to export operational data from the CAD to an appropriate cross domain gateway to support ingestion, processing and/or routing to higher classification levels.

Automate routine processes (e.g. generate and complete Quick Response Cards (QRCs)) and capture mission/case data for records management;

Provide the capability to access and view available sensor data;

Provide CAD-based AI to support queries, briefs and produce tailored operational reports

Integrate with existing or intended USCG enterprise GIS capability;

Provide integration with 911 PSAPS/NextGen 911 capabilities;

Provide automated alerts, updates and operational information to operational staff and supervisors;

Support two-way data transfer between USCG command centers and the USCG technical solution for National Incident Management System operations.

Provide capability that enables users to configure the user-interface to adapt to user-specific needs

The CAD system will be entirely UNCLASSIFIED but will host sensitive data. The CAD system must be able to handle a high volume and velocity of data from various sources, including AI-generated alerts and sensor feeds. The CAD system will be expected to support approximately 1,600 primary users (watchstanders) and approximately 5,000 secondary users at the supported operational commands. The CAD system will need to be highly available, reliable, maintainable, and scalable. The CAD system will need to be cyber secure and resilient, prioritizing modern, API-based integration to ensure a flexible and extensible design.

NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Regional Procurement Office East (RPOE), Network Contracting Office 4 (NCO 4) intends to award a sole source contract pursuant to FAR 19.1406 to Four Points Technology LLC located at 13221 Woodland Park RD, Suite 400, Herndon, Virginia 20171. The Wilmington VA Medical Center requires a 5-year Instrument Manager Software Subscription and 1-time upgrade. STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
 
Spectrum Guard Training and Annual Maintenance 
 
Part 1 
 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
 
1.  INTRODUCTION:  The United States Secret Service Technical Security Division (TSD) 
provides special security activities in support of the United States Secret Service (USSS) 
protective mission. This is a non-personal services contract to provide Spectrum Guard 
Training and annual maintenance coverage. The Government shall not exercise any 
supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services 
herein.  Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor 
who, in turn is responsible to the Government.  
 
1.1 Background:   TSD procured Spectrum Guard Radio Frequency (RF) equipment for 
use in support of its protective mission.  Since the original purchase, there have been 
software changes that require training on the software enhancements and maintenance 
coverage (warranties).   
 
1.2 Objectives:  To provide a 5-day, 40-hour training event designed to fully train the 
USSS personnel on the functionality of the updated software and methodology utilized 
in RF searches utilizing the Spectrum Guard and associated peripheral devices and 
annual maintenance coverage. 
 
1.3 Scope: The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, 
transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services 
necessary to perform the Spectrum Guard Training and annual maintenance as defined 
in this Statement of Work except for those items specified as Government furnished 
property and services.

1. BACKGROUND 
 
 
The National Coordination Office (NCO) is the permanent staff of the National Executive Committee for 
Space-Based Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT). It supports the Committee by coordinating 
GPS-related information across federal agencies, fostering interagency collaboration, and resolving 
issues. The NCO's primary communication tool is its website, GPS.gov, which serves as the 
centerpiece of its public outreach and education efforts, providing timely GPS-related information, 
resources, and data to the public and federal stakeholders. 
However, the current site faces challenges, including outdated technology, limited user engagement, 
and accessibility issues. As digital technologies evolve, the NCO must adopt user-centered design, 
agile delivery practices, and adhere to federal digital policies to ensure government information is 
accessible anytime, anywhere, and on any device. 
 
 
2. OBJECTIVE 
 
 
The objective of this order is to sustain and maintain the GPS.gov website by ensuring stable 
operations, compliance with federal web standards, and incremental feature enhancements. The work 
includes routine maintenance, security updates, content management support, training for contributors, 
coordination with NOAA's hosting services, and the implementation of up to three low-to-moderate 
complexity features to improve usability and accessibility. This effort ensures that GPS.gov remains a 
reliable, accessible, and user-friendly resource for federal stakeholders and the public. 
 
 
3. TASKS 
 
 
3.1 Task 1 – GPS.gov Maintenance 
 
The contractor shall maintain the Drupal-based platform by providing security, performance, and 
accessibility updates in coordination with NOAA’s Web Operations Center (WOC). Services will include, 
but are not limited to: 
● Apply Drupal core and module updates, including security patches and baseline 
system changes. 
● Coordinate with WOC to ensure reliable hosting, secure deployment, and version control using 
contractor-compatible CI/CD or approved manual processes. 
● Maintain compliance with federal digital standards, including Section 508 and 
USWDS alignment. 
● Monitor and address accessibility issues, technical errors, and deprecated content modules. 
 


 
3.2 Task 2 - GPS.gov Enhancements and Feature Development 
 
The contractor shall implement up to three low-to-moderate complexity system changes (updates) to 
improve usability, content access, or backend efficiency, using existing Drupal architecture and 
approved design components. Services may include, but are not limited to: 
● Update existing components and content types for displaying content. 
● Minor updates to the admin user interface. 
● Ensure all updates are accessible, responsive, and tested across devices and browsers. 
● Conduct user acceptance testing (UAT) and make necessary refinements prior to release. 
 
3.3 Task 3 - Content Governance and Training 
 
The contractor shall assist the Government content managers in methods to improve content quality, 
structure, and editorial workflow and provide quarterly refresher training in effective content 
management and publishing practices. Services shall include, but are not limited to: 
● Assist the Government content manager on methods to configure Drupal editorial workflows 
with defined roles and approval processes for publishing. 
● Update existing training materials for live sessions, and recordings to support both new and 
experienced content contributors. Provide refresher training sessions each quarter. 
● Maintain documentation outlining content types, templates, and publishing standards. 
● Provide editorial guidance to content managers that supports plain language, accessibility, 
content length limits, and readability best practices. 
4. TYPE OF ORDER 
 
Firm Fixed Price (FFP) 
5. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
 
The period of performance shall be for one, twelve-month base year and four option years period. 
6. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE 
 
Work will be performed off-premise at the contractor’s facility or remotely, if approved in writing by the 
Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR).

NOAA GNSS Radio Occultation Commercial Data Buy 
SBEM IDIQ Task Order 1 (TO-1) 
Statement of Work 
Introduction 
In this Task Order, NOAA intends to acquire near-real-time global navigation satellite 
system (GNSS) radio occultation (RO) satellite data satisfying the requirements set forth in 
the NOAA Commercial Data Program Space Based Environmental Monitoring (SBEM) 
IDIQ contract Statement of Work (SOW). NOAA intends to use these data in operational 
numerical weather prediction models, space weather models, and other systems. NOAA 
reserves the right to issue subsequent, simultaneous, and additional Task Orders for RO 
data during this period of performance.  
Scope 
NOAA is soliciting commercial near-real-time satellite-based GNSS RO and ionospheric 
measurements that will be processed into neutral atmosphere and space weather products. 
These derived products will be fed into NOAA’s operational data systems, including weather 
and space weather analysis and prediction systems, and used for weather, climate, and 
atmospheric research purposes. All data and products will be archived by NOAA. NOAA 
seeks the following requirements: 
Requirements 
Part I - Data Preparation 
I. Requirements for New GNSS-RO Data Providers 
A. For Contractors who have not previously delivered GNSS-RO data to NOAA, the 
Contractor shall provide all necessary information needed to support NOAA 
implementation and testing of the Contractor’s data. The Contractor shall provide 
technical documentation (SBEM IDIQ SOW Section C.4.5.3: Data Delivery and 
Documentation), including but not limited to data format specifications, sample data, 
and other information required for data ingestion and processing (SBEM IDIQ SOW 
Sections C.3.1: Test Data, C.3.1.1: Limited Test Data Deliveries, C.4.5.4: GNSS-RO 
Test Data). Delivery mechanisms and data handling procedures will be communicated 
to the Contractor. 
B. The Contractor shall provide engineering support as needed to enable Government 
acquisition and processing of the supplied datasets to include supporting technical 
exchanges. The Contractor shall deliver sample data for secure ingest, configuration 
and testing. Additionally, the Contractor shall deliver up to 48 hours of contiguous 
near-real-time data for testing of delivery and data flow processes (SBEM IDIQ SOW 

 
2 
Sections C.3.1: Test Data, C.3.1.1: Limited Test Data Deliveries, C.4.5.4: GNSS-RO 
Test Data). 
C. The Period of Performance for Data Preparation shall be for 35 days from December 
1, 2026 through January 5, 2027 and shall start and end at 11:00 am Eastern Time.  
Part II - Data Delivery 
I. General Requirements for All Data 
A. Period of Performance for Data Delivery. 
1. For Contractors who have previously provided data to NOAA, the period 
of performance shall be for 731 days estimated from December 1, 2026 
through December 1, 2028 and shall start and end at 11:00 am Eastern 
Time.  
2. For Contractors who have not previously provided data to NOAA, the 
Data Delivery Period of Performance shall immediately follow the Data 
Preparation Period of Performance and shall be for 696 days estimated 
from January 5, 2027 through December 1, 2028 and shall start and end 
at 11:00 am Eastern Time.  
B. The Offeror shall deliver Level 0 and Level 1a data (SBEM IDIQ SOW Section C.4.5: 
Delivery Requirements). 
C. Data delivered shall be subject to the terms and conditions specified in SBEM IDIQ 
SOW Section C.3.7
     : Data Rights     . NOAA has no additional obligations under the 
IDIQ contract or this Delivery Order related to data use by third parties. In no event is 
NOAA liable to the contractor for third party use or release of contractor data. 
Delivery of the data will utilize one or more of the following Data Rights options: 
1. Option 1:  Right to distribute all Contractor-provided data to any entity 
immediately after receipt at NOAA with no restrictions on their use or 
further distribution, under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 
International license (CC BY 4.0).  
2. Option 2:  Right to distribute all Contractor-provided data to U.S. 
Government agencies, International Partners, including but not limited to 
those responsible for national meteorological, space weather, or 
hydrological services, and National Meteorological and Hydrological 
Services, WMO-designated Regional Specialized Meteorological 
Centers, members of the Coordination Group for Meteorological 
Satellites, and non-profit entities and academic entities, immediately after 
receipt at NOAA, for non-commercial use but not for further distribution.  

 
3 
3. Option 2A:  In addition to the rights under Option 2, Option 1 rights will 
apply to all Contractor-provided data beginning at 24 hours after 
collection.  
4. Option 3:  Right to distribute all Contractor-provided data to U.S. 
Government agencies, International Partners, including but not limited to 
those responsible for national meteorological, space weather, or 
hydrological services, and National Meteorological and Hydrological 
Services, WMO-designated Regional Specialized Meteorological 
Centers, and members of the Coordination Group for Meteorological 
Satellites, immediately after receipt at NOAA, for non-commercial use but 
not for further distribution.  
5. Option 3A:  In addition to the rights under Option 3, Option 1 rights will 
apply to all Contractor-provided data beginning at 24 hours after 
collection.  
D. Spatial distribution is an important aspect of the data delivery requirements. The 
Government seeks delivery of all global data (all latitudes and longitudes) to meet or 
exceed the requirements specified in SBEM IDIQ SOW Section C.4.3.2: Specific 
Geospatial Distributions, paragraphs 1 and 2 only (paragraph 3 does 
      not apply to 
this task order).  
E. This SOW includes Desired Capabilities.  Desired Capabilities are features of Offeror 
provided data that are requested by the Government but are not mandatory.  Desired 
Capabilities are requested in order to improve the utility of delivered data and are 
considered to add value to the Offeror proposals.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)

 Risk Management Framework (RMF) Process Efficiencies

Issuing Organization: 764 ESS

RFI Number: 

Posting Date: 1 May 2026

Response Due Date: 27 May 2026

Considered NAICS Code: 541512 – Computer Systems Design Services 

Considered PSC Code: DA01 – IT and Telecom – Business Application/Application Development Support Services

Classification: UNCLASSIFIED

1.0 PURPOSE

This Request for Information (RFI) is issued by the 764th ESS Contracting Squadron on behalf of USAFE-AFAFRICA/A6 for planning and market research purposes only. This RFI is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or an Invitation for Bid (IFB), and does not commit the Government to issue a solicitation, award a contract, or pay any costs incurred in the preparation of a response. All information submitted in response to this RFI is voluntary.

The Government seeks information from industry on potential solutions to address the requirements identified within this RFI. Of particular interest are commercial solutions, particularly automation and AI solutions that drive both process improvements and mature technologies to deliver efficiencies in the Risk Management Framework (RMF) process while maintaining full compliance with NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 and DoDI 8510.01. 

2.0 BACKGROUND

Without question, Europe has been a crucible of innovatively dynamic and deadly adversarial threats, a fact that was driven home by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022, an evolution of warfare on that has been on display for the whole world to see. North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) countries race to rapidly respond to these threats with technology underpinning countermeasures. Technology has inherent cybersecurity risk, which the Department of War (DoW) mitigates via the Risk Management Framework (RMF) process (NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5; DoDI 8510.01).

DoW Problem

The RMF's multi-step process, with its numerous tasks, roles, and documentation requirements, can be highly complex and perceived as overly bureaucratic. This complexity can lead to a lengthy and cumbersome process, making it difficult for organizations to navigate and implement effectively. Additionally, the detailed nature of each step, while thorough, can create a significant administrative burden, exacerbated by the transition from NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 to Rev 5, as well as the US Air Force mandating 720 baseline controls for every system seeking a new or renewed authority to operate (ATO). However, those are just baseline controls, and the reality is that NIST SP 800-53 has over 1,100 controls that could apply to a system.

The diagram below is a notional 12-month timeline to secure an ATO. Information Systems Owners (ISOs), as well as the AODR/SCA team collaborate and work together on the Plan step (Step 0). ISOs and their teams are primarily responsible for Steps 1-3 (orange) but receive significant assistance from the AODR/SCA team throughout the steps. The AODR/SCA Team are almost solely responsible for Step 4 but can engage the ISO and security team as needed. Step 5 is mostly preparing the decision brief and documents, while Step 6 is a whole-team effort. 

The RMF's detailed and often lengthy process portrayed above is not always well-suited for today's fast-paced and dynamic environments, particularly those that embrace agile development methodologies and fielding technology at the speed of need. The time required to complete the full RMF cycle for a new system, for an authorized system to make a significant change, or for an authorized system to connect to another system--the latter two situations resulting in more analyses and paperwork--can be a major drawback, hindering innovation and rapid deployment of new technologies.

Specific to USAFE-AFAFRICA (U-A), the war in Ukraine, kinetic and non-kinetic weapon development of adversaries, and developmental testing of Air Force Research Lab capabilities, demanded that U-A have its own Authorizing Official (AO) boundary. Operation EPIC FURY only further drove home the need for U-A to expedite its own capability development and implementation. As a result, U-A’s AO boundary is growing at a rate unsustainable by the current way U-A manages the RMF process. Since August 2024, U-A’s AO Boundary grew from 8 approved systems to 17 approved systems, with another three systems that are working toward approval (one of which still isn’t approved after 17 months). This rate of growth coupled with the Rev 4 to Rev 5 transition milestones set by SAF/CN, required the AODR/SCA team to nearly completely focus on the status quo, and hindered U-A’s cybersecurity program to dedicate the manpower needed to scrutinize existing processes, develop efficiencies, and pilot new automation and/or AI technologies organically.

3.0 NEED STATEMENT

USAFE-AFAFRICA/A6 seeks commercial solutions to prototype and operationally demonstrate efficiencies in all steps of the RMF process while adhering to NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 and DoDI 8510.01. This includes both process improvements (non-technological), and technological innovations that can speed up the RMF process without sacrificing quality of work. The end goal is for the Authorizing Official Designated Representative (AODR) to provide an accurate cybersecurity risk that the AO can weigh against operational risk. Based on the operational urgency, prototype/pathfinder nature, and 12-month implementation window, the Government is considering a layered acquisition approach to utilize Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). However, the Government will consider Industry input in its market research on how to address this requirement.

4.0 SCOPE & GOVERNMENT EXPECTATIONS

This multi-phased approach seeks to identify efficient process improvements, as well as mature commercial technologies that will demonstrate end-to-end objectives within no more than 12 months. This is an operational pathfinder in concert with U-A’s AODR, the Security Control Assessment team, system owners and their support teams (e.g. PgMs, ISSOs, ISSMs), and requirement owners.

Contingent on the quality and completeness of the white papers the Government receives, and should the government choose to execute a contract supporting this effort, the Government expects the vendor to fully implement process improvements and technical capabilities within 12 months from contract award. In turn, the Government is willing to dedicate reasonable time to provide vendors with access to U-A personnel involved in navigating RMF to help vendors better understand the local processes. The Government expects the vendor to examine and analyze each step of the RMF process and deliver process improvements and a functional technology/tool that streamlines each step. Doing so allows both the system owner’s team and the AODR/SCA team to benefit from gained efficiencies, rather than limiting benefits to a single entity by focusing on just one RMF step. The Government expects the vendors to address systems that are unclassified, SECRET, and SECRET//REL (TOP SECRET systems are authorized by a different AO). The Government expects vendors to propose technology that either already meets NIST standards via an ATO or interim authority to test (IATT), a technology that currently possesses a Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation, or technology that is in the process of being evaluated by a competent and independent Common Criteria licensed laboratory. Technology that does not possess an ATO or Common Criteria certificate will be addressed on a case-by-case basis. While vendors may utilize consultants for process mapping, as mentioned earlier in this paragraph, the primary deliverables must be fully implemented within 12 months of contract award.

5.0 COMPELLING SOLUTION CHARACTERISTICS

Required Attributes

- Address all steps of the RMF process

- Include an analysis of all 720 baseline controls and what can be standardized by a template

- Be novel in capability, responsiveness, and delivery accuracy

- Be capable of reducing Step 4 from 90 days to no more than 45 days

- Be mature and ready to demonstrate to key stakeholders, to include U-A’s AO

- Be ready to fully implement within no more than 12 months

- Be adaptable to various types of systems (kinetic, non-kinetic, COTS, GOTS, etc.)

- Incorporate automation and/or AI

- Be cost-effective and friendly to supply chains

Desired Attributes

- A system and/or processes that thoroughly reviews RMF artifacts submitted by the program owners

- A system and/or process that can output results with applicable references (e.g. explain why a control was partially satisfied or failed)

- A system and/or process that can output results in a way the SCAR can easily review the results and make recommendations to the SCA

- A system and/or process that can handle increased load and surge without degraded performance

- A system that is simple to operate and can evolve over time without major cost implications and training requirements

- A system that guarantees confidentiality, integrity, and availability of its data

- A system that offers a consistent user experience and provides a consistent output.

6.0 INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INDUSTRY

Responses should be limited to 12 pages (excluding cover page and capability statements) and address the following:

Company Information: 

- Company name, CAGE code, UEI, address, POC (name, phone, email)

- Business size and applicable socioeconomic certifications

- Contract vehicles currently held (GSA MAS, GWAC, IDIQ, OTA consortia memberships, etc.)

Technical Solution Overview 

- Description of proposed solution (process, technology, or hybrid)

- Mapping of solution capability to each of the six RMF steps

- Approach to standardizing/templating the 720 USAF baseline controls

- Description of automation/AI components and underlying models/architecture

- Approach for reducing Step 4 from 90 to ≤45 days

Maturity & Compliance

- Technology Readiness Level (TRL)

- Existing ATO status (Issuing AO, boundary, classification, expiration) OR

- Common Criteria certification status (EAL level, Protection Profile, lab)

- FedRAMP status (if cloud-based)

- DoD IL level (IL2/4/5/6) supported

- Past performance on similar DoD/Federal RMF efforts

Implementation Approach

- A brief description of how the vendor would conduct a live technical demonstration or pitch (using synthetic/dummy data)

- A proposed milestone schedule that shows how the vendor would achieve full implementation in 12 months (e.g. ## days for analyses, ## days for prototype delivery, ## to pilot prototype, etc.)

- Personnel/access required from the Government

- Use of consultants/subcontractors (if any)

- Risks and mitigation strategies

Pricing Construct (ROM)

- Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate

- Pricing model (FFP, T&M, subscription/SaaS, hybrid)

- Identification of any contract vehicles through which the solution can be procured

Recommended Acquisition Approach

-Vendor recommendation on acquisition pathway (FAR-based contract, OTA, CSO, SBIR/STTR, etc.)

- Recommended contract type and rationale

7.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS

Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI with a white paper. White papers are due no later than 27 May 2026, 1400 CEST. Responses shall be submitted via e-mail to Mr. Corey Chopko at corey.chopko@us.af.mil, Ms. Ina Hemmer at ina.hemmer.de@us.af.mil, and Capt Kevin Sheedy at kevin.sheedy.3@us.af.mil as described for the below sections. Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. To aid the Government, please segregate proprietary information. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

U-A representatives may or may not choose to meet with potential Offerors. Such discussions would only be intended to get further clarification of potential capability to meet the requirements, especially any development and certification risks.

Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing via e-mail to Mr. Corey Chopko at corey.chopko@us.af.mil, Ms. Ina Hemmer at ina.hemmer.de@us.af.mil, and Capt Kevin Sheedy at kevin.sheedy.3@us.af.mil by 13 May 2026, 1400 CEST. Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Questions will be answered by posting answers in response to this RFI; accordingly, questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information. The Government does not guarantee that questions received after 13 May 2026, 1400 CEST, will be answered.

The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding the Government. The Government has not made a commitment to procure any of the items discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 
Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Naval Surface Warfare Center Carderock Division 
(NSWCCD) intends to award a firm fixed price (FFP) purchase order using Simplified Acquisition Procedures under the authority of 
FAR 13.106-1(b) the Contracting Officer has determined only one brand to be reasonably available. The Government intends to solicit 
for: The annual renewal of Lightning Chart Perpetual Licenses and Support, as detailed in the attached solicitation. This solicitation 
is a brand name, small business set-aside (justification attached). This announcement constitutes the only solicitation and a written 
solicitation will not be issued. Quotes are being requested under Request for Quotation (RFQ) no. N0016726Q1101. The NAICS code 
is 541519 and the business size standard is $34M. 
The provisions and clauses included and/or incorporated in this solicitation document are those in effect through the Federal 
Acquisition Circular. This RFQ incorporates all provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC 2022-02 
and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) DPN 20211130. SEE ATTACHED SOLICITATION FOR 
CLAUSES AND PROVISIONS. 
This is a Brand Name Only solicitation; however, interested parties who can provide an equal item may identify their interest to this 
requirement by submitting a capabilities statement no later than Wednesday, 27 May 2026 9:00 am EST. A determination by the 
Government not to compete this proposed purchase order based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the 
Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive 
acquisition in the future. 
All responses shall include official company name, firm fixed price (FFP), FOB destination, a point of contact name and phone 
number, CAGE code, business size and payment terms. 
Each response must also clearly indicate the capability of the quoter to meet all specifications and requirements. Additionally, any 
applicable freight/shipping charges must be incorporated into the line items as we are not authorized to pay standalone shipping/freight 
costs. 
The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible quoter whose quote, conforming to the 
solicitation that will be most advantageous to the Government, price reasonableness and other factors considered. The Government 
intends to evaluate quotations and award a contract without discussions with quoters. 
Evaluation Factors (in order of importance) 
1. Technical – Quotes must reflect the required specifications included in the RFQ. 
2. Price – Quotes must include all applicable costs. 
See 52.212-2- Evaluation—Commercial Products and Commercial Services, incorporated into this solicitation at pages 05-06, for 
additional information regarding the evaluation process for this award. 
Quote packages are due by Wednesday, 27 May 2026 9:00 am EST. Late quotes will not be considered.  
Quote packages shall be submitted to Lametria Smith, at lametria.r.smith.civ@us.navy.mil and, as mentioned 
above, contain the following information: 
a) Official Company Name; 
b) Point of contact including name and phone number; 
c) Manufacturers specifications; 
d) Delivery lead time; and 
e) Cage Code number 
The Government reserves the right to request that the awardee reduce its total price, or adjust CLIN prices with no change to total price, 
in order to reduce administrative costs and avoid unnecessary burdens for the agency pursuant to FAR 12.201-1(d). 
 
The Point of Contact for this acquisition is Lametria Smith, at lametria.r.smith.civ@us.navy.mil

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division - Gillem 
DACID Gillem Staff Support 
 
Part 1 
 
General Information 
                                                                                       
1.  GENERAL. This is a non-personnel service contract to provide technical and staff support 
throughout the Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division (DACID) - Gillem. The 
Government will not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers 
performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to 
the Contractor who, in turn is responsible to the Government. 
 
1.1 Description of Services/Introduction. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, 
supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-
personal services necessary to provide Information Technology Operations Support on Gillem 
Enclave at Forest Park, Georgia as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for 
those items specified as Government furnished property and services. The Contractor shall 
propose the labor category, and number of hours required to professionally meet all the PWS 
requirements. 
 
1.2 Background. DACID Gillem mission is to provide full-service forensic and biometric support 
(traditional, expeditionary, and reach-back) to Army and DoD entities worldwide. Provide 
specialized forensics training and research capabilities, serve as Executive Agent for the DoD 
Convicted Offender DNA database registry commonly known as CODIS, responsible for 
technical management over the DACID criminalistics program, oversees mandatory training and 
certification of employees and laboratory accreditation, conduct research, development, testing, 
and evaluation. Provide forensic and biometric services to other federal departments and 
agencies, as required. 
 
1.3 Objectives. DACID Gillem requires subject matter expertise support to augment critical staff 
and directorate technical positions in order to perform its forensic and biometric mission 
effectively while minimizing loss of operational capacity.   
 
1.4 Scope. The contractor shall perform associated tasks in the following “Core Support” areas: 
Logistics Management Specialist (6), and Supply Technician (1). The technical support 
requirements for this Performance Work Statement (PWS) fall within DACID Gillem’s mission 
and responsibilities and are designed to assist DACID Gillem in meeting its operational needs. 
 
1.5 Period of Performance. The period of performance shall be for one base year and two 
option years (OY):   
Base Year:  13 March 2027 – 12 March 2028 
Option Year 1:       13 March 2028 – 12 March 2029 
Option Year 2:       13 March 2029 – 12 March 2030 
  
 
1.6 General Information 
 
1.6.1 Quality Control. The contractor shall engage in an effective quality control program to 
ensure services are performed in accordance with this PWS. The contractor’s quality control 

 
program is the means by which he assures himself that his work complies with the requirement 
of the contract. The Contractor shall develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent, and 
ensure non-recurrence of defective services. A copy of the Contractor’s basic Quality Control 
Plan shall be provided to the Contracting Officer for approval not later than 10 calendar days 
after receipt of award. An updated copy shall be provided to the Contracting Officer and 
Contracting Officer Representative (COR) as changes occur. 
 
1.6.2 Quality Assurance. The government shall evaluate the contractor’s performance under this 
contract in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP). This plan focuses 
primarily on what the Government must do to ensure that the contractor has performed in 
accordance with the established performance standards. The QASP defines how the 
performance standards will be applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum 
acceptable defect rate(s).        
 
1.6.3 Federal Government Holidays. The contractor is not required to perform services on the 
following holidays:   
 
New Year’s Day    1st day of January 
Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday  3rd Monday of January 
President’s Day    3rd Monday of February 
Memorial Day    last Monday of May 
Juneteenth Day    19
th day of June 
Independence Day   4th day of July 
Labor Day     1st Monday of September 
Columbus Day    2nd Monday of October 
Veteran’s Day    11th day of November 
Thanksgiving Day    4th Thursday of November 
Christmas Day    25th day of December 
 
1.6.4 Hours of Operation. The core hours of operation are from 0600 – 1800 hours during 
normal workdays. However, due to mission related activities, standard work hours are subject to 
change at the discretion of the Government. The normal work hours of the Contractor shall be 
scheduled in agreement with the COR.  
  
1.6.5 Place of Performance. Requirements shall be performed at the Department of the Army 
Criminal Investigation Division (DACID) Gillem - Main, 4930 North 31
st Street, Forest Park, GA 
30297-5205. Contractors are authorized to work from an Alternate duty/remote location during 
emergency situations within the DACID Gillem Main area of operations, with the approval of the 
COR and Contracting Officer. Contractor shall continue to meet tasks, deliverables, and 
required level of support in accordance with the contract. Government reserves the right to 
approve, disapprove, or cancel contract personnel working from an alternate duty/remote 
location. Working from a remote location will be at no additional expense to the government. 
The Government does not authorize the use of off-site rates to accomplish alternate 
duty/remote location work and will not be responsible for any associated costs. Personal or 
company issued equipment may not be used to access the government network infrastructure 
unless pre-approved; examples include using VPN or a corporate network. However, an inability 
to access the government network infrastructure using authorized devices does not necessarily 
prohibit the contractor from performing off-site, whenever the work could be performed without 
such access. 
 

 
1.6.6 Type of Contract. The Government assess that this service can be provided under GSA 
OASIS Section 8(A) and will award a non-personal contract to be determined by a competitive 
cost estimate and the customer. 
 
1.6.7 Security Requirements. Contractor shall be U.S. citizens, possess a Secret Security 
Clearance, and must maintain the Secret Security Clearance for the life of the contract. 
Contractor shall be able to pass general access requirements for the DACID Gillem – Main 
facilities. Contractor shall provide proper documentation of their security clearance to the DACID 
Gillem Security Officer prior to performing their duties. 
 
1.6.7.1 Installation Access. Contractor, including subcontractors, shall comply with applicable 
installation and facility access security policies and procedures at all times. Contractor and 
subcontractors shall be issued an Installation Pass through the Automated Installation Entry 
(AIE) Security System to access the installation. The Gillem Enclave at the DACID Gillem – 
Main location respectfully is a limited access installation. Unscheduled gate closures by the 
security managers at this location may occur at any time. In accordance with Army Regulation 
525-13, paragraph 5-19, Contractor shall undergo a verification process by the installation 
Provost Marshal Office, Director of Emergency Services to determine the trustworthiness and 
suitability prior to being granted access to federal property. This will be accomplished using the 
National Crime Information Center (NCIC) Interstate Identification Index (III). This is the 
minimum baseline background check for entrance onto Army Installations for non-CAC holders 
to include entrance of visitors (Ref AR 190-13, paragraph 8-2). All vehicles and personnel 
entering the installations are subject to search and seizure. Personnel entering or exiting the 
installation may experience a delay due to vehicle inspections, registration checks, verification 
of seat belt use, etc. Contractor shall comply with all entry control requirements and security 
policies/procedures in effect. Security procedures may change without notice. 
 
1.6.7.2 Eligibility Verification for Employment. E-Verify is an Internet-based system that 
compares information from an employee's Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification, to data 
from U.S. Department of Homeland Security and Social Security Administration records to 
confirm employment eligibility. The U.S. Department of Homeland Security is working to stop 
unauthorized employment. By using E-Verify to determine the employment eligibility of their 
employees, companies become part of the solution in addressing this problem. All U.S. 
employers must complete and retain a Form I-9 for each individual they hire for employment in 
the United States. This includes citizens and noncitizens. On the form, the employer must 
examine the employment eligibility and identity document(s) an employee presents to determine 
whether the document(s) reasonably appear to be genuine and relate to the individual and 
record the document information on the Form I-9. The list of acceptable documents can be 
found on the last page of the form. E-Verify is mandatory for employers with federal contracts or 
subcontracts that contain the Federal Acquisition Regulation E-Verify clause. 
 
1.6.7.3 Physical Security. The contractor shall be responsible for safeguarding all government 
equipment, information and property provided for contractor use. At the close of each work 
period, government facilities, equipment, and materials shall be secured. 
 
1.6.7.4 Key Control. All references to keys include key cards and badges. Contractors will be 
given access to perform required duties under this PWS and adhere to DACID Gillem Key 
Control procedures at all times. The Contractor shall establish and implement methods of 
ensuring all government issued keys are not lost or misplaced, nor used by unauthorized 
persons. No keys issued to the Contractor shall not duplicate any keys issued by the 

 
Government. The Contractor shall immediately report any occurrence of lost or duplicate keys to 
the Contracting Officer and return all keys to the Government upon termination of employment. 
 
1.6.7.5 DoD Common Access Card. Contractor must be able to obtain a U.S. Department of 
Defense Common Access Card (with photo) in order to: (1) gain access to the Federal 
Government’s Installations at USACIL and FXD; (2) gain access to the Department of Defense 
computer network; and (3) maintain an official Department of Defense photo ID Card for security 
purposes while working at DACID Gillem.   
 
1.6.7.6 Training. Contractors will be required to complete DoD Information Assurance training 
before access to government computers can be granted, and Anti-terrorism (AT)/Force 
Protection (FP)/Operations Security (OPSEC) and IWATCH training prior to arrival or within 30 
days of arrival, complete on-going training as needed and annual DoD training as directed. The 
training websites will be listed in the contract cover sheet.  
 
1.6.8 Staffing and Personnel Qualification. The contractor is responsible for the overall 
management and personnel supervision of all contract employees on this contract. It is the 
contractor’s responsibility to staff and deploy qualified contractor personnel to meet all of 
requirements of this PWS. The contractor shall possess the proper education, experience, 
training, or certification to perform his/her duties. 
 
1.6.8.1 Logistics Management Specialist (5 each) 
• Possess a High School Diploma or equivalent and 5-7 years of general warehouse 
experience 
• Ability to organize, plan, and execute logistical sustainment operations in conjunction 
with guidance form the Chief of the Gillem Logistics Operation Center (GLOC) 
• Prepare logistics requirements plans in support of DACID Gillem and its forward 
missions 
• Knowledge and skill in the application for the Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) Plan 
• Ability to analyze and solve conventional problems or conditions that impede adequate 
and timely integrated Logistics Support assigned projects 
• Must be able to communicate effectively at levels involving Intra-Army contracts, mid-
level officials, managers, and laboratory managers, and professional Army, Air Force, 
DoD and contract representatives 
• Knowledge of DoD logistics regulations, AR 710-2, DA Pam 710-2-1, and related DA 
and DD Forms 
• Knowledge of Relief of responsibility IAW Army Regulation 735-5 
• Knowledge of Inventory Management below national level IAW Army Regulation 710-2 
• Ability to assist in refining internal SOP and all other procedural processes to help 
maintain appropriate accountability of property 
• Knowledge of Warehouse and Storage Operations IAW Army Regulation 740-1 
• Knowledge of DLA Property Disposal Process 
• Familiar with GCSS-Army 
• Possess ability to review and analyze logistical problems to prevent work stoppage 
within warehouse operations 
• Knowledge of Container Management IAW Army Techniques Publication (ATP) 4-12 
and FM 55-80 
• Knowledge of the Command Deployment Discipline Program (CDDP) 
• Have experience with deployment transportation of supplies and equipment  

 
• Formally HAZMAT trained/certified to complete required documentation to transport 
various supplies and equipment IAW DOT 49 CFR, Maritime Regulations, the IATA, 
AFMAN 24-604, and EPA Guidelines 
• Ability to maintain a valid state issued driver’s licenses 
• Ability to operate forklifts up to 30,000 lb. capacity 
• Operate up to 10-ton box and flatbed trucks  
• Ability to lift up to 60 lbs. 
 
1.6.8.2 Supply Technician (1 each) 
• Possess a High School Diploma or equivalent and 5-7 years of general supply and 
property accountability 
• Formally trained on the Global Combat Support System – Army (GCSS-A) 
• Possess the knowledge and skills to perform all supply related functions within the 
GCSS-A system 
• Familiar with GCSS-A operations in both the Property Book and Unit Supply modes 
• Ability to provide daily property oversight for all property assigned to the DACID Gillem 
• Knowledge of Army Accountability, Relief of Responsibility (FLIPLS), Inventory 
Management and Timelines Procedures

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
Digital Communication and Graphic Design Services 
 
PART I GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
General: This is a non-personal services contract to provide digital media strategy, digital media content 
creation, social media management, and graphic design services. The Government shall not exercise any 
supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract 
service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn, is responsible to the 
Government. The Contractor, in turn, shall be accountable to the Government for Contractor or 
subcontractor personnel. 
 
1.1 Description of Services/Introduction: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, 
equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, subject-matter-
expertise, and all other items or non- personal services necessary to perform social media 
management, executive communication strategies, and graphic design, as defined in this 
Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor shall perform in accordance with 
(IAW) the terms and conditions of the contract and consistently with the established 
standards in this PWS and contract. 
 
1.2 Goals: The goal of this contract is to support the I Corps Public Affairs Office in 
the planning, production, and assessment of digital communication activities that inform 
internal and external audiences, reinforce command messaging, and maintain awareness 
of the information environment. The contractor shall support the Public Affairs Office by 
producing and/or managing digital media products and analytical insights that contribute 
to the commander’s communication objectives and reinforce themes and messages 
originating from I Corps, U.S. Army Pacific, and Department of the Army guidance. The 
contractor provides technical and production support only. Final authority for messaging, 
content approval, and information release remains with the Government. 
1.3 Services provided under this contract will be evaluated annually by the Government 
to assess the effectiveness of digital communication activities supporting the dissemination 
of official information. Performance evaluation may include comparison of digital 
communication metrics to recognized industry benchmarks and publicly available analytics 
standards in order to provide context regarding reach, visibility, and audience interaction 
across digital platforms. 
1.3.1 Benchmarking information may be derived from recognized social media 
analytics and digital communications assessment sources; however, contractor 
performance will be evaluated primarily on the contractor’s ability to support the 
dissemination of accurate and timely information, monitor the information 
environment, and provide analytical reporting as required under this contract. 
1.3.2 No specific commercial analytics provider or vendor shall be required for 
benchmarking or performance evaluation. 

2 
1.4 Objectives: The objective of digital communication activities under this contract is 
to support the I Corps Public Affairs Office in informing internal and external audiences 
about I Corps activities, operations, and priorities through official digital platforms.  
1.4.1 Digital communication products shall communicate accurate, timely, and 
relevant information that supports the commander’s communication objectives and 
reinforces official Public Affairs messaging. The Contractor shall support the 
Public Affairs Office in producing and distributing digital media content that 
increases visibility and understanding of official Army activities. Audience growth 
and engagement metrics may be monitored as indicators of information 
dissemination and audience awareness; however, these metrics are secondary 
outcomes and are not the primary objective of Public Affairs communication 
activities.  
1.4.2 Sentiment analysis and other digital communication analytics may be used to 
assist the Public Affairs Office in assessing audience response, identifying 
emerging topics or concerns, and informing future communication planning. 
Primary evaluation of digital communication activities shall focus on the 
effectiveness of disseminating accurate and timely information, maintaining 
compliance in operational security, and supporting the command’s communication 
objectives. 
1.5 Background: Joint Base Lewis-McChord and America’s First Corps operate in an 
information environment where digital platforms are an increasingly important channel for 
communicating with Service Members, Families, and the public. Timely and accurate 
information distributed through official digital platforms enables personnel and their 
families to remain informed about activities, operations, and events affecting the command. 
Effective digital communication also supports the commander’s ability to communicate 
priorities and maintain transparency with internal and external audiences. 
 
1.5.1 America’s First Corps includes more than 40,000 personnel across multiple 
installations and operational locations. Given the scale and geographic distribution 
of the force, digital communication platforms provide an important mechanism for 
disseminating official information in a timely and consistent manner. 
 
1.5.2 Enhancing and maintaining the command’s digital platforms will enable the 
Public Affairs Office to more effectively distribute accurate information, support 
the commander’s communication objectives, and improve awareness of official 
Army activities. 
 
1.5.3 Effective digital communication also supports public understanding of the 
Army’s mission, strengthens trust with communities and partners, and provides 
timely clarification of inaccurate or misleading information when it occurs. 
 

3 
1.5.4 Target Audience: Digital communication activities supported by this contract will 
address mission stakeholders associated with I Corps operations rather than demographic 
groups. 
• Primary stakeholder audiences include: 
• Internal Audiences 
• Service Members assigned to I Corps and subordinate units 
• Military families 
• Department of War civilian employees 
• Strategic Audiences 
• Department of the Army leadership 
• U.S. Army Pacific and Indo-Pacific command partners 
• Allied and partner militaries 
• Community Audiences 
• Local and regional communities surrounding Joint Base Lewis-McChord 
• Washington State civic leadership 
• Public Audiences 
• The American public 
• Prospective military service members 
 
1.5.5 Operational Context: Official digital platforms are a primary mechanism used by 
Army Public Affairs organizations to communicate timely and accurate information to 
internal and external audiences. 
• Digital communication products produced under this contract support the 
Public Affairs mission to inform audiences about I Corps activities, 
operations, training, and events. 
• Digital media products may include imagery, video, graphics, and written 
content that depict Army personnel, operations, and activities occurring within 
the I Corps area of responsibility. 
• These communication products contribute to public understanding of Army 
missions and provide information about the activities of Soldiers and units 
assigned to I Corps. 
• All information released through official digital platforms must be accurate, 
appropriate for public release, and approved by the Government prior to 
publication 
 
1.6 Scope: The contractor shall support the I Corps Public Affairs Office in planning, 
producing, and coordinating digital communication activities that inform internal and external 
audiences about I Corps operations, training, personnel, and significant events. 
 
1.6.1 The contractor shall assist the Public Affairs Office in translating command 
priorities, themes, and operational messaging into coordinated digital communication 
products and activities across official digital platforms. 

4 
 
1.6.2 Support activities under this contract include development of multimedia 
communication products, coordination of digital communication plans associated with 
command events and operations, and assistance in distributing official information 
through approved digital channels. 
 
1.6.3 The contractor shall not independently determine official messaging or release 
information without Government approval. 
 
1.7 Period of Performance: 
Phase-In Period: A phase-in period for this contract would be a transition where the contractor 
gradually assumes responsibility for the digital media and design services. Key activities would 
include knowledge transfer of existing digital assets and accounts, securing access for all 
contractor personnel, and establishing workflows with the I Corps Public Affairs Office. This 
process ensures a seamless handover of duties, allowing the new team to achieve full 
operational capability without disrupting ongoing communication efforts. 
  
Phase-In Period: June 18, 2026 – June 30, 2026 
Base Year: (1) 12-month Period: July 1, 2026 – July 1, 2027 
1- Option Year: (1) 12-month Period: July 1, 2027 – July 1, 2028 
2- Option Year: (1) 12-month Period: July 1, 2028 – Jun. 1, 2029 
 
1.8 Quality Control: Quality Control is entirely the responsibility of the Contractor. 
The Contractor is responsible for the delivery of quality services/supplies to the 
Government (see FAR 52.246-1 Contractor Inspection Requirements). 
 
1.9 Quality Control Program: The Government is committed to a highly interactive 
relationship between quality control by the Contractor and quality assurance by the government 
recipient of services. This relationship shall be achieved through an effective Prevention Based 
Quality Control Program dedicated to ensuring the best possible products and services to end 
users. The Contractor shall provide the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) and the 
Contracting Officer (KO) with a final written Quality Control Plan (QCP) no later than (NLT) ten 
(10) business days after contract award, and within five (5) business days of any proposed 
changed. 
 
1.10 The Contractor's quality program shall demonstrate its prevention-based outlook by 
meeting the objectives stated in the PWS throughout all areas of performance. The QCP shall be 
developed to specify the Contractor's responsibility for management and quality control actions 
to meet the terms of the contract. The QCP at a minimum shall address continuous process 
improvement; procedures for scheduling, conducting and documentation of inspection; 
discrepancy identification and correction; corrective action procedures to include procedures for 
addressing Government discovered non-conformances; procedures for root cause analysis to 
identify the root cause and root cause corrective action to prevent re-occurrence of 
discrepancies; procedures for trend analysis; procedures for collecting and addressing customer 
feedback/complaints. 
 

5 
1.11 The Contractor shall provide, within 24 hours, all reports generated as a result of the 
Contractor's quality control efforts. This shall include any summary information used to track 
quality control, including any charts/graphs. 
 
1.12 Proposed changes made after KO acceptance shall be submitted in writing through the 
COR to the KO for review and acceptance prior to implementing any revision. The 
Contractor's QCP shall be maintained throughout the life of the contract and shall include the 
Contractor's procedures to routinely evaluate the effectiveness of the plan to ensure the 
Contractor is meeting the performance standards and requirements of the contract. 
1.13 Contractor Discrepancy Report (CDR): When the Contractor's performance is 
unsatisfactory, a CDR will be issued. The Contractor shall reply in writing within five (5) work 
days from the date of receipt of the CDR, giving the reasons for the unsatisfactory performance, 
corrective action taken, and procedures to preclude recurrence. 
 
1.14 Quality Assurance: The COR will evaluate the Contractor's performance under this 
contract in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP). This plan is 
primarily focused on what the COR must do to ensure that the Contractor has performed in 
accordance with the performance standards. It defines how the performance standards will be 
applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum acceptable defect rate(s). When an 
observation indicates defective performance, the COR will require the Contractor or designated 
on-site representative to initial the observation to acknowledge the defective performance. The 
acknowledgement of the observation does not necessarily constitute Contractor concurrence 
with the observation, only that the Contractor has been made aware of the defective 
performance. 
 
1.15 Place of Performance: Performance under this contract shall primarily occur at the I 
Corps Public Affairs Office located at Joint Base Lewis-McChord. The contractor will have 
allocated and assigned office space co-located with the I Corps Public Affairs Office to 
support the Public Affairs mission and coordinate directly with Public Affairs personnel on 
communication products, digital media activities, and other tasks described in this 
Performance Work Statement. Workspace, computing equipment, and network access 
necessary to support connectivity will be provided by the Government within the Public 
Affairs Office area. The contractor provides services in support of the I Corps Public Affairs 
Office and the communication objectives of the command. Tasking and work priorities 
associated with this contract will originate from the Public Affairs Office and will be 
coordinated through the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) in accordance with the 
terms of the contract. Other staff sections, directorates, or organizations may coordinate with 
the Public Affairs Office regarding communication support requirements. However, tasking 
of contractor personnel shall occur only through the COR assigned to the Public Affairs 
Office and within the scope of this contract. Contractor personnel shall not be reassigned, 
relocated, or directed to perform duties without coordination through the COR and approval 
from the Contracting Officer. Remote work is authorized when it does not interfere with 
performance of contract requirements or the Public Affairs mission. 
 
1.16 Minimum Qualifications: The Contractor shall meet or exceed the minimum 
qualifications of being a digital media engagement, graphic design, and content management

SUBJECT  RFI - Veterans Health Administration Radiology and Cardiology 
Enterprise Imaging System   
 
DESCRIPTION
Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) 
Veterans Health Administration (VHA)  
Request for Information (RFI) 
 
I. INTRODUCTION: 
This RFI is issued by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Technology Acquisition Center 
(TAC), for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor 
does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with 
Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers 
and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. 
 
Pursuant to FAR Overhaul Part 10 (Market Research), the purpose of this RFI is to understand 
industry capabilities related to national enterprise imaging systems and to collect information to 
enable further development of a future acquisition strategy to include socio-economic 
consideration and methods. This RFI is related to earlier RFI #’s 36C10X24Q0024 and 
36C10X25Q0015. 
 
Any information received from a contractor in response to this RFI may be used in creating a 
solicitation. Any information received which is marked with a statement, such as “proprietary” 
or “confidential,” intended to restrict distribution will not be distributed outside of the 
Government, except as required by law. 
 
The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this 
information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested 
vendor's expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future 
Request for Proposal (RFP), if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this 
RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions will become Government property and will not be 
returned.  Interested vendors are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or 
competition sensitive information contained in their response. 
 
II. RFI RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS 
NOTE: The response to this RFI must be clear, concise, and complete. VA is under no obligation 
to provide feedback to the company, or to contact the company for clarification of any 
information submitted in response to this RFI.  
 
RFI responses must include:  
 
A. Company Information: 
 
1. Company Name; 
2. Company Address; 
3. Point of contact name; 
4. Telephone number 
5. Email address

RFI: 36C10B26Q0453
