6. CAGE/SAM UEI under which the company is registered in the System for Award 
Management (SAM); 
7. Small Business Administration (SBA) VetCert certification (if applicable). 
 
B. Responses to the following two (2) areas: 
 
1. List any previous or existing contracts you have with the VA where similar work 
was performed to this requirement. Also, is there an existing contract vehicle you 
recommend be used for this procurement? 
2. Responses to all parts of questions 1-13 in Section IV of this document 
 
Responses to this RFI shall be submitted electronically by 10:00 AM EST, June 2, 2026 via 
email to the TAC points of contact Contract Specialist, Chanté Frith, Chante.Frith@va.gov and 
Contracting Officer Matthew Truex, Matthew.Truex1@va.gov. Please note “Response to RFI - 
Veterans Health Administration Radiology and Cardiology Enterprise Imaging System” in 
the subject line of your response. The email file size shall not exceed 5 MB. 
 
All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the following: 
 
All proprietary/company confidential material shall be clearly marked on every page that 
contains such. 
 
Please keep your response to no more than 15 pages. Responses should be submitted as either 
a Microsoft Word (.docx) or an Acrobat (PDF) format with Arial or Times New Roman font, 12 
pt. minimum that addresses all information. Tables and illustrations may use a reduced font size 
not less than 8-point and may be landscape. Interested parties should exclude marketing material 
in order to allow sufficient space for adequately, directly, and substantively responding with the 
information of most interest to the Government. NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE 
ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI.   
 
  

Request For Information (RFI) 
 
RFI: 36C10B26Q0453 
Page 3 of 10 
III. BACKGROUND/REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION: 
This RFI is issued for the purpose of collecting information about the ability of a vendor to meet 
the requirements for design and implementation of an VHA enterprise wide Radiology and 
Cardiology PACS as described below. 
 
1. The VHA consolidated Radiology/Cardiology PACS initiative, currently in the market 
research phase, is evaluating current and future capabilities for solutions that provide secure 
image acquisition, retrieval, communication, viewing, postprocessing, automated analysis, 
reporting, documentation, importing/exporting/exchange, workflow management, referring 
clinician and patient access and review, image integration into VHA electronic health record 
(EHR), and other critical functionality for image-centric VHA clinical programs. Clinical 
domains include, but are not limited to, the following areas: radiology (including nuclear 
medicine) and cardiology/vascular imaging (invasive and noninvasive). 
 
2. Estimated annual volume of VHA imaging may exceed 12 million Radiology and Cardiology 
exams across 18 VISNs. 
 
3. Important features of interest for VHA enterprise PACS will include, but are not limited to, 
integration with current and future VHA EHR, universal availability of images and reports on 
all VA desktops, specialty-specific diagnostic viewers and clinical tools or compatibility with 
third party specialty-specific diagnostic viewers, specialty-specific integrated artificial 
intelligence (AI) functionality, integrated voice recognition, reporting, communication, 
quality improvement, quality assurance, and data mining capabilities for use in all clinical 
domains, interfaces for all image acquisition modalities/devices as well as workflow 
capabilities in each clinical domain, ability to manage and archive Digital Imaging and 
Communications in Medicine (DICOM) and non-DICOM images, bidirectional exchange of 
images and reports with DoD and community (non-VHA) partners, and viewing capabilities 
for ordering/referring providers and patients.  Viewing capabilities on non-Government 
Furnished Equipment (GFE) mobile devices and multimedia integration of image data for use 
in VHA’s EHR is also preferred.  
 
4. VHA is currently surveying industry to identify potential vendors who would be capable of 
providing VHA with a best in breed, enterprise class Vendor Neutral Archive (VNA) and 
viewer with supporting functionality that incorporates at a minimum the following 
preliminary features: 
 
• Rapid, on-demand access to images across the enterprise; 
• Master patient index (MPI) to address VA’s conversion from VistA to Oracle Health 
Electronic Medical Records (EMR) and the change in primary identifier from Social 
Security Number (SSN) to Electronic Data Interchange Personal Identifier (EDIPI).  
System must be able to seamlessly function with both VistA and Oracle Health or other 
potential EMR interfaces and be able to utilize the appropriate primary patient identifier 
for each respective system to uniquely identify patients and ensure a patient’s data 
appears as a singular instance within the enterprise imaging archive; 
• Migration of all studies and reports currently in local/VISN PACS and cardiology PACS. 
This is approximately 20 petabytes comprising >2 billion individual images. Some 
studies may need to be migrated from the systems of origin; 
• Zero footprint web viewer compatible with VA baseline PC image and associated 
browser; 

Request For Information (RFI) 
 
RFI: 36C10B26Q0453 
Page 4 of 10 
• Advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) support including third-party vendor 
integration/support across all listed imaging specialties. At a minimum, AI modules will 
include: Intracranial Hemorrhage, Large Vessel Occlusion, Mammography Density, 
Quality and breast nodule detection, and lung nodule detection; 
• System must be expandable to diagnostic review, interpretation and reporting of multi-
specialty imaging; 
• Ad hoc query retrieve capability with all non-integrated VHA PACS and DoD PACS 
systems; 
• Ability to store, transfer, reprocess and display Nuclear Medicine raw image data; 
• Full functionality nuclear medicine processing capabilities integrated within viewer; 
• Innovative ways research data can be collected and accessed during the following image 
migration and presented to quality management and research personnel; 
• Functionality for segregation, curation and tracking use of large image and report data 
sets for research, AI assurance and other functions as authorized; 
• Research data must be archived in a secure anonymized silo within the EI system; 
• Integrated voice recognition (VR) for site/VISN-based reporting, cross-VISN reporting 
and enterprise-wide reporting for NTP. VHA is open to both cloud-based and 
workstation-based VR 
• System must include a worklist/assignment engine that presents Radiologists and 
Cardiologists with studies that they are credentialed to read and has configurable logic for 
assignment and workload balancing;  
• Functionality for automated population of templated reports using DICOM Structured 
Report (SR)and AI analysis; 
• Routine redundant archiving of final reports in image series; 
• Functionality to support automated assignment of case reviews and tracking of results for 
Ongoing Professional Performance Evaluation (OPPE); 
• Functionality for identification and annotation of cases for peer learning activities; 
• All components of the system must support VA’s current user authentication 
methodology; 
• Enterprise support for National Telestroke Program image viewing; 
• Enterprise support for national Tumor Board image review; 
• Custom workflows specific to VHA National Teleradiology Program in alignment with 
NTP NextGen PACS: https://sam.gov/opp/b556ed4b32cb4caabd4878bf59af9ab5/view  
• System should include an integrated HL7 broker for inbound and outbound message 
normalization; 
• System must be DICOM promiscuous and must normalize all VistA Radiology exams to 
a consistent format, e.g. site code-MMDDYYYY-###; 
 
Specialty Areas:  
 
1. Radiology and Nuclear medicine:   
• Archiving and Image/report distribution to VA enterprise, including academic and 
community partners / affiliates and DoD; 
• Full featured radiology diagnostic review and reporting system; 
• DICOM Modality Worklist Provider; 
  
2. Cardiology: Cath, Echo, MR, CT, EKG and Holter Monitor: 
• Archiving and Image/report distribution to VA enterprise;  

Request For Information (RFI) 
 
RFI: 36C10B26Q0453 
Page 5 of 10 
• Full featured cardiology diagnostic review and structured reporting system for invasive 
and non-invasive procedures; 
• A strong preference for a zero-footprint diagnostic display and structured reporting client; 
• Post acquisition reprocessing of Echo studies. This functionality must be vendor agnostic; 
• DICOM Modality Worklist Provider; 
• Advanced Visualization Tools for Echo, Cardiac CT/MR, and Nuclear Cardiology; 
• Cardiac focused AI image analysis and reporting tools; 
   
3. National Teleradiology Program 
• Pre-Read QA worklist for NTP Support allowing NTP Support to review images 
submitted for interpretation and query/retrieve additional relevant studies from any PACS 
in VHA; 
• Integration with Foundations from Health Level for STAT Portal and clinical analytics; 
• Integration with NTP’s mammography tracking system; 
 
4. The VNA is expected to be able to store, display, and provide image retrieval of pathology, 
point of care ultrasound (POCUS), dental imaging, retinal imaging, and radiation oncologic 
imaging and treatment planning data (store and retrieve). 
 
 
General Requirements 
 
VHA consolidated PACS is envisioned (subject to change) to meet the following major 
characteristics which will be described in detail in any potential subsequent solicitation: 
 
1. Intuitive, stable, fast and easy to use zero footprint user interface for the viewer; 
 
2. Specialty viewers for listed imaging specialties, with future expansion to serve as a single 
VHA PACS/Enterprise Imaging system; 
 
3. Advanced AI options for image analysis, including stroke and mammography, as well as 
workflow and results tracking AI functionality; 
 
4. HL7 interfaces to all current VA VistA and Oracle Health systems; 
 
5. Supports all VNA image and document management standards, such as Integrating the 
Healthcare Enterprise (IHE); 
 
6. Dose tracking and alerting system to include collecting dose data of migrated studies going 
back to an agreed upon date; 
 
7. Viewer should be designed with a focus on human factors to optimize viewing efficiency, 
while minimizing viewer fatigue and the incidence of repetitive motion injuries; 
 
8. System must support cross-site collaboration, reading and reporting. This is to function in 
both VistA and Oracle Health environments; 
 
9. Viewer supports on-the-fly 3D and other advanced visualization and analysis capabilities;

RFI: 36C10B26Q0453 
Page 6 of 10 
10. Viewer must provide support for archive teaching and research cases with deidentification of 
patient information; 
 
11. Viewer must support export of deidentified reports and images; 
 
12. System must support the electronic transfer and reconciliation of electronic images and other 
records and between VA and outside providers/institutions; 
 
13. Provide automated auto-linking/registration of multi-slice images across series among 
current and prior

Statement of Work 
Page 1 of 2 
 
 
1. BACKGROUND 
The Indian Health Service (IHS) Portland Area Service Units require continued access to Clinical 
Pharmacology Powered by ClinicalKey (Elsevier), an online clinical pharmacology database used 
by pharmacy and medical staff to support medication dosing verification, drug interaction 
screening, medication safety evaluation, therapeutic decision-making, and medication 
identification (“Pill Identifier”). This acquisition is for the annual renewal of an existing and on-
going subscription service currently utilized by the Area SU clinics, with no significant or material 
changes to scope, quantity, scale, or functionality. 
 
Market research was conducted through internet research, reviewing vendor product 
information, personal knowledge of available drug information systems, and feedback from 
current/former users. Comparable products identified included UpToDate (Wolters Kluwer 
Health) and Micromedex (Merative). While these products provide drug reference information, 
they are separate proprietary systems and therefore do not provide access to the Elsevier 
Clinical Pharmacology database. Clinical Pharmacology is specifically formatted to support 
pharmacist/pharmacy workflows. The system has been in continuous use at the SUs for over ten 
years and continued use preserves efficiency and avoids workflow disruption and uninterrupted 
access to the established clinical pharmacology reference resource that would be associated 
with transitioning to an alternative system. 
 
The Clinical Pharmacology database is a proprietary product owned by Elsevier Clinical Solutions 
and marketed as Clinical Pharmacology Powered by ClinicalKey.  
 
2. SCOPE 
The contractor shall provide a subscription-based, web-accessible clinical pharmacology 
information resource for use by authorized pharmacy and medical staff across Service Units. The 
subscription shall provide access to current drug and clinical information for clinical reference 
purposes only. No physical software, equipment, or locally installed applications are required. 
The intended outcome is uninterrupted access to reliable clinical pharmacology information to 
support patient care and clinical decision-making. 
 
3. SPECIFIC TASK OR SPECIFICATIONS 
The contractor shall: 
 Provide continuous subscription access to a web-based clinical pharmacology 
information resource. 
 Ensure the resource includes up-to-date drug information, including but not limited to 
indications, dosing, contraindications, interactions, and safety considerations. 
 Allow access for authorized users at multiple Service Units. 
 Maintain availability throughout the period of performance, excluding scheduled 
maintenance. 
 Provide updates to clinical content as new information becomes available. 
 Provide customer support for access or account-related issues. 
 
The subscription shall be for informational use only and shall not result in physical possession of 
software. 
 

Statement of Work 
Page 2 of 2 
 
 
4. PERFORMANCE MONITORING 
The Government will monitor performance through verification of uninterrupted access during 
the period of performance and confirm that subscription services remain active and available to 
authorized users. Acceptance will be based on continued availability and access to the resource 
as specified. 
 
5. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS 
 The subscription shall be accessed via a secure web interface. 
 No Protected Health Information (PHI) or Personally Identifiable Information (PII) shall 
be stored, transmitted, or accessed by the contractor. 
 The contractor shall not require access to Government networks, systems, or facilities. 
 
6. GOVERNMENT FURNISHED EQUIPMENT (GFE)/GOVERNMENT FURNISHED 
INFORMATION (GFI) 
No Government-furnished equipment or information will be provided. Users will access the 
resource using Government-owned devices and internet connectivity. 
 
7. OTHER PERTINENT INFORMATION OR SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS  
Guidance: Include special considerations the contractor must know, such as environmental 
conditions or coordination needs. 
• IDENTIFICATION OF POSSIBLE FOLLOW-ON WORK 
This requirement includes a base year with three option years. Additional follow-on 
work or renewals may be considered based on continued mission need and availability 
of funds. 
• INSPECTION AND ACCETPANCE CREITERIA 
The subscription will be accepted upon confirmation that access is active and available 
to authorized users for the full period of performance. 
• RISK CONTROL 
Failure to maintain access to a current clinical pharmacology information  resource may 
increase the risk of medication errors, reduced quality of care, and potential accreditation 
impacts. Risk is mitigated through timely renewal and continuous access to the 
subscription service. 
 
8. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE  
Services will be provided remotely via web-based access for use at Government healthcare 
facilities and Service Units. 
 
9. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
 Base Year: 07/10/2026 - 07/09/2027 
 Option Year 1: 07/10/2027 - 07/09/2028 
 Option Year 2: 07/10/2028 - 07/09/2029 
 Option Year 3: 07/10/2029 - 07/09/2030 
 
10. DELIVERY SCHEDULE 
Subscription access shall be active no later than 07/10/2026 and maintained continuously 
throughout the base year and any exercised option years.

NOTICE OF INTENT - SOURCES SOUGHT  
 
The Defense Information Systems Agency/Defense Information Technology Contracting 
Organization intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Apriva Information Security 
Systems, Limited Liability Corporation (Apriva) for their Mobile Endpoint Security Architecture 
(MESA) Virtual Private Network (VPN). A sole source Justification & Approval document is 
being coordinated and, upon approval, a copy of it will be posted here on SAM.gov to comply 
with the public display requirements of FAR 6.301.  
 
The proposed contract action is for Apriva MESA VPN License Agreement and Engineering 
Support Services for the Department of Defense Mobility Classified Capability (DMCC) – 
Secret end user devices (EUDs), consisting of the legacy Samsung Galaxy S20 custom read only 
memory (CROM), S7 Tablet CROM, a Windows Data-at-Rest (DAR) Dell 7320, Windows 
DAR Dell 7210, Hewlett Packard (HP) ProBook G4 and HP ProBook G5. Apriva’s unique VPN 
design supporting the DMCC-Secret effort is currently the only VPN compliant with the 
National Security Agency (NSA) Commercial Solutions for Classified (CSfC) program and 
proven compatible with the current DMCC-S Secure Mobile Device Gateways (SMDG) 
architecture and these legacy EUDs. At inception, the Apriva MESA VPN was the only NSA 
CSfC approved standards-based Internet Protocol Security VPN available. As such, the 
Government requires the Apriva MESA VPN license agreement, which authorizes use of 
gateway operations and associated SMDG testing facilities.  
 
The Apriva MESA VPN design solution cannot be replaced without significant disruption of 
service to the DMCC infrastructure and its end users, as well as potentially disturbing NSA CSfC 
Mobile Access Capability Package compliance of the current architecture. Replacing the existing 
infrastructure is beyond the scope of the Government’s current needs and would result in a loss 
of DISA's $43M investment in the existing infrastructure. Awarding to a source other than 
Apriva would result in substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to 
be recovered through competition. Also, attempts to prematurely transition services would result 
in critical mission failure due to the dependencies listed above. Currently, there is no alternative 
to support the legacy EUDs as the Apriva MESA VPN is the only compatible solution.  
 
Currently, the incumbent contractor, Apriva, is the only source capable of providing all 
necessary services to support the legacy EUDs for the DMCC outer VPN and the Command, 
Control, and Services as they are the sole provider for this current solution.  
 
The statutory authority for other than full and open competition, 10 USC 3204 (a) (1), as 
implemented by FAR 6.103-1(a)(2)(i), only one responsible source and no other supplies or 
services will satisfy agency requirements. Companies who believe they can provide this service 
must indicate their interest in writing within 5 days of this notification and include a detailed 
capability statement. No reimbursement for any cost connected with providing capability 
information will be provided. All responsible sources will be considered in evaluating the 
determination to issue a sole-source contract. Quotations or proposals received in response to this 
notice cannot be accepted since this synopsis cannot be considered a request for quote or a 
request for proposal.  
 

The North American Classification System (NAICS) code 541511 will be used for determining 
company size status.

PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Environmental Management Service (EMS), Bay Pines VA Healthcare System requires the continued procurement of annual software licensing and reporting services for the Brand Name Walsh QA Inspection Platform to ensure uninterrupted functionality of the existing quality assurance and environmental inspection system. The Walsh platform, originally procured in 2019 and deployed across the Bay Pines and Cape Coral facilities, supports four critical EMS section programs consisting of customizable checklists, accounts, web portal follow-ups, dashboards, and reports—along with 14 additional checklists, 48 inspector licenses, and 110 operator user licenses essential for EMS operations. The system integrates with UltraSnap ATP swabs and ATP handheld analyzers that transmit cleanliness data directly into the Walsh QA Inspection Platform, making compatibility and data integrity vital to EMS’s mission requirements. The contractor is the only source capable of providing the necessary brand-specific licensing, system extensions, ATP integrations, and recurring on-site training delivered three times per year for new and existing EMS personnel. Continued acquisition from this source is required to maintain operational consistency, system interoperability, and compliance with established EMS processes.

Walsh QA Inspection Software empowers EMS managers, supervisors, housekeeping staff, and pest control personnel to perform inspections, track service quality, and ensure compliance with sanitation and environmental standards. The platform includes exclusive Walsh Ecosystem Extensions—Pest Control, Linen Management, Housekeeping, Fleet Management, and Mattress & Stretcher Accountability—delivering unmatched integration and operational continuity. Walsh Integrated also provides annual on‑site training (nine days) and full technical support to ensure optimal performance and VA compliance. The Walsh Integrated software licenses will not be used on the VA network.

The period of performance will be from July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027, consisting of one (1) 12‑month base period and one (1) 12‑month option period, to be exercised at the Government’s discretion.

NOTICE OF THE FEDERAL ACCESSIBILITY LAW AFFECTING ALL INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) PROCUREMENTS (SECTION 508)

On January 18, 2017, the Access Board issued a final rule that updated accessibility requirements covered by Section 508 and refreshed guidelines for telecommunications equipment subject to Section 255 of the Communications Act.  The final rule went into effect on January 18, 2018.  The revisions and updates to the Section 508-based standards and Section 255-based guidelines are intended to ensure that information and communication technology (ICT) covered by the respective statutes is accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities.

SECTION 508 – INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) STANDARDS

The Section 508 standards established by the Access Board are incorporated into, and made part of all VA orders, solicitations and purchase orders developed to procure ICT.  These standards are found in their entirety at: Revised 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines (access-board.gov).  A single PDF file version of the Revised Section 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines will be supplied upon request, or can be obtained from the Access Board website.  Federal agencies must comply with the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended. 

The Contractor shall comply with “508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements” for all electronic ICT and content delivered under this contract. Specifically, as appropriate for the technology and its functionality, the Contractor shall comply with the technical standards marked here: 

	E205 Electronic Content – (Accessibility Standard -WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA Guidelines)

	E204 Functional Performance Criteria

	E206 Hardware Requirements

	E207 Software Requirements

	E208 Support Documentation and Services Requirements

COMPATABILITY WITH ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY

The standards do not require installation of specific accessibility-related software or attachment of an assistive technology device. Section 508 requires that ICT be compatible with such software and devices so that ICT can be accessible to and usable by individuals using assistive technology, including but not limited to screen readers, screen magnifiers, and speech recognition software.

ACCEPTANCE AND ACCEPTANCE TESTING

Deliverables resulting from this solicitation will be accepted based in part on satisfaction of the Section 508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements standards identified above.

The Government reserves the right to test for Section 508 Compliance before delivery.  The Contractor shall be able to demonstrate Section 508 Compliance upon delivery.

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY USING SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTS AND SERVICES

The Contractor shall comply with Sections 524 and Sections 525 of the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007; Section 104 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005; Executive Order 13221, “Energy-Efficient Standby Power Devices,” dated August 2, 2001; and the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) to provide ENERGY STAR®, Federal Energy Management Program (FEMP) designated, and products and services that meet EPA Recommendations of Specifications, Standards, and Ecolabels in effect as of October 2023 (e.g. Electronic Product Environmental Assessment Tool (EPEAT) registered products) in providing information technology products and/or services. The Green Procurement Compilation (GPC) website available at Green Procurement Compilation - GSA Sustainable Facilities Tool (sftool.gov) provides a comprehensive list of sustainable products and services and sustainable acquisition guidance. 

The Contractor shall provide products that meet the definition of sustainable products and services if the products are delivered to the Government; furnished by the Contractor for use by the Government, incorporated into the construction of a public building or public work, or acquired by the Contractor for use in performing services under a Government contract where the cost of the products is a direct cost to a Government contract (versus costs which are normally applied to a contractor's general and administrative expenses or indirect costs).

Specifically, the Contractor shall provide sustainable products under this contract in accordance with FAR 52.223-23.  The applicable products with their associated certification, designation, and/or ecolabel (e.g. Energy Star, FEMP, and/or EPEAT) are identified within the product specifications in this PD.  The Contractor shall ensure proposed products meet the certification(s) / designation(s) / ecolabel(s) specified at the time of submission of proposals and at the time of award.

ELECTRONIC SHIPPING OF LICENCES

Electronic delivery of licenses is required for this procurement because each license consists of individualized website access credentials (unique username and password) assigned to EMS personnel. The Contractor shall provide the initial setup and account activation information directly to each authorized user via email, ensuring secure and immediate access. Once logged into the system, users are able to access all electronic checklists, dashboards, and reports necessary to perform required EMS quality assurance and inspection functions. This method of electronic distribution is integral to the operation of the Walsh QA Inspection Platform and aligns with the system’s design and workflow requirements.  The Walsh QA Inspection Platform is not accessed on the VA network.

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

VA TECHNICAL REFERENCE MODEL

The Contractor shall comply with the VA OIT Technical Reference Model (VA TRM). Compliance with the VA TRM is achieved by using only technologies and standards that are listed as approved for use in the VA TRM.  The Contractor shall provide all necessary information requested by VA to ensure TRM approval is obtained prior to use on VA’s network.

ZERO TRUST – VA CRITICAL SECURITY CONTROLS

VA has established minimum mandatory security requirements and requires that any network connected software system or service must meet the VA Critical Security Controls as outlined in the VA Memorandum, “VA Security Controls”, https://www.voa.va.gov/DocumentView.aspx?DocumentID=5010.  VA Critical Security Controls identify the minimum mandatory requirements that must be implemented across all VA enterprise infrastructure, cloud computing environments, information systems, networks, and specialized devices (medical devices/systems, special-purpose systems, and research scientific computing devices) that process, store, and/or transmit VA data.  Effective July 1, 2025, the Contractor shall implement these VA Critical Security Controls, within any network connected software system or service prior to being authorized for use in the VA.  This functional requirement is not negotiable, and Plan of Action & Milestones (POAM) will not be accepted in the event these controls cannot be implemented for new systems.  Critical Security Controls are intended to increase VA’s security posture and provide security and privacy risk visibility into the VA network and is not a new requirement.  The Contractor’s failure to maintain these VA Critical Controls after implementation will result in VA discontinuing the use of the system.

SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER (SSN) REDUCTION 

The Contractor solution shall support the Social Security Number (SSN) Fraud Prevention Act (FPA) of 2017 which prohibits the inclusion of SSNs on any document sent by mail.  The Contractor support shall also be performed in accordance with Section 240 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act (CAA) 2018, enacted March 23, 2018, which mandates VA to discontinue using SSNs to identify individuals in all VA information systems as the Primary Identifier.  The Contractor shall ensure that any new IT solution discontinues the use of SSN as the Primary Identifier to replace the SSN with the Integrated Control Number (ICN) in all VA information systems for all individuals.  The Contractor shall ensure that all Contractor delivered applications and systems integrate with the VA Master Person Index (MPI) for identity traits to include the use of the ICN as the Primary Identifier. The Contractor solution may only use a Social Security Number to identify an individual in an information system if and only if the use of such number is required to obtain information VA requires from an information system that is not under the jurisdiction of VA.

INTERNET PROTOCOL VERSION 6 (IPV6)

The Contractor solution shall support IPv6-Only based upon the memo issued by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) on November 19, 2020 (https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/M-21-07.pdf). Which defines IPv6-only as the state of an operational system or service when IPv4 protocol functions (addressing, packet forwarding) are not in use. The NIST USGv6 profile defines technical requirements for a product to be capable of operating in IPv6-Only environments.  IPv6-Only technology, in accordance with the USGv6 Program (https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/usgv6-program/usgv6-revision-1), NIST Special Publication (SP) 500-267B Revision 1 “USGv6 Profile” (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.500-267Br1), and NIST SP 800-119 “Guidelines for the Secure Deployment of IPv6” (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-119), compliance shall be included in all IT infrastructures, application designs, application development, operational systems and sub-systems, and their integration.  In addition to the above requirements, all devices, applications, and systems shall support all applicable functionality on native IPv6-Only as well as dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) connectivity without additional memory or other resources being provided by the Government, so that they can function in a mixed environment.  All public/external facing servers and services (e.g., web, email, DNS, ISP services, etc.) shall support native IPv6-Only and dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) users and all internal infrastructure and applications shall support using native IPv6-Only and dual stack (IPv6 / IPv4) for all functionality and operations.

SOFTWARE AND LICENSING REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall be responsible for the provision of all software licenses and any associated licensing maintenance required for any development,

Examples of occurrences include acts of God or the public enemy, acts of the Government in either its sovereign or contractual capacity, fires, floods, epidemics, quarantine restrictions, strikes, unusually severe weather, and delays of common carriers. (1) Notify the Contracting Officer in writing as soon as possible;

(2) Remedy the delay as quickly as possible; and

(3) Notify the Contracting Officer when the occurrence is over.

(i) Payment—

(1) Items accepted. Payment shall be made for items accepted by the Government that have been delivered to the delivery destinations set forth in this contract.

(2) Prompt payment. The Government will make payment in accordance with the Prompt Payment Act ( 31 U.S.C. 3903) and prompt payment regulations at 5 CFR part 1315.

(ii) Provide a copy of the remittance and supporting documentation to the Contracting Officer.

RFI Response Questions  
                                                                                                                                            Set #3 
Page 1 of 2 
 
 
Conscription Simulation Model RFI Questions  
 
Q1. Could you confirm that the desired deliverable is a Discrete-event simulation 
model to be hosted on SSS IT systems and to be operated by SSS staff, rather than a 
model hosted and operated by the vendor? If Government hosted, are there any 
restrictions on the development tools and database access that would affect design 
and development? 
A1. The model will be hosted within SSS information technology environments and 
operated by SSS personnel. The vendor will design and develop the tool within an 
SSS-designated cloud development environment that complies with Agency information 
technology and security requirements. Vendors may recommend development tools or 
platforms, as the Agency is seeking a commercially supported, stand-alone solution. The 
Agency will provide the data elements required for model design and development, and 
vendors are expected to supply or derive any additional data or assumptions necessary to 
support scenario analysis and model flexibility 
 
Q2. Will the model need to be able to consider alternative policy scenarios for Mission 
Essential Function, or will it be focused largely on modeling the impact of changes in 
different demand scenarios (e.g., size of the conscription)? 
A2. The model must be capable of executing multiple configurable scenarios to assess a 
wide range of policy and operational conditions. 
 
Q3. Would the model assume automatic registration of individuals or should it be able 
to model alternative scenarios? Should it also be able to consider scenarios in which 
females are required to register? 
A3. The model must be capable of executing multiple configurable scenarios to assess a 
wide range of policy and operational conditions. Automatic registration becomes effective 
on December 18, 2026. 


RFI Response Questions  
                                                                                                                                            Set #3 
Page 2 of 2 
 
 
Q4. Will SSS provide access to model input data (e.g., disaggregated counted of 
registered individuals, counts of unregistered individuals)? 
A4. The Agency will provide the data elements required to support the design and 
development of the model. Vendors are also expected to identify and recommend 
supplemental or derived data needed to support comprehensive scenario analysis and 
comparative modeling.  
 
Q5. Will SSS provide development, testing, and deployment workspaces for the 
model, or is the vendor expected to develop the model in its own development 
environment? 
A5. The model will be hosted within SSS information technology environments and 
operated by SSS personnel. The vendor will design and develop the tool within an 
SSS-designated cloud development environment that complies with Agency information 
technology and security requirements. 
 
Q6. Should the model be able to consider both General and Special Skills selection 
scenarios? 
A6. Yes, the model must be capable of executing multiple configurable scenarios to assess 
both General and Special Skills selection conditions.

Conscription Simulation Model RFI Questions 
Q1. Does the Agency anticipate a follow-on RFP , or will award be made through an 
existing contract vehicle (GSA MAS, SEWP , OASIS+, NITAAC, an SSS BPA), and what 
contract type is contemplated (FFP , T&M, hybrid)? 
Why we ask: Vehicle and contract type drive proposal format, teaming arrangements, and 
pricing structure. Knowing this now lets us mobilize the right partners before the solicitation 
drops. 
A1.  This requirement is new. The Agency anticipates issuing an RFQ on SAM.gov and also 
anticipates using an FFP contract structure. 
 
Q2. Is a small-business set-aside, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, or HUBZone preference 
contemplated for the follow-on action? 
Why we ask: Set-aside posture determines whether this company competes as a prime, as 
a subcontractor to a small-business prime, or under a teaming arrangement —  and that 
decision must be made early. 
A2. Any set-aside determination will depend on the information the Agency receives 
through the RFI process. 
 
 
Q3. Without disclosing budget, is there a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) range the 
Agency considers reasonable for this effort, and what is the anticipated period of 
performance (base plus options) and target Initial Operating Capability date? 
Why we ask: A ROM band and two anchor dates let vendors right-size the proposed 
solution and credibly back-plan stand-up activities, rather than guessing and either 
overbuilding or underbidding. 
A3. The Agency is not providing a ROM at this time and is using the RFI to gather additional 
information from industry. The Period of Performance and Initial Operating Capability dates 
will be provided in the forthcoming RFQ.   
 


Page 2 of 5 
 
Q4. Will the Agency host an Industry Day or pre-proposal conference, and will it 
accept live demonstrations of operational capability from interested vendors prior to 
the follow-on solicitation? 
Why we ask: Our agency has an operating SSS SIM-NET platform that can be demonstrated 
at no cost. A live demo is the most efficient way to align Agency intent with what is 
technically achievable today. 
A4. The Agency is open to all engagement formats, including an Industry Day, a 
pre-proposal conference, and live demonstrations. 
 
Q5. What is the Agency's preferred hosting environment — SSS-operated on-premise, 
SSS-controlled FedRAMP Moderate (or High) commercial cloud, GSA Cloud.gov, or a 
partner-agency enclave — and is the system expected to carry an Authority to Operate 
at award, or is operation under an Interim Authority to Test acceptable? 
Why we ask: Hosting choice and ATO posture together drive security architecture, 
schedule, ATO package scope, and cost. They are the two single largest cost-and-schedule 
drivers in the entire effort 
A5. The model will be hosted within SSS information technology environments and 
operated by SSS personnel. Vendors will conduct development and testing within an 
SSS-designated cloud development environment in accordance with Agency information 
technology and security requirements. The Agency is willing to operate under an Interim 
Authority to Test, provided that all applicable compliance requirements are consistently 
implemented and maintained throughout the testing period. 
 
Q6. Will the Agency furnish authoritative reference values for key parameters — 
registration coverage by age, MEPS daily throughput by station, no-show and lost-
notification rates, medical-DQ and CO classification rates by mobilization posture — 
or should the contractor propose defaults derived from public planning documents? 
Why we ask: Government-furnished parameters dramatically shorten the validation cycle 
and give the model definitive provenance the Agency can defend before Congress and 
OSD. Without them, schedule must include independent derivation. 
A6. The Agency will furnish the authoritative parameters required to support the design and 
development of the model. Vendors are additionally expected to recommend 

Page 3 of 5 
 
supplemental or derived parameters necessary to enable comprehensive scenario 
analysis and comparative assessments. 
Q7. What level of Validation, Verification, and Accreditation (VV&A) is expected — 
informal SSS subject-matter expert review, formal documented VV&A under MIL-STD-
3022 / DoDI 5000.61, or accreditation against a specific Agency or DoD standard — and 
who is the designated validating authority? 
Why we ask: VV&A scope can swing the deliverable list and the schedule by months. 
Identifying both the standard and the validating SME up front prevents downstream 
stakeholder churn. 
A7. The Agency does not require compliance with MIL-STD-3022, DoDI 5000.61, or any 
other Department of War validation, verification, and accreditation standards. All 
verification and validation activities will be performed internally and certified by SSS 
subject-matter experts. External accreditation is not required. 
Q8. Should the model integrate with — or merely export to — adjacent SSS systems 
such as the Registrant Information Management System (RIMS), the SSS data 
warehouse, or USMEPCOM systems, and what identity/access framework should it 
use (SSS AD, USAccess/PIV, Login.gov)? 
Why we ask: Integration scope is the difference between a contract change and a CSV 
button. IAM choice cascades into the auth subsystem, session model, and SSS analyst 
onboarding path. 
A8. The model will operate as a stand-alone application and will not integrate directly with 
other SSS or partner systems. As a stand-alone application, it will integrate with Microsoft 
Entra ID for identity and access management, using SAML 2.0 as the primary federation 
protocol. 
Q9. Will the system process Personally Identifiable Information (such as registrant 
SSNs, addresses, or selective-service numbers), or only anonymized aggregates and 
derived statistics? 
Why we ask: PII handling triggers Privacy Act, PIA, SORN, and additional NIST 800-53 
control families. Confirming scope avoids accidental over- or under-engineering of the 
security and privacy posture. 
A9. The system will process only anonymized aggregates and derived statistical outputs. 
No Personally Identifiable Information (PII) will be ingested or stored within the model. 
 

Page 4 of 5 
 
Q10. What rights in technical data and software does the Agency expect — 
Government Purpose Rights, Unlimited Rights, or rights tailored under DFARS 252.227-
7013/7014 (or FAR 52.227-14) — and where should the source code be delivered (SSS-
operated repository, code.gov, both)? 
Why we ask: Rights basis affects open-source-component selection, the SBOM/supply-
chain attestation chain, and the post-award sustainment plan. This company can deliver 
under any regime, but pricing and approach are tuned to the chosen rights basis. 
A10. The Government requires full and unrestricted delivery of all technical artifacts, 
including all source code, build pipelines and instructions, database schemas, 
infrastructure configuration files, and all other materials necessary to compile, deploy, 
operate, and maintain the system. The source code will be developed and tested within an 
SSS-designated cloud development environment in accordance with Agency information 
technology and security requirements.  
Q11.  For the government-owned predictive DES model requirement, does the agency 
have preferred architectural considerations, development frameworks, or 
maintainability standards intended to support long-term internal government 
management and future modification of the platform? 
A11. The model will be hosted and operated within SSS information technology 
environments. The vendor will develop the tool within an SSS-designated cloud 
development environment, consistent with Agency information technology and security 
requirements.  Vendors may recommend appropriate tools or platforms, as the Agency 
seeks a commercially supported, stand-alone solution. 
Q12. Are there specific operational bottlenecks or readiness variables the agency 
considers highest priority for modeling within the initial implementation phase (e.g., 
personnel throughput, mobilization timing, resource coordination, geographic 
distribution constraints, reporting workflows, etc.)? 
A12. The Agency identifies personnel throughput, mobilization timing, and resource 
requirements as the highest-priority variables for initial modeling. 
Q13. Can the agency provide additional guidance regarding interoperability 
expectations with existing government systems or external data environments, 
particularly around preferred integration methodologies or real-time data exchange 
requirements? 
A13. The model will operate as a stand-alone application and will not integrate directly with 
other SSS or partner systems. 

Page 5 of 5 
 
Q14. Does the agency currently anticipate preferred deployment environments or 
security requirements for future implementation (e.g., government cloud 
environments, isolated environments, FedRAMP alignment considerations, or other 
cybersecurity standards)? 
A14. The model will be hosted within SSS information technology environments and 
operated by SSS personnel. The vendor will conduct development and testing within an 
SSS-designated cloud development environment in accordance with Agency information 
technology and security requirements. 
Q15. Is the agency evaluating the future potential for the platform to expand beyond 
the initial readiness simulation case into broader operational coordination, reporting, 
or decision-support workflows over time? 
A15. The Agency is evaluating the possibility of future expansion into broader operational 
coordination, reporting, and decision-support workflows; however, no decisions have been 
made at this time.

Cheyenne River Health Center 
Performance Work Statement 
 
Background 
Indian Health Service (IHS), a federal agency within the Department of Health & Human Services 
(DHHS), is responsible for providing health services to American Indians and Alaska Natives. IHS 
provides a comprehensive health service delivery system for appr oximately 1.14 million American 
Indians and Alaska Natives who belong to 573 federally recognized tribes, in 35 states. IHS 
Headquarters is located in Rockville, MD , and is divided into twelve physical areas: Alaska, 
Albuquerque, Bemidji, Billings, Califor nia, Great Plains, Nashville, Navajo, Oklahoma, Phoenix, 
Portland, and Tucson. 
 
The Great Plains Area Office (GPAO) collaborates with its 19 IHS and Tribally managed service units 
to deliver healthcare to approximately 130,000 Native Americans residing  in North Dakota, South 
Dakota, Nebraska, and Iowa. The Area Office’s service units include seven hospitals, eight health 
centers, and several smaller health stations and satellite clinics.  
 
The Cheyenne River Health Center (CRHC)  falls under the GPAO. CRHC provides medical care for 
approximately 11,000 tribal members living on the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe (CRST) Reservation 
and within the established Purchased/Referred Care Delivery Area (PRCDA). Serving a rural area, 
many patients that travel approximately 165 miles round-trip to receive care. The CRHC was built in 
2011 to provide an expanded level of health care services specifically designed to meet the needs of 
the CRST population. The CRST, through a 638 contract with IHS, operates four satellite health 
stations that offer basic ambulatory services in the  Cherry Creek, Red Scaffold, Swiftbird, and 
Whitehorse communities. Services at CRHC include:  Emergency Room Department, Primary Care 
Clinic, Pharmacy, Physical Therapy, Radiology, Immunization Clinic, Inpatient Care, Laboratory, 
Purchased/Referred Care, Dietary, Eye Care, Well -Child Clinic, and Specialty Clinics: Audiology, 
ENT, MRI, OB/GYN, Podiatry and Telemedicine (Cardiology, Dermat ology, Endocrinology, Internal 
Medicine, Hepatology, Nephrology, and Rheumatology). 
 
Purpose 
The Cheyenne River Health Center requires a secure exchange data software solution to provide 
connectivity to the Medicare DDE (Direct Data Entry)/FISS (Fiscal Intermediary Standard System), 
eligibility verification, eligibility searches, and perform third party insurance medical (emergency, 
inpatient, outpatient, and specialty clinic) claims (professional and facility) validation, approval and 
processing services for Medicare, Medicaid, VA and Commercial Payers for the Cheyenne River 
Health Center, providing confidentiality, authentication, integrity and non -repudiation for the Eagle 
Butte Hospital. 
 
IHS Headquarters mandates  that payment systems are updated to reflect changes in medical 
practice and the relative value of services. Based on this, secure exchange-managed services are 
necessary for the medical claims process to ensure compliance. 
 
Work Schedule/Availability 
24/7 availability of all payer eligibility verification and search services for health care center staff 
(with exceptions to scheduled service disruption) 
 
 

 
Period of Performance 
Base Year: July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2027 
Option Year One (1): July 1, 2027, to June 30, 2028 
Option Year Two (2): July 1, 2028, to June 30, 2029 
Option Year Three (3): July 1, 2029, to June 30, 2030 
Option Year Four (4): July 1, 2030, to June 30, 2031 
 
Place of Performance 
Cheyenne River Health Center 
Business Office/Patient Registration 
P.O. Box 1012 
24276 166th Street Airport Road 
Eagle Butte, South Dakota 57625 
 
Scope 
The contractor shall provide a secure exchange data software solution that includes technology for: 
 
• Connectivity to the Medicare DDE (Direct Data Entry) /FISS (Fiscal Intermediary Standard 
System) and automated claims status reporting, payment floor details, and other reports. 
• Eligibility verification for third-party payers to include Medicaid and Medicare. Anticipated 
monthly volume for Eligibility Checks: 100. 
• Eligibility results must include start and end dates of coverage. 
• Capability to search eligibility for third -party coverage for patients who do not provide or 
present insurance information. Anticipated volume for Insurance Searches per month: 1000. 
• Third-party insurance medical claims validation, approval, and processing services via a 
clearinghouse for Medicare, Medicaid, VA,  and Commercial Payers (not limited to but 
including United Health Group) for the Cheyenne River Health Center.  Anticipated volume 
for Claims Submission per month: 2,500. 
• Processes all claim types (professional and facility):  Emergency, Inpatient, Outpatient, and 
Specialty Clinics; and provides  both solicited and unsolicited claims status. Anticipated 
volume for Claims Status per month: 1000. 
• The software must provide rigorous and thorough claims rules and custom business rules. 
• Capability for self-monitoring usage of services for thresholds. 
• Training and support related to the scope of work –  training provided either on -site or via 
teleconference. 
 
The software services shall comply with the following constraints: 
 
The software service shall not require Cheyenne River Health Center to install contractor 
software within the Cheyenne River Health Center or the Indian Health Service network. 
 
The service shall enable Cheyenne River Health Center to exchange data utilizing a Secure 
File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) as approved by the Indian Health Service Office of Information 
Technology. 
 
The service shall support Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) transactions and interactive 
Telnet application protocol sessions. 

 
 
The service should support an unlimited number of users, and access should be workstation 
independent. 
 
The service shall not entail development of Health Insurance Portability and Accountability 
Act (HIPAA) transaction set translation or mapping processes, non- CMS or non -IHS-
generated data or messages, or data reformatting. 
 
The service shall also conform to a Business Associate Agreement to be established 
between the Cheyenne River Health Center and the Contractor. 
 
The contractor shall support end-to-end communication testing, implementation, and daily 
operations of the data transfers from the contractor to the Cheyenne River Health Center, 
which shall include, at a minimum: 
 
The contractor should  provide routine technical support to implement corrections to 
services that occur as a result of errors, flaws, or other failures within their service. 
 
The contractor shall notify a designated Cheyenne River Health Center point of contact 
(Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR)) of any scheduled maintenance that shall result 
in downtime at least two (2) days before the maintenance period. 
 
The contractor shall notify a designated Cheyenne River Health Center point of contact of 
any issues that result in a disruption of data exchange capabilities.  This notification shall 
occur as soon as possible after the disruption has been identified. 
 
The contractor shall provide customer support for reporting, documenting, tracking , and 
resolving service problems, which shall be available via telephone and email to the 
Cheyenne River Health Center technical staff. 
 
The contractor shall provide the capability for self-monitoring usage of services that have a 
threshold. 
 
Contractor Responsibility 
 
Secure internet-based connectivity to all current fiscal intermediaries. 
 
Ability to send medical emergency, inpatient, outpatient, and specialty claims to Medicare 
Contractor and other payers using secure data exchange technology. 
 
Unlimited Direct Data Entry (DDE) online Medicare claims status/corrections for Medicare 
Part A. 
 
All electronic transactions and DDE/FISS shall provide confidentiality, authentication, 
integrity, and non-repudiation. 
 
Reports and acknowledgements on all claims sent. 
 

 
Automated batch 997/999 acknowledgement reports.   
 
Automated batch 276/277 claims status capability. 
 
Accept electronic claims from the Resource Patient Management System (RPMS). 
 
 
Provide a single secure electronic location to manage all electronic claims, including VA 
claims. 
 
Verify Medicaid, Medicare, and Commercial Payer eligibility in real-time and in batches. 
 
Provide knowledgeable support personnel to assist with any issues related to the processing 
of medical claims. 
 
The Contractor shall provide toll-free telephone/technical support during 7:00 am to 7:00 pm 
Mountain Standard Time, Monday through Friday, except Government holidays. 
 
The Contractor shall provide a two (2) hour minimum response time from notification by IHS 
at no additional cost to the Cheyenne River Health Center. 
 
The medical claim processing services shall meet the following standards: 
 
Third-party insurance medical claims shall be submitted to the appropriate carrier/payer via 
the Contractor- provided clearinghouse by the close of the next business day after receipt 
from IHS. 
 
Third-party insurance medical claims shall be transmitted electronically to the appropriate 
carrier/payer. 
 
The Contractor shall use routine editing procedures to detect defects in medical claims 
information supplied by the government. The Contractor shall reject and not process all 
medical claims with defects. The Contractor shall provide the service location w ith edit 
status reports that list the deficiencies, enabling the service location to correct the detected 
issues. 
 
The Contractor shall provide for the correction of all claims rejected by all carriers/payers for 
any reason other than the inappropriate format of the claims. 
 
The Contractor shall provide the capability for medical claim errors to be corrected and 
resubmitted electronically and provide a report of rejected medical claims within 4 hours of 
batch submission. 
 
The Contractor shall make available productivity and submission reports within 24 hours of 
batch transmission. 
 
Past Performance: 
 

 
If the Contractor has held previous contracts with the Indian Health Service, please provide 
supporting information, including the government contract number. 
 
Performance-Based Service Delivery Summary 
 
The contractor’s performance will be measured based on the following Performance 
Requirements. The Performance Requirements will be measured against Government 
Performance Standards and monitored in accordance with the following Methods of 
Government Surveillance, also known as a Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP),  to 
determine compliance. A 5% deduction will be assigned to each Performance Requirement. 
Deductions shall be assessed against individual invoices when services are not performed 
or do not meet contract requirements. The deficient category will make deductions.

Contracting Officer’s Representative Designation 
The COR is responsible for: 
1. Monitoring the Contractor’s technical progress. 
2. Interpreting the statement of work. 
3. Technical evaluation as required.

Contractor Compliance 
The Contractor shall adhere to all official coding and billing rules as published by the American

The Contractor shall maintain records of confidentiality in accordance with the Health Insurance

1. Introduction 
This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. Do not submit a formal quote. This RFI is 
for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for 
Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation, or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, 
there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services 
described in this RFI. Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for 
the Government to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect 
costs that you incur in responding to this RFI. This request does not constitute a 
solicitation for quotes or the authority to enter negotiations to award a task 
order/contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. 
The information provided may be used by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in 
developing its acquisition strategy andProduct Description (PD). Any information 
submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary; however, any information 
received shall become the property of the Government and will not be returned to the 
respondent. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, 
restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The 
Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this 
RFI. Product information, brochures, part numbers, and/or other description information 
may be included with the submission. 
 
The NAICS for this requirement is undecided at this time. Small Business companies 
with the capability to perform this requirement, in total or in part, are encouraged to 
participate. If you are interested only in subcontracting opportunities, please indicate 
this fact clearly in your submission. Please indicate a suggested NAICS code for the 
requirement requested under this request for information. Please indicate your 
company size and socio-economic status for applicable NAICS codes. 
 
Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in 
response to this RFI. Responses should be as complete and informative as possible. 
 
2. Background 
The mission of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Integrated Service 
Network (VISN 22), Office of Capital Asset Management (CAM) is to provide support for 

 Page 2 of 5 
all VA Medical Centers in relation to their capital improvement programs which include 
design, construction, and lease project management, operations and maintenance, and 
planning. This allows each healthcare system to deliver high-quality, cost-effective 
facilities in support of our nation's Veterans. VISN customers are VA employees in 
medical centers, and community-based clinics across Southern California, Arizona and 
New Mexico who proudly work at the front lines of service delivery to our nation’s 
Veterans.  
 
Daily Project Management (PM) decisions require distribution and review of 
documentation for analysis, justification, and approval. Decisions in PM workflows 
require collaboration amongst a variety of stakeholders to provide information 
necessary to support decisions. Project Management Information Systems (PMIS) 
provide engineers with the opportunity to improve accountability and collaboration while 
capturing a digital record of all PM decisions and supporting information.   
 
This procurement requires a Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS), Software as a Service 
(SaaS) brand name Kahua or equal solution to replace its current project management 
process. The solution shall be Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program 
(FedRAMP) authorized at a Moderate or higher impact level. The Contractor shall 
provide licenses to PMIS software along with comprehensive support services to ensure 
successful deployment of the PMIS for 400 users (150 VA staffs and 250 support 
contractors). The system shall be a collaborative cloud-based communication and 
project management information system for the architect/engineering and construction 
(AEC) community.  
 
The PMIS solution shall support VISN-level portfolio management and oversight across 
all VA Medical Centers, outpatient facilities, and leased assets within VISN 22. VISN 
CAM users shall have portfolio-wide visibility, reporting, and governance authority while 
preserving facility-level execution control. The PMIS shall support high-volume, Non-
Recurring Maintenance (NRM) and Minor Construction projects, including template-
based project creation, lightweight workflows, and rapid project setup and closeout to 
meet fiscal year execution demands. 
 
The consumption model for this PMIS shall be License based where the total cost is 
based on total users with access to the system. 
 
The required Brand Name or Equal to Kahua shall meet all of the salient characteristics 
identified in this PD.

STATEMENT OF WORK  
 
1. Objective/Requirements 
 
The Icing Research Tunnel (IRT) at NASA Glenn Research Center calibrates the 
icing cloud every five years and checks the calibration every six months after that 
full calibration.  Part of the IRT cloud calibration consists of measuring the size of 
the drops in the icing cloud.  Each cloud is made up of a distribution of many 
different sized drops and quantified by the median volumetric diameter (MVD). Up 
to three different instruments are used to capture this full range of sizes in each cloud 
condition.  Every cloud condition in the IRT requires the use of a probe that 
measures the smallest drops from 2-50µm.  Cloud conditions with a median 
volumetric diameter of >15µm require a probe that measures drops larger than the 
aforementioned probe that measures the smallest drop.  This encompasses around 
90% of the IRT’s operating envelope. For context, the FAA certification cloud 
conditions START at 15µm so the tunnel would be of little to no use for FAA 
certification purposes if unable to measure the full spectrum of the drops. 
 
The current probe that the IRT has that measures that middle range of drops is called 
the OAP-230X (Optical Array Probe). The OAP-230X is a 1990s-technology 
instrument and is showing its age.  Parts are no longer available, and repairs require 
careful troubleshooting and “Band-Aid” efforts to maintain operability.  A similar 
situation also arises with another similar probe in IRT, the large-range probe, the 
OAP-230Y.  To mitigate the risk of losing the ability to measure the largest size 
drops, a replacement probe was purchased, the OAP-1D2DY.  Developed in the 20-
teens, the OAP-1D2D probes have upgraded components and measurement 
technologies as well as added capability of 2D data.  The OAP-230s only give 1D 
data.  The transition from the 230Y to the 1D2DY is underway, thankfully, as the 
OAP-230Y continuously fails and test time is lost for troubleshooting and re-pairs. 
  
 
2. Characteristics, Scope, and Specs 
a. Scope of Work: 
i. The IRT has a requirement to measure both a 2D image data stream and a 
1D histogram data stream from an Optical Array Probe that measures the 
middle part of the droplet spectrum. Science Engineering Associates, 
SEA, shall fabricate an OAP with both a 1D data stream and a 2D data 
stream similar to the capabilities of the OAP-1D2DY that NASA owns. 
This probe shall interface with SEA’s M300 Data Acquisition System. 
b. Objectives: 
i. The goal of the icing cloud calibration team is to have both the (desired) 
OAP-1D2DX and (already purchased) OAP-1D2DY properly vetted for 
use in the next full cloud calibration set to take place in 2028.  It is not 
expected that the OAP-230X shall perform optimally in 2028 thus putting 
the IRT at risk of going out of calibration and tarnishing the “Gold 
Standard Calibration” status and reputation it has held for decades.  

Purchasing the OAP-1D2DX is quickly becoming a requirement/need and 
no longer “an option.” 
 
c. Description of the Work/Contractor Tasks: 
i. The Contractor shall make an Optical Array Probe capable of measuring 
drop sizes from 15 µm to at least 450 µm.  The probe shall be compatible 
with the M300 data system and output both the 1D data and the 2D image 
data.   
ii. TASKS 
1. SEA shall make the OAP-1D2DX. 
2. The probe shall be equipped with deice capabilities that include a 
full heat front dome. 
3. SEA shall clean, align and calibrate the OAP-1D2DX. 
4. NASA shall work with SEA to ensure the M300 system has all 
necessary components for the network communication. 
5. SEA shall ship the probe and components to NASA 
6. SEA shall provide some training/guidance on the new interface 
(virtual training is acceptable). 
d. Deliverables:  
i. The contractor shall provide:

b. 220VAC Instrument & Deice Power 
c. Saphire window modification

respective bin

STATEMENT OF WORK

FEDERAL MOTOR CARRIER SAFETY ADMINISTRATION (FMCSA)

PRE-EMPLOYMENT SCREENING PROGRAM (PSP) SUPPORT AND SERVICES

(May 19, 2026)

SCOPE

Background

Title 49 of the U.S. Code, section 31150, titled “Safety performance history screening” as adopted as Public Law 109-59 section 4117 of the Safe, Accountable, Flexible, Efficient Transportation Equity Act: A Legacy for Users (SAFETEA-LU) requires the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) to provide persons conducting pre-employment screening services for the motor carrier industry electronic access to crash and inspection data in FMCSA’s Motor Carrier Management Information System (MCMIS).  The full text of the statute is as follows:

Sec. 31150. Safety performance history screening.

In General.  The Secretary of Transportation shall provide persons conducting pre- employment screening services for the motor carrier industry electronic access to the following reports contained in the Motor Carrier Management Information System:

Commercial motor vehicle accident reports.

Inspection reports that contain no driver-related safety violations.

Serious driver-related safety violation inspection reports.

Conditions on Providing Access.  Before providing a person access to the Motor Carrier Management Information System under subsection (a), the Secretary shall –

Ensure that any information that is released to such person will be in accordance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.) and all other applicable Federal law; the Contractor shall further be subjected to the civil liabilities for willful or negligent noncompliance of the FCRA and shall be required to indemnify the government from same;

Ensure that such person will not conduct a screening without the operator- applicant's written consent;

Ensure that any information that is released to such person will not be released to any person or entity, other than the motor carrier requesting the screening services or the operator- applicant, unless expressly authorized or required by law; and

Provide a procedure for the operator-applicant to correct inaccurate information in the System in a timely manner.

Design.  The process for providing access to the Motor Carrier Management Information System under subsection (a) shall be designed to assist the motor carrier industry in assessing an individual operator's crash and serious safety violation inspection history as a pre-employment condition.  Use of the process shall not be mandatory and may only be used during the pre-employment assessment of an operator-applicant.

Serious Driver-Related Safety Violation Defined.  In this section, the term "serious driver-related violation" means a violation by an operator of a commercial motor vehicle that the Secretary determines will result in the operator being prohibited from continuing to operate a commercial motor vehicle until the violation is corrected.

In 2006, FMCSA released the Driver Information Resource (DIR) for use by FMCSA and State partner enforcement personnel.  The DIR creates a “driver profile” using the Motor Carrier Management Information System (MCMIS) crash and inspection data.  The DIR is comprised of crash data from the past five years and inspection data from the past three years from MCMIS, organized by driver characteristics utilizing matching algorithms and data clean-up techniques.  Current access to the DIR is restricted by password and is not available to the public or motor carriers.

Making the DIR available to entities hiring operators of motor carriers is the core component of the statutory requirement.  In 2006, FMCSA considered and analyzed the options for FMCSA to meet the requirements of section 31150.  Two general strategies were considered:  (1) an “in-house” option, where FMCSA would develop the relevant systems and administer the entire program itself, and (2) a “third party” option where the DIR data would be distributed to companies or service providers able to meet strict laws, regulations and guidelines and assist FMCSA to meet the requirements of the Pre- Employment Screening Program (PSP).  After reviewing requirements, efficiencies in systems, and legal, logistical and fiscal options, FMCSA has decided to solicit the assistance of offerors via the “third party option.”  FMCSA would provide a snapshot, or “extract” of the DIR database to Contractor able to meet specific measures based on FMCSA policy, applicable federal laws and guidance.

In addition, FMCSA currently has a system in place to meet the requirement of section 31150(b)(4).  The FMCSA DataQ’s system is currently available to motor carriers to challenge data and correct data in the MCMIS system.  FMCSA is not seeking assistance in complying with section 31150(b)(4).

In May 2010, FMCSA launched PSP, a safety initiative that provide trucking and bus companies with secure, instant access to commercial drivers’ crash and inspection histories during the hiring process.  By offering access to a driver’s five-year crash history and three-year roadside inspection history, PSP informs hiring decisions that help FMCSA achieve its mission to reduce crashes, injuries, and fatalities involving large trucks and buses and lead to improved commercial motor vehicle safety on the Nation’s roadways.
