1.2	Purpose / Objectives

The purpose of the Statement of Work (SOW) is to assist FMCSA in meeting certain aspects of the pre-employment screening requirements of Section 31150.  The specific objectives of the Pre-Employment Screening Program (PSP) are aligned with the requirements of the statute:

Provide driver-related Motor Carrier Management Information System (MCMIS) safety and inspection data to motor carriers requesting the screening service, industry service providers requesting the screening service on behalf of a motor carrier or operator- applicant, or to the requesting operator-applicant (for his/her personal data) in a timely and professional manner;

Release data only with the account holder’s attestation that they have received the operator-applicant’s written consent or consent provided through FMCSA approved electronic means; and

Maintenance, handling, storage, and distribution of FMCSA MCMIS data must conform to applicable laws, rules, regulations and policies.

Certain requirements of the PSP will be the responsibility of FMCSA and SHALL NOT be performed by the Contractor:

FMCSA will be responsible for any other release of data to any person or entity other than the motor carrier or industry service provider (or representative) requesting the screening information or the operator-applicant as required in section 31150(b)(3);

FMCSA will be responsible for the integrity of the MCMIS data and will provide a procedure for the owner-operator to correct inaccurate information via the DataQs system currently maintained by FMCSA;

FMCSA will be responsible for ensuring the participating contactor has access to the Agency’s Information Technology cloud environment and hosting services; and

FMCSA will be responsible for performing audits of the participating Contractor to ensure performance and security objectives are being met.

Government Terms and Conditions/Definitions

Appendix A contains the Terms and Conditions for the PSP Support and Services contract, and a list of definitions, acronyms, and abbreviations commonly used within the FMCSA community and for this particular project.

Security/Data Requirements

Appendix B contains prevailing Department of Transportation (DOT) FMCSA, and Federal Information Technology (IT) Security standards, policies and reporting requirements.

Security/Data Requirements

Appendix C contains the program’s audit requirements, penalty, and appeal process. The Contractor and FMCSA will rely on an ongoing, random-selection audit process to monitor compliance with the written disclosure and authorization obligation.  The Contractor shall assume responsibility for the completion of the audit and report each set of audit results to FMCSA.  This appendix focuses on the audit process, the reporting of results, the consequences if a PSP account holder does not satisfy an audit request, and how a terminated account may be returned to a state of good standing.

GOVERNMENT FURNISHED RESOURCES

FMCSA will furnish the following to the Contractor:

Five years of driver crash data and three years of driver inspection data as reported to the Motor Carrier Management Information System (MCMIS).  The data will be organized by driver characteristics as found in the Driver Information Resource (DIR), currently used by FMCSA and State Motor Carrier Safety Assistance Program (MCSAP) inspection officers.  The DIR data will be provided periodically, most likely on a monthly or bi-monthly basis from FMCSA.

A description of how the MCMIS data has been arranged and the criteria for the matching algorithms in the DIR.

Procedures for obtaining the DIR data extract in a secure and efficient manner.

Access to FMCSA’s IT cloud environment and hosting services (see Section 1.4), as well as Federal and Department policies, standards and guidance as they apply to operations prescribed within this statement of work.

3.0	CONTRACTOR FURNISHED PROPERTY AND PERSONNEL

The Contractor shall furnish all facilities, materials, equipment, and services necessary to fulfill the requirements of each task specified in the Statement of Work (SOW), with the exception of items identified in Section 2.0.

The Contractor shall have experienced personnel working on this program with the following qualifications:

Program manager with a minimum of 5 years experience managing no-cost government contract(s).

Demonstrated expertise with marketing government programs to the motor carrier industry.

Individuals with project management certificates to include Project Management Professional (PMP) or Certified Scrum Master.

IT security expert with Certified in Governance, Risk, and Compliance (CGRC), Certified Information Security Manager (CISM), Certified Business Continuity Professional (CBCP), and CompTIA Security+ designations, and demonstrated experience implementing and operating systems compliant with NIST SP 800-53 and FedRAMP Moderate or higher baselines.

Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL)-certified service management capability across the organization, including demonstrated experience managing high-volume customer support operations with measurable service level performance.

Demonstrated experience implementing enterprise risk management practices in support of Federal IT systems, including continuous monitoring and risk mitigation stratetgies.

Demostrated experience architecting, designing, deploying, and operating high-volume, transaction-based systems in a FedRAMP-authorized cloud environment supporting over 1 million annual transactions.

Demonstrated expertise in the motor carrier industry through relevant certification (e.g., Certified Transportation Professional (CTP)) or equivalent experience.

DATA RECORDS

In accordance with Section 1.4, “Security/Data Requirements” and Appendix B, “Cybersecurity – Privacy Requirements for Unclassified Information Technology (IT) Resources (September 2017)”, the Contractor shall be responsible for -

Processing requests from motor carriers, industry service providers and drivers.  The Contractor shall distribute the required data in a timely fashion and provide customer service in support of the distribution of the data such as handling inquiries, concerns and resolving disputes which are related to the offeror’s operations.  FMCSA estimates that approximately 140,000 PSP records may be processed monthly, or nearly 1.7 million annually.

Maintaining an information technology infrastructure equipped with hardware and software that supports the operational, technical, security and privacy requirements documented with this SOW.  This includes, but not is limited to, adherence to the following:

encryption of sensitive data in transit and at rest;

audit and monitor identification, authentication and access to sensitive  data, including masking or redaction of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and other sensitive data elements on PSP reports and user-facing displays;

boundary protection and sensitive data isolation from public access or access channels through shared resources; i.e., peer-to-peer networks, instant messaging, internet, intranet and extranet;

Contractor must build and use their own payment processing solution for PSP that is in compliance with Payment Card Industry’s Data Security Standards (PCI/DSS Level 4.0.1), as well as all applicable federal privacy and security laws;

prohibition on user remote access to data; and

intrusion detection and prevention system.

Robust diaster recovery, contingency, incident response, and emergency preparedness plans and procedures in accordance with FMCSA guidelines.

Securing privacy information, maintaining data integrity, and preventing loss, theft, or accidental viewing or release of sensitive data.

REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall assist FMCSA with aspects of the PSP and meet the performance standards in providing these services as described below.

TASK 1:  Provide driver-related MCMIS safety and inspection data to motor carriers and industry service providers requesting the screening service or to the requesting operator- applicant (for their particular data).

The Contractor shall develop a process by which operator-applicants can release their MCMIS crash and inspection data file to motor carriers with whom the operator-applicant is seeking employment.

The Contractor shall develop a process by which the operator-applicant may obtain his/her own MCMIS crash and inspection data file.

The Contractor SHALL NOT alter MCMIS data found in the DIR or attempt to address the integrity of data provided by FMCSA.  If a data discrepancy is discovered, FMCSA will provide a process for operator-applicants to correct data in their record.

The Contractor shall have and maintain the capacity to handle the expected high volume of requests for driver records as well as provide quality customer service to motor carriers, industry service providers, and operator-applicants. Statement of Work

Planning and Execution Design for USCGC Campbell (WMEC-909) Availability

1. Background

A 10.5-month delivery is a non-negotiable requirement for the USCGC Campbell availability. To meet this requirement, the shipyard must develop an executable plan that accounts for the major constraints and uncertainties that can affect completion.

These include constraints in preparatory work, supply chain readiness, technical and commercial approval of change orders during execution, and contention for resources shared with other efforts both inside and outside the shipyard.

Traditional planning and execution approaches often rely on detailed schedules to manage constraints, then change priorities as delays and changes occur during execution. This creates significant waiting time in both the schedule and execution, while also causing constant churn in priorities.

The Campbell availability therefore requires a different planning and execution approach: one that minimizes waiting time and priority churn while protecting the 10.5-month delivery requirement.

2. Purpose

The purpose of this Planning and Execution Design workshop is to support the U.S. Coast Guard Yard in developing a realistic and executable plan for USCGC Campbell, along with the execution enablers and risk mitigations required to protect the 10.5-month delivery requirement.

This effort will be based on the Focus & Finish approach. Focus & Finish is currently being deployed by NAVSEA at Norfolk Naval Shipyard against a similar backdrop: the need to deliver availabilities faster and on time. Realization initially developed this approach for aircraft MRO in NAVAIR, and later deployed it in the USAF, USMC, commercial airlines, and other project environments.

3. Plan of Action

The planning and execution design effort will be completed over two to three consecutive weeks.

The effort will include the following steps:

Establish ambitious target timelines for the Campbell availability.

Confirm the project breakdown into workstreams and execution buckets.

Understand the work content, dependencies, and assumptions within each workstream and bucket.

Determine how the workstreams should be staggered, including what to stagger on and how much stagger is required.

Challenge bucket durations within each workstream to determine how the plan can fit within the target timelines.

Identify constraints, risks, and obstacles, and define how they will be elevated, mitigated, or overcome.

Design the execution management processes required to maintain focus during execution.

Map the technical plan to the Focus & Finish plan.

PURPOSE: 
STATEMENT OF NEED  
(145027-26-0025) 
Upgrade/ renewal of a Computer Aided Design (CAD) software package with associated Finite 
Element Analysis (FEA) computer modeling software, Solidworks 2026, for conducting 
Computer Aided Design and Finite Element Analysis of PMEL EDD designs. A Single Source 
Determination is included in procurement supporting documents. 
SCOPE OR MISSION: 
This software will support PMEL EDD’s core research and development mission, including 
instrumentation and platform development, existing instrumentation and platform support, and 
high-quality data collection. 
BACKGROUND: 
PMEL is a research and development laboratory that conducts both scientific and engineering 
R&D. A key purpose of the laboratory is to enhance NOAA’s observational capability through 
the development of technology, including sensors, vehicles and observational arrays. To fulfill 
this mission, PMEL engineers are constantly designing, building, and testing prototype 
instruments. PMEL EDD accomplishes this mission using Solidworks to design and draw 3-D 
Computer Aided Design (CAD) parts, conduct Finite Element Analysis (FEA) stress modeling 
and Fluid and Heat Transfer analyses on these parts, generate shop drawings in order to 
manufacture these parts, and then manage these electronic files throughout the part’s decades 
long life using Product Data Management software (PDM). This Solidworks CAD/FEA/PDM 
software package is the core software tool that PMEL EDD uses to accomplish NOAA’s 
mission. Because CAD file formats are proprietary to the CAD program, and Solidworks files 
are not forward compatible (i.e. older versions of Solidworks cannot open files generated on 
newer versions of Solidworks), PMEL EDD must upgrade/ renew their Solidwork’s licenses on a 
regular basis so that they can continue to collaborate with external partners both within and 
external to NOAA. 
TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS: 
Item 1: 4 Network licenses Solidworks + 1yr Support. 
 
Item 2: 1 Network licenses Solidworks Premium + 1yr Support. 
 
Item 3: 1 Network license for Solidworks Flow Simulation + 1yr Support. 
Item 4: 1 Network license for Solidworks Simulation Premium + 1yr Support. 
Item 5: 4 Network licenses Solidworks PDM Professional + 1yr Support. 
Period of Performance: 
06/01/2026 – 5/31/2027

NOAA Acquisition Manual 1330-52.222-70 NOAA SEXUAL ASSAULT AND SEXUAL HARASSMENT 
PREVENTION AND RESPONSE POLICY (MAY 2018)
In accordance with NOAA Administrative Order (NAO) 202-1106, NOAA Sexual Assault and Sexual 
Harassment Prevention and Response Policy, it is the policy of NOAA to maintain a work environment 
free from sexual assault and sexual harassment. NOAA prohibits sexual assault and sexual harassment 
by or of any employee, supervisor, manager, contractor, vendor, affiliate, or other individual with whom 
NOAA employees come into contact by the virtue of their work for NOAA.

1333MJ26Q0010 BASE
Page 7
(a) Definitions.
Contractor Employees - The term “contractor employees,” as used in this solicitation and contract 
language, refers to employees of the prime contractor or its subcontractors, affiliates, consultants, or 
team members.
Sexual Assault - The term sexual assault, as used in this solicitation and contract language, means any 
conduct proscribed by state or federal sexual abuse laws, including, but not limited to, those defined in 
chapter 109A of title 18 of the U.S. Code (sexual abuse), and assaults committed both by offenders who 
are strangers to the victim and by offenders who are known or related by blood or marriage to the 
victim.
Sexual Harassment - As defined by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, sexual harassment 
is a form of sex discrimination that violates Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. It includes unwelcome 
sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, and other verbal, non-verbal, or physical conduct of a sexual 
nature when any of the following are true:
● Submission to such conduct is made either explicitly or implicitly as a term or condition of an 
individual's employment;
● Submission to or rejection of such conduct by an individual is used as the basis for employment 
decisions affecting such individual;
● The conduct unreasonably interferes with an individual's work performance or creates an intimidating, 
hostile, or offensive working environment.
The main characteristics of sexual harassment are that the harasser's conduct is targeted against the 
recipient’s sex, gender identity, or sexual orientation, and is unwelcome to the recipient. It may include, 
but is not limited to: offensive jokes, slurs, epithets or name calling, undue attention, physical assaults 
or threats, unwelcome touching or contact, intimidation, ridicule or mockery, insults or put-downs, 
constant or unwelcome questions about an individual's identity, and offensive objects or pictures.
(b) Requirements.
1. It is the responsibility of the contractor to ensure that contractor employees maintain the highest 
degree of conduct and standards in performance of the contract. In support of this, NOAA urges its 
contractors to develop and enforce comprehensive company policy addressing sexual assault and sexual 
harassment.
2. The contractor shall include wording substantially the same as this solicitation and contract language 
in every subcontract so that it is binding upon each subcontractor.
3. If a contractor employee observes or is the object of sexual assault or sexual harassment, he or she is 
highly encouraged to report the matter, as soon as possible, to their immediate supervisor, the COR, 
subset of the COR (e.g. Task Manager or Assistant COR), or contracting officer (CO) if a COR is not 
assigned to the contract. The contract employee may also contact the NOAA Civil Rights Office to obtain 
guidance on reporting instances of sexual assault or sexual harassment. If deemed necessary, the 
contractor employee may also report such instances to local law enforcement. In the case where the 
incident occurs while performing at a remote location, such as at sea or in the field (at a field camp or 

1333MJ26Q0010 BASE
Page 8
other isolated location) where the above referenced individuals are unavailable, the contractor 
employee should follow the reporting procedure set forth in NAO 202-1106, Section 6.07, Reporting 
from Remote Locations.

Acquisition Office 
NCIA/ACQ/2026/ 07172  
 
  Page 2 
 
Introduction 
 
The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA)  hereby notifies the following 
Procurement O pportunity in accordance wit h the Procedure for NATO Competitive 
Procurement (link). This notification is issued to foster open and fair competition among 
eligible vendors from participating nations. This notification does not constitute a commitment 
to award a contract. 
 
Vendors are invited to review the requirements described herein and to submit their bids in 
accordance with the instructions provided in the subsequent solicitation documentation . All 
interested vendors are reminded that timely registration and compliance with eligibility 
requirements are essential, as deadlines for submission may not be extended.  Vendors are 
advised to regularly check for updates to this notification. 
 
This opportunity reflects NATO’s commitment to transparency, equal treatment of suppliers, 
and the efficient delivery of goods, works, and services in support of NATO missions and 
participating nations. 
 
All eligible and responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, which s hall be 
considered by the NCIA. 
 
1. Title of Procurement Opportunity 
 
Provision o f System Software Engineering Services and System Transition for Additional 
Modules for Advanced Rapid, Targeting and Effects Mission Information System (ARTEMIS). 
 
2. Description of Requirement 
 
ARTEMIS is the next generation Joint Targeting System which will enable NATO to enhance, 
expand and improve federated Target Material Production in order to respond to crisis using 
full spectrum of targeting capabilities. Additionally, ARTEMIS is expected to overcome the 
technical obsolescence and address the need for improvements for a modern targeting 
system. 
 
The current Joint Targeting System / Functional Area Service for dynamic and time-sensitive 
targeting (JTS/FAST or JTS) remains a valid targeting capability; however, it is based on 
obsolete underlying technology and architecture and has limited interopera bility with other 
functional systems and national targeting systems. In addition, JTS/FAST primarily supports 
the physical dimension of targeting and does not adequately support targeting activities 
within the virtual and cognitive dimensions. 
 
ARTEMIS Additional Modules (AAM) will deliver an enhanced, scalable, and cloud -ready 
architecture supporting improved interoperability, maintainability, and future capability 
expansion. The capability will support the management of diverse target types across all 
operational domains and within the physical, virtual, and cognitive dimensions, while 
facilitating secure data exchange and interoperability through open standards and 
Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). 
 
Updates to the ARTEMIS Basic Modules (ABM) may also be undertaken where necessary 
to support and facilitate the enhancement and integration of the AAM. 
 
The outcome will be a fully developed, integrated, and operational ARTEMIS capability. 
 

     
  
Acquisition Office 
NCIA/ACQ/2026/ 07172  
 
  Page 3 
 
The aim of the IFB-424334-ARTEMIS-AAM and prospective contract is to deliver three main 
work packages as described below: 
 
a. Work Package “System Software Engineering Services for Back End Modules” 
 
Through an Agile approach, this work package will deliver the development, 
integration, and support of new state -of-the-art backend services for the AAM. 
Backend services refer to the underlying server -side software components, 
application logic, databases, APIs, integration services, processing engines, and 
supporting infrastructure required to store, process, manage, secure, and 
exchange targeting and operational data. The solution shall be interoperable and 
provide a more efficient, scalable, and reliable targeting data management 
platform. 
 
This work package component will deliver comprehensive administrative 
management services covering all activities related to the development, 
integration, testing, and deployment of the AAM backend services and 
associated integrations. 
 
One of the primary interoperability mechanisms to be implemented will be based 
on the emerging STANAG 5658 standard. 
 
In addition, this work package will continue the establishment of foundational 
interfaces and dependencies necessary for effective data exchange and 
interoperability with other systems, thereby supporting maintainability, scalability, 
reliability, and future capability integration.  
 
b. Work Package “System Software Engineering Services for Front End Modules 
 
Also through an Agile approach, this work package will include the development 
of front -end software modules designed as web -browser-based applications 
supporting the new ARTEMIS system capabilities. These modules shall be 
developed in accordance with applicable NATO and industry standards and will 
support joint targeting activities to create, coordinate, and manage effects across 
the physical, virtual, and cognitive dimensions.  
 
c. Work Package “System Transition” 
 
Installation, configuration, migration and rollout of AAM alongside the existing 
targeting capability. It will ensure continuity of operations during the transition 
period and provide the necessary support until AAM reaches full operational 
functionality. After transition , this work package  also encompasses  an initial 
onsite floor-walking support to assist users with system -related issues, deliver  
technical support, and ensure effective user on-boarding and familiarization with 
system operations. 
 
Additionally, the prospective contract will include an evaluated option for O perations and 
Maintenance (O&M) services for up to five years. These services will include routine software 
maintenance, system performance monitoring under s econd and third level support , and 
release management of deployed baselines under third - and fourth-level support to meet 
availability requirements.

USE OF NAVY SUPPORT CONTRACTORS FOR OFFICIAL CONTRACT FILES
(a) NAVSEA may use a file room management support contractor, hereinafter referred to as "the support contractor", to manage its file room, in

is considered a trade secret, proprietary, business sensitive or otherwise protected pursuant to law or regulation, hereinafter referred to as "protected 
information". File room management services consist of any of the following: secretarial or clerical support; data entry; document reproduction, 
scanning, imaging, or destruction; operation, management, or maintenance of paperbased or electronic mail rooms, file rooms, or libraries; and 
supervision in connection with functions listed herein.

for the period of performance of its contract and for an additional three years thereafter unless otherwise provided by law or regulation; and,
(4) In addition to any other rights the contractor may have, it is a third party beneficiary who has the right of direct action against the support 
contractor, or any person to whom the support contractor has released or disclosed protected information, for the unauthorized duplication, release, or 
disclosure of such protected information.

markings or the nature of the information submitted, by its file room management support contractor for the limited purpose of executing its file room 
support contract responsibilities.

Performance Work Statement

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)

Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP)

Program Management Off0ice (PMO)

Table of Contents

Performance Work Statement

Student Exchange and Visitor Program (SEVP) Program Management Office (PMO) Support

Background

The Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) is part of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) National Security Division (NSD) within Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Department of Homeland Security (DHS). SEVP regulates international students in F-1 academic and M-1 vocational programs at SEVP-certified schools and provides compliance oversight to these institutions.

System Management Unit (SMU) delivers Information Technology (IT) services and products to support SEVP’s mission. SMU collects, maintains, and analyzes information to ensure only legitimate nonimmigrant students and exchange visitors gain entry into the United States. SMU also ensures that participating institutions are certified and comply with federal regulations, aligning IT systems with SEVP and ICE strategic goals while improving cost, schedule, and performance of IT investments. The SMU Unit Chief manages the SMU portfolio, ensuring applications meet all applicable security and federal standards and align with SEVP and ICE mission priorities.

The Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) is the web-based system that the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) uses to maintain information regarding:

Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP)-certified schools.

F-1 and M-1 students studying in the United States (and their F-2 and M-2 dependents).

U.S. Department of State-designated Exchange Visitor Program sponsors.

J-1 visa Exchange Visitor Program participants (and their J-2 dependents).

On behalf of DHS, SEVP manages SEVIS. The system is a critical tool in SEVP’s mission to protect national security while supporting the legal entry and stay of the more than one million F, M and J nonimmigrants coming to the United States for educational and cultural exchange programs.

SMU is divided into two sections:

Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) Programs Section (SPS): 

The SEVIS Programs Section (SPS) is responsible for ensuring that SEVIS and its subsystems continue to meet not only the evolving oversight and compliance mission and needs of the federal government but also of the schools and programs that admit foreign students and exchange visitors.

With over a million foreign students and exchange visitors (EVs) in the U.S. each year, international education and cultural exchange bring billions of dollars annually into the U.S. economy. SEVIS is used by schools and programs across the United States and its territories to create and maintain foreign student, EV, and dependent records. Government officials from several federal departments and agencies rely on SEVIS data to determine nonimmigrant eligibility for visas, for admission to the United States for immigration benefits, for removal from the country for status violations, and to identify immigration fraud. Institutions are monitored for compliance with applicable regulations. SEVIS shares information with other systems to allow stakeholders to better monitor the status of a student or EV throughout their stay in the United States. This allows SEVIS to meet requirements of the Unifying and Strengthening America by Providing Appropriate Tools Required to Intercept and Obstruct Terrorism (USA PATRIOT) Act (Public Law 107-56 passed on October 26, 2001). As a result, SEVIS has been designated a high-value asset by ICE. The Study in the States website contains extensive information on the functionality in SEVIS.

SPS is responsible for strategically planning the evolution of SEVIS and its subsystems, so it continues to meet changing laws and policy guidance as well as the changing needs of a dynamic law enforcement agency, its federal partners and the systems’ end users.  

SPS is responsible for:

The collection of system requirements from SEVP business units, federal interface partners who use SEVIS interface data, and end users

Strategically planning the SEVIS and Subsystems product roadmap and working with Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Information Technology Project Management (ITPMs) to ensure the Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) they develop includes a healthy balance of business-related functionalities and technical debt/innovation

Writing user stories that capture business needs for system development/enhancements

Collaborating with OCIO ITPMs and the development team(s) they manage with the development of SEVIS, its subsystems, and any new SEVIS-related priorities that may arise

Test developed functionalities to ensure that developed applications, functionalities, etc. meet SEVP’s business needs

Provide end-user, system-focused help materials

Identify, monitor, and mitigate risk

Provide responses to SEVIS-related taskers, requests for business analysis, reports, progress updates, etc.

SEVP Business Automation Section (SBAS):

The SEVP Business Automation Section (SBAS) is responsible for overseeing SEVPAMS, managing business process automation initiatives (including RPA bots), maintaining the SEVP Interactive Dialog (SID) chatbot, and supporting analytics and visualization through Tableau. SBAS provides business process management, documentation, and operational support for these tools and initiatives. This contract will provide program management and administrative support functions for SBAS, explicitly excluding technical development, coding, or direct system maintenance. 

SEVPAMS Application

SEVPAMS is an application built on Microsoft SharePoint, Dynamics 365, Power Apps, and Azure Studio. It is a customized platform used by SEVP staff, both federal and contract, and is not publicly accessible. SEVPAMS stores documentation and data from public sources, which are received via interfaces with SEVIS or through email, rather than direct ingestion.

SEVPAMS supports all units and sections within SEVP, including:

School Certification Unit

Appeals

SEVIS Response Center (SRC)

Policy Response Unit

SEVP Analysis and Compliance Center (SAOC)

Strategic Communications Team (SCT)

Executive Office (EO)

Fee Management Section (FMS)

Systems Management Unit

Government business partners may access SEVPAMS as needed to share information and collaborate.

SEVPAMS Purpose and Functionality

The goal of SEVPAMS is to provide SEVP users with a single portal for accessing the information (data and documents) necessary to make informed decisions and perform their duties. Staff can collaborate, manage tasks, share information, and access applications that automate work processes, regardless of their location. Data for metrics and reporting is systematically collected and stored in a denormalized Microsoft SQL database, optimized for use with Tableau.

Scope of Work

This effort requires providing three teams that utilize Agile-driven, proven program management techniques to support, maintain, and manage SEVP systems and programs in alignment with SEVP’s mission. 

The SMU team shall provide unit level program management support. The SEVIS Systems Team shall provide program and project support for a section-level program management support, which includes supporting backlog grooming, user acceptance testing, production support, communication support, user guide development, and coordination with other teams for requirements gathering and process improvements.

The SBAS Team shall provide section level support for Program Management. This includes support for planning, task management, documentation/records management support, and technical writing. It does not include requirements gathering, backlog grooming, user acceptance testing, technical support for requirements, testing, or technical user support. 

Library Management

The Contractor shall support the operational management of the Program repository within SEVPAMS, including the maintenance of all program-related documents and artifacts. The Contractor shall utilize good SharePoint practices to maintain version control and consistent metadata, and shall continue to populate, revise, and maintain Knowledge Management libraries and System and Subsystems Resource Documents (SSRD) 

Taskings: 

The PMO must utilize project management best practices, ensuring deliverables are submitted in alignment with government-approved delivery dates and timelines. Deliverables must meet objectives and be supported by data, with continuous product quality reviews to ensure accuracy, clarity, formatting, and alignment to government acceptance requirements. Deliverables should be professionally prepared, clear, concise, and editable by the government. Timeliness is critical, with a 98% timely submission rate required; more than two business days late is considered unacceptable. The PMO must also track risk management to ensure projects stay on schedule and inform the government of anticipated risks in a timely manner. Adequate staffing levels must be maintained, with monthly reviews to ensure at least 90% staffing during hours of operation, and immediate replacement of underperforming personnel.

 Reporting: 

The PMO is required to prepare a Monthly Contractor Count Report and upload it into the Personnel Management Application (PMA), including detailed information such as contract and task order numbers, employee names, positions, program/project, supervisor, clearance level, start/end dates, and location. The first report is due 30 calendar days after award and every month thereafter.

Reporting will occur on an as-needed basis to match the needs and lifecycle of the SEVP Program, with an expected cadence of weekly reports at the time of award. Status meetings shall be held quarterly or more frequently as needed between the Contractor’s Project Manager, COR, and Federal Lead to review performance and discuss issues. Formal reviews will be performed annually or at the government’s request, monitoring progress and compliance with policy changes. Interim reviews may be conducted for ongoing monitoring and process improvement. The PMO is expected to provide innovative methods for improvement and implement proven performance monitoring.

Deliverables must be created in electronic format, delivered via SEVPAMS (SharePoint) and email, and be compatible with Microsoft Office or other mutually agreed applications. The government will provide written notification of acceptance or rejection of final deliverables within 14 business days, with explanations for any rejections. Deliverables are deemed acceptable if they cover all required topics, meet general quality measures, are professionally prepared, and delivered on time.

Business Owner Support:

The Contractor shall provide administrative, planning, and operational support to business owners, including support for executive briefings, taskers, and requirements analysis. The Contractor shall support the Government’s strategic communications requirements 

Calendar and Schedule

The Contractor shall maintain unit calendars and schedules, ensuring visibility of key dates and events. The Contractor shall create and maintain the SMU Portfolio Roadmap and schedules, including critical milestones, dependencies, and expected delivery dates or targets for desired capabilities. The Contractor shall maintain the Program Integrated Master Schedule with milestones, dependencies, and expected delivery dates, and coordinate with other schedule owners to ensure updates are provided and incorporated into the Program Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) 

These services are intended to improve program efficiency and ensure transparent, timely, and accurate reporting to SEVP, NSID, HSI, ICE, and DHS management.

All systems shall leverage best practices identified in the U.S. Digital Services Playbook, DHS Agile Guidance, and ICE Agile Handbooks.

SEVIS Programs Section Support

The Contractor shall be responsible for developing plans, requirements, testing, and user support materials for SEVIS and its subsystems. This scope excludes technical tasks such as coding, development, and environment management. The Contractor shall collaborate with development teams managed by OCIO Information Technology Project Managers (ITPMs), contractors, federal employees in SEVP units, and other government agencies, as directed by Federal leads, to achieve SEVP objectives.

SEVP Business Automation Section Support

Description of Requirements 

The Contractor shall provide three teams of qualified, experienced personnel. The team supporting SEVIS will assist in the management, testing, and administration of both program-wide and project-specific requirements. Program Management Office (PMO) support services will include the development and maintenance of program support documentation as required by Management Directives Volume 4000 – Information Technology Systems.  The contractor shall be responsible for providing staff members with significant skill in using generative AI tools. DHSChat and any other ICE approved chat tools shall be used appropriately to help produce documents and other deliverables. 

Applicable Policies and Standards

The Contractor shall comply and ensure that the latest versions of all technology standards and architecture policies, processes, and procedures applicable to the ICE or DHS  IT environment are being used. If a contractor needs to request documentation such as standards or guidelines, contact the assigned ITPM or email address provided in the PWS. For Section 508 compliance information, the contractor is directed to email accessibility@dhs.gov for approved testing methods and tools.  These publications are available on request and include, but are not limited to, the following:

DHS Systems Engineering Life Cycle Guidebook

https://www.dhs.gov/sites/default/files/publications/Systems%20Engineering%20Life%20Cycle.pdf.

ICE Architecture Test and Evaluation Plan.

ICE Security Authorization Requirements.

STATEMENT OF  WORK  
 
Indian Health Services (IHS) Enterprise Computerized Maintenance Management System 
(CMMS) System Implementation for Office of Environmental Health and Engineering (OEHE) 
 
 
 
A. BACKGROUND 
 
The Indian Health Service (IHS), an agency within the Department of Health and Human Services, is 
responsible for providing federal health services to American Indians and Alaska Natives. The IHS is 
the principal federal health care provider and health advocate for Indian people and its goal is to raise 
their health status to the highest possible level. The IHS provides a comprehensive health service 
delivery system for American Indians and Alaska Natives. IHS services are administered through a 
system of 12 Area offices and 170 IHS and tribally managed service units. 
 
The mission of the Office of Environmental Health and Engineering (OEHE) aims to provide and 
operate safe buildings and patient care equipment for the delivery of health care services to Native 
American Indians and Alaska Natives. A Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) 
provides innovative ways to improve health care delivery and quality, record preventive and unscheduled 
maintenance activities, enhance asset tracking, increase staff mobility, and modernize administrative 
functions for both facility and biomedical device management to meet accreditation. An existing CMMS 
(Nuvolo) is currently deployed within the agency as an enterprise-level solution, providing a single, 
standardized solution for all IHS employees to utilize per national requirements. 
 
OEHE invites prospective offerors to provide information on a proposed approach to continue technical 
support to the existing Nuvolo CMMS along with software enhancements and training, including related 
functions, tools, and services. All responses must conform to the requirements and instructions outlined in 
this document. 
 
Offerors are required to have and provide FedRAMP certification of their solution and cloud 
service provider (CSP). The offerors must provide either a Provisional Authority to Operate (P- 
ATO) or Joint Authorization Board (JAB) authorization documentation. 
 
All proposals must provide full documentation to include (but not be limited to): conceptual network 
diagrams, logic/dataflow diagrams, communications protocols, user/operator guides, all information 
necessary for the technical evaluation team to create an accurate security assessment, use/operation 
assessments of the system. 
 
B. OBJECTIVES 
 
This will consist of required SaaS licenses, data collection and/or data migration, and SaaS vendor 
support.  The solution provided shall also be aligned with CMMS healthcare industry best practices and 
provide the flexibility necessary to enable improvements and address agency initiatives in facility and 
biomedical operational and service management processes. 
 
The objective is to provide access and support services for the IHS Nuvolo computerized maintenance 
management system (CMMS) platform capable of providing service desk, incident, problem,
 change, 
knowledge, configuration management, and other CMMS processes delivered through an “off- 
premises” model (e.g., Software as a Service (SaaS), cloud-based offering, etc.). The solution will 
consist of required SaaS licenses, data collection and/or data migration, and SaaS vendor support. The 
solution provided shall also be aligned with CMMS healthcare industry best practices and provide the 
flexibility necessary to enable improvements and address agency initiatives in facility and biomedical 
operational and service management processes, and provide a model that supports a healthcare 
organization by: 
 

 
 Licensing on a ‘concurrent’ user basis. Other licensing schema (role-based, platform based, 
named-user, requestor, mobile, etc.) must be explicitly described and all tiers/types of 
licensing/pricing submitted for review/evaluation. 
 Improving facility and biomedical service delivery consistency, quality and responsiveness. 
 Improving visibility and collaboration across facility, biomedical, and IT support tiers. 
 Providing reports and analytics for facilities and biomedical teams to track and communicate 
the value and support efforts they provide. 
 Providing and supporting mobile application functionality via iPads, Microsoft, or 
Android devices with offline capability and synchronization when connectivity is 
available. 
 Meeting statutory requirements of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) 
Conditions of Participation (42 USC), the Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act (21 USC), and others. 
 Incorporating accreditation standards of various entities such as The Joint Commission 
(TJC), DNV-GL Healthcare, Accreditation Association for Ambulatory Health Care (AAAHC), 
and others. 
 Incorporating various maintenance standards/codes such as NFPA 99, NFPA 101, 
AAMI/ANSI EQ56, IEC 60601, and others 
 
The solution shall include Development, Test and Production systems, all of which are hosted as part of 
a FedRAMP Low or Moderate service offering with a current FedRAMP Provisional Authorization 
(PA). 
 
Respondent should clearly articulate in their response their ability to fulfill the aforementioned 
delivery requirements. 
 
C. SCOPE 
 
The IHS CMMS project will follow a phased implementation with incremental delivery of capabilities 
developed through software upgrades or platform enhancements. This will allow lessons learned to be 
incorporated as additional groups are on-boarded to using the new toolset and processes. Technical 
capabilities will be released in phases, while the roll-out to IHS organizations shall be completed in 
waves. 
 
Ideally, full implementation at IHS would span: 
 Across ten out of the twelve Regional Areas Offices (Albuquerque, Bemidji, Billings, 
California, Great Plains, Nashville, Navajo, Oklahoma, Phoenix and Portland), Alaska and 
Tucson may opt to adapt the same solution at a future implementation. 
 Implementations/“rollouts” and trainings at the facilities or through online platforms within the 
respective Areas are at the discretion of each Area office. The training module is based on a 
“train the trainer” model, and implementations can be done remotely with the assistance from 
Area Office staff. 
 Future implementations are optional and will be funded, executed at the discretion of IHS, 
and planned with the vendor. 
 Approximately 800 total users exist for Local Facility and Biomed staff at the Hospitals, 
Health Care Centers, Clinics, and Area Offices. 
 
C1.1.1 Task 1 – Software as a Service (SaaS) Licensing and Support – Base Year 
The Contractor shall provide their license schema to accommodate 800 solution licenses which are valid 
for 12 months from the date the licenses are provided to IHS based on usage. These licenses can be 
formatted as user, role-based, or concurrent in order to benefit IHS and the government. The Contractor 
shall propose a delivery schedule in support of required licenses to support the Contractor’s delivery of 
the required IHS CMMS capabilities and waves during the base period of performance. The Contractor 
is authorized to propose additional licenses to account for organizational growth, of which shall not 

 
exceed 10% of the total required license count provided within the SOW. 
 
Licensing shall include support from the SaaS vendor to include access to vendor support via a self- 
service portal. Vendor support personnel will be available to assist in resolving software errors, 
answering questions regarding installation procedures, compatibility with other software, and general 
questions of the licensed services and products during and after installation. The self-service portal shall 
also facilitate status reporting (acceptance and socialization) of software problems, and provide 
downloads of software patches, fixes, and documentation. 
 
The Contractor will provide quarterly reports on support requests (to include, user name, email address, 
Regional Area, location and description of the request). The Contractor will not authorize any software 
modifications or permissions changes. These requests are required to be forwarded to the Regional Area 
Point of Contacts (POC) and to include the HQ CMMS Coordinator. 
 
The CMMS solution shall include Development, Test and Production systems, all of which are hosted as 
part of a FedRAMP service offering with a current FedRAMP Provisional Authorization. 
 
The Contractor shall clearly describe and distinguish the level of effort required to accredit the solution. 
 
 
Operational Requirements 
This section contains free form questions and/or requirements for completion by the Contractor to ensure 
understanding of the operation of the proposed solution. The Contractor shall include an evaluation of all 
requirements as part of their proposal. 
 
 
Operational 
 
Requirement 
 
O1 
The contractor shall define their ability to provide CMMS services and support in the 
Nuvolo platform, including any documentation about service partnerships. 
 
 
O2 
The contractor shall describe the established framework for customizing the platform. 
Please describe how you distinguish between customization and configuration of the 
platform. 
 
O3 The contractor shall describe how upgrades and new releases are managed and 
deployed to minimize impact and disruption to customers. 
 
 
 
O4 
The contractor shall establish the level of effort in hours required by internal IHS 
support staff as well as skills required to maintain and operate the solution post 
implementation. This should include analysts, administrators, and owners. In 
response to this requirement, the contractor shall clearly distinguish these resources 
apart from the resources required to implement the solution. 
 
O5 The contractor shall specify the solution support organization locations, hours/days of 
operation and the level of support provided. 
 
O6 The contractor shall define service level agreements, response time, and commitments 
are available for each support level. 
 
O7 
Service Level Agreements (SLA) will provide performance, backup information, 
support requests (results, frequency, etc), and any useful information to provide better 
processes for IHS. 
O8 The contactor shall enable the ability of the solution to support single sign on. 
 
 
O9 
The contractor shall define the licensing and ongoing support/maintenance costs, as 
well as estimates for implementation (including installation, demonstrations/ 
training, configuration of systems, deployment, ongoing support for future 
implementations, etc.). 
 
O10 The contractor shall provide process, procedures and supporting documents which 
will be provided to IHS to operate and maintain the system. 

 
 
Functional Requirements 
The Contractor shall propose their approach in fulfilling and supporting the potential functional 
requirements listed below. The Contractor shall include an evaluation of all requirements as part of their 
proposal. The Contractor’s evaluation responses shall be limited to one of the below statements for each 
requirement (comments may be provided): 
 
 5 - Requirement is met by out of the box, no configuration or customization needed ("just add 
data"). 
 4 - Requirement is met with additional configuration of existing structures, using built-in 
administrator's tools. 
 3 - Requirement is met with additional customization, e.g. adding tables, building customized 
reports, building custom workflow. 
 2 - Requirement is met by the use of a separate module or third-party product. Not included in 
core product. 
 1 - Requirement is met by software that is currently under development, has not been installed at 
a single client site, or in Beta test 
 0 - Requirement is not met. 
 
 
Service Desk 
Management Requirements 
F1 Support for after-call closure capabilities such as performing automatic follow-up on 
specific date/time via visual or sound notification 
F2 
Support for automated escalation capabilities such as automatically calculating the 
total cost to the customer associated with an incident or service request (from total 
time spent, hourly rates, cost of parts, etc.) 
F3 Support for cutting and pasting text, embedding html, bitmaps, screenshots, attachments 
etc. List any other types of functionalities such as drag and drop. 
F4 Ability to translate time zones to local times for active ticket timestamps and reporting 
analytics 
F5 Automated matching rules for Incidents, Problems, Known Errors, and Workarounds, 
based on categorization or Configuration Item rules 
F6 Ability to report on the number of contacts (calls, emails, web requests) received. 
F7 Ability to report the percentage of repeat contacts for the same Incident (e.g., status, 
inquiry) 
F8 Ability to report the number of Incidents escalated hierarchically and functionally. 
F9 Ability to provide a suggestion box capability for customers and users to submit 
feedback. 
Knowledge 
Management Requirements 
F10 Full feature knowledgebase search capability, such as full text, keyword and catalog 
content 
F11 Automatic use of description to search knowledgebase 

 
 
F12 Ability to support integration or link with prebuilt knowledgebase or external Web- 
crawling capability that allows our KM to find content on other sites 
 
F13 
Ability to search categorized/indexed documents or Frequently Asked Questions 
(FAQs) based on a symptom driven menu 
 
F14 
Ability to search previously resolved tickets and integration with Incident and 
Problem Management (e.g. ability to propose solution based on key words within 
incident or problem record) 
 
F15 
System to highlight which Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) are needed based on 
top searched or clicked articles 
 
F16 
Ability to publish globally as well as to a specified audience based on their role. 
Articles viewable by assigned Support Groups

Sole Source Synopsis 
Spectrum System Development Architecture (SSDA) 
 
Subject: Notice of Intent to Sole Source  
This is to award a contract on sole-source basis for all technical and operational support for the 
Spectrum System Development Architecture (SSDA) Program in support of the United States Air 
Force (USAF). This follow-on contract is required to continue providing the standard 
infrastructure design for the Depot Maintenance System Integration (DMSI) components.  
 
Solicitation Number: FA877025RB016 
 
Agency/Office: Department of War / Business Enterprise Systems (BES) 
 
Location: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base 
 
Description: 
The Department of War, BES AFLCMC/GBK4M, intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed-
price contract on a sole source basis to Empower AI, INC., located at 11730 Plaza America Dr, 
Suite 400, Reston, V A 20190-4764. 
 
The acquisition is for a 12-month contract for continued SSDA services, one 12-month option 
period, a 6-month option period, and a 6-month extension of services for the Air Force Materiel 
Command (AFMC), Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Business and 
Enterprise Systems (BES), Enterprise Logistics Systems Division (GB), Depot 
Maintenance Workflow Product Line (GBM), to provide technical support for maintenance, 
sustainment and modification for the DMSI SSDA. This requirement provides for the software 
maintenance/enhancement support services needed to maintain and enhance SSDA. SSDA has 
been uniquely modified to be utilized by DMSI systems based on direction provided by the 
Program Management Office (PMO). These services include providing scheduled and 
unscheduled upgrades to SSDA, maintenance of all DMSI wide objects incorporated into SSDA 
to support the AFLCMC/GBM Depot Maintenance systems and the expert technical support for 
using SSDA. Throughout the period of performance, the Contractor will be required to modify 
the SSDA code for items such as role-based security to support changing cyber requirements, 
increased error handling due to increased specificity required by users, updated audit logging for 
compliance with auditor findings, and surveillance and patching of the Appeon toolset. Without 
the surveillance, development, and maintenance to sustain / enhance the SSDA, the application 
developers will not be able to effectively sustain/enhance the DMSI systems. The contract type is 
a mix of Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) with Cost Reimbursement (CR).  
 
Justification: 
This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented 
by RFO 6.103-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy 
agency requirements." This action is critical to ensure the uninterrupted continuation of 
enhancement and sustainment services for the SSDA system. The contractor is the only 
responsible source capable of continuing these critical services without disruption. The 
contractor possesses an unmatched and immediate understanding of the complex requirements, 

architecture, and operational dependencies of the SSDA system. The Government does not 
intend to use RFO Part 12 for this acquisition.  
 
Response Instructions: 
This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible 
sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by 
the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based 
upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information 
received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct a 
competitive procurement. The Government will not pay for any information submitted as a result 
of this synopsis. This synopsis shall not be construed as an obligation on the part of the 
Government to acquire any products or services. 
 
Capability statements must be received by 04 June 2026 before 1700 EST and must clearly 
demonstrate the vendor's ability to meet the requirements described herein.  
 
Point of Contact: 
Antonio Ayubi, Contracting Officer 
Email: antonio.ayubi@us.af.mil

BACKGROUND

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is the second-largest federal department, serving approximately 19 million Veterans in over 1,700 facilities and sites worldwide, making it the largest integrated health care system in the United States. This impressive service delivery is made possible through the coordinated efforts of three major line organizations: the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), the Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA), and the National Cemetery Administration (NCA). These efforts are orchestrated at the VA Central Office (VACO) located in Washington, D.C.  

OIT delivers available, adaptable, secure, and cost-effective technology services to the VA and acts as a steward for all VA's Information Technology (IT) assets and resources. Currently, 60% of the 16,000 plus OIT employees and contractors are Veterans. 

The Connectivity and Collaboration Services (CCS) team delivers world class Telephony, Network, and Collaboration Services in an environment that encourages transparency, innovation, flexibility, fiscal responsibility, and accountability with 100% focus on Veteran outcomes.​

CCS serves at the forefront of VA’s digital transformation, enabling enterprise collaboration and connecting Veterans to VA through secure and resilient voice, video, data, and messaging services. 

CCS is divided into three pillars.

Core Network Services (CNS) - This pillar fuses the development, engineering, and operation of VA network services into a single organization, driving efficiency and enabling a unified strategy for our network infrastructure.​​​​​​​

Collaboration Services (CS) - CS provides enterprise level support focused on providing dynamic, flexible and efficient collaboration amongst VA staff and Veteran outreach. CS nationally supports the Microsoft 365 suite of products that VA currently employs for enterprise messaging and collaboration. These products include Exchange, Teams, OneDrive and others.

Unified Communications (UC) - UC continues to modernize, enhance, and operate world class enterprise Unified Communications services and solutions to connect Veterans, their families and VA professionals to the resources and services they need.

Direct Contractor support for this Task Order (TO) will reside within CCS Division under the Office of Information and Technology.  Mainly under CNS with optional tasks under the CS, UC, and ETS Business Office pillars.

Under CCS, The CNS team is a vital team supporting the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) mission by providing robust and reliable network infrastructure that connects VA facilities, Clouds, Internet, contractors, guests, and Veterans to critical VA resources and services. CNS enables seamless access to essential applications, data, and services across all VA divisions, ensuring that VHA,(VBA, and NCA can deliver top-tier healthcare, benefits, and cemetery services to Veterans across the nation. In doing so, CNS directly impacts the quality and timeliness of the VA's service delivery by maintaining the infrastructure that powers every networked interaction within VA facilities.

CNS is responsible for overseeing the telecommunications and networking technologies that serve as the backbone for VA operations. This includes provisioning the high-speed, secure, and resilient connections that allow VA personnel to collaborate effectively, enable contractors to access necessary resources, support guests’ informational needs, and allow Veterans direct access to their own health and benefits information. By providing stable network connectivity, CNS plays a crucial role in critical system availability to the VA workforce, whether they are in medical centers, regional offices, veteran centers, or remote clinics.

CNS Priorities

Communications - internally within network operations, engineering, and provisioning teams

Site Availability - Uptime for sites, redundancy, resiliency, minimizing downtime, and data supporting this.

Compliance - baseline configuration compliance, code standards, time to deploy, tracking Known Exploited Vulnerabilities/Zero Days.

Scope of Work

Purpose:

The Oklahoma City Area Indian Health Service requires a software application that provides a secure exchange, that assures all electronic transactions and DDE(Direct Data Entry) /FISS (Florida Information Shared System) access provide confidentiality, authentication, integrity and non-repudiation for the twelve IHS facilities. 

It is mandated by IHS Headquarters that payment systems are updated to reflect changes in medical practice and relative value of services. Based on this; secure exchange managed services are needed for claims process to keep in compliance.  

Statement of Work:

The contractor shall provide a secure exchange data software solution that provides a unique technology approach for connectivity to the Medicare DDE(Direct Data Entry) /FISS (Florida Information Shared System) products, eligibility verification and third party insurance claims validation, approval and processing services via a clearinghouse for Medicare, Medicaid, VA and Commercial Payers for the Oklahoma City Area (OCA).   The contractor shall be able to process both medical and dental claims.

The OCA facilities include the Claremore Indian Hospital, Lawton Indian Hospital, Anadarko Indian Health Center, Carnegie Indian Health Center, Pawnee Indian Health Center, Clinton Indian Health Center, EL Reno Indian Health Center, Watonga Indian Health Center, Wewoka Indian Health Center and the Oklahoma City Area Office all located in Oklahoma and the Haskell Indian Health Center and White Cloud Indian Health Station located in Kansas. 

   

The software services shall comply with the following constraints:

The service shall not require OCA facilities to install contractor software within the Oklahoma    City Area Indian Health Service Environment

The service shall enable OCA facilities to exchange data utilizing a secure File Transfer protocol (FTP) as approved by the Indian Health Service (IHS) Office of Information Technology.

The service shall support EDI transactions and interactive telnet sessions

The service shall support multiple users and access shall be workstation independent

The service shall not entail development of HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) transaction set translation or mapping processes, non-CMS or non-IHS generated data or messages, or data reformatting

The service shall conform to the information agreements to be established via an Interconnection Security Agreement and Memorandum of Understanding between Indian Health Service and the Contractor.

The service shall also conform to a business associate agreement to be established between the OCA facilities and the Contractor.

The contractor shall support end-to-end communication testing, implementation and daily operations of the data transfers from the contractor to the OCA facilities, which shall include, at a minimum:

The contractor shall provide routine technical support to implement corrections to service occurring as a result of errors, flaws, or other failures within their service.

The contractor shall notify a designated OCA point of contact (Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR)) of any scheduled maintenance that shall result in downtime at least two (2) days prior to the maintenance period.

The contractor shall notify a designated OCA point of contact of any issues as their facilities or at the contractor that result in a disruption of data exchange capabilities.  This notification shall occur as soon as possible after the disruption has been identified.

The contractor shall provide customer support for reporting, documenting, tracking and resolving of service problems, which shall be available via telephone and email to the OCA technical staff during the period 8:00 am to 5:00 pm central standard time.

The contractor shall provide:

Secure internet based connectivity to all current fiscal intermediaries.

Ability to send claims to Medicare Contractor using a secure date exchange technology.

Unlimited DDE and PPTN online Medicare claims status/corrections, etc. for Medicare Part A.

All electronic transactions DDE/FISS access provides confidentiality, authentication, integrity and non-repudiation 

Automated batch 837/835 file transfers.  
Automated batch 276/277 claims correction capability.

Accept electronic claims from RPMS.

Obtain reports and acknowledgements on claims sent.

Provide a single location to manage all electronic claims, including VA claims.

Verify Medicare and Commercial Payer eligibility in real time.

Flat fee for unlimited transactions.

Provide knowledgeable support personnel.

The Contractor shall provide toll free telephone/technical support during normal business hours, 8 am to 5 pm, Monday thru Friday, except Government holidays. The Contractor shall provide a two (2) hour minimum response time from notification by IHS as no additional cost to each IHS facility

The Clearinghouse services must meet the following:

Third party insurance claims shall be submitted to the appropriate carrier/payer via the Contractor provided clearinghouse by the close of the next business day after receipt from IHS.

Third party insurance claims shall be transmitted electronically to the appropriate carrier/payer.

The Contractor shall use routine editing procedures and best efforts to detect defects in claims information supplied by the government. The Contractor shall reject and not process claims with defects. The Contractor shall provide the service location with edit reports listing the defect to aid the service location in the correction of the detected defects.

The Contractor shall return to the appropriate IHS facility for correction any claims rejected by the carrier/payer for a reason other than the inappropriate format to the claims. The Contractor shall not charge for any claims rejected prior to the submission to the carrier/payer.

Errors in processing or submission of claims shall be limited to reprocessing and resubmission at the Contractor’s expense.

The Contractor shall provide a productivity spreadsheet within 24 hours of batch transmission to be submitted to the originating facility.

Contractor Compliance:

The Contractor shall adhere to all official coding rules as published by the American Hospital Association (AHA), regulations and guidelines in order to ensure the highest levels of integrity compliance and ethics. 

The Contractor shall maintain a record of confidentiality in accordance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPPA), Privacy Act of 1974, Alcohol and Drug Abuse Patient Records, Freedom of Information Act and other pertinent Federal regulations.

Administrative:

	Billing:  Billing will be at a flat rate for all services.

Meetings/Conference Calls: The Contractor shall attend meetings or conference calls schedule by the PO to address areas of concern and exchange information to ensure consistent high levels of professional services. The PO shall be responsible for scheduling and coordination of all meetings and conference calls.

Equipment Failure: Any delays or downtime due to Contractor equipment failure shall be communicated to the COR or their designee within two hours via telephone. The Contractor shall not be penalized for delays due to equipment failure beyond the Contractor’s control. (e.g., IHS server downtime).

Reports:

	Claims Approval: The Contractor shall deliver a standardized report to each facility on a weekly basis, which includes at the minimum the following:

	

Claim #			d. Insurer Billed

Date of Service		e. Date Billed

Total Amount Billed 

Clearinghouse: The Contractor shall deliver a standardized report to each facility on a weekly basis, which includes at a minimum the following:

Patient name 		g. Insurance carrier

Claim #			h. Total # claims submitted 

Date of service 		i. Total # claims accepted

Total Amount Billed 	j. Total # claims rejected

Date Transmitted		k. Rejected claim reasons (per claim)

Type of transmission (paper/electronic)

Period of Performance:

One Year with an Option to extend 4 additional Option Years.

Background:  
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the largest investigative arm in the Department of 
Homeland Security (DHS), is responsible for identifying and shutting down vulnerabilities in the 
nation’s border, economic, transportation, and infrastructure security. The US Homeland 
Security Investigations (HSI) directorate is a critical asset in the ICE mission, responsible for 
investigating a wide range of domestic and international activities arising from the illegal 
movement of people and goods into, within, and out of the United States. The ICE Office of the 
Chief Information Officer (OCIO) is responsible for the overall management, planning, 
development, deployment, operation, maintenance, coordination, and evaluation of ICE 
technology programs and activities.  
 
ICE seeks to leverage a business-centric approach to system design, minimizing duplicative 
tasks, leveraging common functionality, and reducing the complexity associated with systems 
maintenance. ICE also seeks to leverage best practices in open architecture to minimize cycle 
time and costs associated with acquiring and maintaining third-party tools. Leveraging ICE’s 
Agile environment, all of this should be accomplished through cloud-based hosting and 
Development, Security and Operations (DevSecOps) tools.

Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) Software 
Application Storefront, Pipeline and Tailorable Warﬁghting 
Applications – Industry Day Q&A  
 
1. What is the RFI expecting from vendors that will be a supportive capacity (i.e. 
App Provider) versus a vendor that is managing a Storefront?  
 
The RFI is requesting all responses that get after the capabilities associated with the 
1) Storefront, 2) Platform/Pipeline, 3) Application(s), and 4) Team Lead. While the 
Government sees the concept of a team lead to ensure all “pieces” of these 
capabilities can be provided, we are not limiting the responses to only those 
vendors willing to provide all capabilities.  If you can and want to provide all 
capabilities, please explain that in the RFI. We also want to hear/know if you can 
only provide one (1) of these capabilities or even a part of those capabilities. Our 
goal is to see all possible solutions in order to deliver “best of breed” capabilities to 
the warﬁghter.  
 
2. CECOM ASIC briefed that they have an approved pipeline. Are there partnership 
requirements with them? 
 
The government does not want to limit itself to a single source solution at this 
moment and is exploring all possibilities. 
 
3. In this process what role do you see the team lead playing? And what role does 
the Government team playing? 
 
We are looking for all solutions for how a team-lead would centrally manage a 
DevSecOps environment to enable a secure, fast integration process for the 
tailorable warﬁghter applications through a DevSecOps pipeline pushed to the 
Storefront solution.  
 
4. Where do you expect to host this platform in your own cloud or a FedRamp 
environment? 
 

We are looking at all solutions to include hosting in a commercial cloud and/or 
Government Cloud.  
 
5. Do you want a consolidated multi-impact level security marketplace, or should 
these be segmented by security level? Should we submit trial access to already 
production marketplaces at various security levels. 
 
We want to know what works best for industry and leverage best practices in an IL5 
and an IL6 solution that is segmented by security level. We are open to solutions 
that could promote an IL5 container to IL6 then apply IL6 application updates or 
changes automatically into the Storefront. 
 
6. Regarding the question on license management: Is the Army looking to buy 
software licenses through the app store, or will the companies on the app store 
already be under contract? 
 
 This depends on feedback from Industry and the potential strategy in teaming. The 
vision of the App Store would provide telemetry data on licensing usage and provide 
links for purchase. As of now, we are seeking your innovative solutions to help shape 
this process. For example, if we were to use a “teaming approach,” we might expect 
the Team Lead to “own the contract” and the requirements/money would ﬂow 
through there. The licensing would be conducted through those business 
relationships, where an application license would be paid through the lead and be 
“loaded” into the App store once it passes pipeline protocols.  Another option is to 
potentially set up Enterprise licensing agreements where the government would pay 
for the licensing (separate from the structure) and provide it to the App store 
“owner” and/or the Team Lead as Government Furnished Equipment (software). 
While these are two (2) examples, many more scenarios exist andw e are interested 
in feedback to see what industry believes is best/most achievable approach. 
 
7. Does the Government expect the lead to own the storefront/pipeline product, 
or simply operate it? 
 
 While that is a viable option, we are not limiting the lead to the storefront/pipeline 
product.  A lead could stem from someone who only has interest in creating a 
storefront, a pipeline, or a warﬁghter application. The lead could also be a different 
vendor who supports the business relationship between these industry providers. 
 

8. Will both an IL5 and IL6 solution be delivered with data separation and deﬁned 
data transfer across the levels, or will there be a single solution that will be 
deployed in IL5 or IL6 depending on a later decision?  
 
We want to know what works best for industry and leverage best practices in an IL5 
and an IL6 solution that is segmented by security and data levels. We are open to all 
cross-domain solutions that could promote an IL5 container to IL6 then apply IL6 
application updates or changes automatically into the Storefront. If you have a 
single solution, we value your feedback. 
 
9. Is it ok to submit protype?  
 
Yes, the government will consider prototypes for offered capabilities and as a 
deﬁned solution for requirements.  
 
10. Is there an anticipation of a solicitation in 3rd Qtr (sam.gov RFI reference)? 
 
Depending on feedback from this RFI, the application storefront, pipeline, or team 
lead concept may have additional RFIs. Please continue to monitor sam.gov for 
additional information. 
 
11. What are all the target networks for these Apps, and will vendors have access to 
their test networks during automated testing?  
 
Networks will consist of IL5 and IL6. In the Development environment, you will have 
access to your system. When the system is under test, you will not have access, but 
the results will be provided, and you may remediate. 
 
12. You mention Agile in your RFI. re you expecting or wanting an Agile 
Development Framework being proposed to govern the execution of the 
Gov't/Industry relationships as the Storefront and integration into it to include 
lessons learned on the implementation on other large solutions? 
 
We are looking for an Agile development and sprint cycle to ensure continuous 
integration and continuous deployment. We are open to lessons learned on how to 
implement DevSecOps. 
 

13. Should the response include new application discovery, application provider 
recruitment? 
We are looking for solutions for application discovery to include application providers.  
 
14. For scaling/sizing purposes, can the Government provide approximate order of 
magnitude of number of applications in the storefront, users of the solution?  
 
We are currently experimenting with around 90 applications. Please keep in mind 
that all information shared today reﬂects current intentions and are subject to 
change.    
 
15. How does the Government deﬁne the role of “the lead” in this construct?  
 
Conceptually, the lead will integrate the Storefront, Pipeline and Applications into 
the NGC2 ecosystem and manage the business relationships. They may also 
provide an application or solution that brings everything together. The government is 
looking for industry approaches and all feedback. Please refer to Question 1, table 1 
in the RFI. 
 
16. You mention Agile in your RFI, are you expecting or wanting an Agile 
Development Framework being proposed to govern the execution of the 
Gov't/Industry relationships as the Storefront and integration into it to include 
lessons learned on the implementation on other large solutions?  
 
We are looking for an Agile development and sprint cycle to ensure continuous 
integration and continuous deployment. We are open to lessons learned on how to 
implement DevSecOps. 
 
17. Is it your intent to leverage the Army Software Factory for this effort? Or are 
other SWF's going to be considered?  
 
Yes, the government is open to and considering different avenues to obtain 
software. 
 
18. Can a Federally Funded Research and Development Center respond to the RFI?  
 
Yes.
