Synopsis 
The following Request for Information (RFI) is to gain an understanding from Industry on the 
capabilities offered to support Project Manager for Command and Control Applications (PM 
C2 Apps) entire portfolio. The Government is considering an acquisition strategy that uses a 
"teaming" model to consolidate the PM C2 Apps portfolio under a singular lead, tasked with 
managing a unified development pipeline and application storefront. This approach mirrors 
the Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) "clean-slate" methodology, which 
emphasizes Agile and Development, Security and Operations (DevSecOps) environments to 
rapidly deliver and iterate on mission-focused software. By partnering with a lead entity to 
integrate a mix of Government-Off-The-Shelf (GOTS), Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS), and 
tactical solutions, the strategy aims to provide the Warfighter with a flexible, modular, and 
interoperable suite of applications that can be updated at the "speed of relevance". The 
Government is particularly interested in solutions offered by entities with direct control over 
the capability's development and innovation. Respondents should clearly describe whether 
they are the original capability provider or an intermediary (reseller/integrator), and 
demonstrate their ability to drive innovation, influence product roadmaps, and provide direct 
technical support. The government envisions mission success by establishing group 
collaboration among all industry partners for the overall success of the program to include 
the application development/oversight from various partners (GOTS/COTS/etc) through 
pipeline/DSO to the storefront for User Access. The government intends to conduct an 
industry day to provide an overview to further support and enhance market research. 
Understanding this is a new concept, the Government welcomes feedback on the feasibility of 
this approach from Industry as well as the specific questions detailed in later sections of this 
RFI.
 
Description 
1. Description  
1.1 PM C2 Apps seeks industry interest regarding the availability of a software application 
storefront, pipeline and tailorable warfighting application solutions. This Request For 
Information (RFI) is being issued to conduct market research for solutions using an Agile and 

DevSecOps environment. Furthermore, this advanced notice is being issued to obtain insight 
and responses from Industry regarding some or all of the questions and requests listed in 
Table 1. These responses will help PM C2 Apps shape requirements, understand capability 
gaps, and/or understand Industry provided solutions that PM C2 Apps may pursue through 
the Army Open Solicitation (AOS) during 3rd quarter (Q3) Fiscal Year (FY) 2026.  
 
1.2 THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION: The Government is not obligated to pursue any 
procurement as a result of this request. This RFI is for informational purposes only; this is not 
an Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Proposal (RFP), or Request for Quotation (RFQ). All 
information contained in this RFI is preliminary as well as subject to modification and is in no 
way binding on the Government. The Government will not pay for information received and is 
in no way obligated by the information received in response to this RFI. Responders to this 
invitation are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI and 
will NOT be reimbursed. The information provided will be used by the Government for the 
purpose of conducting market research and this RFI will be the basis for collecting 
information on capabilities available. Interested parties are responsible for adequately 
marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained in their response. It is 
the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor SAM.gov for additional information 
pertaining to this RFI.  
 
1.3 The information provided may be used by the Army in developing its acquisition strategy 
or developing system Performance Specification.  The applicable North American Industry 
Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541511 with a Small Business Size 
Standard of 1250 employees. 
 
2. Background 
The expected operational mission of PM C2 Apps is to deliver and continuously update the 
foundational platform that enables rapid, secure, and continuous software delivery for the 
Army's Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) ecosystem. While navigating the 
requirements below, the initial set of features will focus on establishing an end-to-end "thin 
thread" of capability: a basic Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipeline for 
onboarding software applications and a rudimentary storefront interface to display it. This 
established the foundation for PM C2 Apps to support their primary mission to provide 
warfighting function applications.  
 
 
 

3. Responses 
3.1 Responses: Interested parties are asked to respond to this RFI with the enclosed 
Attachment 1 – Response Form.  The Attachment 1 Response Form shall be submitted as one 
(1) document in Microsoft Word for Office 2000 compatible format. Respondents are asked to 
use the template “Attachment 1 Response Form” to identify their solution(s) that could 
answer the requests and inquiries in section 3.3, , 3.41 (table 1), and section 3.4.2.  The 
Government will not consider inserted textboxes/pop-ups or internet links to additional 
information as part of the response.  Responses shall be limited to no more than twenty-five 
(25) pages using 11-point font for the entire submission (including company information,

Respondents are permitted to replace the cover page in the template with their own but it 
must be one (1) page and shall only include what is outlined in Section 3.2 and 3.3.   
Responses are due NLT 27 MAY 2026, 1200, Eastern Time (ET) and must be submitted via e-

3.2 Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. To 
aid the Government, please segregate proprietary information. Please be advised that all 
submissions become Government property and will not be returned. In addition to

Agency: 			Department of Commerce (DOC)

Office: 			National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)

Location: 			Office of Satellite and Product Operations (OSPO)

Notice Type: 			Special Notice - Notice of Intent to Sole Source

This notice is not a Request for Quote, Request for Proposal, or an Invitation for Bid. The intent of this synopsis is to provide notice of a proposed contract action. 

This is a notice of intent to issue a firm, fixed price commercial purchase order to SpaceNav, LLC, located at 2601 Spruce St., Suite A, Boulder, Colorado 80302 under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 518210 “Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services” with a small business size Standard of $40,000,000.00.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS), Office of Satellite and Product Operations (OSPO) Mission Operations Division (MOD) has a requirement for membership to the Space Data Association with a period of performance of July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. The place of performance for this requirement is NOAA Satellite Operations Facility (NSOF) located in Suitland, MD. 

SpaceNav, LLC, is currently the sole industry provider for Web-based Space Situational Awareness set of conjunction assessment tools and services (WSSA), for conjunction analysis of Low-Earth Orbiting (LEO) spacecraft events, analysis visualization, risk assessment probabilities of events based on positional uncertainties, and design of collision-avoidance maneuvers. There are no authorized resellers at this time.  

A sole source justification was prepared in accordance with RFO 12.201-1. The statutory authority permitting this sole source acquisition is 41 U.S.C. 1901. A determination by the Government not to conduct a competitive acquisition based on potential submissions to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Any documentation submitted in response to this notice is strictly voluntary. Therefore, the Government: 1) will not pay for any documentation submitted in response to this notice; and 2) will not award a contract solely based on documentation submitted in response to this notice.

This capability is particularly valuable for the USMC, which operates installations 
in diverse locations with varying cost structures nationwide.   
RSMeans Data Online Complete is best suited for those who need highly detailed, 
industry-standard construction cost data for commercial or public projects, though 
it often requires additional software for takeoffs, scheduling, and project 
management, increasing total operating costs. In contrast, Buildxact provides a 
more affordable all-in-one solution for residential builders and remodelers by 
combining estimating, takeoffs, quoting, scheduling, and accounting integrations 
into a single platform. While RSMeans offers greater depth and benchmarking 
accuracy, Buildxact is generally more cost-effective and easier to implement for 
small to mid-sized construction businesses focused on operational efficiency and 
faster project workflows. RSMeans enables more accurate initial cost estimates, 
reducing the likelihood of project modifications and change orders that often 
result in significant cost increases and schedule delays.  The system's defensible 
methodology also strengthens the Corps' position during contract negotiations and 
provides auditable documentation for cost decisions.  These capabilities directly 
support the Marine Corps' responsibility to Congress and the American taxpayer 
for efficient use of appropriated funds.

The implementation of this product requires minimal training and can be 
integrated into existing Marine Corps project management workflows.  The 
system's standardized approach ensures consistency across different installations 
and project teams, reducing variability in cost estimation quality.  This 
standardization is particularly valuable for the Marine Corps, which frequently 
rotates personnel between installations and requires consistent processes and 
procedures. 
 
RSMeans is already in use at multiple USMC installations under separate 
contracting orders.  One additional advantage resulting from this procurement 
request is to bring all MCICOM licensing for RSMeans under a single MCICOM 
contracting order, while also ensuring that all individuals who should benefit by 
the use of RSMeans, are able to do so.  
RSMeans Online Complete Plus as a cost estimation tool, the Marine Corps faces 
significant risks including unreliable cost estimates, inconsistent pricing 
approaches across installations, increased vulnerability to contractor pricing 
manipulation, and reduced ability to justify budget requests to higher 
headquarters.  These risks directly impact the Corps' ability to maintain and 
improve infrastructure necessary for mission accomplishment.
RSMeans Online Complete Plus is only available from the Original Equipment 
Manufacturer (OEM), or there is only one authorized distributor or technical 
representative for the OEM. RSMeans Company LLC, was acquired by The 
Gordian Group in 2014, and is the Sole Source and distributor for RSMeans 
Online Complete Plus. The Gordian Group provided sole source letters to support 
their ownership of RSMeans.

PURPOSE: 
The purpose of this requirement is to establish a new contract for continued support of McIDAS-
X (Man computer Interactive Data Access System) existing software licenses, quantity 54, and 
support in use on systems within the National Weather Service 
 
SCOPE OR MISSION: 
McIDAS-X software is used to support NCEP Center’s satellite data processing requirements in 
order to meet their forecast mission and support the National Weather Service's mission to 
protect life and property. 
 
BACKGROUND: 
McIDAS- X is the Space Science and Engineering Center’s (SSEC) sophisticated package used 
for visualization and manipulation of geophysical data in a wide variety of formats. Typical data 
types include geostationary and polar orbiting meteorological satellites, NEXRAD radar, surface 
and upper-air observations, gridded numerical forecasts, NOAAPORT text products, and data 
from special observing networks.  McIDAS-X software is the only system that provides timely 
display and analysis of meteorological data. McIDAS-X also contains a historical database of 
meteorological parameters unavailable from any other source.   
 
TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS:  
• Software Support Level: Next business day 
• License support for more than six (6) units. Purchasing 54 licenses 
• Support for McIDAS-X Software running on Windows-based OS computers. 
• Support for McIDAS-X Software running on Linux-based OS computers.

Performance Work Statement

Insider Threat User Activity Monitoring (UAM) Tool

1.0 Background:

The Secretary of War (SecWar) approved an Operations Security (OPSEC) Campaign directing the Department of War Chief Information Officer (DoW CIO), in conjunction with the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (USW I&S) and the DoD General Counsel to establish a User Activity Monitoring (UAM) pilot.  The goal of the activity is to understand the extent of unauthorized disclosures and exfiltration of sensitive/classified information using DoW networks. The UAM tool comprises the continuous and full-time observation and logging of unclassified computer activity by DoW personnel.  Services and Agencies are required to participate and independently resource the DoW designated tool set outlined in the “ENHANCED MONITORING PILOT AT THE PENTAGON RESERVATION CONCEPT OF OPERATIONS (CONOPS), NOV 2020.”

As part of the Marine Corps Insider Threat Program, there is a user monitoring capability and system auditing capability requirement to support UAM on the Marine Corps Enterprise Networks (MCEN) the Non-classified Internet Protocol (IP) Router Network (NIPRNet). The UAM information compiled from these sources, integrated with information from various other sources (e.g., human resources, law enforcement, and counterintelligence) supports analysis and response to counter insider threats on the MCEN.

The Marine Corps Insider Threat Program’s UAM is partially fielded. The platform includes the following capabilities: 

User Activity Monitoring (UAM)

Behavioral Analytics Platform (User Behavior)

Case Management System

Objectives:

The Contractor shall field, operate, and sustain a comprehensive Insider Threat Monitoring System. The overarching system comprises the following component platforms at varying stages of operational readiness:

User Activity Monitoring: 
The UAM solution must be maintained to actively maintain compliance and continue to identify, analyze, and prioritize potential insider threats. Maintain all capability necessary to capture user keystrokes, full content from applications (e.g., email, chat), user screen activity, and tracking file movements (file shadowing) across the enterprise network. All data collected must be linked to a specific user.

Behavioral Analytics Platform: 

Deploy and sustain (maintain) a fully functional Behavioral Analytics Platform. The foundations of the Behavioral Analytics Platform have been constructed; however, the system is not currently functional and is behind in obtaining its Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG). The STIG is currently in remediation due to numerous unresolved findings. Resolution is required to bring the system to MCEN standards, so it is compliant with DoD security mandates. 

Case Management System:

The Case Management System requires software maintenance to ensure compliance with DoW security mandates. Additionally, the system requires customization and enhancements to meet Government needs. 

Scope:

The scope of this effort encompasses the fielding, enhancement, and full lifecycle technical support of a Protection Level 4 (PL4) commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) Insider Threat Monitoring system. This integrated system comprises a User Activity Monitoring (UAM) solution, a Behavioral Analytics platform, a Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW), and a Case Management System in support of the United States Marine Corps (USMC) Insider Threat Program (InTP). The Contractor shall provision all necessary hardware, software, application support, and Cybersecurity/Risk Management Framework (RMF) services required to deploy and sustain these capabilities across the Marine Corps Enterprise Network (MCEN) on the Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet). Technical implementation boundaries include continuous 24x7x365 monitoring of up to 200,000 endpoints and support for up to [Insert Number] administrative users.

Exclusions: This scope is strictly limited to the technical deployment, infrastructure sustainment, and secure operation of the UAM and analytic systems. It does not include the operational analysis of the collected data, the execution of insider threat investigations, or law enforcement actions.

Tasks:

General System Support (all platforms):

The Contractor shall implement a continuous vulnerability management program for all systems supporting InTP. Upon notification or discovery of vulnerability (via automated scans, vendor alerts, STIG\SRG checks or government notification), the Contractor shall apply patches, updates, or approved mitigation strategies within the following strict timeframes:

The Contractor shall provide comprehensive cybersecurity services to execute and manage the Risk Management Framework (RMF) process for all Insider Threat Program (InTP) systems. The Contractor shall ensure full compliance with Department of War (DoW), United States Marine Corps (USMC), and National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) security controls. 

The Contractor shall facilitate the system through the complete RMF lifecycle, specifically performing all requirements for the six phases: Categorize, Select, Implement, Assess, Authorize, and Monitor.

The Contractor shall develop, update, and maintain the complete Assessment and Authorization (A&A) package. This includes, but is not limited to, the System Security Plan (SSP), Security Assessment Plan (SAP), Security Assessment Report (SAR), and the Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M).

The Contractor shall maintain and manage all system data, artifacts, and compliance status within the des ignited DoW tool of record (e.g., Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service (eMASS)). 

The Contractor shall act as the primary technical liaison during independent assessments, providing the Security Control Assessor (SCA) Representative with all necessary system access, compliance evidence, and technical responses required to successfully evaluate all managed platforms.

The Contractor will implement and validate Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and Security Requirements Guides (SRGs) for all operating systems, applications, and network devices. 

The Contractor shall review and analyze security vulnerability scans (e.g., Assured Compliance Assessment Solution (ACAS) / Nessus) across all managed systems. The Contractor shall prioritize remediation efforts based on risk severity and formally document all identified false positives or required risk acceptance/waiver requests with comprehensive technical justifications.

Execute a continuous monitoring strategy to ensure the security posture is maintained throughout the system lifecycle, including annual control assessments and incident response reporting.

The Contractor shall ensure all system infrastructure (ESXi, servers, databases, collectors, switches, NGFW) maintains a 99.9% operational uptime during core mission hours.  

The Contractor will provide monthly updates to the Marine Corps eMASS system record to include artifacts, diagrams and supporting documents.

The Contractor shall deliver a Monthly Status Report (MSR) detailing a summary of accomplishments achieved during the reporting period, alongside the status of all open, unresolved, and pending issues. Additionally, the report shall include a labor utilization summary, specifying the labor hours expended to date and the remaining balance of allocated labor hours for the current Period of Performance (PoP).

The Contractor shall develop and deliver formal, role-based training to designated personnel to ensure operational proficiency across all implemented systems. This training shall be continuously updated to reflect the current operational configuration and software baselines of the mission environment. The scope of training shall encompass all hardware and software components, specifically including the User Activity Monitoring (UAM) solution, Behavioral Analytics platform, and the Case Management System.

 

The Contractor shall create, maintain, and deliver comprehensive user manuals encompassing all platforms, ensuring the documentation provides detailed operational guidance for end-users.

User Activity Monitoring (O&M):

 

The contractor shall Maintain the UAM solution to actively ensure compliance and continuously identify, analyze, and prioritize potential insider threats on a 24x7x365 basis across the MCEN (NIPRNet).

The contractor shall Sustain the technical capability to accurately capture user keystrokes, full application content (e.g., email, chat), user screen activity, and file movements (file shadowing).

The contractor shall Ensure all collected data remains reliably linked to specific users across the enterprise network, supporting up to 200,000 endpoint clients.

The contractor shall provide engineering, system administration, and technical support necessary to maintain the UAM infrastructure. The scope encompasses:

UAM servers, ESXI virtual nodes and endpoint Agent health monitoring and deployment.

Backend server O&M, database management, and storage optimization. UAM rules set configuration, tuning, and policy management in coordination with cyber analysts.

The contractor shall ensure UAM backend infrastructure (servers, databases, collectors) maintains a 99.9% operational uptime during core mission hours.  Monitor and remediate UAM endpoint agents. Ensure 95% or greater of active network endpoints are successfully reporting data to the UAM servers.

The contractor shall implement approved changes to UAM detection policies, triggers, and alerts to reduce false positives and enhance threat detection capabilities.

The contractor shall respond to system outages or data flow disruptions. Acknowledge critical outages within 30 minutes and restore service within 4 hours.

Behavioral Analytics Platform (User Behavior): 

The contractor shall provide data science, cyber analytics, and threat hunting expertise to manage and optimize the User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) environment. The scope includes:

 Integrating data feeds (e.g., UAM endpoint data, SIEM logs, network    	traffic).

Configuring and tuning Machine Learning (ML) models and behavioral 	baselines.

 Triaging anomalous alerts and escalating credible threats.

 Minimizing false positives through continuous threshold adjustments.

The contractor shall configure behavioral models to establish accurate "normal" baselines for users and peer groups. Adjust risk scoring algorithms to accurately reflect Marine Corps InTP mission priorities.

The contractor shall actively monitor UEBA dashboards for high-risk behavioral anomalies (e.g., unusual data exfiltration, lateral movement, or abnormal access times).

The contractor shall analyze alert data to identify systemic false positives and tune detection logic without compromising true positive detection capabilities.

The contractor shall configure the system to evaluate interactions between people, data, devices, and applications. Enable discovery risk scoring, prioritization, and real-time ad hoc analysis functions.

Upon successful deployment, the contractor shall transition the platform to steady-state sustainment, ensuring continuous vulnerability scanning, patching, and STIG compliance.

Case Management System: 

The contractor shall install and baseline configuration of the software stack. Development of automated data pipelines and API integrations.  Creation and tuning of operational workflows (e.g., Alert-to-Case automation).   Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and dashboard customization.

The contractor shall develop, test, and integrate the following system enhancements:

                                                     	  (a.) A customized role-based user interface (define)

           	  (b.) Workflow functions (define)

            		  (c.) Reporting capabilities and Robotic Process Automation (RPA) (define)

    (d.) Incorporate data visualization tools (e.g., entity association charts) (define)

The contractor shall maintain and enhance the document management capabilities to compile threat indicator data. Ensure the system meets all National Insider Threat Task Force (NITTF) and NARA recording and retention requirements.

The contractor shall Sustain centralized repository functions, document linking, and strict document security/audit trails to support up to 150 maximum administrative/analyst users.

Hardware:

NGFW:

(a.)  The Contractor shall design, deploy, configure, and maintain NGFW infrastructure across designated Marine Corps InTP network enclaves, ensuring robust perimeter security, deep packet inspection, and compliance with all Marine Corps, DoD/DoW security mandates.

(b.) The Contractor shall provide dedicated lifecycle support for the NGFW infrastructure, ensuring perimeter defense integrity, traffic visibility, and continuous compliance with Marine Corps, DoW cybersecurity mandates.

The contractor shall maintain all associated components of the monitoring tool. This support includes maintenance (e.g. screening for vulnerabilities, patching, updating, installation of licenses, configuration management, etc.) for all associated infrastructure and services, such as servers, network switches, software applications, storage systems (SAN), firewalls, cybersecurity functions, and all activities required to complete the full Risk Management Framework (RMF) assessment and authorization process. All work shall ensure secure, reliable, and compliant IT operations that meet Federal, DoD, and Marine Corps requirements.

Configure Unity XT storage processors, drive shelves, and back end connectivity.

Create storage pools, RAID groups, and LUNs based on mission requirements.

Manage and maintain storage Unity XT components to include hard drives, controllers and supporting hardware. 

The contractor shall install, configure, managed and support Cisco switches supporting InTP systems.

Implementation of Port Security and 802.1X (Identity Services Engine/ISE integration). Firmware management and IOS/IOS-XE security patching. Request for Information (RFI)
Office of Policy, Planning and Resources for Public Diplomacy
Digital Analytics for Countering Foreign Adversarial Propaganda

1. Introduction
The Office of Policy, Planning, and Resources for Public Diplomacy (R/PPR) is seeking information from qualified technology and data access providers regarding solutions for analyzing foreign adversarial propaganda from state and non-state actors. The Department is interested in solutions that enhance our ability to access relevant open-source data, identify adversarial propaganda influence networks, conduct digital media forensics including deep fake detection, assess linkages between activity across the information environment and real world behavior, while ensuring compliance with all applicable statutes and regulations. Must be FedRamp compliant. 

2. Purpose
This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this RFI will assist the Department in understanding available technologies, industry capabilities, and best practices for implementing an open-source digital analytics solution that meets the Department’s needs.

3. Desired Capabilities
Respondents are requested to provide information on solutions that address the following requirements:

 Data Access to Digital and Social Media Sources

Ability to access and analyze global digital and social media data sources to identify adversarial propaganda narratives and promulgators.

Ability to query digital and social media data sources in near-real time with built-in language translation services. 

Ability to visualize and track narratives across foreign information environments. 

Ability to customize and curate data sources per client requirements. 

Ability to train new users and troubleshoot issues, as needed. 

Digital and Social Media Data Analytics

Integrated quantitative and qualitative analytics tools within the data access platform, to include digital network analysis, narrative propagation networks, AI-enabled forensic image analysis, deep fake detection, and synthetic media detection. 

Capability to conduct link analysis between digital domains and real-world events to assess relationships and impacts between domains. 

Ability to create tailored monitoring dashboards to track specific narratives, hashtags, accounts, or online networks.  

Ability to customize and develop new analytic tools per client requirements. 

E. User Experience and Support

Intuitive, user-friendly interface for client.

Availability of training materials and user support during and after implementation.

System availability and technical support in line with industry best practices.

Staff/support account flexibility

4. Response Instructions
Interested parties are requested to submit a written response that includes the following:

A brief overview of the company and relevant experience with social and digital media access and analytic solutions.

A description of the proposed solution and how it meets the desired capabilities outlined above.

Details on implementation approach, training, and support services.

Case studies or references from similar projects, if available.

Estimated timelines for implementation or access.

Any additional information, recommendations, or innovative features that may benefit the Department.

5. Submission Details
Respondents must submit their answers in the forms link here:

https://forms.cloud.microsoft/g/JP9C02BTYd

6. Disclaimer
This RFI is for informational purposes only and does not obligate the Department to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Department will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response to this RFI.

The US Naval War College (NWC) requires a subscription to Kpler MarineTraffic maritime domain awareness 
and vessel-tracking services, including access for approximately 1–10 user licenses that will be shared across 
the NWC research community and relevant analytical stakeholders. The subscription will provide access to real-
time and historical AIS vessel tracking data, voyage reconstruction tools, geospatial analytics, port-call 
monitoring, and maritime intelligence functions required to support research, teaching, and operational analysis 
related to global naval and commercial maritime activity. 
 
Period of Performance: Base Year 5/30/2026-5/29/2027

In conclusion, the requested supplies or services represent the minimum requirements of the government. 
 
Describe in detail why only this source(s) can furnish the requirements to the exclusion of other sources.  
KPLER Marine Traffic is the only commercial vendor that enables users to obtain five years of track history on 
vessels of interest. Kpler MarineTraffic would provide CMSI, and NWC, with a powerful, enterprise-grade 
maritime intelligence capability that significantly enhances the institute’s ability to monitor, analyze, and assess 
global naval and commercial shipping activity in near real time. By integrating terrestrial, satellite, and roaming 
AIS data, Kpler tracks hundreds of thousands of vessels globally with very low latency and extensive historical 
archives, allowing researchers to reconstruct deployments, identify operational patterns, monitor port activity, 
and analyze long-term maritime trends. Beyond basic ship tracking, the platform links vessel movements to 
ownership data, cargo flows, sanctions risk, and predictive analytics, enabling deeper insight into Chinese 
maritime operations, logistics networks, overseas presence, and gray-zone activities. The system’s historical 
AIS playback, custom alerts, voyage-event detection, and API integration capabilities would directly support 
CMSI’s research mission by improving the rigor, speed, and evidentiary basis of maritime analysis products for

the addition of KPLER MarineTraffic annual subscription to CMSI and NWC.

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The mission of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Electronic Health Record 
Modernization Integration Office (EHRM-IO) is to transform how the VA delivers 
health care by implementing an enterprise-wide electronic health record (EHR) to 
standardize care across facilities, strengthen interoperability and collaboration with 
federal and community partners, foster innovation, improve provider and Veteran 
experiences, and ensure the continued delivery of high-quality, safe, and efficient 
health care to our nation’s Veterans. EHRM-IO is in the process of migrating VA’s 
170 Medical Centers (VAMCs) from the Veterans Information Systems and 
Technology Architecture (VistA) to the Oracle Health (OH) Millenium EHR.  
Many of these VAMCs operate a blood bank and/or perform transfusion services 
and will be using the Oracle Health Pathnet Blood Bank system after go-live. 
Validation Services are required by regulatory and accreditation organizations (VA, 
Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Association of Advancement of Blood and 
Biotherapies (AABB), Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) and 
The Joint Commission (TJC)) to ensure patient and blood products 
safety. Compliance with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Regulations 
requires that these environments are validated prior to go-live. 
The VA schedule for go-lives has 24 go-live events between September 2027 and 
November 2031. Each go-live event has between two (2) and 14 sites which will 
require validation to be completed simultaneously. There are 109 blood bank sites 
which require validation prior to go-live. 
EHRM-IO seeks a contractor to provide blood bank validation services at each site 
with Full Blood Bank/Transfusion Medicine Services and those with transfusion 
only services to validate the build and configuration of the system, both for the local 
site build and enterprise review of all orderables, interpretation patterns, blood 
products, instrumentation connectivity and patient product compatibility. 
Development of the contractor management plan shall begin at award. Site 
validation services are expected to start no later than four months prior to site go-
live, last up to 12 weeks per site and be completed no later than one month prior to 
the Go-Live deployment date. 
The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 541519 
“Other Computer Related Services”; the Product Service Code (PSC) IS Q301 
“Reference – Laboratory Testing Services”.

INTRODUCTION AND BACKGROUND

The Appeals Centralized Database System (ACDS) within the Compliance Domains is a critical tool used by Appeals Officers, Settlement Officers, managers, and technical analysts to track case receipts, record case time, document case actions and monitor the progress of the Appeals workload. It contains sensitive information, including Taxpayer identifier information, case status and case action items. It also contains Appeals staffing information, including demographic and experience summaries, time sheets and employee reviews. This system is part of Appeals Automated Environment (AAE), and its functionality is not available from any other system. It includes eCase which allows ACDS to electronically receive and store case data from the database of partner organizations. It also includes the Docket Information Management System (DIMS) which provides an automated listing of docketed cases. It also includes a Business Intelligence reporting subsystem component. ACDS Valuation is used by the Appraisers and the manager of the valuation section to track case receipts, record case time, document case actions and monitor the progress of the Appeals workload. It contains sensitive information, including Taxpayer identifier information, case status and case action items. It also contains Appeals staffing information, including demographic and experience summaries, time sheets and employee reviews.

Currently, the ACDS, particularly its ColdFusion-based application layer, is facing technological obsolescence risks. It is not compatible with the latest server technologies, posing a significant risk of being quarantined by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and/or Cybersecurity protocols. There is an urgent need for modernization to ensure the system's security, efficiency, and functionality. 

The IRS seeks contract support from a vendor with expertise in ColdFusion to provide comprehensive support and implementation services. The aim is to improve operational efficiency, refine customer engagement processes, and ensure system scalability and adaptability for future business needs.

The candidates must possess advanced proficiency in ColdFusion programming and have substantial experience with MS SQL Server and the Windows operating system. Their responsibilities will include ColdFusion development, system and database administration, assisting in the transition to MS SQL Server, and upgrading to Windows Server 2022. The objective is to successfully migrate from ColdFusion 2016 to ColdFusion 2023, transition from Windows Server 2012 R2 to Windows Server 2022, and address any issues arising during this process.

OBJECTIVES

This Request For Information (RFI) seeks information from vendors with a proven track record in ColdFusion development, system and database administration, particularly with MS SQL Server and Windows OS. The project will require expert-level skills in ColdFusion, along with strong competencies in MS SQL Server and Windows OS.  The Contractor shall provide qualified personnel, technical expertise, and management oversight necessary to successfully execute the modernization, migration, integration, operations, maintenance, and sustainment requirements identified in this PWS.  The primary objectives of this RFI are to:

Update and Migrate ACDS Application: The Contractor shall migrate the ACDS application from Adobe ColdFusion 2016 to Adobe ColdFusion 2023 to ensure continued compatibility with current enterprise server technologies, supported software platforms, and IRS technical standards.

Server Upgrade: The Contractor shall upgrade and transition the existing server infrastructure from Microsoft Windows Server 2012 R2 to Microsoft Windows Server 2022 to improve system security, stability, maintainability, and overall operational performance.

Ensure System Integrity and Security: The Contractor shall identify, remediate, and mitigate system vulnerabilities and security deficiencies to maintain compliance with DHS, IRS, and Federal cybersecurity requirements and to safeguard sensitive taxpayer and operational data contained within ACDS.

Troubleshoot and Resolve Issues: The Contractor shall resolve operational incidents, defects, and migration-related issues within Government-approved service level timelines to minimize disruption to Appeals operations.

Operational Efficiency and Cost Reduction: The Contractor shall implement solutions that improve operational efficiency and reduce Operations and Maintenance (O&M) costs by simplifying the existing technical environment, supporting the retirement of legacy technologies, and consolidating disparate programming languages, frameworks, and system components into a standardized and maintainable architecture.

Framework Standardization and Modernization: The Contractor shall support the IRS modernization strategy by implementing standardized frameworks, enterprise cloud capabilities, and agile development best practices, including the use of modern software development methodologies, tools, and automated deployment processes.

Streamlining O&M: The Contractor shall streamline O&M activities through the implementation of automation, system integration, and enhanced case management capabilities designed to improve reliability, reduce manual intervention, accelerate deployment and update activities, and increase overall operational efficiency.

SCOPE OF WORK AND DESCRIPTION OF TASKS

This Performance Work Statement details a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract aimed at delivering mission-oriented outcomes with performance measures and incentives to ensure project success within the Compliance Domain. It includes contractor support for project management, migration to modern development frameworks, implementation of ColdFusion solutions, and comprehensive technical integration services. The goal is to enhance operational efficiency, ensure seamless integration of new technologies with existing systems, and adopt agile methodologies for responsive and flexible project execution. The contractor shall be responsible for providing comprehensive ColdFusion contracting support, encompassing:

ColdFusion Development: 

The Contractor shall modernize, optimize, test, and maintain the ACDS application environment to ensure compatibility with ColdFusion 2023, improve maintainability, and support secure operational performance.

IOLA OIC:

The Contractor shall support the development, integration, enhancement, testing, deployment, and maintenance of the IRA Individual Online Account – Offer in Compromise (IRA IOLA–OIC) Submission Tool capability (WR 978065). The Contractor shall implement functionality that enables taxpayers to electronically submit Offers in Compromise through the Individual Online Account platform, including the capability to upload and attach supporting documentation, submit payments, and view Offer and payment status information.

The Contractor shall design, develop, and maintain the required interfaces and system integrations between the IRA IOLA–OIC Submission Tool and the Automated Offer in Compromise (AOIC) internal application to ensure secure, accurate, and timely transmission of taxpayer data, supporting documentation, and payment information in accordance with IRS security, privacy, and system integration standards.

System and Database Administration: 

The Contractor shall provide system and database administration support required to facilitate the migration of the ACDS environment to Microsoft Windows Server 2022 and SQL Server platforms, including system configuration, installation, testing, deployment, performance tuning, and operational support. The Contractor shall ensure data integrity, system reliability, security compliance, and optimal application and database performance throughout all migration, transition, and post-implementation activities.

Technical Support and Troubleshooting: 

The Contractor shall provide continuous technical support throughout all migration and transition activities, including the identification, troubleshooting, and resolution of system, application, and infrastructure issues, to maintain system stability, operational functionality, and uninterrupted support for business operations.

Tasks include, but are not limited to:

Collaborating with existing system owners to define requirements.

Analyzing systems for content and functionality.

Developing and transitioning functionalities to the ColdFusion development platform.

Testing and validating solutions to meet project requirements.

Providing development services for retiring individual systems as the ColdFusion platform matures.

Conducting Operations and Maintenance for developed solutions.

Contractor support is also required for technical integration services to manage the coordination and integration activities of IT projects affecting multiple IT domains or delivery partners for successful delivery.

Sub-Task 3.1.1, Orientation Briefing   

Within one week of the task order award, the Contractor will conduct an orientation briefing for the Government. The Government does not desire an elaborate orientation briefing, nor does it expect the Contractor to expend significant resources in preparation for this briefing. Rather, the intent of the briefing is to initiate the communication process between the Government and Contractor by introducing key task order participants, explaining their roles, reviewing communication ground rules, and assuring a common understanding of award requirements and objectives.  

The orientation briefing will be held at the Government’s facility or virtually and both parties will mutually agree upon the date and time.

Any issues concerning the Contractor clearances for Contractor personnel will be discussed.

The Contractor shall demonstrate confirmation of their understanding of the work to be accomplished under this PWS.

The Contractor shall provide the accounting period end dates to be used for the term of this award.

Sub-Task 3.1.2, Ramp-Up Knowledge Transfer

Ramp-Up Knowledge Transfer is defined as the Contractor acquiring and understanding the necessary documentation, information, and processes related to any work in progress. Military Cemeteries (ANMC) and the Office of Army Cemeteries (OAC).  The OCIO CEAS is 
responsible for support for the following areas, project management, change management and 
governance, and Enterprise Architecture (EA) and OCIO strategic planning support.  This is not 
a software development contract. 
 
1.1  Description of Services/Introduction:  The Contractor shall provide all personnel, 
equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and 
non-personnel services necessary to perform the tasks as defined in this PWS except, for those 
items specified as government furnished property and services.  Contractor shall perform to the 
standards defined in this contract. 
 
1.2  Background: The Office of Army Cemeteries (OAC) is defined by Public Law as the 
statutory authority to manage and oversee operations at Arlington National Cemetery, the United 
States Soldiers’ and Airmen’s Home National Cemetery.  The Department of the Army created a 
special staff Principal, the Executive Director for Army Cemeteries and a policy oversight 
directorate and compliance for all Army cemeteries, both post cemeteries and national 
cemeteries.  In accordance with this law, this PWS outlines the contractor responsibilities in 
providing program management support, defining and establishing business processes, 
developing, implementing and sustaining plans for operations and maintenance for ANMC/OAC 
business systems which contain Department of War Cemetery data.  Additionally, the contractor 
shall provide enterprise architecture support in accordance with the DOW Architecture 
Framework.  Based on the special significance and the attention that national and post cemeteries 
receive, strict adherences to these specifications are essential. 
 
1.3  Objectives: The objective of this effort is to provide program management support across the 
evolving Cemetery Management suite of cloud applications.  The basic services in this PWS 
shall enable the Project Management Office to manage the development and operations of IT 
based systems to conduct cemetery operations and oversee the Change Control Board (CCB) and 
Enterprise Architecture Governance Board (EAGB).  These services shall be leveraged to align 
IT investments with ANMC/OAC strategic goals and objectives outlined in the ANMC Goals 
and Objectives and OAC Strategic Plan. 
 
1.4  Scope: The Contractor shall provide specialized professional expertise and program 
management support to implement the goals of the Government and OCIO operations and 
management.  The Government intends to acquire contract support to all activities outlined in 
this Performance Work Statement in support of the Army’s current and future goals and 

 
 2 
objectives for program level planning, operations and maintenance, and migrations.  The scope 
and project shall contain tasks and milestones to allow for efficient planning and budgeting for 
IT solutions. Scope will include inter-agency coordination with external cemetery stakeholders to 
include but not limited to Depmant of War Mortuaty and Casulaity Affairs, American Battle 
Monuments Commission (ABMC) and National Cemetery Administration (NCA) Veterans 
Affairs (VA).  
 
1.5 Period of Performance:  The period of performance shall be a base twelve (12) months with  
three (3) twelve (12) month options from date of award.  Option periods may be exercised in 
accordance with FAR Clause 52.217-9 entitled, “Option to Extend the Term of the Contract”. 
The period of performance reads as follows: 
 
Base Year:   19 Novmeber 2026 – 18 November 2027    
Option Year I:  19 Novmeber 2027 – 18 November 2028   
Option Year II: 19 Novmeber 2028 – 18 November 2029 
Option Year III:  19 Novmeber 2029 – 18 November 2030   
 
1.6  General Information 
1.6.1  Quality Control: Quality control is the responsibility of the contractor.  The contractor is 
responsible for the delivery of quality services/supplies to the government (see FAR 52.246-1, 
Contractor Inspection Requirements). 
The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain an effective quality control system that 
includes a written quality control plan (QCP).  The QCP shall implement standardized 
procedure/methodology for monitoring and documenting contract performance to ensure all 
contract requirements are met.  The contractors’ QCP must contain a systematic approach to 
monitor operations to ensure acceptable services/products are provided to the government.   The 
QCP, as a minimum, shall address continuous process improvement; procedures for scheduling, 
conducting and documentation of inspection; discrepancy identification and correction; 
corrective action procedures to include procedures for addressing government discovered non-
conformances; procedures for root cause analysis to identify the root cause and root cause 
corrective action to prevent re-occurrence of discrepancies; procedures for trend analysis; and 
procedures for collecting and addressing customer feedback/complaints.  The contractor shall 
upon request provide to the government its quality control documentation The Contractor shall 
deliver the QCP within thirty (30) days after contract award.  QCP must address test plan 
development, release coordination with ANMC and its stakeholders, and code promotion 
documentation. After acceptance of the quality control plan the contractor shall receive the 
contracting officer’s acceptance in writing of any proposed change to its QC system.   
 
1.6.2  Quality Assurance:  The Government shall evaluate the contractor’s performance under 
this contract in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP).  This plan is 
primarily focused on what the Government must do to ensure that the contractor has performed 
in accordance with the performance standards.  It defines how the performance standards will be 
applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum acceptable defect rate(s). 
 
 
 
 

 
 3 
1.6.3  Federal Government Holidays: ANMC and OAC observe the following Federal holidays: 
 
            New Year’s Day   1st day of January 
 Martin Luther King Jr. Day   3rd Monday of January 
 Presidents Day   3rd Monday of February 
 Memorial Day    Last Monday of May 
 Juneteenth Day   19th day of June 
 Independence Day    4th day of July 
 Labor Day    1st Monday of September 
 Columbus Day   2nd Monday of October 
 Veterans Day    11th day of November 
 Thanksgiving Day   4th Thursday of November 
 Christmas Day               25th day of December 
 
1.6.4  Hours of Operation: The Contractor is responsible for conducting business to best align 
with ANMC’s operating hours between 0600-1800 Eastern Standard Time, Monday through 
Friday, except federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national 
emergencies, administrative closings, occupational safety or health hazards, or similar 
Government directed facility closings.  The Contractor shall maintain an adequate work force at 
all times for the uninterrupted performance of the tasks defined within this PWS when the 
Government facility is not closed for these reasons.  When hiring personnel, the Contractor shall 
keep in mind the stability and continuity of the workforce are essential. 
 
1.6.5  Place of Performance:  The primary place of performance shall be Arlington National 
Cemetery and Contractor facility. 
 
1.6.6  Type of Contract:  The Government anticipates award of a firm fixed price contract. 
 
1.6.7  Security Requirements: This is an Unclassified contract.  There are no requirements for 
Contractor personnel to have route access to classified Government information in the 
performance of this contract; however, Contractors with elevated privileges shall be required to 
have/maintain a SECRET clearance in order to access any environment(s) connecting or crossing 
Army or DOW Information systems.  If Contractor personnel are required to attend meetings, 
briefings or work on a full time basis on site at a secure Government facilities, a valid, current 
final SECRET eligibility and access must be granted and posted in the Joint Personnel 
Adjudication System (JPAS) to gain access. 
 
1.6.7.1  P hysical Security:  The contractor shall be responsible for safeguarding all government 
equipment, information and property provided for contractor use. At the close of each work period, 
government facilities, equipment, and materials shall be secured. 
1.6.7.2  Key, Key Code.  All references to keys include key cards or fobs (and also  implies any 
other government issued means of access to allow the contractor to enter any ANMC secured area 
or facility. AN MC shall issue key cards/codes to the Contractor (and subcontractor). The 
Contractor shall be responsible for keys and key codes provided by the Government.  Keys shall 
not be lost, misplaced, or duplicated by Contractor personnel, nor used by unauthorized Contractor 
personnel. The Contractor shall develop and implement procedures to ensure that keys issued to 

 
 4 
the Contractor by the Government are safeguarded. The Contractor developed procedures covering 
key control shall be included in the Quality Control Plan. Such procedures shall include turn-in of 
any issued keys by personnel who no longer require access to locked areas.  
The Contractor shall prohibit the use of Government issued keys/key cards by any persons other 
than the Contractor’s employees. The Contractor shall prohibit the opening of locked areas by 
Contractor employees to permit entrance of persons other than Contr actor employees engaged in 
the performance of assigned work in those areas, or personnel authorized entrance by the 
Contracting Officer. 
The Contractor shall report any occurrence of duplicated, misplaced, or lost keys to the Contracting 
Officer and COR within twenty-four (24) hours after discovery of occurrence and submit a written 
report to the Contracting Officer by close of business the  next workday. The written report shall 
provide complete details relating to duplication, misplacement, and/or loss. 
1.6.7.2.1. In the event keys, other than master keys, are lost or duplicated, the c ontractor shall, 
upon direction of the contracting officer, re-key or replace the affected lock or locks; however, the 
government, at its option, may replace the affected lock or locks or perform re-keying.  When the 
replacement of locks or re -keying is performed by the government, the total cost of re -keying or 
the replacement of the lock or locks shall be deducted from the monthly payment due the 
contractor.  In the event a master key is lost or duplicated, all locks and keys for that system shall 
be replaced by the government and the total cost deducted from the monthly payment due the 
contractor. 
 
1.6.7.2.2. The contractor shall prohibit the use of government issued keys/key cards by any 
persons other than the contractor’s employees.  The contractor shall prohibit the opening of 
locked areas by contractor employees to permit entrance of persons other than contractor 
employees engaged in the performance of assigned work in those areas, or personnel authorized 
entrance by the contracting officer. 
 
1.6.7.3 Lock Combinations  The contractor shall establish and implement methods of ensuring that 
all lock combinations are not revealed to unauthorized persons.  The c ontractor shall ensure that 
lock combinations are changed when personnel having access to the combinations no longer have 
a need to know such combinations.  These procedures shall be included in the Contractor’s Quality 
Control Plan. 
 
1.6.8 Federal Facility Access, General Protection, Security Policies and Procedures. Contractor 
personnel (including subcontractors’ employees) entering government properties shall abide by 
the applicable installation, facility and area commander’s access and local policies and 
procedures.  The contractor shall provide required information for background checks to meet 
installation access requirements.  Contractor workforce shall also comply with all personal 
identity verification requirements as directed by DOW, HQDA, and/or local policy.  In addition 
to the changes clause otherwise authorized by this contract, should the Force Protection 
Condition Level (FPCON) or Health Protection Condition Level (HPCON) at any individual 
facility or installation change, the government may require changes in contractor security matters 
or processes.  Contractor employees, including sub-contractors, shall immediately report 
suspicious activity to the ANMC G2/3 - Directorate of Security and Operations at 703-614-4303 

 
 5 
during business hours, and 703-588-2800 during after-hours. Emergencies should be reported 
immediately by calling 911. 
 
ANMC/OAC Contractor personnel will be issued vehicle passes (hangtag/placards) that must be 
displayed when entering the Cemetery (regardless of whether the vehicle is privately or company 
owned, or as designated by ANMC G2/3 - Directorate of Security and Operations. The 
contractor shall maintain a current list of all vehicles and individuals issued such passes. The 
contractor shall provide a list of these vehicles to include make, model, color and associated 
license plate information to the COR within five (5) days of contract award and within one (1) 
day of any changes to the list through contract period of performance.   Additionally, contractors 
shall park in designated parking locations, as directed by ANMC, and if required, access/key 
cards shall be issued to Key Personnel to enter secured parking areas (see Section 1.6.7.2 Key 
and Key Control). 
 
1.6.9 Visit Notification.  Contractors visiting ANC shall provide 24 hour notice for all site-visits, 
provide vehicle information, and proper contractor identification may be required. Contractor 
employees whose duties require on site work at ANMC or OAC will be issued a photo ID badge 
and must be presented or visible to ANMC/OAC staff. 
 
1.6.10   Key Personnel and Special Qualifications:  The Government considers the Senior Project 
Manager (PM), Senior Management Analyst, and Enterprise Architect as Key Personnel.  Key 
Personnel identified in the proposal shall be identified in the proposal including resumes.  
Projected replacement of Key Personnel shall be submitted to the COR and KO for approval 
prior to a replacement.  All Key Personnel shall have means of verbal and email communication

CUI 
CUI 
 
 
 
 
 
STATEMENT OF WORK 
FOR 
VIRTUAL SUITE UPGRADE  
AT 
MOODY AFB, GEORGIA 
16 APRIL 2026 

 
 
CUI 
CUI 
1. SCOPE 
Transition from a standard host replacement to multi-site high-availability architecture. The 
project focuses on deploying a vSAN storage layer using two (2) new Cisco UCS-C220 M8S 
servers distributed across two separate buildings to provide failover targets for existing 
workloads currently running on two (2) legacy Cisco UCS-C220 M6 servers. The contractor 
hereby agrees to configure all required Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) to the 
system, provide on-the-job training, document final configurations, and adhere to the standards in 
this statement of work (SOW). 
 
1.1 PROJECT UNDERSTANDING AND ASSUMPTIONS 
 a. Site Distribution: One (1) M6 and one (1) M8S server will be located in each of the two 
designated buildings. 
 b. vSAN Architecture: The M8S servers will be configured as a vSAN cluster to provide a 
resilient storage tier. 
 c. Failover Logic: VMware High Availability (HA) and vMotion will be configured to allow M6 
workloads to failover to the M8S vSAN tier in the event of hardware or building-level failure. 
 d. Network Requirements: The site must provide low latency 10Gb/25Gb connectivity between 
buildings to support vSAN synchronization and vMotion traffic. 
 e. Classification: The assigned technician maintains an active Secret Classification. 
 
1.2 OBJECTIVES 
a. Multi-Site Planning & Network Prep 
1. Review inter-building latency and MTU settings for vSAN/vMotion compliance. 
2. Finalize IP schema for vSAN VMkernel interfaces. 
b. Core vSAN Deployment & Configuration 
1. Configure CIMC and install VMware ESXi on both M8S hosts. 
2. Enable and configure the vSAN cluster, including disk claiming for cache and capacity 
tiers. 
3. Integrate both M8S vSAN nodes and both legacy M6 nodes into a unified vCenter 
management instance. 
c. Resiliency Setup & Testing 
1. Establish VM-Host affinity rules to keep primary workloads on M6 hardware during 
normal operations. 

 
 
CUI 
CUI 
2. Configure HA failover priorities to ensure the M8S vSAN tier is the designated recovery 
target. 
3. Conduct "Building Isolation" and "Host Failure" testing to verify seamless VM recovery. 
4. Configure all required Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs).  
5. Document final configurations and provide documentation to 23 Comm Squadron (23 CS)  
d. On Job Training 
1. Provide on the job training to 23 CS Networking Airmen throughout the installation.  
2. Provide conclusive post-installation training on troubleshooting and maintenance.  
1.3 DELIVERABLES 
Provide test and measurement data for all work accomplished during installation. Contractor 
will submit reports electronically to the 23 CS within five (5) calendar days of work 
completion. Reports shall be available in an electronic format that is Microsoft Word, 
Microsoft Excel or Adobe PDF compatible. 
2. BUILDING & SITE ACCESS: 
The Contractor will provide, in advance, a well-coordinated schedule to 23 CS Network 
Admin (23CS/SCOO) and 23 CS Plans & Programs (23CS/SCXP) to ensure ready access 
to all sites and buildings necessary to complete all required inspection work. Any 
customer keys issued to the Contractor shall be returned to the customer upon 
completion of the installation. 
3. SCHEDULING. 
Scheduling of all work shall be coordinated and approved by 23CS/SCOO at 229-257-9798 
prior to the start of any work. 
4. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE. 
Period of performance TBD. 
 
5. WORKING CONDITIONS. 
The Contractor shall take all necessary and prudent safety precautions to ensure the safety of the 
workforce and other exposed personnel as per Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA) and 
state regulations. 
6. OPERATIONAL SECURITY (OPSEC) 
Any network infrastructure drawing(s) (locations, fiber paths, etc.) developed or provided to the 
contractor are items on the 23 CS Critical Information List and must be protected. 

 
 
CUI 
CUI 
The Contractor shall take appropriate measures to protect detailed information pertaining to the 
installation effort, to include appropriate marking of documents as “Controlled Unclassified 
Information (CUI),” and ensuring limited distribution of documents and schematics/drawings to 
only those individuals with a valid need to know. 
7. PERSONNEL QUALIFICATIONS 
Site POC, and respective alternate(s) shall be able to read, write, speak, and understand English. 
Assigned technicians must maintain an active Secret Classification through the duration of the project. 
The contractor shall be responsible for employing technically qualified personnel to perform the 
work specified in this statement of work. The contractor shall maintain the personnel, organization, 
and administrative control necessary to ensure that the work delivered meets the contract 
specifications and requirements. 
The work history of each Contractor employee must contain experience directly related to the 
task and functions he/she is intended to perform under this contract. 
Personnel assigned to or utilized by the Contractor in performance of work shall be fully capable 
of performing the contemplated functions of this SOW in an efficient, reliable, and professional 
manner. 
8. UTILITIES. 
All reasonable amounts of electricity for the completion of this project will be furnished to the 
Contractor without charge from existing Government facilities where feasible. 
9. SAFETY. 
The Contractor shall observe all Safety, Security, Traffic and Fire regulations presently enforced 
at Moody Air Force Base. Contractors shall comply with the OSHA (OSHA, Public Law 
91-596) and the resulting standards, OSHA Standards 29 CFR 1910 and 1926. The detailed 
provisions of the act for accident prevention are directly applicable to all Contractor operations. 
Prime Contractors are also responsible for ensuring any sub-contractors also adhere to OSHA 
Guidance. OSHA compliance officers can visit Contractor worksites on the installation. 
Contractors are responsible for ensuring all industrial safety provisions for this type of work are 
followed: 
1. Contractors shall report all accidents involving Air Force people, property, or equipment 
damage, and any contractor personnel injured in the performance of the Air Force 
contract to the Contracting Officer. 
2. The contractor shall comply with the corrective action determined by the Contracting 
Officer if any violations of the safety regulations occurs. 
10. INSTALLATION 
All material and parts furnished by the contractor for this job shall be new and unused material 
of high quality. All work shall be done in a neat and workmanlike manner, in keeping with 

 
 
CUI 
CUI 
generally accepted standards for similar work as well as conform to the Headquarters Air 
Combat Command and equipment manufacturer specifications, and follow standard installation 
practices as determined in Air Force Instructions, American National Standards Institute, 
Technical Institute of America, Energy Information Administration standards, Institute of 
Electrical and Electronics Engineers standards, electric codes, local/national codes, and 
standard industry practices. 
All newly installed equipment shall be properly grounded to existing grounding points. 
Grounding hardware shall be installed with properly sized cabling and terminated with corrosion 
resistant hardware. 
The contractor shall be responsible for preventing any unscheduled outages (i.e. cutting or 
disabling any in-service cables or equipment). Contractor-caused interruptions of 
communications capabilities must be corrected by the contractor. The contractor shall 
coordinate planned outages with the 23 CS/SCOO at least 24 hours in advance of the outage if 
the implementation necessitates disruption of services. 
The contractor shall perform testing and inspections of all systems to ensure the technical 
adequacy and accuracy of all work, including reports and other documents required in support of 
that work. The contractor shall conduct on-site testing IAW Original Equipment Manufacturer’s 
installation manuals, practices, and the appropriate vendor’s test procedures.  
JOBSITE MAINTENANCE AND STORAGE AREAS. 
The contractor shall maintain the jobsite and staging areas in conformance with the 
following standards: 
1. Lay down/staging areas shall be always kept neat and free of loose debris. 
2. Cleaning: The contractor shall maintain the premises, including any staging area or 
storage areas, free from accumulations of waste, debris, and rubbish caused by the 
contractor's work and shall minimize the spread of dust and flying particles. At the 
end of each workday, the site shall be cleared and all waste material shall be properly 
disposed of. 
3. Any temporary storage trailers or containers shall present a neat and clean appearance 
and shall be in a state of good repair. 
4. Work areas shall be secured to prevent unauthorized access. 
11. ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION. 
Contractor personnel shall always perform all work and take such steps required to prevent any 
interference or disturbances to the ecological balance of the environment. All work must be 
performed in accordance with applicable Federal, State, Local, and Air Force environmental 
regulations. Use good management practices to protect air, water, land and wildlife and to 
prevent noise, solid waste, radiant energy, dust and radioactive pollutants. In the event of a 
chemical or hazardous material spill, the contractor must immediately notify the Moody Fire 
Department at 911 (identify that you are located on Moody AFB). 

 
 
CUI 
CUI 
12. WASTE MATERIALS. 
Unless otherwise specified, all waste materials shall be disposed of at an approved off-base 
location in accordance with all applicable Federal, State, County and Municipal laws. 
Contractor is responsible for procedures in collecting and storing C&D waste on project sites, 
including designating locations for waste containers, sorting or separating methods, handling and 
transporting of wastes, special handling requirements, and scheduling for waste and recycling 
collection. 
13. HAZARDOUS MATERIALS. 
If hazardous materials will be used in the execution of this contract, the contractor will be 
required to provide a list of materials, quantities, and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) to the 
Contracting Officer before work begins. 
14. PERFORMANCE. 
Place of Performance: Moody AFB Buildings 454 (Network Control Center & SCOO Shop), 
803, and locations deemed absolutely necessary for installation.  
Normal Hours of Operation. The Contractor shall perform the services required under this 
contract during normal duty hours, 8:00 am - 5:00 pm, Monday – Friday. Any other work 
scheduled outside of normal duty hours requires Contracting Officer approval. 
System downtime. No downtime is expected with the expected work to be accomplished. In the 
event the contractor shall require systems to be interrupted: the contractor shall coordinate with 23 
CS/SCOO staff and the Contracting Officer for approval. 
Holidays. The Contractor shall not perform under this contract on federal holidays or site-unique 
down-days unless expressly coordinated through 23 CS and is authorized by the Contracting 
Officer. 
15. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS. 
Base Access contractor must provide the names, DOB, DL number, State of Issue, and expiration 
date to 23 CS/SCXP 14 days prior to arrival on site, 23 CS/SCXP has 14 days following receipt 
of required information to complete the base access request to Security Forces. 
The contractor shall have or obtain a U.S. security clearance at the minimum level of “Secret” for 
all contractor personnel required to perform maintenance, engineering, or installation services on 
equipment that processes classified information. Onsite contractor personnel should have an 
active clearance prior to reporting for duty. Such clearance must be obtained through the Defense 
Investigative Services. Access to classified areas will be required; escorts will be 

 
 
CUI 
CUI 
required, as work will be performed in secure facilities. It is the Government’s responsibility to 
provide escorts. 
Prior to the start of the project the contractor shall provide personnel listing and contract 
information to 23 CONS prior to commencing work, and update information on a continual basis, 
as personnel changes occur to ensure it is always current and correct throughout the life of the 
contract. The following information will be required: 
Length of time for the contract and/or duration that the employee will be performing work 
Full name of Contractor employees assigned to work this project and their employment status 
(Full-time/Part-Time/Temporary) of employee with the Contractor. 
The last six digits of the Social Security number for each employee assigned to work this project. 
The above information will immediately be updated by the contractor as changes occur during 
the duration of this contract and provided to the 23 CONS Officer. 
Base Pass and Identification Items: The contractor shall coordinate with the 23 CONS officer to 
ensure the following pass and identification items required for the contract performance period 
are obtained for employees and their use of non-government owned vehicles: 
For vehicle operators: 
• Current driver license for each employee in support of work on MAFB 
• Vehicle Registration and Proof of Insurance 
For non-vehicle operators: 
• Employee identification: Current driver license, official ID card, or passport 
Traffic Laws: All contractor employees shall comply with all federal, state, local and base traffic 
regulations while on MAFB properties. 
Contractor Employees: The contractor shall ensure employees have a current and valid driver’s 
license and commercial permits/licenses for the type of vehicle operated, before allowing the 
employee to operate a contractor-owned or rental vehicle on Moody AFB. The contractor shall 
not employ persons for work on this contract if such employee is identified by the government as 
a potential threat to the health, safety, security, general well-being or operational mission of the 
installation and its population, nor shall the contractor or subcontractor employ persons under 
this contract who have an outstanding criminal warrant as identified by Law Enforcement 
Agency Data System (LEADS) through the National Crime Information Center. LEADS checks 
will verify if a person is wanted by local, state, and/or federal agencies. All contractor and 
subcontractor personnel must consent to LEADS background checks. Contractor and 
subcontractor personnel who do not consent to a LEADS check will be denied access to the 
installation. Information required to conduct a LEADS check includes: full name, driver’s 
license number, and/or social security number, date of birth of the person entering the 
installation, and completion

Statement of Work (SOW)
 For: VMware Cloud Foundation Software Licensing
1. Background
The 87th Communications Squadron (87th CS) requires enterprise-grade virtualization software to
support its infrastructure. The 87th CS is procuring VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) licensing to
sustain and modernize its virtual environment, ensuring continued mission readiness and
operational efficiency.
2. Objective
The objective of this procurement is to acquire the necessary VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF)
software licenses and external ordering fees to support the squadron's virtual environment. This is
strictly a software and licensing procurement; no hardware installation, site readiness validation, or
physical decommissioning services are required.
3. Scope of Work
The scope of this contract is limited to the procurement of software licenses and standard
manufacturer support. The Contractor shall provide the exact software part numbers and quantities
specified in the Software Bill of Materials (BOM) below.
4. Specific Requirements
4.1 Required Software Bill of Materials
The Contractor shall procure the following software licenses for the Base Year, with optional
additional licensing for Option Years 1 through 4:
Part Number
Description
Quantity
VCF-CLD-FND-A
VMware Cloud Foundation (Annual Subscription)
256
EXT-ORDER-FEE
External Ordering Fee
1
4.2 Period of Performance
The periods of performance for the software subscriptions are as follows:
 Base Year: 02/01/2026 – 08/05/2026
 Option Year 1: 08/06/2026 – 08/05/2027
 Option Year 2: 08/06/2027 – 08/05/2028
 Option Year 3: 08/06/2028 – 08/05/2029
 Option Year 4: 08/06/2029 – 08/05/2030


5. Software Subscription and Support
This procurement includes a standard manufacturer's software subscription. This subscription shall
provide the 87th CS with access to all software updates, security patches, and remote technical
support provided by the vendor for the duration of the active license term. No on-site parts or labor
are required.
6. Deliverables
The primary deliverable for this requirement is the provisioning of the software licenses. The
Contractor shall provide the license keys and/or proof of entitlement to the designated
Government Point of Contact (POC) electronically upon award.
Kaitlin Diaz
87th CS, Plans and Programs
