Statement of Work 
Customizable Communication Platform 
VA Northern California Health Care System 
 
The VA Northern California Health Care System is soliciting quotes for communication boards 
throughout the respective Station’s medical centers and Community Based Outpatient Clinics. 
The general scope of this project is to remove existing equipment, where applicable, at the 
VANCHCS, install a patient communication system with state-of-the-art electronic components 
(i.e. electronic digital sign), and provide services to include message management software, 
installation to customer’s computers, support, maintenance, and training customer on software.  
Product/Solution must be Brand Name or Equal To Choisys Technology/PatientPoint 
Solution  
This project consists of installation, servicing, and maintenance of a patient communication 
system throughout the medical center located at the Mather VAMC campus of the VA Northern 
California Health Care System. It also encompasses the CBOCs located throughout Northern 
California and the East Bay. The requirement is for 60 screens total distributed throughout the 
health care system in high traffic areas. 
- VANCHCS Main (Mather) Campus – 10535 Hospital Way, Mather, CA 95655 
- Martinez VA Medical Center – 150 Muir Rd., Martinez, CA 94553 
- Chico VA Clinic – 1601 Concord Ave., Chico, CA 95928 
- Fairfield VA Clinic – 103 Bodin Circle, Bldg. 778, Travis AFB, CA 94535 
- Mare Island VA Clinic – 201 Walnut Ave., Bldg. 201, Mare Island, CA 94592 
- McClellan VA Clinic – 5342 Dudley Blvd., Bldg. 88, McClellan Park, CA 95652  
- Redding VA Clinic – 3455 Knighton Rd., Redding, CA 96002 
- Louis A. Conter VA Clinic – 11985 Heritage Oaks Place, Suite 100, Auburn, CA 95603 
- Yreka VA Clinic – 101 East Oberlin Rd., Yreka, CA 96097 
- Yuba City VA Clinic – 425 Plumas Blvd., Yuba City, CA 95991 
- Richard A. Pittman VA Clinic – 7777 South Freedom Rd., French Camp, CA 95231 
- Sonora VA Clinic – 13663 Mono Way, Sonora, CA 95370 
- Modesto VA Clinic – 1225 Oakdale Rd. Modesto, CA 95355  
The Digital Screen Program will deliver educational information to patients within the lobby, 
hallway and waiting room environments. This Program will be a flexible, engaging 
communication system for VANCHCS’ high-traffic locations, which will reinforce critical safety 
information, drive service-line growth and provide a wide array of VA content. The Program will 
offer a customizable, engaging communication platform with innovative digital and mobile 
technology which will help provide a uniquely integrated experience in its waiting room areas. 

36C26126Q0611 
Page 5 of 61 
 
Salient Characteristics:  
• The leased Systems must include electronic digital signs with a single face screen size of 50 
to 65 inches with a screen resolution of 1920 x 1080.  
• The leased Systems must be able to feature the VA’s brand name and colors.  
• The leased Systems must be able to Inform visitors of key hospital locations and policies. • 
The leased Systems must be able to promote service lines and market upcoming events.  
• The leased Systems must be able to promote healthy lifestyles and disease management, 
educate viewers on key patient safety and satisfaction initiatives (e.g. The Joint Commission, 
CMS, CDC), and reinforce Patient Guide messaging with a library of 250-300 health information 
segments.  
• The leased Systems must be able to support a minimum of 30 minutes of video content 
running through a loop. Audio should be optional.  
• The leased Systems must contain software that offers pre-loaded fonts, animations, videos, 
and range of creative tools that develop custom graphics.  
• The leased Systems must have the ability to upload video clips, stories, and other screen-
ready content.  
• The least Systems will not display ads or any content not approved by the VANCHCS Office 
of Public Affairs.  
• The leased Systems must be able to display customizable content by each screen (i.e. 
content on CBOC screen could be different than facility screens) or the same content, if 
necessary.  
• The leased Systems will provide leasing warranty for the products as is industry standard for 
scope and duration. 
 • The Vendor must provide a dedicated customer service representative who will be able to 
update the screens with the content the VA provides within 12 hours. In addition, the Vendor 
must provide the VA the ability to manage and upload content during normal and urgent 
conditions.  
• The Vendor will be responsible to troubleshoot and repair any issues with the system within 3 
business days but at a maximum of 5 business days.  
• The Vendor will need to have a connection to the screens and be responsible to notify the 
station if a screen is malfunctioning.  
• The Vendor will be responsible to professionally install each screen (see Schedule Delivery 
and Install below). In addition, the Vendor must be able to move and re-install screens to a new 
location a maximum of 10 times per year per Station (inclusive of all screens) due to the 

36C26126Q0611 
Page 6 of 61 
anticipation of construction projects during the contract duration at no additional cost to the 
Government.  
• The Vendor will need to provide stand-alone Wi-Fi service or equivalent cellular service to 
connect with the equipment as the vendor will NOT have the ability to reliably connect to the 
VANCHCS network system. 
 • The Vendor must provide periodic training to operate electronic digital sign messaging and 
graphics features.  
• The Vendor must provide an educational library of content to display on the screen

NCIA Request for Information (RFI)

NCIA Request for Information (RFI) 
 
To: Industry Partners 
 
  
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is conducting market 
research to identify qualified vendors and gather input on potential solutions to support 
the upcoming acquisition for an Integrated Event Operations (IEO) Platform. To that 
end, we are issuing the attached Request for Information (RFI) RFI-07127-IEO to solicit 
feedback from capable and interested industry partners. 
 
2. This RFI is issued for planning purposes only and is not a request for bids . It is part of 
NCIA’s effort to ensure it has a clear understanding of the marketplace, available 
capabilities, and potential acquisition strategies. 
 
3. We value your insight and invite you to: 
a. Share relevant corporate capabilities and experience; 
b. Review and comment on our draft requirements (Annexes A and B) with a view in 
providing recommendations for improving performance outcomes, competition, and 
efficiency; and i dentifying any risks or concerns that should be considered during 
planning. 
 
4. Submission instructions and additional details can be found in the enclosure to this 
RFI. 
 
5. Only companies from a NATO member country can participate in or respond to this 
RFI (https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/nato_countries.htm). 
 
6. Should you have any questions or need clarification, please contact Sven 
Schumacher, Senior Contracting Officer at RFI-07127-IEO@ncia.nato.int . 
 
7. We thank you in advance for your time and input, and we look forward to engaging 
with you as we shape this potential acquisition. 
 
 
 
 
For the Chief of Acquisition:

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION  
 
A. Introduction 
 
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is conducting market 
research to identify potential sources and gather information regarding industry 
capabilities to support an Integrated Event Operations (IEO) Platform to support 
the end- to-end event lifecycle for NATO Education, Training, Exercises and 
Evaluation (ETEE) activities (e.g., create, plan, coordinate, approve, publish, 
execute and close events), and to provide for data exchange with other relevant 
services and applications . This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for 
informational purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), 
Request for Quotation (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB).  
 
B. Purpose 
 
1. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain input from industry to help inform the NCIA’s 
acquisition planning. Responses to this RFI will assist in refining requirements, 
identifying capabilities, and shaping the strategy for any future solicitation. 
2. NCI Agency is primarily interested in solutions that support two core capability 
areas:  
a) event registration / participant management workflows;  
b) event-related resource management (e.g., rooms/venues, IT resources, 
catering, accommodation, transportation), including 
request/approval/allocation tracking and change handling. 
3. In addition, NCIA seeks industry input on:  
a) realistic integration/toolset approaches where a single COTS product does not 
cover all capability areas;  
b) on-premises and multi-network deployment constraints;  
c) cybersecurity maturity/security-by-design evidence;  
d) support models, service delivery maturity, and user experience/usability; 
e) the supplier’s ability to operate under an underpinning support contract where 
NCIA remains accountable for service delivery to the user community (i.e., 
supplier maturity, support governance, and responsiveness); 
f) Rough Order of Magnitude ( ROM) costs (licensing, implementation, 
integration, O&M). 
 
C. Background 
1. The IEO Platform is expected to support use by multiple entities/communities, and be 
adaptable/configurable to different processes across those entities. 
2. The IEO Platform shall support the end-to-end event lifecycle for NATO ETEE 
activities (create, plan, coordinate, approve, publish, execute and close events). 
3. In addition to registration/participant management and resource management, the 
solution shall support event-adjacent processes such as Real-Life Support (RLS) 
planning/coordination and IT provisioning, either natively or via integration. 
4. The solution must be deployable and operable on-premises within NATO secured 
networks (Software-as-a-Service (SaaS)-only solutions are not acceptable), and it 

 
 
 
  
 Page 6 
 
 
must support controlled data exchange with other applications (e.g., IT Service 
Management (ITSM) systems) using standard integration mechanisms (e.g., APIs). 
5. Detailed capability and evidence requests are provided in Annex A (structured 
tables) and Annex B (draft requirements). 
 
D. Submission Instructions 
 
1. Interested parties are invited to respond in accordance with the instructions below: 
 
a. Submit responses via the email address in section H no later than 12:00 hours 
Central European Time (CET) on 29 May 2026. 
 
b. Responses should be submitted in PDF or Word format and must not exceed 15 
pages, including: 
i. Responses to Annex A and comments on Annex B
 
excluding: 
i. Cover page 
ii. Company brochures or product literature (if included) 
iii. Attachments such as past performance references 
 
c. Use the following subject line for submission 
i. “Response to RFI-07127-IEO – [Company Name]” 
 
d. All responses should address the items listed in Annex A – Requested 
Information. 
 
e. Respondents are also encouraged to review and comment on the draft 
requirements in Annex B – Draft Requirements. 
 
E. Industry Engagement 
 
1. Technical discussions and/or demonstrations may take place following the 
submission of responses, with the purpose of clarifying or further augmenting those 
responses where required. Respondents are requested to await further instructions 
after their submi ssions and are requested not to contact any NCI Agency staff 
directly other than the POC identified at paragraph H. 
 
F. Disclaimer 
 
1. This RFI is for planning and informational purposes only and shall not be construed 
as a solicitation or obligation on the part of the NCIA. The NCIA does not intend to 
award a contract based on responses to this RFI. Respondents are solely 
responsible for all costs incurred in responding to this RFI. The NCIA will consider 
and analyse all information received from this RFI and may use these findings to 
develop a future solicitation. The NCIA will consider all responses as confidential 
commercial information and will protect it as such. 
 
2. NCIA reserves the right, at any time, to cancel this informal market survey, partially 
or in its entirety. No legal liability on the part of NCIA for payment of any sort shall 
arise and in no event will a cause of action lie with any prospective participant for 
the recovery of any costs incurred in connection with the preparation of 
documentation or participation in response hereto. All effort initiated or undertaken 

 
 
 
  
 Page 7 
 
 
by prospective informal market survey participants shall be done considering and 
accepting this fact. 
 
G. Use of Information Provided through Responses 
 
1. Confidentiality of Responses 
 
The NCIA may incorporate industry comments and responses, in part or in whole, into 
a future release of a solicitation.  Should respondents include proprietary data in their 
responses that they do not wish to be disclosed to the public for any purpose, or used 
by NCIA (except for internal evaluation purposes), they must: 
 
a. Mark the title page with the following legend:  
This document includes data that shall not be disclosed outside NATO and shall 
not be duplicated, used, or disclosed – in whole or in part – for any purpose other 
than for NCI A internal evaluation purposes, unless otherwise expressly 
authorised by [insert company name]. This restriction does not limit the NCI A’s 
right to use information contained in this data without restriction if it is obtained 
from another source.  The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets 
[insert numbers or other identification of sheets]

B.2 STATEMENT OF WORK

Objective

The objective is to procure a 12-month subscription, with four (4) option years to an online, evidence-based clinical decision support resource for VISN20 Medical Centers to use for patient care.

Technical Requirements:

The Contractor shall provide an online subscription with the following capabilities:

V20 requires online access to a product that shall provide, via one interface and one search platform, access to comprehensive databases. Databases shall provide drug information, dosing and therapeutic tools, and drug identification relevant to VISN20 staff to assist them in providing safe and effective care to Veterans. This includes:

Comprehensive Medication Monographs (including but not limited to)

Information regarding FDA and non-FDA indications

Summaries of clinically relevant primary literature within the resource (more than just a reference to the source)

Side by side comparative drug evaluations and comparative efficacy evaluations

Adverse drug reactions

References to abstracts, tertiary electronic resources, and/or full text articles

Pharmaceutical Product Identification·

IV Compatibility Tools

Toxicology/Poison Control Management

Patient Education Materials

Drug Interaction Tools

Medication Dosage and Laboratory Calculators

Medication Safety Data Sheets

Teratogenic Medications Database

Ability to Search Across all Databases contained within the Resource with One Search Term

Tasks

For the above list, the contractor shall provide the following:

License rights for 24/7 desktop web access for VISN20 in:

Alaska VA Healthcare System and Regional Office (Anchorage, AK)

Boise VA Medical Center (Boise, ID)

Portland VA Medical Center (Portland, OR)

Roseburg Healthcare System (Roseburg, OR)

VA Puget Sound Healthcare System (Seattle and American Lake, WA)

Mann-Grandstaff VA Medical Center (Spokane, WA)

Jonathan M. Wainwright Memorial VA Medical Center (Walla Walla, WA)

VA Southern Oregon Rehabilitation Center & Clinics (White City, OR)

Customer service shall be available to troubleshoot website and connectivity issues via phone or email.

Costumers require a single access interface to search across multiple resources. This type of simultaneous searching reduces the need for multiple searches and saves the agency researchers time and the cost of purchasing multiple print subscriptions through various contractors. 

Deliverable

The Contractor shall provide:

Static URL, password information {if necessary), product training, technical support numbers, account number, promotional materials, monthly usage statistics.

The contractor shall have the ability to provide usage statistics on a quarterly basis. The format of the usage statistics is provided either via email or contractor provided login and should include session count, search count and total document retrievals per title.

Contractor shall provide online tutorials. Contractor shall also provide on-site training, briefings and updates to VISN20.

If a plug-in, additional software or recommended software is required for optimal use, please include specific requirements. Contractor will address any questions or problems encountered when using this product with supported software or hardware.

Salient Characteristics – Clinical Rx Database Online Subscription

Product quoted must meet these characteristics: 

VISN20 requires online access to a product that shall provide, via one interface and one search platform, access to comprehensive databases. Databases shall provide drug information, dosing and therapeutic tools, and drug identification relevant to VISN20 staff to assist them in providing safe and effective care to Veterans. 

This includes:

Comprehensive medication monographs (including but not limited to)

Information regarding FDA and non-FDA indications

Must have summaries of clinically relevant primary literature within the resources (more than just a reference to the source)

Grade and strength of evidence ratings

Side by side comparative drug evaluations with primary literature summaries to allow time effective comparison of more than one agent with one search. This feature assists VA providers in formulary management and is essential for optimal medication use, safety and cost effectiveness.

Must have comparative efficacy and place in therapy evaluations to allow VA clinicians to have immediate access to high quality, in-depth drug information. Detailed and referenced comparative efficacy evaluations are also essential for formulary management.

Most comprehensive information available about drug use in special populations including renal impairment, hepatic impairment, geriatrics, dialysis, obesity, and other relevant disease states that will vary by drug (e.g. for phenytoin, relevant disease states include hypoalbuminemia, trauma and critical illness).

Adverse drug reaction information

Risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) information

References to abstracts, tertiary electronic sources, and/or full text articles

Ability to search across all databases contained within the resource with one search term.

 Detailed drug consults providing detailed answers to clinical questions including comprehensive primary literature evaluation.

Alternative medicine database

Pharmaceutical product identification including capability of searching by imprint, description, or slang term.

Comprehensive IV compatibility tool

Toxicology/Poison control management database including:

Substance exposure specific treatment information on providing life support, monitoring, managing oral exposure and enhancing elimination.

Comprehensive evidence based, current data reviewed and evaluated by clinical experts.

Patient education materials in at least English and Spanish Drug interaction tool.

Capability of entering multiple drugs and allergies for a given patient.

Output from entry of one list of drugs shall include detailed drug-drug, drug­ allergy, drug-ethanol, drug-lab, drug-food, drug-tobacco, drug-pregnancy, and drug-lactation.

Interaction information shall include severity, assessment of level of documentation, summary, detailed literature discussion and references, and management recommendations.

Medication dosage, clinical, and laboratory calculators including easy to find antidote dosing calculators and monograms.

Material Data Safety Sheets.

Teratogenic Medications Database.

Access to most comprehensive information from multiple databases devoted to teratogen information.

Access to this information is highly valued be VISN20 Women's Health providers and supports VA Strategic Health Initiative for Women.

Web based mobile access available for commonly used device such as iPhone®, iPad®, DROID®, and Blackberry®.

Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. This is a request for information and does not obligate the Government in any way, nor does it commit the Government to any specific course of action. Product information, brochures, part numbers, and/or other description information may be included with the submission.  

Requirements:

The Office of Information & Technology (OIT) serves the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as a Veteran-centric provider of secure and cost-effective technology services. OIT collaborates with its business partners to create the best experience for all Veterans by endeavoring to provide seamless and unified Veteran experience via state-of-the-art information technology (IT) solutions and service delivery. Within OIT, End User Services (EUS) provides enterprise-level infrastructure engineering, system implementation, production operations, and IT service management. EUS is responsible for the design, testing, deployment, and sustainment of platforms and supporting infrastructure. EUS is OIT’s main service line with more than 3,500 IT professionals across the United States and its territories comprising of two main divisions, End User Operations (EUO) and Enterprise Command Operations (ECO). 

Currently, VA is experiencing massive growth, in large part as a response to the Sergeant First Class Heath Robinson Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics (PACT) Act of 2022 and anticipates significant expansion of its customer base over the next several years. To support this increased need for its services, OIT needs to scale its mission to modernize and standardize information technology services and support across the VA enterprise. To effectively scale and sustain its mission in alignment with the growing demands of the VA enterprise, EUO must enhance and formalize its Information Technology Asset Management (ITAM) capabilities. ITAM is a critical function that ensures the accountability, lifecycle management, and strategic utilization of VA’s vast inventory of endpoint devices and IT infrastructure.

In response to the increasing volume and complexity of assets—driven by expanded service delivery under the PACT Act and ongoing modernization efforts—EUO is in the initial stages of building a centralized ITAM program that will serve as the authoritative ITAM office for the entire Department of Veterans Affairs. This foundational effort requires dedicated program management support to establish governance structures, standardize processes, coordinate activities across geographically dispersed teams, and ensure compliance with federal regulations and VA policies. Program management support will be instrumental in shaping the program’s strategic direction, driving operational efficiency, and enabling enterprise-wide visibility and control over IT assets, ultimately contributing to a more resilient and responsive IT environment for VA staff and Veterans.

The period of performance is comprised of a 12-month base period, two 12-month options periods. The option periods are required for continued support services. 

VA seeks to identify competitive IT support services and strategies that could be implemented to assist EUS in achieving its mission of serving Veterans and the public by delivering effective technical and programmatic support to the EUO ITAM program.   

VA desires identification of enterprise proven alternate products that have been demonstrated to operate at a similar level of size, scope, and complexity of the current VA environment.

Questions per Key Functional Area:

Describe your organization’s experience supporting large‑scale, enterprise IT Asset Management (ITAM) programs, particularly within federal agencies.

What experience do you have implementing or supporting ITAM programs aligned with CMMI Level 3 practices?

Provide examples of past performance delivering program management, strategic planning, governance, and policy development in a federal environment. Specifically, for an ITAM Program.

What tools and methodologies do you use to manage scope, schedule, cost, quality, and risk for complex IT programs?

Describe your experience conducting ITAM process optimization, including workflow analysis, Lean Six Sigma, or value stream mapping.

What methods do you use to assess and improve asset lifecycle processes (e.g., asset sprawl, underutilization, data quality)?

Provide examples of developing strategic roadmaps for Hardware Asset Management (HAM) and Software Asset Management (SAM).

Describe your experience evaluating or implementing advanced ITAM technologies, such as AI‑driven discovery, predictive analytics, or digital twins.

 What tools or platforms does your organization typically use for enterprise asset discovery, inventory accuracy, and compliance reporting?

 Describe your experience developing governance frameworks, RACIs, and policy documentation aligned to federal laws such as FITARA, FISMA, and NIST standards.

 How does your organization support audit readiness and compliance with federal cybersecurity and privacy requirements?

THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE AND NOT A REQUEST FOR 
QUOTATION OR PROPOSAL.  
The U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC), Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), located 
in Washington, D.C., intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis and award a one-year base contract 
to PRIMETRICA INC., 1 Thomas Circle, Washington, DC 200005-5824.  
This acquisition i s being conducted under the authority of permitting other than full and open 
competition, implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302 -1 “only one 
responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements”. 
The National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) is the Executive 
Branch agency responsible for advising the President on telecommunications and information 
policy issues. NTIA’s programs and policymaking efforts focus on expanding broadband Internet 
access and adoption across the United States, promoting efficient and effective use of spectrum by 
all users, and ensuring that the Internet continues to serve as an engine for innovation and economic 
growth. 
 
TeleGeography provides global telecommunications data and research, including information on 
telecommunications infrastructure, broadband markets, submarine cables, network pricing, and 
traffic patterns. The Office of Policy and International Affairs (OPIA ) supports a range of 
initiatives, including data center policy, submarine cable policy, and Team Telecom activities. 
Access to TeleGeography’s Data Center Research Service, Transport Networks Research Service, 
and IP Transit Database, and integration of these resources into OPIA’s workflow, would provide 
staff with verified, up -to-date information that enhances the quality of reports, analysis, policy 
development, and policy refinement produced by the office. 
 
This notice is NOT a solicitation for quotations, quotation abstracts, a request for 
competitive quotations; however, all responses received within 1 5 days from the date of 
publication of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. Responses must clearly and 
thoroughly defend any claims or assertions that attempt to refute the Government’s claim. A 
determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses to 
this notice is solely with the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be 
considered for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive  procurement. 
Information received on this notice must eliminate the Government's concerns and address how 
the items can be provided without jeopardizing the on-going projects. If no affirmative responses 
are received within 15 days of this notice to deter mine whether a qualified source is more 
advantageous to the Government, a contract  will be issued to PRIMETRICA INC.  There is no 
solicitation package available. Any questions regarding this notice must be submitted in writing 
via email to ecrawford@doc.gov.

Classification 
 
Original Set Aside: 100% Small Business Set Aside 
Product Service Code: DA01 -  IT and Telecom – Business Application/Application Development 
Support Services 
NAICS Code: 541512 – Computer Systems Design Services 
Place of Performance: New Boston Space Force Station – New Boston NH 
 
Synopsis: 
 
New Boston Space Force Station (NBSFS) operates a mixed environment of physical and virtual 
servers across its NIPRNET and SIPRNET enclaves. A significant portion of this server infrastructure 
is at or near its end-of-life (EOL) and end-of-service (EOS), creating substantial risks to mission 
operations, cybersecurity posture, and system reliability. To address these deficiencies and align with 
Department of the Air Force Instruction (AFI) 17-140, which mandates industry best practices for 
hardware refresh cycles, NBSFS requires a comprehensive modernization of its server and services 
infrastructure. 
This Scope of Work details the requirements for a contractor to execute a full lifecycle, turnkey project 
to survey, design, procure, install, configure, and operationalize a new server solution. 
 
The objective of this RFI is to solicit Letters of Interest (LOI) from potential contractors that can 
complete the following: 
 
Requirements 
 
The primary objective of this initiative is to replace the outdated server infrastructure with a modern, 
secure, and resilient solution. The key goals are as follows: 
Enhance Security Posture: Systematically eliminate vulnerabilities associated with unsupported 
hardware and software by deploying a new infrastructure that is compliant with all applicable 
DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and DoD cybersecurity mandates. 
Improve System Reliability and Performance: Increase mission-critical service availability and 
operational efficiency through the deployment of modern, high-performance server hardware with 
full vendor support. 
Achieve Full Compliance: Ensure the new environment adheres strictly to the DoD Approved Products 
List (APL) and all relevant DAF standards for IT procurement and configuration. 
Deliver a Turnkey Solution: Provide a fully integrated and operational server environment, complete 
with comprehensive documentation and training to ensure seamless government takeover and 
sustainment. 
 
The contractor is considered the subject matter expert for all tasks and responsibilities. The contractor is 
responsible for proactively identifying and resolving all technical and logistical challenges required for the 
successful execution of this project. The government will rely on this expertise throughout the design and 
implementation process. The contractor shall perform the following tasks, organized into distinct project 
phases: 
1. Phase 1 – On-Site Survey and Discovery  

2. Phase 2 – Turnkey Solution Design and Engineering 
3. Phase 3 – Procurement, Installation and Configuration 
4. Phase 4 – Transition, Verification, and Post-Implementation Support 
Interested parties should submit a Letter of Interest detailing how their organization would meet the 
requirements listed above.  Please provide a capabilities statement that outlines your company's 
experience and expertise in performing similar work, particularly within secure Do W or government 
facilities. Your response should highlight your ability to meet the on-site support requirements and your 
familiarity with the specified compliance standards.  Please provide a point of contact for your 
organization as well as the name of a person (if different) with authority to enter into agreements with 
outside parties. 
Letters of Interest are due on or before 1:00 PM ET, 1 June 2026.  
Special Note: This is not a request for proposal (RFP), applications, proposal abstracts, or quotations, 
nor does its issuance obligate or restrict the Government to an acquisition approach. The Government 
does not intend to award a contract based on any responses or pay for the preparation or use of any 
information submitted. All information received will be used for planning and market research purposes 
only. Any proprietary information submitted should be marked accordingly. The Government will not 
be liable, or suffer any consequential damages, for any proprietary information not properly identified. 
Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. 
Points of Contact: Please address any comments/questions regarding this request for information to Ms. 
Kristin Morrison AFLCMC/PZI, at kristin.morrison.1@us.af.mil.

Description of the supplies or services required, the estimated price/cost, and required delivery date or 
period of performance. 
 
The Navy Clothing & Textile Research Facility (NCTRF) is seeking procurement of a  3D virtual design 
software that will address the need for quick, affordable, and accurate prototyping. The software will bring 
NCTRF closer to design industry standards by shrinking turnaround time of prototyping and the dependency on 
a decreasing domestic manufacturing pool, while cutting down the overall cost, and creating a more sustainable 
development process. 
 
Period of Performance: 1 June 2026 to 31 May 2027 
 
In conclusion, the requested supplies or services represent the minimum requirements of the government. 
 
Describe in detail why only this source(s) can furnish the requirements to the exclusion of other sources. 
  
NCTRF uses Gerber Accumark for the creation, manipulation, and storage of pattern data. CLO 3D works 
cohesively with Gerber AccuMark 2D Pattern Design Software, with the ability to import pattern data files. 
CLO 3D meets the needs of NCTRF in a unique manner as the only software with the ability to work in 2D and 
3D to produce true to life virtual prototypes with the use of functioning components and accurate fabric 
representation to meet the goal of efficient and sustainable prototyping. 
 
CLO specifically has superior technology and ability to work with complex virtual prototypes such as ballistic 
vests and protective coveralls, which other 3D software does not have the ability to do. CLO also uniquely can 
reposition and “rig” avatars. With this capability we can reposition the avatar’s body to stand in a real-life Navy 
specific position. This is unique and a specific feature that will directly be assessed and to be able to accurately 
fit our garments to our sailors.  
 

 
Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 
 
Market Research was performed using mandatory sources such as GSA, UNICOR, and AbilityOne that yielded 
negative results with CLO being the only authorized contractor within the scope is a leader in 3D virtual design 
software throughout the clothing design industry, with proven results that provide a valuable return on 
investment. 
   
CLO is the only manufacturer of this software with no other authorized resellers. No other vendor can meet the 
needs of the government under this requirement. 
 
☒ A patent, copyright or proprietary data limits competition.   
 
CLO owns and maintains all proprietary data for their software.

Synopsis: 
NASA/NSSC has a requirement for Base Coat software.  
NASA/NSSC intends to issue a sole source contract to GREENFIELD DIVERSIFIED, LLC under the authority 
of FAR 12.102(a). It has been determined that GREENFIELD DIVERSIFIED, LLC is the sole provider of Base 
Coat software. 
NASA/NSSC will be the procuring center for this effort. Performance will be located at NASA/ Langley 
Research Center (LARC). 
The Government intends to acquire Commercial items or services using the provisions, clauses and procedures 
prescribed in FAR Part 12 for Commercial 
The NAICS Code for this procurement is 541511. 
Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort in writing to the 
identified point of contact not later than 12:00 p.m. Central Standard Time on 5/19/2026. Such 
capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this 
procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed effort on 
a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the 
government. 
Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. 
NASA FAR Supplement Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this

This recommendation is for the acquisition of supplies or services determined to be reasonably available 
from only one source/only one manufacture. Competition is impractical for the following reasons (please 
answer the questions below): 
 
1. What are the reasons for soliciting only the suggested source/suggested brand name? Please provide  
The unique characteristics of the items or services along with the supporting rationale and the market 
research performed to substantiate your reason for the suggested source/brand name. 
 
NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) Center Operations Directorate requires the procurement of 
Consulex’s Base.Coat Software. Consulex is the sole provider and owner of the Base.Coat software and 
associated inspection methodology. No other vendor has legal access, licensing rights, or the ability to 
furnish, integrate, or support the Base.Coat platform. The company’s inspection services are designed 
specifically around this proprietary software ecosystem and therefore cannot be replicated, substituted, or 
provided by any alternative source. Base.Coat is required specifically because of its integrated, end-to-
end corrosion management capabilities that are not available in other commercial software solutions. 
These capabilities include: a unified database framework modeled after NASA’s Pressure Systems 
Database and tailored for corrosion management, integrated tracking of both visual and ultrasonic 
inspection history, tools for prioritizing maintenance actions based on corrosion severity and coating 
performance, evaluation of coating-system lifecycle and degradation trends, and direct support from 
vendor-qualified personnel using proprietary Consulex workflows. Base.Coat is already in use at NASA 
Kennedy Space Center (KSC). Leveraging this proven implementation minimizes risk, eliminates 
redundant research or pilot efforts, and ensures compatibility and consistency across NASA Centers. 
 
2. What is the impact to the government if another vendor/brand is used? Include any dollar, schedule, 
or compatibility impacts if possible. 
 
   Using any vendor other than Consulex would impose significant cost, schedule, and compatibility 
impacts on the Government. Alternate commercial tools provide only partial corrosion‑management 
functionality and would require extensive customization, workflow development, and system integration, 
likely delaying operational capability by 12–24 months and adding substantial cost for software 
modification, inspection workflow development, and separate contracting for inspection personnel. 
Additionally, a non‑Consulex solution would be incompatible with the existing Base.Coat 
implementation already in use at NASA KSC, reducing standardization, hindering data‑sharing, and 
increasing technical and operational risk. These factors make alternative options impractical and not in 
the Government’s best interest.

STATEMENT OF WORK  
 
1. Objective/Requirements 
 
NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) Center Operations Directorate requires the procurement 
of Consulex Base.Coat Software.  
 
2. Characteristics, Scope, and Specs 
 
BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVES 
The facilities, structures, and equipment managed by NASA at Langley Research Center are 
complex and characterized by many safety/operation-critical assets that reside in a highly 
corrosive coastal environment. NASA has determined that a structured corrosion control 
program is required to ensure the cost-effective preservation of program assets and maintain 
operational safety, readiness, and reliability of critical facilities, structures, and equipment. A 
formally structured corrosion management program requires an information system to 
efficiently capture, store, analyze, and report on asset condition data. Base.Coat® provides 
this informationsystem. Specifically, the software enables NASA to: 
• Efficiently schedule, collect, store, and analyze asset corrosion and coating 
condition data. 
• Baseline asset conditions and monitor changes at a frequency appropriate for each 
asset. 
• Track and forecast condition trends over time at the program, group, and item 
levels. Identify and quantify current and future maintenance needs for each asset. 
• Prioritize and budget required work according to asset criticality and condition. 
• Mine lessons-learned (identify repair/maintenance drivers for program 
improvement). 
• Share centralized corrosion program data and facilitate corporate memory. 
•  Foster predictive, proactive maintenance as opposed to emergency, unplanned 
repairs. 
•  Reduce life-cycle costs of corrosion control and protective coatings. 
• Maintain an information dashboard for insightful visualization of program data. 
 
BASE.COAT® (CORR.BASE™) SOFTWARE OVERVIEW  
Base.Coat® is a patented web-enabled software application that provides an information system 
and framework for implementing a structured protective coatings and corrosion control 
management program. The software facilitates a proactive approach to facility asset management 
and provides a centralized knowledge base for corporate memory. Users access the application 
through a standard internet browser (Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, or Mozilla Firefox). 
Unlike traditional desktop applications, it does not require installation on the user’s device and 
can be accessed from anywhere within NASA’s network. Functional capabilities include: 
• Asset digital model: structured catalog of facilities, structures, and equipment with 
hierarchical breakdown by program, group, item, area, and element. 
• Coating system library: production rates, costs, surface preparation, and material data for 
budget cost forecasting and standards enforcement. 
• Condition assessment data capture: configurable inspection plans, mandatory data points, 

photo documentation, and hotspot tracking. 
• Composite performance indexes: condition data translated into trend charts and program 
level dashboards. 
• Reporting: standard reports for program management plus the ability to develop 
customized reports tailored to NASA Langley’s reporting requirements. 
• Audit trail and corporate memory: data is retained centrally and persists across personnel 
and contractor changes. 
 
NETWORK AND SERVER REQUIREMENTS FOR ON-PREMISES DEPLOYMENT 
Base.Coat® is delivered as a web application installed on NASA-controlled hardware within 
Langley’s network boundary. NASA owns and operates the database and application server; all 
program data resides on NASA infrastructure. The following describes the recommended 
environment for installation and operation. Final sizing will be confirmed jointly with NASA IT 
prior to installation based on anticipated user count, asset count, and document storage volume. 
 
Table 1 – Minimum Hardware and Software Requirements 
 
Hardware Requirement 
Processor  2 GHz CPU or faster (4+ cores 
recommended) 
RAM  8 GB minimum (16 GB recommended for 
>25 concurrent 
users) 
Disk Space 5 GB minimum for application; additional 
capacity for 
database (see below) 
Operating System Windows Server 2019 or later (2022 
recommended) 
Software Requirement 
Web Server Microsoft IIS 10.0 or later 
.NET Framework 4.6.2 or later 
Database Microsoft SQL Server 2019 or later (Standard 
or 
Enterprise) 
Initial Database Allocation 100 GB recommended (scales with asset 
count and 
embedded documentation) 
Browsers Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, or Mozilla 
Firefox 
(current versions) 
 
Network Architecture and Connectivity 
 
Base.Coat® is designed for deployment on NASA’s intranet (local network) at Langley. 
Authorized 
network users access the application by HTTPS through a standard web browser. Specifically: 

• Inbound application traffic: HTTPS (TCP 443) from authorized client subnets to the 
application server. HTTP (TCP 80) may be enabled and configured to redirect to HTTPS. 
• Application-to-database traffic: TCP 1433 (default SQL Server) between the application 
server and the database server. Application and database may be co-located on a single 
server or split across two servers depending on NASA’s preferences. 
• TLS: TLS 1.2 minimum (TLS 1.3 supported); a server certificate trusted by NASA’s PKI 
is required for HTTPS termination at the IIS host. 
• Outbound internet: not required for normal operation. Software updates and patches are 
delivered to NASA on physical or NASA-approved digital transfer media for installation 
by NASA IT. 
• DNS: an internal DNS A record (e.g., basecoat.nasa.larc internal) is recommended for 
stable client URL resolution. 
• Firewall placement: the application server resides inside NASA’s network perimeter; no 
External (public internet) access to the application is required or recommended. 
 
Authentication and Single Sign-On (SSO) 
Two authentication modes are supported and may be combined as appropriate for NASA’s 
environment: 
• Form-level authentication: usernames and passwords managed within the application 
database. Suitable for limited-user scenarios or for non-domain accounts (e.g., visiting 
auditors, contractor accounts). 
• SAML 2.0 single sign-on (SSO): the application acts as a SAML Service Provider (SP) 
and federates with NASA’s Identity Provider (IdP). This enables NASA users to sign in 
using existing NASA credentials and inherit account lifecycle, MFA, and conditional-
access policies enforced by the IdP. 
For SAML SSO, Consulex will provide standard SP metadata (entity ID, ACS URL, certificate 
fingerprint) for exchange with NASA’s IdP team. Required SAML attributes are minimal: a 
stable unique identifier (NameID), and optionally email, display name, and group/role claims 
used for authorization. Role-based access (Administrator, Editor, Inspector, Read-Only) is 
enforced inside the application; role assignment can be driven by SAML group claims or 
managed in-application.  
 
Database, Backup, and Disaster Recovery 
All application data — asset records, condition assessments, photographs, system catalog, user  
accounts, and audit history — resides in a single Microsoft SQL Server database under NASA 
control. NASA’s standard database operations apply, with the following considerations: 
• Backup model: SQL Server FULL recovery model is recommended to enable point-in-
time recovery. Daily full backups plus periodic transaction log backups will provide an 
appropriate recovery point objective (RPO) for most program use cases. 
• Backup integration: backups are produced by NASA’s standard SQL Server Agent jobs 
or backup tooling (Veeam, Commvault, NetBackup, etc.) and stored on NASA-managed 
backup media. No vendor-specific backup tooling is required. 
• Photographs and embedded documents: stored inside the database (or on a shared file 
path, depending on NASA’s preference). The 100 GB initial allocation accommodates a 
substantial photo library; growth is roughly proportional to the number of inspections and 
photo retention policy. 

• Disaster recovery: the application is stateless and can be re-deployed to a recovery host in
under one hour given a current database backup. A warm-standby DR host with database
log shipping or Always-On Availability Groups is supported but not required for typical
use.
• Database maintenance: standard DBA tasks (index maintenance, statistics updates,
integrity checks) follow NASA’s normal SQL Server maintenance plans.
U
ser Concurrency and Scaling 
The minimum hardware specification supports a typical Langley deployment. The following 
sizing guidance helps plan capacity: 
• Light use (up to ~10 concurrent active users, primarily data entry and reporting):
singleserver deployment with the minimum specification is sufficient.
• Moderate use (10–25 concurrent users, including field inspectors syncing photo-rich
assessments): increase RAM to 16 GB and consider separating the application and
database tiers onto two hosts for improved I/O and reporting throughput.
• Heavy reporting/analysis: a SQL Server instance with at least 8 logical processors and 16
GB of RAM dedicated to SQL is recommended. Custom reports against large asset
histories benefit from dedicated database resources.
• Field tablets/laptops: any current Windows, macOS, or iPadOS device running a modern
browser. No native client is required. Bandwidth requirements are modest; connectivity
over Wi-Fi or VPN at typical NASA-internal speeds is adequate even for photo upload.

NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION 
NASA SHARED SERVICES CENTER 
 
RECOMMENDATION AND DETERMINATION TO SOLICIT FROM ONE SOURCE  
OR BRAND NAME 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Brand Name Justification: 
☒I recommend that NASA, NASA Shared Services Center negotiate only with vendors who can provide the subject band name from 
Astrodyne Corporation.for Astrodyne Fuel Cell Testing Load Bank . The total estimated cost of this effort is  and the 
estimated period of performance or lead-time for delivery is 20 Weeks. 
 
This recommendation is for the acquisition of supplies or services determined to be reasonably available from only one source/only 
one manufacture. Competition is impractical for the following reasons (please answer the questions below): 
 
1. What are the reasons for soliciting only the suggested source/suggested brand name?  Please provide the unique characteristics 
of the items or services along with the supporting rationale and the market research performed to substantiate your reason for the 
suggested source/brand name. 
    
Glenn Research center intends to procure three Astrodyne TDI Model XBL-400-1K-12K-LM-LF water-cooled programmable DC 
load banks. Existing fuel cell test facilities currently utilize Astrodyne TDI load banks that have proven reliable and fully capable of 
supporting testing requirements. The proposed units offer equivalent specifications, ensuring compatibility with existing fuel cell 
stacks and infrastructure in Building 334.Standardizing on Astrodyne TDI allows for seamless integration as drop-in replacements 
and leverages existing personnel familiarity, eliminating the need for additional training or system modifications. Use of an alternate 
vendor would require significant reprogramming and integration effort, resulting in increased cost and schedule risk. This 
procurement maintains hardware commonality across the facility, improving operational efficiency and supportability. Accordingly, 
Astrodyne TDI is the only responsible source that meets the Government’s requirements without unacceptable delay or duplication 
of cost. 
 
2. What is the impact to the government if another vendor/brand is used?  Include any dollar, schedule, or compatibility impacts if 
possible. 
 
Selecting a vendor other than Astrodyne TDI would introduce additional cost, risk, and schedule impacts. Unlike Astrodyne TDI 
systems, which are already proven compatible with existing fuel cell test setups, an alternate load bank would require performance 
validation, consuming labor and test resources. This evaluation is further constrained by the lack of available spare fuel cell stacks 
and introduces risk to customer-owned hardware. Additionally, current facility control systems are configured to communicate with 
Astrodyne TDI load banks via RS232. A different vendor would require significant reprogramming and validation of PLC 
interfaces, resulting in increased engineering effort and delays. In contrast, Astrodyne TDI units provide seamless drop-in 
replacement capability, avoiding these costs. Finally, Astrodyne TDI’s modular design supports future system expansion, offering a 
more cost-effective path to increased capacity without requiring full system replacement.

CONTRACT TYPE 
 
ABMC intends to utilize a  predominantly time & materials  contract type, but vendors may 
propose any contract type they believe is most advantageous to the Government.   
 
PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
ABMC is seeking services for a base year plus four option years.

If interested in this requirement, please submit a proposal via email to the undersigned at

Part One: Scope of Services 
1. General Information 
1.1 Background 
The American Battle Monuments Commission (ABMC) is an independent agency of the executive 
branch of the US government, established by legislation in 1923. It maintains military cemeteries 
and memorials in countries around the world commemorating the US war-dead. 
 
ABMC is staffed by around 575 full-time civilian employees, around 90 of whom are US citizens. The 
agency employs approximately 420 permanent and 50 temporary/seasonal civilian foreign nationals 
in the 10 countries where ABMC installations are located – six in Europe (France, Belgium, Italy, 
Netherlands, United Kingdom and Luxembourg), plus Tunisia, the Philippines, Panama and Mexico. 
See Appendix I for the list of covered countries and foreign national employee populations, which 
range from 300 in France, down to two in Mexico. 
 
The agency is headquartered in Washington, D.C. and has an Overseas office in Paris, France, where 
HR and finance directorates oversee the administration of foreign nationals, all of whom are directly 
employed and managed by the agency. 
 
ABMC has a requirement for payroll services for foreign national employees in 7 countries (France, 
Belgium, Italy, Netherlands, United Kingdom, Luxembourg, and Tunisia). The Philippines, Panama, 
and Mexico may be added at a later date.  Human Resources Information System (HRIS) 
requirements are covered under a separate solicitation  (see 74330226R0044, available at 
ABMC.gov). 
 
1.2 Special Conditions 
Please note that: 
• While ABMC is part of the foreign mission of the government of the United States it is not 
considered an “embassy” and is not exempt from local labor practices. 
• ABMC makes payroll and benefits payments directly from the United States Department of 
the Treasury and generally cannot use the services of a commercial bank to make payments. 
See Appendix II for more details. In the exceptional cases where benefits of payments are 
required to be paid or debited from a bank in the country of service, ABMC will require 
additional payroll services to act as the intermediary. Currently this is required in France 
(income tax) and Italy (social security and pension.  
• Accounting services are outsourced through a shared service agreement with the US 
Department of the Interior. This is an Oracle-based accounting system, and the new payroll 
service provider will be required to provide a balanced GL output file for accounting. (See 
Appendix III for more details.) 

3 
 
 
2. Objective 
The main objective is to deliver an accurate, timely monthly payroll to ABMC foreign national 
employees that is compliant with both local labor laws and ABMC internal regulations. The second 
objective is to reduce manual processes and dependency on country ‑specific workarounds. The 
third objective is to provide customer service to ABMC and provide consistent social and legal watch. 
 
3. Scope of services 
The scope of services for this project covers a typical set of payroll managed services across all 7 
countries listed in Appendix I, with the possible future addition of 3 more countries (the Philippines, 
Panama, Mexico). 
 
These services include: 
• Gross to Net Processing 
• Pay slips 
• U.S. Treasury disbursements 
• Inbound & Outbound interfaces 
• Legal & Statutory reporting 
• Lodgment service to local authorities 
• Employee queries 
• Year-end preparation 
• Year-end report distribution 
• Accounting interface 
  
4. Project Timeline 
ABMC will agree on a timeline with the chosen payroll supplier, in conjunction with the chosen 
human resources information system supplier that is being selected separately but concurrently. 
However, its goal is to select a provider and to go-live by January 2027.  

4

Interested Contractors shall provide proposals that are clearly written, technically sound, detailed, 
and tailored to each element of ABMC’s performance work statement.  Contractors shall not simply 
rephrase or summarize the specific requirements of this s olicitation without offering a clear 
solution.  
  
ABMC acknowledges the evolving role of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in content development. 
However, all submitted proposals shall reflect the Contractor’s own understanding, capabilities, and 
proposed approach. Proposals that are generic, lack relev ance, and/or contain AI -generated text 
drafted without thoughtful human analysis and input will be considered non-responsive.   
  
Contractors shall ensure that proposal submissions are written, reviewed and refined by subject 
matter experts familiar with ABMC’s specific requirements, and that proposals demonstrate a 
meaningful grasp of ABMC's mission, constraints, and operating envir onment.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)

ENTERPRISE MIDDLEWARE SOFTWARE MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

Department of Veterans Affairs
Financial Services Center

1.0 PURPOSE

This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research purposes in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Part 10.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Financial Services Center is seeking information from industry regarding the availability and capability of industry to provide software licensing, maintenance, and technical support services necessary to sustain the VA enterprise middleware transaction processing environment. 

The Government is conducting this RFI to:

• Identify capable vendors
• Assess available contract vehicles
• Obtain rough order of magnitude (ROM) pricing
• Validate industry capability to support the requirement
• Obtain feedback regarding the technical requirements

This RFI does not constitute a solicitation and does not represent a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract.

The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this RFI.

2.0 BACKGROUND

The Department of Veterans Affairs Financial Services Center operates an enterprise electronic commerce middleware platform used to support system-to-system transaction exchange between internal VA enterprise applications and external trading partners.

The platform supports structured electronic transactions including financial, supply chain, healthcare, and other enterprise electronic commerce transactions.

The Government currently operates the environment under a Processor Value Unit (PVU) licensing model supporting both production and non-production environments.

The current licensed capacity for the VA enterprise middleware environment is as follows:

The environment includes the following core components:

• Enterprise middleware integration platform
• Transformation capabilities supporting multiple electronic transaction domains
• Secure proxy gateway licensing supporting controlled inbound connectivity
• Technical advisory and middleware health-check services

The Department of Veterans Affairs anticipates up to thirty percent (30%) growth in the middleware environment during the period of performance as additional enterprise systems, integrations, and external trading partners are on-boarded.

To support this anticipated growth, the Government may acquire additional middleware licenses of the same type currently deployed within the environment.

Additional licensing capacity may be acquired in increments of 100 PVU.

3.0 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

Technical requirements associated with this environment are provided in:

Attachment A – Enterprise Middleware Software Maintenance and Support Technical Requirements 

ENTERPRISE MIDDLEWARE SOFTWARE

Respondents shall review Attachment A when preparing responses.

4.0 CONTRACT VEHICLE INFORMATION

The Government is interested in understanding which existing contract vehicles are available to support this requirement.

Respondents should identify whether the capability can be provided through:

• NASA SEWP
• GSA Multiple Award Schedule
• Other Government-Wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs)

If responding under NASA SEWP, vendors should identify the applicable SEWP contract number and category. Vendors should identify in their response if they are on a GSA MAS Schedule and have a GSA contract number.  

5.0 INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INDUSTRY

Respondents are requested to provide the following information.

5.1 Company Information

Company Name
Company Address
Point of Contact
Phone Number
Email Address
Applicable Contract Vehicles

Business Size/Socioeconomic Category

5.2 Capability Statement

Provide a summary describing the organization's capability to provide the software licensing, maintenance, and technical support services described in Attachment A.

5.3 Technical Capability and Relevant Experience

Describe your experience supporting enterprise middleware environments, specifically those involving: 

• enterprise electronic commerce transaction processing
• enterprise system integration
• electronic data interchange (EDI) transformation capabilities
• secure external transaction connectivity
• middleware platform operational support

5.4 Contract Vehicle Availability

Identify any applicable existing contract vehicles through which the vendor can provide the required licensing, maintenance, and support services.

5.5 Technical Feedback (Optional)

Respondents may provide feedback regarding the technical requirements described in Attachment A including:

• recommended clarifications
• industry best practices
• considerations for projected middleware platform growth

Feedback should be constructive and based on current industry practices, standards, or emerging technologies.

5.6 Past Performance Supporting Middleware Platforms

Provide examples of relevant middleware environments your organization has supported, including:

• enterprise electronic commerce transaction processing
• enterprise application integration
• electronic data interchange (EDI) transformation
• secure proxy gateway connectivity supporting external trading partners

Responses should include examples of similar environments supported by the respondent.

5.7 Platform Licensing and Architecture Knowledge

Respondents shall describe their experience providing software licensing, maintenance, and support services for middleware platforms operating under processor-based licensing models (e.g., Processor Value Unite (PVU)-based models). 

Respondents should address:

• experience supporting production and non-production middleware environments
• experience managing license capacity growth
• experience performing platform architecture assessments or health checks

6.0 PRICING INFORMATION REQUESTED (ROM)

The Government requests rough order of magnitude (ROM) pricing for the licensing, maintenance, and technical support services described in Attachment A.

All pricing shall clearly identify underlying assumptions. ROM pricing may be provided in ranges if appropriate for early-stage estimation.

Pricing information provided in response to this RFI is for market research purposes only and will be used to support acquisition planning and budgeting.

Pricing provided shall not be considered binding and will not be used as the basis for a contract award.

7.0 PRICING TABLE

Respondents should complete the following table for existing software products currently in use.  Respondents are encouraged to provide their own pricing table (following the format below) for equivalent products if applicable. 

8.0 CAPABILITY MATRIX

Respondents should complete the following matrix.

Responses shall include the following sections, in order:

Company Information

Capability Statement

Technical Capability

Contract Vehicle Availability

Capability Matrix

Estimated ROM Pricing

Responses should be limited to ten (10) pages, excluding pricing tables and marketing materials.

Responses should be submitted in PDF format.

10.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS

Responses shall be submitted electronically via email to:

Sandra Vargo

Contract Specialist
Department of Veterans Affairs


email: sandra.vargo@va.gov

Responses are requested no later than:

March 18, 2026 @ 10am EST.

11.0 DISCLAIMER

This RFI is issued for market research purposes only.

This RFI:

• does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP)
• does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation
• does not obligate the Government to award a contract

The Government may use information received in response to this RFI to support acquisition planning and strategy development.

ATTACHMENTS

Attachment A
Enterprise Middleware Software Maintenance and Support Technical Requirements

PRODUCT DESCRIPTION

ENTERPRISE MIDDLEWARE SOFTWARE MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

1.0 EXISTING MIDDLEWARE ENVIRONMENT

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Financial Services Center operates an enterprise electronic commerce middleware environment used to support system-to-system transaction exchange between internal enterprise applications and external partner organizations.

The current environment is implemented using the IBM B2B Gateway middleware platform and associated transformation components, which provide transaction routing, data transformation, and secure external connectivity capabilities used to support enterprise electronic commerce operations.

The environment enables the exchange of financial, supply chain, and other structured electronic transactions between VA enterprise systems and authorized external trading partners.

The Government requires continued software licensing, maintenance, and technical support services necessary to sustain operation of this middleware environment and maintain compatibility with existing transaction mappings, system integrations, and operational workflows.

2.0 CONTINUITY OF OPERATIONS AND PLATFORM COMPATIBILITY

The Contractor shall provide software licensing, maintenance, and technical support services necessary to maintain the operational capability of the Government’s existing middleware transaction processing environment.

The solution shall support compatibility with the Government’s current middleware architecture, transaction mappings, integration interfaces, and operational workflows currently operating within the IBM B2B Gateway middleware environment.

The Contractor shall ensure that maintenance and support services enable uninterrupted operation of the enterprise middleware platform supporting electronic commerce operations.

3.0 SECURE ELECTRONIC TRANSACTION GATEWAY

The middleware platform shall support secure electronic transaction exchange between internal enterprise systems and authorized external partner organizations.

The platform shall provide controlled connectivity mechanisms that enable inbound and outbound transaction processing while preventing direct external access to internal enterprise systems.

The solution shall support authenticated and encrypted communication channels for the exchange of structured electronic transactions with external entities.

4.0 BUSINESS-TO-BUSINESS TRANSACTION PROCESSING

The middleware platform shall support the receipt, validation, processing, and delivery of electronic business transactions exchanged between the Government and external partner organizations.

The platform shall support reliable transaction handling capabilities to ensure accurate delivery and processing of transactions between participating systems.

The system shall support enterprise electronic commerce operations involving multiple internal systems and external trading partners.

5.0 DATA TRANSFORMATION AND MESSAGE TRANSLATION

The middleware platform shall provide configurable capabilities to transform and translate structured data between differing transaction formats used by external partners and internal enterprise applications.

The solution shall support configurable data mapping and transformation rules necessary to enable interoperability between disparate systems and differing message structures.

6.0 INDUSTRY TRANSACTION STANDARD SUPPORT

The middleware platform shall support structured electronic transaction formats commonly used in financial, supply chain, and healthcare transaction exchanges.

The solution shall support industry-recognized electronic data interchange (EDI) standards and other structured messaging formats used to facilitate enterprise system integration and electronic commerce transactions.

7.0 TRANSACTION ROUTING AND PROCESSING RULES

The platform shall support configurable routing and processing of electronic transactions based upon defined business rules.

The system shall support directing transactions to appropriate internal applications, services, or external partner systems based upon defined routing criteria and transaction attributes.

8.0 SECURE COMMUNICATION PROTOCOL SUPPORT

The platform shall support secure communication protocols used to facilitate the exchange of electronic transactions between the Government and external organizations.

The solution shall support encrypted communications and secure data transport mechanisms consistent with Federal information security requirements.

9.0 ENTERPRISE SYSTEM INTEGRATION

The middleware platform shall integrate with enterprise information systems, including financial management systems and other internal enterprise applications, to enable automated exchange of structured transaction data.

The platform shall support integration with enterprise messaging frameworks, application interfaces, and other integration mechanisms required to support enterprise electronic commerce operations.

10.0 PRODUCTION AND NON-PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT SUPPORT

The middleware platform shall support deployment across multiple environments including production, development, testing, and staging environments.

The solution shall allow validation and testing of configuration changes, transaction mappings, and integration workflows prior to implementation within the production environment.

11.0 TRANSACTION MONITORING AND OPERATIONAL VISIBILITY

The middleware platform shall provide monitoring capabilities that enable operational personnel to observe transaction processing activities and identify transaction failures or system exceptions.

The system shall provide visibility into transaction status and processing activity necessary to support operational oversight and troubleshooting.

12.0 RELIABILITY AND AVAILABILITY

The middleware platform shall support reliable processing of enterprise electronic transactions and maintain operational availability sufficient to support enterprise electronic commerce operations.

The solution shall support mechanisms that protect transaction integrity and prevent loss or corruption of transaction data during processing operations.

13.0 TRANSACTION PROCESSING CAPACITY

The middleware platform shall support enterprise-scale electronic transaction processing and shall be capable of processing large volumes of structured transactions exchanged between internal enterprise systems and external trading partners.

The platform shall support scalable transaction processing capacity sufficient to support current enterprise electronic commerce operations and future growth in transaction volume.

14.0 EXTERNAL TRADING PARTNER CONNECTIVITY

The middleware platform shall support connectivity with multiple external trading partners participating in enterprise electronic commerce transactions.

The platform shall support secure onboarding, configuration, and management of external partner connections used for transaction exchange with Government systems.

15.0 SOFTWARE MAINTENANCE AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT

prescribed in FAR Part 12 for Commercial

identified point of contact not later than 4:00 a.m. Central Standard Time on 5/18/2026. Such

procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed effort on 
a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the 
government. 
Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice.

EMORANDUM FOR: Prospective Vendors 
FR
OM:  PAE C3BM/C3IWK 
S
UBJECT:  Request for Information (RFI) for Imagery Post Processing Capability 
1. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) Command and Control
Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C2ISR) Division requires site support
functions and logistics sustainment necessary to maintain capabilities for Global Network
Systems. Through this requirement, the Government is seeking individuals with strong
background and experience with algorithm management. These individuals must be able to
perform higher integration and orchestration functions in the management and oversight of
the architecture, its systems and programs. They must also possess an exceptional
understanding of the fundamental principles of algorithm invocation and workflows for
processing against geospatial imagery and integrating algorithm marketplace systems with
existing complex geospatial processing capabilities.
2. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is issued solely for
information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a
promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract
for any service whatsoever. Further, the Air Force is not at this time seeking proposals and
will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will
not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs
associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party's expense. Not
responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued.
3. I
nterested parties are requested to respond to this RFI by providing a company capability
statement pertaining to the below areas of expertise. ONLY prime contractors shall complete
a capability statement; however, prime contractors are able to include information provided
by their subcontractors in their response. Capability statements shall not exceed 20 pages in
length and must address the following:
a. GEOINT AI/ML Algorithm Orchestration Framework
Please describe your experience with modular design and open architecture approaches
for integrating, testing, and hosting advanced algorithms and cataloging data in support of
GEOINT exploitation. Detail experience handling the ingest of GEOINT products
(imagery, geoJSONs, etc.) or data from external sources and performing automatic
tasking, workflow management, or algorithm retraining/implementation accordingly.
Include information on your experience with machine learning algorithm orchestration or

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Regional Procurement Office Central (RPOC), Network Contracting Office 10 (NCO 10), intends to award a sole source contract in accordance with FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12 to Geotab USA, Inc., 621 North Ave NE STE C170 Atlanta, GA 30308.

The VA Northern Indiana Healthcare System requires a fully integrated, FedRAMP authorized telematics and video recording solution for government vehicles. The period of performance shall be August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2027, with four (4) option year periods exercisable at the Government’s discretion.

It is the Government's belief that only the proposed candidate possesses the required capabilities to successfully meet this requirement. It is the Government's intention to solicit and negotiate with only this source. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. In accordance with FAR 5.207, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency.

This notice is not a request for competitive quotes; however, any responsible firm that believes it can meet the requirements may give written notification and capability statements prior to the response due date and time. Vendors shall indicate if they are the direct supplier of the items. Supporting evidence must be furnished in sufficient detail to demonstrate the ability to perform the requirements and must include relevant corporate experience along with the applicable contract number, total contract dollar amount, contract period of performance, details of the relevant services, and customer point of contact with corresponding telephone number and email address.

Responses must include the following information:

Company Name

SAM UEI number

Company's address

Point of Contact information (title, phone number, and email address)

Business size

Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information provided will not be returned.

Responses are due by Tuesday May 19, 2026, at 12 PM (ET). No submissions will be accepted after this date and time. Responses shall be submitted via email to tiera.sims@va.gov. 

The NAICS code for this acquisition is 541519 for Other Computer Related Services with a standard size of $34 Million.
