DOL AI/Section 508 Compliance Tooling - Requirements Document

Department of Labor (DOL) Version 1.0

1.0 Purpose and Background

The Department of Labor (DOL) is seeking to procure an AI-enabled accessibility compliance tooling solution to support the Department's Section 508 program. This acquisition represents a foundational investment in DOL's Section 508 program maturity. The selected solution will serve as the basis for establishing a systematic baseline of DOL's current Section 508 conformance posture, enabling ongoing monitoring, remediation, and reporting across the Department's digital asset portfolio.

DOL currently lacks a robust, methodical capability for capturing Section 508 conformance status or accessibility risk across its digital properties. This procurement is intended to address that gap by providing DOL personnel — including developers, quality assurance testers, and the Section 508 Program Office — with the tools, guidance, and data necessary to identify, prioritize, and remediate accessibility defects independently and systematically.

2.0 Scope

2.1 In-Scope Digital Assets

The solution must support accessibility testing and remediation across the following digital asset types:

Public-facing websites and web applications (primary CMS: Drupal)

Internal websites and web applications

Web applications built on the Appian platform

Web applications built on the Salesforce platform

PDF documents — testing and remediation, including tagging and reading order

Content authored in Microsoft SharePoint — content-level testing and remediation

Content authored in Microsoft 365 applications (e.g., Microsoft Word, Microsoft PowerPoint) — content-level testing and remediation

The solution shall support accessibility testing and remediation workflows across development, test, staging, and production environments.

2.2 Out-of-Scope Digital Assets

The following are explicitly out of scope for this requirement:

Mobile applications (iOS and Android)

SharePoint and Microsoft 365 as platforms (platform-level testing is not required)

Recurring vendor-performed accessibility audits of DOL digital content

Recurring vendor-performed remediation of DOL digital content

3.0 User Personas and License Requirements

3.1 Primary User Personas

The solution must support three distinct user personas, each with different functional needs:

3.1.1 Developers Developers require tool capabilities that integrate into existing development workflows, provide code-level accessibility feedback, and support shift-left testing practices within CI/CD pipelines.

3.1.2 Quality Assurance (QA) Testers QA testers require guided manual testing workflows, browser-based testing tools, and semi-automated testing capabilities sufficient to identify and document accessibility defects across DOL digital assets.

3.1.3 Section 508 Program Office The Section 508 Program Office requires dashboards, compliance analytics, issue tracking, and exportable reporting sufficient to monitor DOL's accessibility posture, track remediation progress, and satisfy reporting obligations including the GSA Annual Governmentwide Section 508 Assessment. Section 508 Program Office personnel also perform hands-on accessibility testing and require full access to the solution's manual and automated testing capabilities, including code-level tools where applicable.

3.2 License Requirements

The solution shall provide a minimum of 50 user licenses, distributed across the following roles:

Offerors shall clearly describe how their licensing model accommodates role-based access and whether license types differ by user persona.

DOL reserves the right to reassign licenses across personnel as organizational needs change, including due to staff turnover, role changes, or organizational restructuring. The contractor shall support license reassignment without additional cost or unreasonable restriction.

4.0 Compliance Standards

4.1 Applicable Standards

The solution shall support testing and remediation against the Revised Section 508 Standards (36 CFR Part 1194).

Where the Revised Section 508 Standards incorporate WCAG 2.0 Levels A and AA by reference, DOL substitutes WCAG 2.1 Levels A and AA. The solution must be capable of testing against all applicable WCAG 2.1 Level A and AA success criteria.

4.2 GSA Annual Governmentwide Section 508 Assessment

The solution shall be capable of testing all applicable automated and semi-automated Section 508 / WCAG 2.1 A & AA criteria required by the GSA Annual Governmentwide Section 508 Assessment. For each identified issue, the solution must provide actionable outputs — including issue identification, severity classification, and remediation guidance — sufficient to enable DOL staff to understand, prioritize, and remediate findings.

Testing criteria that are inherently manual or human-judgment-based (e.g., video and media accessibility, including captioning and audio descriptions) are out of scope for the tool and will be addressed by DOL through separate manual processes.

5.0 Minimum Required Capabilities

5.1 Core Tooling Capabilities

The contractor shall provide a solution that includes, at a minimum, the following capabilities:

5.1.1 Automated Accessibility Scanning and Testing — The solution shall perform automated scanning of in-scope digital assets to identify Section 508 / WCAG 2.1 A & AA accessibility defects.

5.1.2 Guided Manual Accessibility Testing — The solution shall provide structured workflows to support semi-automated and manual accessibility testing by QA testers, developers, and Section 508 Program Office personnel.

5.1.3 Document Remediation and Tagging Assistance — The solution shall support remediation of non-web content, including PDF tagging, reading order correction, and remediation of content authored in Microsoft Office and Microsoft 365 applications. DOL prefers an automated solution where feasible, or a solution that enables DOL personnel to perform remediation independently without reliance on recurring contractor services.

5.1.4 Code Review and Repair Suggestions — The solution shall provide developers with actionable, code-level remediation guidance sufficient to understand and resolve identified accessibility defects.

5.1.5 Chatbot or Copilot Capability for Section 508 Guidance — The solution shall include a conversational AI or copilot capability that provides DOL personnel with on-demand Section 508 and WCAG guidance.

5.1.6 Dashboards and Compliance Analytics — The solution shall provide dashboards and analytics capabilities including: issue counts and severity by application and digital property; remediation progress over time; conformance scores per digital asset; and historical trend reporting. The solution shall support exportable reporting in standard formats (e.g., PDF, CSV) for audit and leadership briefing purposes.

5.1.7 Accessibility Training and Embedded Authoring Assistance — The solution shall include role-based training resources and/or embedded authoring guidance. See Section 9.0 for detailed training requirements.

5.2 Additional Technical Capabilities

The solution shall also provide:

API Access — The solution shall provide API access sufficient to support custom integrations with DOL systems and workflows.

Multi-User Collaboration — The solution shall support collaborative workflows enabling multiple users across personas to work within shared projects, issue queues, and reporting environments.

Role-Based Access Controls (RBAC) — The solution shall enforce role-based access controls to ensure appropriate permissions are applied across user personas.

6.0 AI Requirements

6.1 Mandatory AI Capability

The proposed solution must incorporate AI-enabled capabilities as a core functional component. Solutions that do not include AI-enabled testing, remediation guidance, or workflow assistance will not be considered. Legacy rule-based scanning tools without AI integration do not meet this requirement.

6.2 AI-Enabled Actions

The solution shall support AI-assisted and, where authorized by the Government, automated actions including remediation, modification of source files, and publishing workflows.

The solution shall provide controls for such actions, including:

Role-based permissions

Workflow approvals

Versioning and rollback capability

Auditable logging for all AI-assisted or automated changes

6.3 AI Model Flexibility

Where contractor-provided tools incorporate AI or machine learning capabilities, the contractor shall support the ability for DOL to substitute or integrate Government-approved AI models in place of or in conjunction with vendor-default models. Tools that rely on AI models that are prohibited by federal policy or executive directive shall not be deployable unless an approved model substitution capability exists.

The contractor's AI capabilities shall be designed to support integration with external, Government-approved AI models — enabling DOL to leverage vendor accessibility intelligence (e.g., issue detection, remediation guidance) to augment approved models rather than being locked into vendor-default AI dependencies.

NOTE: The contractor's AI capabilities shall comply with all applicable DOL and federal AI policies. Specific AI governance requirements will be incorporated into the contract at award. Offerors should describe their current AI model architecture, any model dependencies, and their roadmap for supporting Government-approved model substitution or integration.

7.0 Integration Requirements

7.1 CI/CD Pipeline Integration

The solution shall integrate with the following CI/CD platforms used by DOL developers:

Jenkins

GitHub Actions / GitHub Pipelines

Integration must be sufficient to enable automated accessibility testing within DOL's existing development pipeline workflows.

7.2 Browser Support

The solution's browser-based components (e.g., browser extensions, testing interfaces) shall support the following browsers:

Google Chrome

Microsoft Edge

8.0 Platform and Environment Coverage

8.1 Appian and Salesforce

Because DOL performs significant development using Appian and Salesforce products, the solution shall be capable of supporting and improving the accessibility of applications built on these platforms.

Support for Appian and Salesforce shall be sufficient to enable DOL personnel to identify, analyze, and address accessibility issues in applications built on those platforms, consistent with the solution's proposed testing, remediation, and reporting capabilities.

8.2 Non-Web Content — Subcontracting

Offerors may propose a primary solution supplemented by a subcontractor or partner to fulfill non-web content (PDF and Office document) requirements, provided that:

The proposed solution collectively meets DOL's non-web content testing and remediation needs

The offeror (prime contractor) assumes full responsibility for the performance and integration of any subcontractor or partner solution

The combined solution enables DOL personnel to perform non-web content remediation independently, without reliance on recurring contractor services

DOL will not hold separate contracts for non-web content remediation. All proposed capabilities, including those delivered through subcontractors, must be covered under a single contract with a single prime contractor.

9.0 Training Requirements

The contractor shall provide role-based training resources sufficient to enable DOL personnel to independently identify, understand, and remediate Section 508 / WCAG 2.1 A & AA accessibility defects. Training shall address both the creation of accessible content and the remediation of identified accessibility defects.

Training may be delivered via:

Guidance and remediation assistance embedded directly in the tool (e.g., inline issue explanations, contextual remediation steps)

Access to a vendor-hosted training platform with role-based course offerings

Training priorities by persona:

Live, instructor-led training is not required.

10.0 Vendor Services

10.1 In-Scope Vendor Services

The contractor shall provide the following services in support of the solution:

Tool Onboarding and Implementation Support — The contractor shall provide structured onboarding support to enable DOL to deploy and configure the solution effectively at the start of the contract.

Technical Support — The contractor shall provide dedicated technical support during business hours (Monday–Friday, core business hours). A dedicated account and technical support representative shall be assigned to DOL for the duration of the contract.

10.2 Out-of-Scope Vendor Services

The following services are explicitly out of scope and shall not be proposed as part of this requirement:

Accessibility consulting services

Vendor-performed manual accessibility audits of DOL digital content

Vendor-performed remediation of DOL digital content

10.3 Accessibility of Contractor-Provided Tools

The Government recognizes that software defects may occur and that complete conformance in all circumstances is not achievable. However, because this acquisition is for tools intended to enable accessibility, the accessibility of the tools themselves is a material and high-priority performance requirement.

The contractor shall act diligently and aggressively to identify, document, prioritize, and remediate accessibility defects in contractor-provided products.

When the Government reports an accessibility defect in contractor-provided products or services, the contractor shall acknowledge and/or validate the reported defect within ten (10) business days and shall provide an estimated timeline for remediation.

11.0 Security, Hosting, and Deployment

11.1 Deployment Model

The contractor may propose any deployment model (e.g., Software-as-a-Service, on-premises, hybrid) provided that the proposed solution meets all applicable federal information security requirements. The Government does not express a preference for any particular deployment model.

11.2 Federal Security Requirements

The proposed solution shall comply with all applicable federal information security requirements, including:

FISMA (Federal Information Security Modernization Act)

NIST SP 800-53 security controls as applicable to DOL's environment

Any DOL-specific security requirements communicated during the acquisition process

The contractor shall document the proposed deployment model and associated security controls in sufficient detail to enable DOL's security team to assess and authorize the solution in accordance with the Department's Authority to Operate (ATO) process.

11.3 FedRAMP Authorization

FedRAMP Authorization is preferred and will be evaluated as a competitive advantage. FedRAMP Authorization is not a mandatory requirement. Offerors that are not currently FedRAMP Authorized should describe their current authorization status and roadmap.

NCIA Request for Information (RFI) 
 
To: See Distribution List (Annex B) & Industry Partners 
 
Subject: GEOAI SOLUTIONS TO SUPPORT SELECTED NATO 
USE CASES 
 
RFI-187262-GEOAI 
 
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is conducting market 
research to identify qualified vendors and gather input on potential solutions to support 
selected operational Geospatial Intelligence (GeoInt) use cases  with Geospatial Artificial 
Intelligence (GeoAI) feature extraction technology. To that end, we are issuing the 
attached Request for Information (RFI)  RFI-187262-GEOAI to solicit feedback from 
capable and interested industry partners. 
 
2. The NCI Agency requests the assistance of the Nations and their Industry to identify 
potential Service Providers that can meet or exceed all requirements under the scope of 
this project. 
 
3. This RFI is issued for planning purposes only and is not a request for bids . It is part of 
NCIA’s effort to ensure it has a clear understanding of the marketplace and available 
capabilities and prepare potential acquisition strategies.  
 
4. NCIA requests the broadest possible dissemination by the NATO Nations of this Market 
Survey - Request for Information ("RFI”) to their qualified and interested industrial base. 
 
5. This is a Request for Information (RFI). It is NOT a solicitation for proposals nor a pre-
solicitation notice. 
 
6. At this stage, clarification requests or any further questions are not accepted in return. NCI 
Agency reserves the right to invite respondents to explain their proposed tools. 
 
7. Respondents are requested to await further instructions after submission of their 
responses regarding any potential future bidding process, and are requested to contact 
only the NCI Agency POC identified below  in Paragraph H with any further requests for 
information or clarification. 
 
8. Any response to this Request for Information shall be provided on a cost-free voluntary 
basis. 
 
9. Not responding will not prejudice or cause the exclusion of companies from any future 
procurement that may arise from this Market Survey RFI. Responses to this request, and 
any information provided within the context of this survey, including but not limited to 
pricing, quantities, capabilities, functionalities and requirements will be considered as 
information only and will not constitute a commitment or obligation on the part of 
NCIA/NATO to enter into any procurement process or make any purchase

NCIA-ACQ-1.017(07.25) 
 
10. We value your insight and invite you to share corporate capabilities and experience 
relevant to the stated operational requirements. 
 
11. Submission instructions and additional details can be found in the enclosure to this RFI. 
 
12. Only companies from a NATO member country can participate in or respond to this RFI 
(https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/nato_countries.htm). 
 
13. Should you have any questions or need clarification, please contact Emira Kapetanovic 
at RFI-187262-GEOAI@ncia.nato.int.  
 
14. We thank you in advance for your time and input, and we look forward to engaging with 
you as we shape this potential acquisition.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION  
 
A. Introduction 
 
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NC IA) is conducting market 
research to identify potential sources and gather information regarding industry 
capabilities to Identify the availability and technical capability of all qualified NATO 
nation businesses that can provide the services described in this announcement. This 
Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for informational purposes and does not 
constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or invitation 
for bid.  
 
B. Purpose 
 
1. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain input from industry to help inform the NCIA’s 
acquisition planning. Responses to this RFI will assist in refining requirements, 
identifying capabilities, and shaping the strategy for any future solicitation. 
 
C. Background 
 
1. The Joint Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (JISR) Centre within NCIA 
provides full life cycle support of all assigned JISR services within NATO. In this 
context, the Geospatial, Meteorology and Oceanography (GeoMetOc) Branch within 
JISR is res ponsible for the Core Geographic Information System (CoreGIS) 
Application Service that provides both ACO customers as well as NATO Nations with 
a suite of geospatial data, services and products that ensure all phases of military 
operations are conducted on the same geospatial reference. The CoreGIS Application 
Service is Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) based and uses the Esri ArcGIS software 
product suite in a NATO-specific configuration. 
 
2. Geospatial data typically consists of any raster (e.g. maps or imagery) and vector (e.g. 
transportation, infrastructure, land cover, etc.) data that is relevant for NATO to fulfil 
its mission.  
 
3. This project is specifically aiming to identify suitable solutions and tools for (semi -) 
automated 2D and 3D vector feature extraction and classification from geospatial 
source datasets  using GeoAI technology  to stated use cases  to ultimately support 
provision of actionable intelligence. 
 
4. Potential solutions should support at least one of the following six predefined 
operational use cases and enable the relevant feature extraction, ideally through the 
use of machine learning, deep learning and/or natural language processing: 
 
a. Roads: Extraction of roads with width, number of lanes, building material, 
and condition. 
b. Railroads: Extraction of railroads including track gauge, tunnels, stations, 
and transfer points. 
c. Bridges: Extraction of bridges with likely use (road, railroad, other), type, 
number of spans, width, height, condition, and material 
d. Building footprints: Extraction of building footprints including number of 
floors and estimated volume. 

 
NCIA/ACQ/2026/07098 
 
  
 Page 5 
 
NCIA-ACQ-1.017(07.25) 
 
e. Building material: Identification of building material for man‑made features 
(e.g. buildings, bridges, etc.). 
f. Terrain & soil: Terrain classification and soil composition for terrain 
analysis. 
 
5. This survey focuses on identifying solutions that consider imagery and geospatial data 
types, including but not limited to the following: 
 
 High-resolution: ~ 20-30cm optical imagery 
 High-resolution: ~ 20-30cm optical stereo imagery 
 SAR imagery 
 Infrared imagery 
 Geospatially enabled video (Full motion Video (FMV)) 
 Point cloud data 
 Text with geospatial aspects. 
 
6. NCIA reserves the right to use the returns of this survey in any related work internally 
and to follow up on any information emerging from this survey. 
 
7. Interoperability with NATO’s CoreGIS and other existing systems, integration with its 
networks as well as compliance with governance, security regulations and relevant 
STANAGs are important considerations, together with compliance to common industry 
standards. 
 
 
D. Submission Instructions 
 
1. Interested parties are invited to respond in accordance with the instructions below: 
 
a. Submit responses via the linked Microsoft Forms survey (Annex A) no later 
than 17:30 hours Central European Time (CET) on 23 June 2026. 
 
b. Responses should be submitted in the linked Microsoft Forms survey (Annex A) 
and aim to be kept concise, ideally not exceeding four sentences per question. 
 
c.  All responses should address the items listed in the linked Microsoft Forms 
survey at Annex A (Link: NCIA Request for Information (RFI)). 
 
 
E. Industry Engagement (Optional) 
 
1. The Agency may request a demonstration of the described solution. Respondents will 
be contacted if such a demonstration is desirable to make further arrangements. 
Respondents are requested to await further instructions after their submissions and 
are requested not to contact directly any NCI Agency staff other than the POC 
identified below in Paragraph H.  
 
2. Interactive demonstration, capabilities, functionalities will be considered as indicative 
and informational only and will not be considered as binding on the participant or on 
NATO within the context of any future acquisition. 
 

 
NCIA/ACQ/2026/07098 
 
  
 Page 6 
 
NCIA-ACQ-1.017(07.25) 
 
3. If requested, companies should be willing to provide this demo free of charge to NCI 
Agency. 
 
F. Disclaimer 
 
1. This RFI is for planning and informational purposes only and shall not be construed as 
a solicitation or obligation on the part of the NCIA. The NCIA does not intend to award 
a contract based on responses to this RFI. Respondents are solely responsible for all 
costs incurred in responding to this RFI. The NCIA will consider and  analyse all 
information received from this RFI to share results within a report and may use these 
findings to develop a future solicitation. 
 
2. NCIA reserves the right, at any time, to cancel this informal market survey, partially or 
in its entirety. No legal liability on the part of NCIA  for payment of any sort shall arise 
and in no event will a cause of action lie with any prospective participant for the 
recovery of any costs incurred in connection with the preparation of documentation or 
participation in response hereto. All effort initiated or undertaken by prospective 
informal market survey participants shall be done considering and accepting this fact. 
 
G. Use of Information Provided through Responses 
 
1. Confidentiality of Responses 
 
The attached Microsoft Forms survey includes a section where respondents are be able 
to indicate any proprietary data in their responses that they do not wish to be disclosed

REQUEST FOR QUOTE 
CISCO ENTERPRISE LICENSING 
 
This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in 
subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement 
constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. 
Solicitation no. 7571TE26Q00023 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ). 
The solicitation is a Buy Indian Set-aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 
code 541519 with an associated small business size standard of 150 employees. 
See attachment A SOW and below for more details 
The delivery is upon award or PoP start date.  


REQUEST FOR QUOTE 
CISCO ENTERPRISE LICENSING 
GALLUP INDIAL MEDICAL CENTER 
1. Statement of Work:
1.1. Contractor shall provide Cisco Unified Call Manager (CUCM) – Flex Plan Enterprise and CUBE
Enhanced services for our newly installed/u pgrade CUCM Phone System. Contractor to provide 
all necessary software and current OS server applications for CUCM . 1 year software/hardware 
support agreement for the new Cisco Unified Call Manager Upgrade of all equipment. 
2. Scope of Services
2.1. The scope of this project includes the following components:
2.2.  Cisco Flex Plan Enterprise Services
2.2.1. Licensing management for the Cisco Flex Plan Enterprise Agreement. 
2.2.2. Deployment and configuration of Flex licensing for unified communication solutions, 
including 
2.2.2.1. Webex Calling, Meetings, and Messaging. 
2.2.2.2. Integration of Flex licensing into existing infrastructure to ensure seamless 
operations. 
2.2.2.3. Validation of license assignments and usage. 
2.3. Cisco Unified Border Element (CUBE) Enhanced Services 
2.3.1. Deployment and configuration of CUBE to provide secure, reliable SIP trunking for voice 
and video communication. 
2.3.2. Design and implementation of call routing policies. 
2.3.3. Enabling CUBE redundancy for high availability. 
2.3.4. Security enhancements including TLS/SRTP configuration and DoS protection. 
3. Migration & Integration
3.1. Migration from the existing system to Cisco Flex Plan and/or CUBE.
3.2. Testing and validation of migrated services.
4. Support Services
4.1. 24/7 monitoring and technical support for Cisco Flex Plan and CUBE services.
4.2. Regular health checks and performance tuning.
4.3. Software updates, patch management, and feature upgrades.
5. Deliverables
5.1. Project plan and schedule
5.2. Cisco Flex Plan Enterprise setup and activation report
5.3. Fully configured and operational Cisco CUBE solution
5.4. Documentation of all configurations, policies, and procedures
5.5. Comprehensive user and administrator training
5.6. Final project completion report and sign-off
6. Place of Performance:
6.1. Gallup Indian Medical Center, 516 E Nizhoni Blvd Gallup, New Mexico 87301
7. Period of Performance:
7.1. One base year and four option years:
7.1.1.  06/02/26-06/01/2027 
7.1.2.  06/02/27-06/01/2028

Lynx Keyboard Panics System

PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), requires the implementation of the brand name Lynx Keyboard Panic Solution to enhance staff safety and emergency response capabilities at the Western North Carolina VA Healthcare System based in Asheville, North Carolina.

This solution shall include the installation and configuration of Lynx software with licensing to support up to 4,000 keyboard panic buttons (3,843 units requested). The solution shall have the ability to integrate with the existing CCURE-9000 Access Control System, as installed currently, at the Charles George VA Medical Center in Asheville, NC. The LYNX keyboard-based duress alarm system must be installed on every VHA workstation computer at the Charles George Veterans Affairs Medical Center (CGVAMC), Franklin Community-Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC), Hickory (CBOC), and Master Sergeant Jerry K. Crump VA Clinic.

To support real-time emergency communication, the project includes deployment of the Lynx Dispatcher, allowing alerts and notifications to be transmitted via existing VA Police dispatch radio systems.

Radio Interface Integration: The LYNX-DISP-3 radio interface appliance enables Lynx alarm notifications to be broadcast over VA Police handheld radios using text-to-speech functionality. The unit requires continuous power, a network connection, and installation in a secure location with reliable radio coverage.

The VA Medical Center will provide two handheld radios—one for integration within the LYNX-DISP-3 unit and one for testing and return. One portable radio unit will be permanently installed in the LYNX-DISP-3 appliance. The LYNX-DISP-3 MUST be installed by a local (Asheville, NC Based) company with understanding and foreknowledge of the system as a whole, and its installation requirements, including the particular elements of the existing and installed security hardware (CCURE 9000) that it will be integrated with. 

The period of performance will be from June 30, 2026, through June 29, 2027, consisting of one (1) 12‑month base period, to be exercised at the Government’s discretion.

The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, software, licensing, integration, and configuration necessary to deliver a fully operational Lynx Keyboard Panic Solution, including radio communication capabilities and system integration with existing infrastructure.

Must operate when logged on, logged off, or locked.

NOTICE OF THE FEDERAL ACCESSIBILITY LAW AFFECTING ALL INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) PROCUREMENTS (SECTION 508)

On January 18, 2017, the Access Board issued a final rule that updated accessibility requirements covered by Section 508 and refreshed guidelines for telecommunications equipment subject to Section 255 of the Communications Act.  The final rule went into effect on January 18, 2018.  The revisions and updates to the Section 508-based standards and Section 255-based guidelines are intended to ensure that information and communication technology (ICT) covered by the respective statutes is accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities.

SECTION 508 – INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) STANDARDS

The Section 508 standards established by the Access Board are incorporated into, and made part of all VA orders, solicitations and purchase orders developed to procure ICT.  These standards are found in their entirety at: Revised 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines (access-board.gov).  A single PDF file version of the Revised Section 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines will be supplied upon request, or can be obtained from the Access Board website.  Federal agencies must comply with the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended. 

The Contractor shall comply with “508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements” for all electronic ICT and content delivered under this contract. Specifically, as appropriate for the technology and its functionality, the Contractor shall comply with the technical standards marked here: 

	E205 Electronic Content – (Accessibility Standard -WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA Guidelines)

	E204 Functional Performance Criteria

	E206 Hardware Requirements

	E207 Software Requirements

	E208 Support Documentation and Services Requirements

COMPATABILITY WITH ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY

The standards do not require installation of specific accessibility-related software or attachment of an assistive technology device. Section 508 requires that ICT be compatible with such software and devices so that ICT can be accessible to and usable by individuals using assistive technology, including but not limited to screen readers, screen magnifiers, and speech recognition software.

ACCEPTANCE AND ACCEPTANCE TESTING

Deliverables resulting from this solicitation will be accepted based in part on satisfaction of the Section 508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements standards identified above.

The Government reserves the right to test for Section 508 Compliance before delivery.  The Contractor shall be able to demonstrate Section 508 Compliance upon delivery.

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY USING SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTS

The Contractor shall comply with Sections 524 and Sections 525 of the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007; Section 104 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005; Executive Order 14148, “Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions,” dated January 20, 2025; Executive Order 13221, “Energy-Efficient Standby Power Devices,” dated August 2, 2001; and the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) to provide ENERGY STAR® certified and Federal Energy Management Program (FEMP) Designated Low Standby Power information technology products, see https://www.energy.gov/femp/search-energy-efficient-products.  See http://www.energystar.gov for complete product specifications and updated lists of Energy Star certified products.  FEMP low standby power product listing can be found at https://www.energy.gov/femp/low-standby-power-product-list.

The Contractor shall provide products that meet the definition of sustainable products if the products are delivered to the Government; furnished by the Contractor for use by the Government, incorporated into the construction of a public building or public work, or acquired by the Contractor for use in performing services under a Government contract where the cost of the products is a direct cost to a Government contract (versus costs which are normally applied to a contractor's general and administrative expenses or indirect costs).

Specifically, the Contractor shall provide sustainable products under this contract in accordance with RFO 52.223-23 (NOV 2025).  The applicable products with their associated certification and/or designation required (e.g. Energy Star, FEMP Low Standby Power) are identified within the product requirements specifications in this PD.  The Contractor shall self-certify that its proposed products meet the certification(s) and/or designation(s) specified.

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

VA TECHNICAL REFERENCE MODEL

The Contractor shall comply with the VA OIT Technical Reference Model (VA TRM). Compliance with the VA TRM is achieved by using only technologies and standards that are listed as approved for use in the VA TRM.  The Contractor shall provide all necessary information requested by VA to ensure TRM approval is obtained prior to use on VA’s network.

ZERO TRUST – VA CRITICAL SECURITY CONTROLS

VA has established minimum mandatory security requirements and requires that any network connected software system or service must meet the VA Critical Security Controls as outlined in the VA Memorandum, “VA Security Controls”, https://www.voa.va.gov/DocumentView.aspx?DocumentID=5010.  VA Critical Security Controls identify the minimum mandatory requirements that must be implemented across all VA enterprise infrastructure, cloud computing environments, information systems, networks, and specialized devices (medical devices/systems, special-purpose systems, and research scientific computing devices) that process, store, and/or transmit VA data.  Effective July 1, 2025, the Contractor shall implement these VA Critical Security Controls, within any network connected software system or service prior to being authorized for use in the VA.  This functional requirement is not negotiable, and Plan of Action & Milestones (POAM) will not be accepted in the event these controls cannot be implemented for new systems.  Critical Security Controls are intended to increase VA’s security posture and provide security and privacy risk visibility into the VA network and is not a new requirement.  The Contractor’s failure to maintain these VA Critical Controls after implementation will result in VA discontinuing the use of the system.

SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER (SSN) REDUCTION 

The Contractor solution shall support the Social Security Number (SSN) Fraud Prevention Act (FPA) of 2017 which prohibits the inclusion of SSNs on any document sent by mail.  The Contractor support shall also be performed in accordance with Section 240 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act (CAA) 2018, enacted March 23, 2018, which mandates VA to discontinue using SSNs to identify individuals in all VA information systems as the Primary Identifier.  The Contractor shall ensure that any new IT solution discontinues the use of SSN as the Primary Identifier to replace the SSN with the Integrated Control Number (ICN) in all VA information systems for all individuals.  The Contractor shall ensure that all Contractor delivered applications and systems integrate with the VA Master Person Index (MPI) for identity traits to include the use of the ICN as the Primary Identifier. The Contractor solution may only use a Social Security Number to identify an individual in an information system if and only if the use of such number is required to obtain information VA requires from an information system that is not under the jurisdiction of VA.

The Contractor solution shall support IPv6-Only based upon the memo issued by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) on November 19, 2020 (https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/M-21-07.pdf). Which defines IPv6-only as the state of an operational system or service when IPv4 protocol functions (addressing, packet forwarding) are not in use. The NIST USGv6 profile defines technical requirements for a product to be capable of operating in IPv6-Only environments.  IPv6-Only technology, in accordance with the USGv6 Program (https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/usgv6-program/usgv6-revision-1), NIST Special Publication (SP) 500-267B Revision 1 “USGv6 Profile” (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.500-267Br1), and NIST SP 800-119 “Guidelines for the Secure Deployment of IPv6” (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-119), compliance shall be included in all IT infrastructures, application designs, application development, operational systems and sub-systems, and their integration. Instructions to Offerors 
 
1. GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS TO OFFERORS 
 
1.1. This is a Full and Open Best Value Tradeoff competitive procurement.  
This competitive procurement shall result in the award of a firm fixed price/labor hour single award 
contract.  No proposal costs shall be reimbursed.  The Government reserves the right to award on initial 
proposals, without discussion.  The selection process will follow an advisory multi-step process to 
evaluate offerors.  The steps will include a step 1: Relevant Experience, and a step 2: Technical Approach 
Data Usage Rights, and Price.  All offerors should submit their best relevant experience, technical 
approach, data usage rights, and price proposal(s).  The electronic version of the RFP is the official 
version for this acquisition.  No hard copy or facsimile copies of the Request for Proposal, or 
amendments, will be provided. 
 
The Government intends to award a single contract.  The period of performance will consist of a base 
period of one year, followed by four option years.      
 
Should the Offeror be willing to provide different Data Usage Rights at different prices, the Offeror may 
submit up to two (2) alternate Data Usage Rights Proposals (three Data Usage Rights Proposals in total) 
and an associated alternate Price Proposal for each Data Usage Rights proposal.  Each Data Rights Usage 
Proposal should include only one (1) proposed set of Data Usage Rights.  Offerors shall not include 
more than one set of data usage rights in a single Data Usage Rights Proposal.  For each Data Usage 
Rights Proposal, there should be an associated Price Proposal pricing out that set of data usage rights.  A 
single price proposal may not include multiple or alternative pricing options.  The alternate Volume IV – 
Data Usage Rights and Volume V – Price Proposals must be clearly identified as such, and it must be 
clear which Volume IV – Data Usage Rights proposal is associated with which Volume V – Price 
proposal.  An alternate Volume V – Price proposal may only be submitted if the Offeror submits an 
associated alternate Volume IV – Data Usage Rights proposal (i.e. if an Offeror submits only one (1) 
Volume IV – Data Usage Rights proposal, it may only submit one (1) Volume V– Price proposal).  Only 
one proposal each may be submitted for Volumes I, II and III.  If an Offeror submits a proposal that is 
non-compliant with Instructions to Offerors, the proposal will be considered non-compliant, so as to 
preclude further meaningful evaluation, and will be determined to be unacceptable and thus ineligible for 
award.  
 
All proposals shall include the Offeror and any subcontractor Name(s), UEI, CAGE Code, and a brief 
description of the services to be performed by any subcontractors. 
 
2. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS

James.Batten@fcc.gov and EAC-Proposals@fcc.gov.  Include “RFP Number 273FCC26R0001,

solicitation by completing blocks 17a, 17b, 30a, 30b and 30c of the SF1449.  All proposals and 
correspondence shall be submitted no later than the proposal due date stated in block 8 of the SF1449.

The electronic technical proposal shall be submitted in MS Word or Portable Document Format (PDF),

and label each electronic PDF to afford easy identification from the proposal table of contents.

Experience, Volume III– Technical Approach, Volume IV-Data Usage Rights, and Volume V – Price, 
with a possible Volume IV– Data Usage Rights, Alternate I and Alternate II and corresponding Volume V

Richard P. Feynman Center for Innovation
Technology Snapshot
Overview
ReactorCast is a custom system dynamics platform 
that models and ties strategic decisions and investment 
considerations with workforce requirements across 
the entire lifecycle of nuclear programs—from initial 
planning through decades of operation to eventual 
decommissioning. The platform provides real-time 
analytics and visual dashboards that track workforce 
flows from identified populations to education and training 
programs through employment across utilities, developers, 
contractors, regulators and support organizations. 
ReactorCast also models the impact of policy, regulatory 
and investment decisions on workforce development 
trajectories. Unlike individual HR management systems, 
ReactorCast operates at the strategic level—modeling the 
workforce potential to answer questions that matter most 
to executives, investors and leaders: Can this organization 
or region supply the talent we need? What does workforce 
availability mean for our site selection? How do different 
technology choices impact long-term staffing costs? 
These aren’t HR questions—they’re business strategy 
questions. 
The underlying modeling methodology— developed at 
Los Alamos and licensed to the IAEA as the basis for 
their national nuclear workforce planning workshops and 
tools—has been applied internationally across numerous 
nuclear programs. 
Challenges and Problems Solved
• In many deployment scenarios, lifecycle workforce 
costs can equal or exceed nuclear plant capital costs.
• ReactorCast ensures the human capital dimension 
receives the strategic attention it deserves, before 
workforce gaps derail timelines and budgets.
Technology Description
For those realizing new nuclear deployments, 
ReactorCast models workforce requirements across 
different reactor technologies and sites.
• Compare the human capital implications of a large 
light-water reactor versus multiple small modular 
reactors. 
• Assess whether different reactor technologies affect 
your ability to recruit and retain talent in specific 
regions. 
• Understand how workforce costs—which can exceed 
capital costs over a plant’s lifetime—vary based on 
technology and location decisions made today.
ReactorCast separates serious strategic planning 
from optimistic assumptions, giving stakeholders the 
intelligence to make informed decisions about workforce-
related project risk. 
ReactorCast
A strategic nuclear workforce intelligence 
platform that de-risks deployment
Value Proposition
Workforce shortages and uncertainties have derailed 
nuclear projects worldwide—causing delays, 
cost overruns and lost investor confidence. The 
specialized talent nuclear needs to succeed requires 
years to develop. The ReactorCast platform answers 
human capital questions, coupled to strategic 
decisions and financial considerations, before the 
issues become crises.
Technical Specifications
• Custom developed software for system dynamics 
modeling
• Modular, extensible design for evolving analysis 
needs
• Local deployment (secure, non-cloud 
infrastructure framework)
• Interfaces with external data sources and 
planning tools
• Outputs include: regional, statewide or 
national mapping, workforce opportunities and 
competency projections, gap analyses and 
scenario-based deployment comparisons

☒I recommend that NASA, NASA Shared Services Center negotiate only with vendors who can provide

This recommendation is for the acquisition of supplies or services determined to be reasonably available 
from only one source/only one manufacture. Competition is impractical for the following reasons (please 
answer the questions below): 
 
1. What are the reasons for soliciting only the suggested source/suggested brand name?  Please provide 
the unique characteristics of the items or services along with the supporting rationale and the market 
research performed to substantiate your reason for the suggested source/brand name. 
    
This requirement is for the renewal of maintenance and software support for existing, deployed data 
diode systems currently in operation within the Wind Tunnel System Branch. These systems are already 
integrated into the isolated wind tunnel network architecture and are critical to enforcing one-way data 
transfer between security zones.The requested vendor (Sentryron, formerly Fox-IT) is the original 
equipment manufacturer and sole provider of the proprietary software, firmware updates, and 
maintenance support required to sustain these deployed diodes. Due to the proprietary nature of the 
system design, software, and licensing model, equivalent support cannot be obtained from third-party 
vendors without introducing significant risk to system integrity and security compliance. While 
alternative data diode solutions exist, they are not directly compatible with the currently deployed 
hardware and would require full system replacement rather than a maintenance renewal. Additionally, 
comparable solutions—particularly at higher throughput tiers—are significantly more expensive and 
would exceed current budget constraints. 
 
2. What is the impact to the government if another vendor/brand is used?  Include any dollar, schedule, 
or compatibility impacts if possible. 
 
Utilizing an alternate vendor would require removal and replacement of the currently deployed data 
diode infrastructure, as other solutions are not compatible with the existing hardware or software 
environment. This would result in substantial cost increases due to new hardware procurement, system 
integration, and revalidation efforts.From a schedule perspective, replacing the existing solution would 
introduce delays associated with procurement, installation, testing, and security accreditation. This would 
impact ongoing operations that rely on secure, one-way data transfer within the wind tunnel 
environment.From a technical and operational standpoint, transitioning to a different vendor would 
introduce risk to system stability and could disrupt established data flows supporting wind tunnel testing 
and associated instrumentation. Maintaining continuity with the current solution ensures compatibility, 
minimizes risk, and supports uninterrupted mission operations.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

STaCS Database Software

US Army Criminal Investigation Laboratory

GENERAL: This is a non-personnel service contract to provide technical support and maintenance for the Sample Tracking and Control System (STaCS) software by STaCS DNA Inc. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn is responsible to the Government.

  Description of Services/Introduction: The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to complete requested support and maintenance as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract.

  Background: The United States Army Criminal Investigation Laboratory (USACIL) is designated as the CODIS program manager for the Department of Defense. The DNA Database Division of the USACIL is responsible for the analysis of DNA samples collected from military convicted offenders and arrestees. The DNA samples are collected using a kit developed and provided by the USACIL. The kits are received and processed by the DNA Database Division. The DNA profiles developed from the convicted offender and arrestee samples are entered into the Combined DNA Index System (CODIS), the database program that stores and searches the profiles. In CODIS, offender profiles are searched against forensic evidence profiles developed in the casework lab and are uploaded to the National DNA Index System (NDIS). At NDIS, the profiles are searched against casework profiles from all over the country. The DNA Database Division receives over 25,000 offender samples each year. In order to efficiently manage, track, and process this large quantity of samples, the Division utilizes a Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) specifically designed for DNA database labs, the Sample Tracking and Control System (STaCS). STaCS tracks samples throughout the laboratory process and maintains records regarding sample status, actions taken by personnel, and reagents and instrumentation used, among other things. The STaCS software allows the DNA Database Division to easily demonstrate compliance with the FBI’s Quality Assurance Standards for DNA Databasing Laboratories as well as ISO/IEC 17025, both of which are required continue CODIS participation.

  Objectives: The objective is for the vendor to remotely provide technical support and maintenance for the STaCS software currently in place at the USACIL’s DNA Database Division.

 Scope: Services include technical support and maintenance

 Period of Performance: The period of performance shall be for one (1) Year of 12 months.  

	Base Year (01 June 2026-31 May 2027)

1.6.1 Quality Control:  The contractor shall engage in an effective quality control program to ensure services are performed in accordance with this PWS.  The contractor’s quality control program is the means by which he assures himself that his work complies with the requirement of the contract. 

1.6.2 Quality Assurance:  The government shall evaluate the contractor’s performance under this contract in accordance with the USACIL Quality Manual, Casework DNA Division Technical Procedures and the ASCLD-LAB/ISO requirements.  These standards primarily focus on what the Government must do to ensure that the contractor has performed in accordance with the performance standards.  The standards define how the performance standards will be applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum acceptable defect rate(s).       

1.6.3 Recognized Holidays:  The contractor is not required to perform services on holidays.

When hiring personnel, the Contractor shall keep in mind that the stability and continuity of the workforce are essential.

1.6.6   Type of Contract:  The government will award a Fim-Fixed Proce (FFP) service contract.  

1.6.7   Security Requirements:  Contractor personnel performing work under this contract must be able to pass general access requirements for Gillem Enclave.

1.6.7.1.a  AT Level I Training. All contractor employees, to include subcontractor employees, requiring access Army installations, facilities and controlled access areas shall complete AT Level I Awareness training within 30 calendar days after contract start date or effective date of incorporation of this requirement into the contract, whichever is applicable. The contractor shall submit certificates of completion for each affected contractor employee and subcontractor employee, to the COR or to the contracting officer, if a COR is not assigned, within 15 calendar days after completion of training by all employees and subcontractor personnel. AT level I Awareness training is available at the following website: http://jko.jten.mil.

Contractor and all associated subcontractor employees shall provide all information required for background checks to meet installation access requirements to be accomplished by installation Provost Marshal Office, Director of Emergency Services or Security Office. Contractor workforce must comply with all personal identity verification requirements (FAR clause 52.204‐9, Personal Identity Verification of Contractor Personnel) as directed by DOD, HQDA and/or local policy. In addition to the changes otherwise authorized by the changes clause of this contract, should the Force Protection Condition (FPCON) at any individual facility or installation change, the Government may require changes in contractor security matters or processes.

1.6.7.1.c  Access to a DoD Facility or Installation. This local developed training will be used to inform employees of the types of behavior to watch for and instruct employees to report suspicious activity to the COR. This training shall be completed within calendar days of contract award and within calendar days of new employees commencing performance with the results reported to the COR NLT calendar days after contract award.

1.6.7.1.e  OPSEC Training. Per AR 530‐1, Operations Security, the contractor employees must complete Level I OPSEC Awareness training. New employees must be trained within 30 calendar days of their reporting for duty and annually thereafter.

1.6.7.1.f  Threat Awareness Reporting Program. For all contractors with security clearances. Per AR 381-12 Threat Awareness and Reporting Program (TARP), contractor employees must receive annual TARP training by a CI agent or other trainer as specified in 2-4b.

At these meetings the contracting officer will apprise the contractor of how the government views the contractor's performance and the contractor will apprise the Government of problems, if any, being experienced.  Appropriate action shall be taken to resolve outstanding issues.  These meetings shall be at no additional cost to the government.

The COR is authorized to perform the following functions: assure that the Contractor performs the technical requirements of the contract: perform inspections necessary in connection with contract performance: maintain written and oral communications with the Contractor concerning technical aspects of the contract: issue written interpretations of technical requirements, including Government drawings, designs, specifications: monitor Contractor's performance and notifies both the Contracting Officer and Contractor of any deficiencies; coordinate availability of government furnished property, and provide site entry of Contractor personnel. PART 2

DEFINITIONS & ACRONYMS

DEFINITIONS AND ACRONYMS:

DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY

Request for Information (RFI) on Scientifically Relevant Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Systems.		

THIS REQUEST IS FOR INFORMATION ONLY for conducting market research and does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation.  Responses are voluntary.  We will use the responses to inform strategic planning, program design, and future funding mechanisms.

AGENCY:  Office of Science, Department of Energy 

RFI Number:  892431-26-RFI-0001

Issue Date:  May 12, 2026

Response Due:  June 9, 2026 

Introduction

The United States (U.S.) Department of Energy (DOE) has a long history of deploying leading-edge computing capabilities for science and national security.  DOE is interested in integrating fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) into the U.S. and national laboratory scientific computing infrastructure.  DOE envisions quantum computing as an important tool that will enable scientific discovery.  This request for information (RFI) is to provide DOE with information on:

The viability of achieving identified technical targets for an FTQC by 2028.

An overview of a technical approach that is capable of achieving those targets.

The specific scientific applications such a system would enable and how they relate to the DOE mission.

Other factors that DOE should consider if a solicitation for such a system were to be developed.  

What, if any, non-recurring engineering (NRE) activities could accelerate delivery and enable them to be more capable, perform higher, have lower total ownership cost, and be more productive.  

DOE seeks input from respondents that may be interested in contributing hardware and/or software to this effort, if a future solicitation occurs.  DOE encourages respondents to use external expertise in their responses to complement their core capabilities.  Your written response should include your answers to the questions along with any other information you think will help us structure this potential solicitation.

Requested Information

Responses should address the six areas specified below.  If a topic does not apply to your organization or proposed approach, briefly explain why. 

DOE target capabilities 

DOE believes the deployment and demonstration of a scientifically relevant FTQC may be possible by 2028 that provides at least:

150-250 logical qubits

A computationally universal instruction set

The ability to accurately execute quantum circuits containing at least 105 hard operations (e.g., T or Toffoli gates) and a logical error rate of 10-8 per quantum operation.

Your response to this question should describe: 

Your view on the feasibility of this goal.  If this goal is infeasible, your recommendation on achievable, but still ambitious, goals for this timeframe

How you expect your architecture to achieve or approach these targets

Any alternative or additional metrics that describe your architecture to indicate its capabilities

How progress, milestones, and achievement of this capability should be tracked and evaluated. 

The hardware and software solution

Provide a high-level description of your contributions to the proposed system, including the following elements, as applicable:

Notional system architecture sketch including characteristics of the quantum register (e.g., physical qubits)

Logical architecture for fault-tolerant computation, including quantum error correction, logical gate set, and planned scheme for universal gates

Software environment, including development, compilation, execution, and system management components

Packaging, including site requirements, consumables, power, cooling, floor space, and weight (if you have a site preparation guide, please include it)

How the proposed solution fits into your long-term roadmap.

DOE scientific needs 

Discuss how the proposed system will demonstrate a scientific computing capability within the 2028 timeframe, along with how it will scale to provide high scientific value to DOE by the early-to-mid 2030s:

Comment on the accuracy of these resource estimates for high-impact scientific quantum computing in the 2028 timeframe.

Comment on how using current Federal initiatives—along with partnerships with the national laboratories, industrial, and academic complex—could accelerate and impact efforts. 

Identify specific, high-impact scientific problems or demonstrations the proposed quantum computing system is uniquely positioned to address, potentially in concert with High-Performance Computing and Artificial Intelligence.  

Provide resource requirements for these applications to the capability of the solutions proposed in the hardware and software section above.  

Propose examples of intermediate milestones that could benchmark progress toward the demonstration.

Ensure the problems are more specific than a broad application to a scientific domain. 

Describe other scientific domains (if any) impacting DOE’s mission where your implementation of scientifically relevant quantum computing will provide value.

Current estimates suggest future general DOE science campaigns must execute quantum circuits involving O(109) hard gates on 1000+ logical qubits to achieve broad impact on scientific domains, including chemistry, materials, plasma physics, and high energy physics.  Comment on: 

These resource estimates

High-impact problems your system expects to solve by early-to-mid 2030s

Your ultimate timeline to scale up to these systems. 

Describe any ways the proposed solution is uniquely suited, optimized, or codesigned for DOE’s science mission, as opposed to generic quantum computation.

Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE) considerations

NRE activities are work packages uniquely required for delivering a particular system or version of technology.  So, NRE costs are one-time expenses required to design, develop, and test a new product or process before it goes into production.  Once completed, that work does not have to be repeated and the outcomes typically apply to subsequent uses of the system.  This method is a way to support activities that may not already be on a vendor’s plan of record. 

Specific areas of NRE investment include activities leading to: 

Accelerated delivery schedule

Reduced system costs

Increased resilience and fault tolerance

Improved programmability

Any other innovations that improve time-to-solution or total cost of ownership

Describe the potential impact of NRE funding on the proposed system:

What are the primary areas where you feel NRE funding is needed?

How would NRE funding alter the system that might otherwise be bid (compressed schedule, improved technology, reduced cost, etc.)?

How would the NRE work complement your related R&D funding (internal and external)?

How does NRE funding impact cost?  For example, would it provide higher capability at the same cost or a reduced cost for the same capability?

Subsequent Systems and Innovations

Describe how the proposed system concept is expected to advance beyond 2028 to the early-to-mid 2030s timeframe, including, as appropriate:

Qubit technology and logical architectures

Fault tolerance and quantum error correction techniques

Infrastructure, packaging, ease of system management, or system-level integration

Other innovations relevant to improving capability or usability.

Cost and pricing

Provide cost estimates for the proposed system that would address the previously described technical specifications and, if applicable, unit costs for smaller, fully functional quantum computing modules that may be offered.  Include any other cost considerations such as cost drivers, hardware, software, licenses, support cost, and customizations.  This information will be used for internal budgeting purposes only and does not constitute a commitment from either DOE or your organizations.  

Partnership Structure

Describe how DOE can most effectively structure partnerships and provide incentives to achieve quantum computing platforms with the targeted specifications.  In your response, consider: 

Prize challenges or other transaction authorities (OTA) under 

42 U.S.C. §7256(a) and (g)  

Intellectual property rights, e.g., invention and data, for the government, national laboratories, and partners and developers that would best promote and enable innovation 

Any potential barriers to innovation in the standard DOE data rights in Rights in Data—Programs Covered Under Special Protected Data Statutes in Appendix A to Subpart D of Part 910 and standard patent rights in 37 C.F.R. § 401.14 for DOE to address using OTA flexibilities including at 2 C.F.R. Part 930  

Confidential Business Information	

Any person submitting information that he or she believes to be confidential and exempt by law from public disclosure should submit via email two well-marked copies:  one copy of the document marked “confidential” that includes all the information believed to be confidential, and one copy of the document marked “non-confidential” that does not include any information believed to be confidential (10 C.F.R. § 1004.11).

If you don’t follow these marking requirements, unmarked information could be disclosed under the Freedom of Information Act or otherwise.  The U.S. Government is not liable for disclosure or use of unmarked information and may use or disclose such information for any purpose.  If your response contains confidential, proprietary, or privileged information, you must include a cover sheet marked with the following Notice of Restriction on Disclosure and Use of Data identifying the specific pages containing confidential, proprietary, or privileged information:

Notice of Restriction on Disclosure and Use of Data

Pages [list applicable pages] of this response may contain confidential, proprietary, or privileged information that is exempt from public disclosure.  Such information shall be used or disclosed by the Government and its contractors (including DOE’s contractor operated laboratories) only for the purposes described in RFI 892431-26-RFI-0001.  The Government may use or disclose any information that is not appropriately marked or otherwise restricted, regardless of source.

In addition:

The header and footer of every page that contains confidential, proprietary, or privileged information must be marked:  Contains Confidential, Proprietary, or Privileged Information Exempt from Public Disclosure

Every line and paragraph containing proprietary, privileged, or trade secret information must be clearly marked with [[double brackets]] or highlighting.

DOE may make available for public inspection all other comments, in their entirety, submitted by organizations and businesses (except as provided above for proprietary information) or by individuals identifying themselves as representatives of organizations or businesses.

Submission Instructions

Responses should not exceed 20 pages, including attachments and cover letters.  Please also include the organization’s name and point of contact.  Your response can include an (optional) appendix providing feedback or changes to specific terms and conditions or DOE policy.  The appendix does not count toward your page count limit.

Submit your response electronically to QCInput@science.doe.gov and include “Scientifically Relevant FTQC Systems” in the subject line of the email.

Further Information  

You can send questions about this RFI to the DOE Office of Science Quantum Computing Team at QCInput@science.doe.gov.
