U.S. Department of Treasury

Office of the Chief Procurement Officer

FOIA and eDiscovery Management Systems and Supporting Services

Draft Performance Work Statement

TABLE OF CONTENTS

	

1.0	GENERAL INFORMATION

2.0	SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES

3.0	E-DISCOVERY/FOIA TASK DESCRIPTIONS

4.0	INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE

5.0	PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE

6.0	CLIN DETAIL

7.0	PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

8.0	HOURS OF OPERATION

9.0	PERSONNEL STAFFING

10.0	SECURITY

11.0	CONTRACT ADMINISTRATION

 




GENERAL INFORMATION

Purpose

The purpose of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to establish a department-wide Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) to provide a unified, secure, and scalable solution for managing all Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and electronic discovery (eDiscovery) requirements across the U.S. Department of the Treasury. This BPA is intended to consolidate common FOIA and eDiscovery needs under a single, enterprise-wide contract vehicle to enable consistent operations, improve efficiency, and eliminate redundant and fragmented procurements across Treasury bureaus and offices.

The BPA will serve as a strategic vehicle for acquiring cloud-based software licenses, professional services, and related support necessary to fulfill Treasury’s statutory obligations under the FOIA, the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure (FRCP), applicable federal records, and cybersecurity requirements. It will provide the Department with an enterprise-ready platform capable of managing the full lifecycle of FOIA requests and litigation discovery, from data intake and processing to review, redaction, production, and archival, while ensuring compliance with Federal risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP), Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), Section 508, and Treasury cybersecurity directives.

This acquisition will promote standardization, scalability, and innovation across Treasury’s FOIA and eDiscovery operations by leveraging modern commercial technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and advanced analytics, to increase transparency, reduce backlogs, and enhance responsiveness to public and legal information requests.

Background

The mission of the U.S. Department of the Treasury is to maintain a strong economy and create job opportunities by promoting conditions that enable economic growth and stability, strengthening national security through financial enforcement, and managing the federal government’s finances effectively. 

Treasury operates systems critical to the nation’s financial infrastructure, including the production of coin and currency, disbursement of payments, revenue collection, and debt management. It employs more than 100,000 personnel across 50+ offices and bureaus, such as the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), Bureau of the Fiscal Service (Fiscal Service), Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP), U.S. Mint, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (TTB), Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (TIGTA), and the Office of Inspector General (OIG).

Treasury’s operations generate substantial volumes of Electronically Stored Information (ESI) such as correspondence, reports, emails, chat records, multimedia, and database content. These data sets are subject to frequent FOIA requests, litigation discovery obligations, congressional inquiries, and oversight investigations. Treasury currently relies on multiple vendor solutions, such as Nuix Discover, Relativity, and FOIAXpress, operating across both on-premises and software-as-a-service (SaaS) environments. The Department requires a transition to a single, secure, and scalable cloud-based eDiscovery/FOIA platform to streamline compliance, improve transparency, and ensure standardized records management across all bureaus.

Statement of Need

Treasury requires an enterprise-wide eDiscovery and FOIA platform that:

Supports the full lifecycle of FOIA and discovery, including preservation, collection, processing, review, analysis, redaction, and production of ESI. 

Integrates with Treasury’s enterprise systems (MS Office 365, SharePoint, OneDrive, Email Servers, etc.)

Complies with:

Federal Rules of Civil Procedure (FRCP) governing discovery in litigation.

Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), 5 U.S.C. § 552, requiring timely responses to requests for agency records.

Privacy Act of 1974, 5 U.S.C. § 552a, safeguarding personal information.

Department of Justice (DOJ) Office of Information Policy (OIP) reporting requirements.

Records management directives under the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) Universal Electronic Records Management (ERM) Requirements.

Incorporates advanced AI and Machine Learning (ML) capabilities, such as Technology-Assisted Review (TAR), continuous active learning, automated entity recognition, predictive coding, and intelligent redaction, to increase processing speed and improve accuracy.

Given Treasury’s growing data volumes, the system must scale to handle terabytes of information, many concurrent users, and simultaneous FOIA and litigation workloads. 

SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES

The scope of this PWS encompasses the acquisition, implementation, and operation of an enterprise-wide, Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP)-authorized eDiscovery and FOIA Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution for the U.S. Department of the Treasury. The resulting BPA will provide a secure, scalable, and unified platform that consolidates Treasury’s common eDiscovery and FOIA needs under a single enterprise contract vehicle. The Contractor shall provide all software, cloud hosting, migration, integration, training, and support services required to fulfill Treasury’s statutory and operational requirements while ensuring continuity of current operations until full transition to the new SaaS environment is complete.

The Contractor shall:

Provide and maintain a vendor-hosted, FedRAMP-authorized cloud-based eDiscovery and/or FOIA SaaS platform that is fully operational upon award and capable of scaling to meet Department-wide workloads.

Ensure the platform complies with the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure (FRCP), Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552), Privacy Act (5 U.S.C. § 552a), NARA records-management directives, and applicable Treasury cybersecurity and privacy policies, while supporting continued operation of existing authorized systems until transition is complete. 

Develop and implement data-migration tools and processes to transfer documents, metadata, and workspaces from legacy systems to the new SaaS environment, including validation and quality-assurance checkpoints.

Provide access to both active-review data and cold-storage repositories sized to meet Treasury’s maximum projected consolidated capacity requirements.

Support collection, preservation, processing, ingestion, review, and production of data in a wide range of formats, including but not limited to: Adobe PDF, AppleDouble, CAD, compressed and container files, database exports, email, EnCase, Excel, Google Workspace, Hangul, HTML, iCalendar, image files, Lotus, JungUm Global, OneNote, OpenOffice, PowerPoint, Publisher, Project, short-message and chat data (e.g., Slack), text, vector graphics, Visio, Word, WordPerfect, and multimedia files.

Deliver AI/ML-powered capabilities that enhance eDiscovery and FOIA workflows, including continuous active learning, technology-assisted review (TAR), automated redaction, privilege assessment, predictive coding, data visualization, and standardized templates for data ingestion and case processing. These capabilities shall reduce manual workload, improve classification accuracy, and ensure consistent application of FOIA exemptions and legal-privilege protections across large datasets.

Provide granular access controls enabling restriction of access at the document, workspace, or user-role level and support multi-factor authentication consistent with Treasury identity-management policies.

Integrate seamlessly with Treasury and third-party systems, including Microsoft 365 (Outlook, SharePoint, Teams, OneDrive), FOIA.gov, Pay.gov, and other approved repositories and monitoring tools.

Ensure cross-platform compatibility across major browsers and mobile operating systems and maintain full Section 508 accessibility compliance.

Provide professional support services, including data processing and ingestion, end-user and administrator training, help-desk support (Tier I–III), and consulting on the use of advanced tools, analytics, and best-practice workflows.

Obtain and maintain an Authority to Operate (ATO) and Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) for the SaaS solution in accordance with Treasury Cybersecurity and Privacy directives and sustain compliance through continuous monitoring.

Maintain interim continuity by supporting existing Treasury-authorized cloud or on-premises systems until the new SaaS platform receives an ATO and all bureaus have transitioned.

Accommodate future expansion of eDiscovery/FOIA scope and incorporation of new data types, AI capabilities, or regulatory changes aligned with Treasury’s evolving mission and statutory obligations.

The services below shall meet Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) compatibility.

E-DISCOVERY/FOIA TASK DESCRIPTIONS

The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and non-personal services necessary to provide the capabilities to the Department of the Treasury needed for collecting, preserving, processing, assessing, reviewing, analyzing, and producing ESI as defined in this PWS.

TASK 1: INTEGRATED E-DISCOVERY SOLUTION

(SHARED REQUIREMENTS)

Current and SaaS Solution Shared Technical and Functional Capabilities

The Contractor shall provide and maintain an Integrated eDiscovery Platform that supports Treasury’s eDiscovery operations and includes shared technical, security, and infrastructure requirements common to both eDiscovery and FOIA solutions. These shared requirements include hosting, authentication, data management, logging, accessibility, and security compliance capabilities that apply across Treasury’s records management and disclosure processes. The existing solutions shall have received, and currently be, ATO-cleared by Treasury Cybersecurity. Existing solutions will be used in the interim before a future SaaS is available. All requirements apply to both the current and future SaaS solutions unless noted inline. Unique requirements pertaining only to the SaaS solution are listed in section 3.1.10 (eDiscovery/FOIA AI - Shared Future State Specific Requirements).

The existing solutions shall be able to host 240 TB of ESI available for agency review upon initial service phase-in. The SaaS solution shall be able to host 480 TB of ESI.

The existing solutions shall provide scalable storage to seamlessly accommodate growth in data volume up to 400 TB in 5 TB increments. The SaaS solution shall provide scalable storage for growth up to 1500 TB of data in 10 TB increments. Data growth requirement is subject to change.

For the SaaS solution only: Treasury offices have approximately 180 TB of data located in 1,000 workspaces from the on-premises solution, which will migrate to the cloud-based solution. The anticipated storage capacity breakdown is as follows, but is subject to change:

Active Review – 240 TB

Cold Storage – 480 TB

Staging – 60 TB

Shall support up to 225 eDiscovery/335 FOIA concurrent users with minimal reduction in performance in comparison to a single user.

Shall be capable of supporting additional concurrent users, up to 750 concurrent users, with minimal reduction in performance.

Shall have the ability to report on user management.

Network element under the control of the Contractor shall be robust enough to accommodate 560 concurrent users with minimal reduction in performance.

Network element under the control of the Contractor shall be robust enough to accommodate additional concurrent users, to 750 concurrent users, with minimal reduction in performance. 

Shall provide a means of accessing the internal systems for end-users that is compliant with Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12), using the Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials or equivalent thereof.

Shall be able to verify all end-users are accessing the internal systems from the Treasury network or Treasury furnished equipment.

Shall provide a means for registering and accessing the internal user portals that is compliant with multi-factor authentication (MFA) at National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AAL2.

Shall have all hardware (virtual and physical) dedicated to the platform deployed in facilities physically located within the United States (U.S.).

All data stored, processed, analyzed, etc. within the system shall be stored on servers located within the U.S.

Shall be capable of hosting an individual case comprised of more than 25 TB of data. 

Shall comply with Treasury IT Security Baseline:

All Treasury systems, services, and Contractors shall comply with Treasury-wide IT security policies and standards, which incorporate baseline controls such as IRM 10.8.1 (Information Technology Security, Policy and Guidance) and relevant technical and Web Server Security Standard.

The Contractor shall implement, maintain, and demonstrate compliance with these policies and standards, which are aligned with FISMA, NIST Special Publications (SP 800-53, SP 800-171, SP 800-137), OMB A-130, and other federal cybersecurity mandates.

Future state SaaS solution only: These requirements shall apply across all Treasury bureaus and systems, ensuring consistent IT security governance, configuration baselines, monitoring, logging, and vulnerability management.

Contractors shall meet or exceed those requirements Treasury-wide, unless otherwise directed by the Department of the Treasury.

Future state SaaS solution only: bureau specific requirements must be considered during implementation stage.

Desired Outcome: 

	A uniform Treasury-wide security posture that ensures:

Consistency across all bureaus in applying IT security standards.

Resilience against cyber threats through proactive controls and rapid remediation.

Accountability through auditable, standardized documentation and reporting.

Compliance with federal law and Treasury directives, reducing risk of breaches, audit findings, and operational disruptions.

Shall be, and remain, compliant with FISMA.

Future state SaaS solution: shall be, and remain, authorized at minimum as FedRAMP Moderate.

Shall be, and remain, compliant with Treasury Information Technology (IT) and Cybersecurity Operational Cloud requirements for both Vendor hosted SaaS or Treasury hosted cloud solutions.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

Background

The Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS) is an organization of approximately 2,500 personnel of which 700 serve at HQ and the remaining staff serve at offices worldwide.  NCIS is the Department of the Navy (DoN) component with primary responsibility for criminal investigation, law enforcement (LE), counter-terrorism (CT), counter-intelligence (CI), and cyber matters.  NCIS not only has primary responsibility for all criminal investigative, CI, CT, and cyber matters within the DoN, but it also has exclusive investigative jurisdiction in non-combat matters involving actual, potential, or suspected criminal, terrorism, sabotage, espionage, and subversive activities.  NCIS provides the DoN with threat status and warnings associated with terrorist, criminal, cyber, and counter-intelligence activity throughout the world.  NCIS is the only DoN organization that has the information and responsibility to fuse and analyze the national intelligence and law enforcement information necessary to provide these warnings.  Due to worldwide changes and increased threats to the DoN, NCIS must increase its overall capability to provide DoN Commanders with a timely and accurate common operational picture (COP) of security threats and vulnerabilities in and around existing naval facilities.  

The NCIS Cyber Directorate supports and advances the agency’s mission of investigating and defeating criminal, terrorist, and foreign intelligence threats to the DoN – in the maritime domain, ashore, and in cyberspace.  The Cyber Directorate within NCIS provides an agile, enterprise capability that supports the law enforcement/counter-intelligence mission and drives innovation in collaboration with mission partners, industry, and academia to out-maneuver and defeat threats to the Department of the Navy (DoN) in cyberspace.  The strategic goals of the Cyber Directorate are threefold:  (1) Operate a unified cyber capability across the DoN network enterprise in support of law enforcement and counter-intelligence activities and protect DoN personnel, assets and infrastructure from foreign intelligence, criminal and terrorist threats; (2) Conduct operations and investigations in the cyber domain and  provide digital information and analysis of counter-intelligence or evidentiary value; and (3) Enhance shared cyber situational awareness and  implement operational, intelligence, and information-sharing relationships with key cyber counterparts to enable active network defense.

Scope

This Performance Work Statement (PWS) for the Cyber Directorate describes the support services required by the Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS) to meet their strategic goals noted above.  This PWS identifies the tasking requirements of the Government and allows for flexibility in the development and evolution of the Cyber Directorate’s initiatives.  The PWS is not written to tell the Contractor how to provide support.  In this way, the Contractor is given maximum opportunity to provide support as it sees fit, but in accordance with stated Department of Defense (DoD) and Department of Navy (DoN) mandates and/or other requirements to which the Contractor must adhere.  NCIS desires that the Contractor bring a mission focus that continuously identifies new performance methods, processes, and procedures for applying information technology to improve NCIS’ mission performance, as well as recommendations and ideas for executing its mission in a more cost-effective, efficient, but service-oriented fashion.  The Contractor’s approach to the work should be innovative, comprehensive, and executed as an integrated team with the Government.

CYBER DIRECTORATE Core Functional Area Requirements and Outcomes

The tasking efforts identified in this PWS provide the range of technical and operational capabilities that are required to support the NCIS Cyber Directorate’s (NCIS Cyber) ability to use digital information to identify and counter threats to DoN critical assets, personnel, operations, computer networks, and information.  The Contractor shall maintain and develop new capabilities for NCIS Cyber's data aggregation and analysis system.  In addition, the Contractor will identify and assess new capabilities for collecting, analyzing, and exploiting digital data. The system shall be improved to incorporate additional data types and the user interface shall be continuously improved to automatically correlate data from new sources.  High priority information shall be identified and highlighted to users. The system shall make use of artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) capabilities to automatically identify events of interest, reduce the learning curve for new users and reduce the mental strain on all users through data summarization and natural language capabilities. 

The system shall also serve as the backbone for NCIS Cyber's data centralization project.  The system shall enable NCIS and community analysts and agents to leverage NCIS Cyber's digital information to enhance their investigative and operational capabilities.  In executing this PWS, the Contractor shall adhere to the following global set of requirements that apply to each functional areas identified in this PWS.  The Contractor shall: 

Provide personnel that are trained for their roles, flexible, willing to learn, able to adapt to changing stakeholder needs, and follow NCIS Cyber established standards and operating procedures.

Execute cross-division collaboration such that best practices and standards are performed as needed and as required.

Maintain patch/update cycle, centrally manage operating system (OS) builds, and follow configuration management (CM) guidelines as provided by the Government throughout development, testing, deployment, and production.  NCIS follows industry standards for Capability Maturity Model Integration [CMMI] with specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for NCIS implementation.

Follow NCIS Cyber organizational policies and procedures (e.g., Software Development Life Cycle [SDLC], CMMI) and participate in configuration and change management control initiatives.

Document artifacts and deliverables according to standardized formats and approved templates created through collaboration with NCIS Cyber Program Management Division and Cyber Capabilities & Integration Division (Code 20A and Code 20C).

Provide recommendations for process and programmatic improvement areas to reduce cost and enhance IT services.

Provide support for custom classified system, which is based on a proprietary configuration, to include  development and implementation of custom features such as AI/ML capabilities, to meet customer requirements, management of core features (i.e., data post-processing, version control, and data ingest), integrate new datasets with existing data collection feeds, manage the processing of daily data loads, maintain backend database and supporting middleware, manage storage and respond to system faults, maintain persistent virtual machines (VMs) and VM pool.

Cyber Directorate Contractor Program and Task Management

The technical and management efforts in this contract shall be conducted under the direction and coordination of a Program Manager (PM).  The PM shall meet the requirements for this labor category as stated in Appendix D – Position Descriptions and Personnel Qualifications.  While the primary focus for the Contractor will be daily operations and maintenance activities, the Contractor will be expected to improve the data aggregation and analysis system as noted earlier.  Consequently, a key requirement for the PM is to maintain a staffing plan that provides adequate depth of primary and secondary resources such that continuity can be ensured in the event of turnover.   

Cyber Directorate Contractor Program and Task Management Requirements

Requirements for the Contractor Program and Task Management function include:

Provide overall, on-site, day-to-day management of the program and its inherent tasks; costs; personnel; planning; and quality control necessary to ensure effective contract performance.

Ensure Contractor personnel accessing information systems meet the applicable training and certification requirements. 

Manage and execute the tasks for the Government as appropriate and as required.

Follow policies and processes established in conjunction with NCIS Cyber.

Routinely conduct in-depth reviews to identify progress, risks, and other issues that impact the success of contract performance.

Provide status reports and other deliverables as described in Appendix B, Schedule of Deliverables.

Develop, coordinate, and brief program goals and other program aspects, as determined by the Government, in Monthly Interim Progress Reviews (IPRs)(CDRL A002).

Brief project plans to senior NCIS leaders, as required.

Ensure Contractor’s services and products adhere to standards of quality prescribed by NCIS and Cyber Directorate.

Routinely identify and execute, where approved by the Government, recommendations that are innovative ideas for process efficiencies that facilitate better service delivery. 

Provide input to the Government for any disaster recovery/incident after action report, as required.

 Provide monthly status report on past month’s accomplishments (CDRL A001).

Cyber Directorate Contractor Program and Task Management Outcomes

Outcomes for the Contractor Program and Task Management function include:

Staffing levels are maintained with appropriate skill sets such that services are effectively delivered.

Production and on-time delivery of all required deliverables identified herein are achieved.

Costs are monitored and controlled ensuring that the Government is receiving best value for services rendered.

All tasks are completed on time and within budget, and will have had appropriate and significant participation from the Contractor. 

All tasks are executed in compliance with the Cyber Directorate Portfolio Management/Project Management processes.

Risks are identified and mitigated; negative impacts from realized risks and other issues are minimized.

Strengths and weaknesses in the Program and Task Management functional area are identified and addressed, as appropriate.

Underlying gaps in performance drivers will have been diagnosed. 

Performance improvements will have been prescribed.

Cyber Directorate Applications and Software:  Engineering, Data Aggregation and Analysis, Development, Integration, and Maintenance Support

To provide best value to the Government, software efforts must be done in such a way that they ensure NCIS is meeting mission needs while reducing maintenance requirements.  NCIS Cyber requires that software efforts be based on sound engineering principles and practices such that they improve run-time production and support to NCIS Cyber’s user base; however, in engineering the way forward, the vendor must take into account aspects of the infrastructure that are mandated by the DoN and/or the DoD. 

The Contractor shall be responsible for performing development activities that meet customer requirements by including stakeholders through joint application development efforts such as user acceptance testing or requirements elicitation meetings.  By performing in this way, NCIS Cyber can be assured that requirements and use cases are gathered and can be traced throughout the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).  The listing of the NCIS Cyber Directorate’s current software applications and technologies can be found in Appendix C, Cyber Directorate Applications and Technologies.  

This functional area provides much needed capabilities in support of NCIS’ and NCIS Cyber’s missions.  Analytic resources are often used to liaise with end users and engineers to create documents.  The Contractor will be accountable for proper descriptive documentation submitted through NCIS Cyber’s Configuration Management (CM) process.  These documents include, but are not necessarily limited to the following categories: 

Requirements documentation

Test plans, procedures, associated test data, and results

Operations and support manuals

Maintenance and diagnostic manuals with illustrated parts breakdowns

Programmer’s manuals.

Software and application monitoring and maintenance are required to ensure that NCIS mission support is available as needed.  The Contractor will measure and audit application performance using a variety of existing and potentially new capabilities to ensure the identification of relevant system utilization and data accuracy metrics.  These metrics should be used to improve Contractor performance.

Cyber Directorate Applications and Software:  Engineering, Data Aggregation and Analysis, Development, Integration, and Maintenance Support Requirements

Requirements for the Applications and Software: Analysis, Engineering, Data Aggregation and Analysis, Development, Integration, and Maintenance Support functions include: 

1.	Ensure key software components are developed and delivered in support of the SDLC, and that critical Quality Assurance (QA) measures are adopted and implemented.

2.	Recommend, implement and leverage processes, policies, and procedures in support of SDLC practices across the NCIS Cyber Divisions.

3.	Meet mission requirements while reducing maintenance complexities based on sound engineering principles and practices.

4.	Develop a technical architecture that is fully integrated with the developing NCIS Cyber systems architecture and is compliant with Department of Defense Architecture Framework (DODAF) and DoN EAs.

5.	Develop technical roadmaps and architectures that incorporate NCIS Cyber strategic direction and ensure compliance with DoD, DoN, and NCIS Cyber.

6.	Build-in metrics and metadata to capture system statistics that ensure quality application performance (e.g., user loads, usage, outages, data processed) and move to consolidate application system resources whenever possible.

7.	Ensure that cross-division collaboration is executed in a way that best practices and standards are honored.

8.	Perform reviews of existing systems and make recommendations for application systems and components that can be modernized, combined, and retired.

Statement of Work (SOW) FOR Jaglink Sustainment Services In Support of the Office of the Judge Advocate General and Naval Legal 
Service Commands
I. BACKGROUND
The Office of the Judge Advocate General (OJAG) and Commander, Naval Legal Service Command (CNLSC), are responsible for providing legal 
advice and related services throughout the Department of the Navy (DON). The JAGLINK application is a custom contact application that houses 
information on service members and civilians in the JAG community. JAGLINK was developed and hosted inside of SharePoint and is now being 
sustained within the FlankSpeed environment, a Microsoft 365-based platform designed for the DoD that provides a suite of collaboration and 
productivity tools in a secure cloud environment.
II. SCOPE
This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the services, deliverables, and expectations between the contractor and The Office of the Judge Advocate 
General (OJAG) for the ongoing sustainment and support of JAGLINK within the FlankSpeed environment. For the purposes of this SOW, a "small 
change" is defined as any modification or enhancement that can be completed within 20 hours of effort. Any change request anticipated to exceed this 
threshold will be considered a new enhancement and will require a separate scope and approval process.
III. ASSUMPTIONS.
1. Contractor Personnel will report to IT OPS and the Detailers Office and provide weekly reports to IT OPS on hours worked and what actions were 
completed for the week.
2. Contractor Personnel will maintain access to the NMCI Navy Network and an active CAC.
3. Contractor personnel will have the necessary expertise to interface directly with stakeholders to clarify requirements and manage expectations 
regarding the JAGLINK application's capabilities.
4. The underlying FlankSpeed/Microsoft 365 platform will remain stable and accessible, with any platform-wide changes communicated by the 
government in a timely manner.
IV. APPROACH
The contractor shall adopt a three-pronged approach to the sustainment of the JAGLINK application:
1. Proactive Management 
Implement a continuous monitoring strategy to identify and resolve potential issues before they affect users. This includes performing regular 
application health checks and monitoring process flows to ensure optimal performance and minimize downtime.
2. Structured Processes 
Utilize a formal process for managing bug fixes, issue resolution, and user support, guided by the Service Level Agreements (SLAs) defined in this 
SOW. All changes and resolutions will be tracked and prioritized systematically.
3. Continuous Improvement
Prioritize comprehensive documentation, knowledge transfer, and user training to reduce recurring support requests. The contractor will translate user 
feedback and technical analysis into actionable recommendations for future application enhancements.
V. REQUIREMENTS
a) Proactive Monitoring and Health Checks 
1. Continuously monitor application performance to identify and address potential issues before they impact users.
2. Perform routine "health checks" on the app to ensure all components are functioning as expected and are compatible with updates to the underlying 
platform (e.g., Microsoft 365, Dataverse). 
3. Monitor Power Automate run histories to identify and troubleshoot failed flows.
b) Bug Fixes and Issue Resolution
1. Manage a backlog of reported issues, prioritizing "break-fix" problems over enhancement requests. 
2. Troubleshoot and resolve common issues, such as data validation errors or problems with business rules. 
3. Conduct root cause analysis to identify the source of complex issues, which could originate from Power Automate logic, Dataverse data constraints, 
or user permission errors.
4. Adhere to the following Service Level Agreements (SLAs) for issue resolution:
"Priority" "Definition" "Response Time" "Resolution Time"
"Critical" "Application Outage / System Unusable" "1 Business Hour" "4 Business Hours"
"High" "Major Functionality Impaired" "2 Business Hours" "8 Business Hours"
"Medium" "Minor Functionality Impaired" "8 Business Hours" "3 Business Days"
c) Maintenance and Enhancements
1. Create, troubleshoot, and optimize automated, instant, and scheduled flows to handle business logic and notifications
2. Over the course of the period of performance, the contractor shall provide a total level of effort not to exceed 80 hours for developmental support of 
new enhancements. All requests for enhancements will be submitted to the IT OPS Government POC, who will have the final authority to prioritize 
the work and approve the use of these development hours.
3. Implement approved "small changes" to the application, such as adding new fields, modifying forms, or adjusting business rules. 
4. Translate user feedback and recurring support issues into actionable suggestions for future enhancements
d) User Support and Training
1. Provide Tier 2 and Tier 3 technical support for end-users.
2. Develop and maintain user-friendly documentation and a library of short tutorials for any new application features.
3. Provide training to end users to aid them in maximizing use of the application
N0018926QW168
Page 4 of 26

e) COMPLEXITY/RESPONSIBILITY
Work on this requirement demands a high level of knowledge of the Power Platform (Power Apps, Dataverse, Power Automate), Microsoft 365, and 
the business processes of the JAG community. The contractor must analyze and understand JAG's business requirements to ensure the application 
aligns with user goals.
f) GOVERNMENT RESPONSIBILITIES
1. The government will provide timely access to all necessary systems, accounts, and points of contact (POCs) to facilitate the contractor's work.
2. The government will be responsible for providing and maintaining NMCI Navy Network access and active CACs for contractor personnel.
3. Delays in providing necessary access or resources may result in adjustments to project timelines and deliverables.
g) SCOPE OF INTERPERSONAL CONTACTS
Contacts are with IT OPS, government personnel, and detailers.
h) NECESSARY SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:
1. Daily connectivity via cellular telephone, email, or Microsoft Teams is required.
2. CONTRACTOR SHALL NOT:
a. Participate in any situation where it might be assumed that they are an agency employee or representative.
b. Determine agency policy, such as determining the content and application of regulations.
c. Work in any situation that permits or might permit gaining access to confidential business information and/or any other sensitive information.
d. Determine what Government property is to be disposed of and on what terms.
VI. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS.
The minimum is a background investigation T1. There is no expectation that contractor personnel will require a security clearance of Secret. 
Therefore, the contractor must be able to provide individuals who are eligible for a T1 background investigation in order to immediately begin 
performance at the time of task awards.
VII. GOVERNMENT FURNISHED EQUIPMENT (GFE).
None provided
VIII. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE.
1. Performance will be from the contractor's location.
2. Normal working hours are 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, All services shall be provided during the government's standard business days (Monday through 
Friday, excluding Federal holidays). The contractor shall ensure a response to routine inquiries and requests for support within eight (8) business 
hours. For mission-critical system failures, the contractor must be available to respond within two (1) hour of notification, including outside of 
standard business hours
3. The following government holidays are typically observed by government personnel: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King's Birthday, Presidential 
Inauguration Day (metropolitan DC area only), President's Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veteran's 
Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day, and any other day designated by Federal Statute, Executive Order, and/or Presidential Proclamation.
IX. TRAVEL.
Not Required
X. DELIVERABLES.
1. Monthly Sustainment Report: A comprehensive report delivered by the 5th business day of each month, including:
A summary of all maintenance activities and "small changes" implemented.
Key performance metrics, including application uptime and SLA adherence.
2. A list of all support tickets opened, closed, and pending, with resolution times. Updated Documentation: All changes to the application's 
functionality or architecture will be documented and delivered alongside the release, including updates to technical design documents and user guides.
XI. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE
1. POP shall be in effect: 14 MAY 2026 - 13 May 2027
2. Personnel:
One (1) Supervisory Microsoft Power Apps Architect (with 10 or more years' experience)
One (1) Microsoft Power Apps Developer (with 10 or more years' experience) for remote Microsoft Power Apps support.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW)

	

1.  Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR).  

2.  Contract Title.  

Data Aggregator and Viewing Tool

3.  Background.  

The goal for the Research team procuring this service is to aggregate and index VA-housed healthcare data available for Research, and allow in-house researchers and data scientists to easily utilize this data for their work. All data specified below are part of IRB/R&D approved VA studies and are also VA Office of Research and Development (ORD) funded.  Radiologic data for our lung cancer research currently includes 21,201 full-resolution Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) imaging studies, corresponding to approximately 5.3 terabytes of CT data curated from multiple VA medical centers.  Prostate cancer imaging aggregation currently includes 64,068 prostate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies, totaling approximately 14.5 terabytes of radiologic data. In addition, 41,895 digitized pathology slides have been generated from biopsy and surgical specimens, comprising approximately 42 terabytes of whole slide imaging data. The head and neck cancer dataset includes 2,488 radiologic imaging studies, totaling approximately 0.6 terabytes, and approximately 3,703 digitized pathology slides, comprising 3.0 terabytes of whole slide imaging data. This data has also been anonymized using a custom tool already delivered to the VA. This goal will be achieved by building an easy to use web interface backed by a queryable database that contains a manifest of all the data available (identifiable and anonymized/coded). This will be built on a Research Scientific Computing Device approved through enterprise risk assessment (ERA) and located outside of the base VA network.  This system, once complete, will allow VA scientists to see what data is available, and provide an easy ability to get that data into their workspace, whether through downloading or pointing to a network drive. The ultimate goal is to reduce the friction between scattered datasets and novel healthcare breakthroughs within the VA. The datasets are too scattered and there’s too much inefficiency in being able to utilize the data for medical research. This tool will accelerate the VA’s efforts to develop new precision medicine tools for Veterans. 

4.  Scope. 

The procurement for computing services to enable the automated building of a database containing a manifest of available data with a deployed web interface for selecting datasets or subsets, and the ability to download selected data for research within the VA.  The software is custom and only useful our research operations and will only be used on our dedicated RSCD.  The vendor will not be given access to VA data but use publicly data available for creation. All testing and evaluation of the database will be conducted by VA personnel in consultation with the vendor. 

5. Specific Tasks.  

Specification Overview:

Ingestion & Preprocessing

1. Multi-Modality Ingest Engine

Accept manifests (CSV) of pre-anonymized data.

Accept manifests of data with PHI, extract common patient identifiers (SSN+DOB), and generate internal randomized patient keys.

Normalize date formats, field names, and data types across modalities.

2. Data Harmonization Layer

Merge patient data from all modalities into unified data structure.

Resolve discrepancies across modalities (e.g., demographic mismatches).

Flag or log ambiguous merges for review.

Link associated medical imagery to the patient/study.

Add fields like PatientAge, ModalityFlags, LatestLabDate, etc.

Condense one-to-many lab/test records into structured arrays or summaries.

Database Layer

3. Schema Definition and Migrations

Define SQL schema for each of: Patient, CT, MRI, Lab_Test, etc.

Define foreign key constraints.

Include indices on PatientID, StudyDate, etc.

4. Direct-to-DB Loader

Load processed manifest records into SQL database.

Provide hooks for batch ingestion, validation, and rollback on error.

Web-Based Exploration UI

5. Browseable Patient Index

Build a Flask UI to browse by patient fields (e.g., modality, indication, body part, age, lab results).

Support filters, pagination, and search history.

6. Data Visualizations

For both filtered and cumulative data, display charts:

Modality counts (bar/pie chart)

Age distributions (histogram, violin)

Number of studies per year (line/bar)

Longitudinal time length (years of data available per patient, histogram)

7. Patient Record Viewer & Selector

Table or card-based interface for viewing patient summaries.

Include checkbox-style selection with "Select All" and "Deselect All" functions.

Persist selections via session or browser storage.

Data Export

8. Export Interface

Allow the user on the web app to select either all or a subset of filtered data.

Show a “checkout summary” screen, that shows statistics of the selected dataset, such as total size (e.g. in gigabytes) and estimated download time.

Show options to access data via network drive (preferred) or download the data.

Export a manifest file in either JSON or CSV format of the selected dataset showing metadata about the data.

9. Network Drive Access

If the user has access to a network drive with the source data, allow them to download a location manifest to access the source data.

Have the docker container running the backend to create a new directory for the user, with a UUID subfolder name, that contains symlinks to selected data.

10. Downloader Tool

Create a tool that inputs a manifest file and downloads the data locally.

Containerize it.

Secure it with best practices so only authorized users can download the data.

Show progress bar, ETA, graphical elements as needed.

Deployment & Testing

11. Integrations and Unit Tests

Validate merge logic, anonymization, and derived fields.

Simulate user actions across UI: ingestion → filtering → selection → export.

Confirm that selected records are correctly exported in requested format and anonymized.

12. Deployment

Let researchers stand up the web interface within RSCD.

System should regularly check it has access to the network drive of source data.

Have single source of truth (on network drive) of database of available data.

Easy link to downloader tool.

13. User Documentation & Usage Examples

Write clean, public-facing README with:

Overview of the tool

How to ingest and explore data

How to select, anonymize, and export for modeling

Screenshots of the web interface

Create video instructions and examples

System Requirements:

Modalities:
CT, MRI, Digital Pathology, Bloodwork, Test Results

Data Pipeline:
Anonymize → Ingest → Preprocess → Store → Explore → Select → Export

Backend:
Python + SQLAlchemy + SQLite/PostgreSQL

https://www.oit.va.gov/Services/TRM/ToolPage.aspx?tid=5702

https://www.oit.va.gov/Services/TRM/ToolPage.aspx?tid=6406

Frontend:
Flask + Bootstrap + Plotly

https://www.oit.va.gov/Services/TRM/ToolPage.aspx?tid=10316

https://www.oit.va.gov/Services/TRM/ToolPage.aspx?tid=7795

Deployment:
Docker containerization/ Podman - https://www.oit.va.gov/Services/TRM/ToolPage.aspx?tid=14897&tab=2

Evaluation by Research Team:

Step 1 will be to take an existing public data study, ingest it, and then query known data (as a sanity check) on RSCD (non-GFE device).

Step 2 will be to run this on RSCD for several VA data sets, then, someone from the Research team will manually check for accuracy of aggregation and visualization of data.

Step 3 will be to work with the vendor to present aggregate results and set up punch list to fix any errors.

Deliverables:	

Delivery of functional software that passed the evaluation steps shown above. 

Database containing manifest of available data.

Deployed web interface for selecting datasets or subsets.

Successfully downloading selected data for research.

6. Performance Monitoring

The software is expected to be completed within 120 days and the requestor will have weekly meetings to discuss progress on the software.  Once the evaluation steps are completed, the code will be run on a VA device and ensured to operate as described. 

7. Contract Type: Firm fixed price

None
